The fee is allowed if fixed as a lump sum and not as a percentage
explanation: Per 2/4, underwriting the issue is permissible when done without compensation in lieu of underwriting.

title: Credit Agreement
q: Bank A is Rab al-Mal in a Mudarabah; the Mudarib managed the project properly but it made a loss. Who bears the loss?
options: Both parties, in proportion to time and capital
The Bank as Rab al-Mal bears the entire loss
The Mudarib, as he managed the project
Both parties, in their profit-sharing ratio
explanation: Per 3/2/2, in Mudarabah the entire loss is borne by Rab al-Mal unless it is due to transgression or negligence of the Mudarib.

title: Syndicated Financing
q: The participants ask Bank A, the lead manager acting as Mudarib, to guarantee the syndication funds against any loss. What is the ruling?
options: Allowed, but only for half of the funds contributed by the participants
Allowed, since it controls the funds as manager and can protect them better
Not allowed: a trustee is liable only for misconduct or negligence
Allowed, if it is paid an extra fee for giving the guarantee to participants
explanation: Per 8/1, the lead manager (Mudarib, partner or agent) is a trustee and should not guarantee funds except for misconduct, negligence or breach of conditions.

title: Mortgage and its Contemporary Applications
q: Why is a mortgagee barred from benefiting free of charge from the mortgaged asset, per the basis?
options: Otherwise he would be committing Riba
Otherwise he would owe Zakah on the asset
Otherwise the mortgage would become a sale
Otherwise he would breach the notary's rights
explanation: Per the basis, the mortgagee does not have the right to make free of charge benefit from the mortgaged asset because otherwise he would be committing Riba.

title: Agency and the Act of an Uncommissioned Agent (Fodooli)
q: A discriminating minor appoints an agent to receive, on his behalf, a gift that his uncle wants to donate to him. What is the ruling?
options: Invalid, since gifts cannot be received through agency
Invalid, since a minor can never appoint an agent in any matter at all
Valid only after approval of the minor's guardian or the competent court
Valid, since the act results in absolute benefit to the minor
explanation: Per 3/1/2, a partially capable person such as a discriminating minor may appoint an agent in matters of absolute benefit, such as accepting donations.

title: Options to Revoke Contracts Due to Incomplete Performance
q: Ahmad buys a used machine. Neither he nor the seller knew it had a hidden material defect, which later appears. Does Ahmad have an option to revoke due to defect?
options: No, since the seller acted in good faith, without knowledge of the defect
Yes; the seller's unawareness of the defect is irrelevant
No; he may only claim Arsh, not revoke
Yes, but only if the seller knew of the defect
explanation: Per 2/2/3, the buyer must be unaware of the hidden defect at contracting, irrespective of the seller's awareness of it.

title: Agency and the Act of an Uncommissioned Agent (Fodooli)
q: Bank A appoints a broker as agent to sell its shares, effective today, but requires him to refer back to the Bank before each sale. What is the ruling?
options: Valid: agency is effective now; disposal awaits the condition
The condition is void and the broker may sell freely without referral
The agency becomes effective only after the first referral
Invalid: a condition may attach to the contract itself, not to the disposal
explanation: Per 2/2/4, conditions may be confined to disposal: the agency is immediately effective but disposal awaits a condition like referring back to the principal.

title: Distribution of Profit in Mudarabah-Based Investment Accounts
q: Bank A, as Mudarib, mixes its own funds with the investment account funds. How is the profit divided?
options: The Bank takes all profit attributable to the pool
The Bank earns only as partner on its funds, losing its Mudarib share
The Bank earns only as Mudarib, not on its funds
Between the two capitals; the Bank earns as partner and Mudarib
explanation: Per 4/7, mixing makes the Mudarib a partner by its funds and Mudarib for the other funds; profit is divided between the two capitals.

title: Commercial Papers
q: Company X issues a promissory note promising to pay Ahmad 50,000 in six months. How does the standard characterise this note in Shari'ah?
options: As a contract of agency
As a restricted Hawalah
As a certificate of debt
As a contract of Sarf
explanation: Per 2/2, a promissory note is a certificate whereby the issuer (debtor) promises to pay a sum; in Shari'ah characterisation it is a certificate of debt.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: On what principle does the Shari'ah basis rest the permissibility of modern corporations?
options: Custom overrides explicit texts in all commercial matters of the age
Necessity makes the prohibited permissible, and corporations arise from necessity
Modern laws are binding on all parties dealing within a given State
Human transactions are in principle permissible (Mubah)
explanation: Per the basis, transactions are in principle permissible (Mubah) absent a clear injunction, and these corporations parallel 'Inan, Mudarabah and the like.

title: Concession Contracts
q: The State hires a specialized body to conduct mineral exploration on the State's behalf. Which rulings govern this relationship?
options: The rulings of Mudarabah, as the State provides the capital
The rulings of Ijarah and Ju'alah
The rulings of Salam, as the exploration result is delivered later
The rulings of Musharakah, as the State shares in the minerals
explanation: Per 5/2/6, when the State requests a specialized body to survey or explore on its behalf, the relationship is subject to the rulings of Ijarah and Ju'alah.

title: Zakah
q: Company X prepares goods for export under a documentary credit in its favour. How are the amounts retained for the credit treated?
options: Neither Zakatable nor deductible, as not yet possessed
Zakatable at half their value until shipment
Zakatable in full as receivables of the company, since they are due from the issuing bank
Deductible from Zakatable assets as a liability
explanation: Per 5/2/6/8, amounts retained for an export credit are neither Zakatable nor deductible since not yet possessed; goods still held remain Zakatable.

title: Istisna’a and Parallel Istisna’a
q: A manufacturer asks Bank A, as ultimate purchaser in an Istisna'a, for a guarantee. Which may the Bank give?
options: None, since the Bank is the buyer
An undertaking to pay an extra amount if it pays late
Consent to blocking withdrawals from an account
An interest-bearing deposit placed with the maker
explanation: Per 3/3/2, as ultimate purchaser the Institution may give guarantees such as a mortgage, personal guarantee, assignment, accounts or consent to blocking withdrawals.

title: Liability of the Investment Manager
q: A Mudarib enters a large project without a feasibility study, though the contract stipulates one. The project fails. How is the Mudarib's conduct treated?
options: As negligence only if he acted intentionally
As ordinary business risk borne by Rab Al Maal
As a loss shared equally between the parties
As misconduct or negligence, making him liable
explanation: Per 5/3/2, not conducting a feasibility study despite its necessity by stipulation or custom is a form of misconduct and negligence.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: The Sharikah contract grants partner Ahmad, who keeps the partnership's accounts, a fixed monthly fee in addition to his profit share. What is the ruling?
options: Permitted, since accounting is a service and not capital
Not permitted, but he may get a greater profit share instead
Not permitted, and he may not receive any extra profit either
Permitted, provided the fee is charged as an expense
explanation: Per 3/1/3/4, a fixed remuneration for a partner who manages or provides services in the Sharikah contract is not permitted; a greater profit share is allowed.

title: Gold and Its Trading Parameters in Shari’ah
q: An importer deposits money with a gold exporter; a sale is concluded once a shipment is ready. The exporter has used the deposit. At what price is the gold sold?
options: At the market price on the date of the contract
At cost plus a profit agreed in advance
At any price the parties agree on that date
At a price agreed when the deposit was made
explanation: Per 10/5, the price is normally agreed at the contract date, but if the exporter utilized the deposit, the gold must be sold at that date's market price.

title: Hawalah
q: Bakr is transferred to a payer whose creditworthiness he does not know. Per the Shari'ah basis, why is accepting still permissible?
options: The transferor guarantees the payer in all cases
Gharar is always tolerated in Hawalah, as in all transfers
The Hadith sets no condition of the payer's solvency
The payer's solvency is always presumed by law
explanation: Per the Basis, the Hadith's order does not make the payer's solvency a condition for Hawalah's permissibility, so acceptance remains Mubah.

title: Waqf
q: A Waqf superintendent wants to lease Waqf land for 50 years at a fixed rent. Under the standard, when may such a long lease be used?
options: Only if the tenant is a Muslim institution
Only for obvious interest, with a variable index-linked rent
Whenever the Waqif did not forbid long leases
Whenever the tenant pays the whole rent in advance for all 50 years
explanation: Per 6/1, long leases should not be the normal practice for Waqf assets except for obvious interest, with a variable rent linked to an accurate, well-known index.

title: Combination of Contracts
q: Company X proposes a set combining a permissible Ijarah with a contract that is impermissible on its own. Can the combination make the set permissible?
options: Yes, since the set is judged only as a whole, not by its parts
Yes, if both share a single lump sum value
No, each combined contract must be permissible on its own
Yes, if the impermissible part is subsidiary
explanation: Per clause 3, combining contracts is permissible provided that each contract is permissible on its own.

title: Documentary Credit
q: Bank A issues a shipping guarantee so the client can release goods before documents arrive. Which rule governs its commission for this letter of guarantee?
options: A time-based fee for the period until the documents arrive from the seller
Free choice of the Institution and its client
The percentage-of-amount rule that applies to commission on credit services
The ruling on commission in the Shari'ah Standard on Guarantees
explanation: Per 3/3/3, commission for letters of guarantee accompanying credits, such as shipping guarantees, follows Shari'ah Standard No. (5) on Guarantees.

title: Salam and Parallel Salam
q: Bank A bought wheat by Salam from Farmer F and sold similar wheat by Parallel Salam to Mill M. F fails to deliver. May the Bank delay its delivery to M?
options: No, the two contracts stand alone
Yes, as M's contract depends on F's
Yes, and it may also cancel M's contract
Yes, if M was told of the first Salam
explanation: Per 6/3, obligations of the two Salam contracts may not be linked; breach in one gives no right to terminate or delay performance of the other.

title: Combination of Contracts
q: Ahmad sells his house to Karim for 1,000 dinars and rents him his car for 100 dinars per month. Neither is a condition of the other. What form is this?
options: Combined contracts with a single lump sum value
Combined contracts concluded for separate values
A single contract with two instalments
Combined contracts with one stipulated in the other
explanation: Per 2/2/2, combined contracts may be concluded for separate values, e.g. selling a house for 1,000 dinars and renting a car for 100 dinars per month.

title: Online Financial Dealings
q: During a phone conversation about a sale, Bank A's offer is made, then the parties move on to discuss a different subject before any acceptance. What is the status of the session?
options: The session continues for the whole working day
The session continues until the call is finally ended by either party
The contract signing session is considered to have stopped
The offer remains open until expressly withdrawn
explanation: Per 4/1/1, the session is the time of communication on the contract; if the conversation ends, is disconnected, or shifts to another subject, the session stops.

title: Liability of the Investment Manager
q: A Mudaraba contract requires the Mudarib to bear matters usually not carried by him, with the aim of making him liable for losses. What is the ruling?
options: Permitted, if it is stated clearly in the contract
Permitted, as Rab Al Maal may set any conditions
Permitted, if the Mudarib's profit share is raised
Not permitted, as it seeks to impose liability
explanation: Per 3/6, it is not permitted to stipulate on the investment manager what is usually not carried by him for the purpose of imposing liability.

title: Loan (Qard)
q: Bank A grants many small Qard loans in one group programme and cannot assign charges to each loan separately. How may it recover direct costs?
options: Charge direct collective costs, shared in proportion to each loan
Add a fixed percentage margin to every loan
Recover no costs at all, since each loan must bear its own charges only
Charge each loan a flat fee set by Bank A's management
explanation: Per 9/1, where loan-by-loan charging is difficult, as in a group loan, direct collective charges may be borne on the entire sum, each loan bearing its share proportionately.

title: Payment Cards
q: Why does a conversion into the card's currency at the merchant's point of sale need not be limited to actual cost, even on a lending-based card?
options: The merchant bears the exchange risk
It is done by an entity separate from the card issuer
Currency exchange is never limited to cost under any card
The cardholder pays it in cash at the point of sale
explanation: Basis 5/5/2: the exchange is by an entity separate from the issuer, so there is no objection of a loan combined with the exchange service.

title: Financial Paper (Shares and Bonds)
q: Bank A acts only as an intermediary executing share trades for clients in mixed companies. What is its duty regarding prohibited income?
options: Inform clients of the elimination mechanism so they can do it
Eliminate the prohibited income itself from all client accounts
Nothing, as the duty lies only with the company
Deduct the prohibited portion from its commission
explanation: Per 3/4/6/6, in intermediation the institution must inform dealers of the elimination mechanism; it may also offer the service, with or without a charge.

title: Irrigation Partnership (Musaqat)
q: A date-palm Musaqat is silent on by-products. Besides the dates, the palms yield palm leaves each season. How are the leaves treated?
options: They belong to the worker as a reward for work
They are sold and given to charity
Shared as part of the crop per the agreed ratios
They belong to the owner of the trees alone
explanation: Per 9/1, all recurring produce such as fruits and palm leaves is shared as part of the crop, unless the parties agreed to restrict sharing to the fruits.

title: Arbitration
q: In an arbitration with no prior agreement on expenses, Bank A applied for an expert report for its own claim. Who bears the cost of that report?
options: Both parties equally, as a common expense of the arbitration
The party that loses the arbitration
The arbitrator, out of his fees
Bank A alone, as it relates to its own application
explanation: Per 14/2, absent prior agreement, expenses relating to one party's application are borne by that party alone; common expenses are shared.

title: Loan (Qard)
q: Ahmad lent money to his neighbour without stipulating any period. When must the neighbour return its substitute (Badal)?
options: Only when the neighbour can afford it
On demand by Ahmad
Only after a court sets a date
After a customary period of one year
explanation: Per 6, if no period is stipulated in the Qard, it is binding on the borrower to return its substitute (Badal) on demand.

title: Combination of Contracts
q: Ahmad sells his land to Karim and rents him his car for one month, both for a total of one thousand dinars. What form of combined contracts is this?
options: Combined contracts with a single lump sum counter value
Combined contracts with one stipulated in the other
An exhaustive statement of successive stages
Combined contracts concluded for separate values
explanation: Per 2/2/1, combined contracts may have a single lump sum counter value, e.g. selling land and renting a car for one month, both against 1,000 dinars.

title: Irrigation Partnership (Musaqat)
q: Ahmad holds a long lease on an orchard (owning its usufruct, not the land). He contracts Karim to irrigate and tend it for one third of the produce. How is this contract classified?
options: A Mudarabah, since Karim contributes only work
An Ijarah of Karim's services, not a Musaqat
A valid Musaqat, as the owner of usufruct may contract
Invalid, as only the orchard's owner may contract
explanation: Per 2, Musaqat is a contract between the owner of an orchard or its usufruct and a worker (irrigator), sharing the produce in ratios stipulated at contracting.

title: Waqf
q: Ten years ago Ahmad created a cash Waqf of 100,000. Inflation has since halved its purchasing power. What is the Waqf asset now?
options: Nothing, as the Waqf ended when value eroded
Whatever amount the overseer re-values it at
The inflation-adjusted equivalent of 100,000
The nominal 100,000 named at creation
explanation: Per 2/4/13/4, the money nominated at creation is the Waqf asset; change in purchasing power has no influence on the cash Waqf value.

title: Hiring of Persons
q: An employee wants the right to end the contract if the employer fails to pay one or more instalments of pay. May he stipulate this?
options: Yes; this is Khiyar al-Naqd
Yes, but only after a court ruling
No; nonpayment only gives a right to sue
No; only the employer may stipulate termination
explanation: Per 8/2/3, the employee may stipulate termination when the employer fails or delays payment, or does not pay one or more instalments (Khiyar al-Naqd).

title: Murabahah
q: Bank A charges Customer C a fee in return for the Bank's commitment to execute a Murabahah with him later. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible if it reflects the Bank's actual costs
Permissible if deducted later from the price
Permissible if disclosed in the promise document
Not permissible; a commitment fee is prohibited
explanation: Per 2/4/1, it is not permissible for the Institution to receive a commitment fee from the customer.

title: Insolvency
q: Ahmad, a carpenter, is declared insolvent. He owns his carpentry tools and a large villa far exceeding his needs. How are these assets treated?
options: The tools are sold; the villa is kept as his residence
The villa is kept and the tools are leased out for creditors
Tools are kept; the villa is sold and replaced by a suitable home
Both the tools and the villa are sold for the creditors
explanation: Per 7/2, tools of trade and a suitable home are excluded from the sale; a home exceeding his requirements is sold and replaced by a suitable one.

title: Financial Rights and How They Are Exercised and Transferred
q: Which Hadith does the basis cite for the recognition of rights to tangible or intangible assets?
options: People share in three things: water, pasturage and fire
No harm and no reciprocal harm
The heirs of a deceased person inherit his estate
The neighbour of the house has a greater right to it
explanation: Per the basis, the recognition of rights, whether to tangible or intangible assets, rests on the Prophet's saying: 'No harm and no reciprocal harm'.

title: Concession Contracts
q: In a construction concession structured as Istisna'a and Parallel Istisna'a, the State is al-Mustasni' and Bank A is al-Sani'. What is the price of the product?
options: A share of the State's general tax revenue over the concession term
A lump sum paid by the State to Bank A at completion of the project
Income from fees or rent collected from the public
Bank A's construction cost plus a fixed profit margin agreed upfront
explanation: Per 8/2, in Istisna'a the State is al-Mustasni', the Institution al-Sani', and the price is income from fees or rent collected from the public for services.

title: Islamic Reinsurance
q: A traditional reinsurer announces a redistribution of its insurance surplus to its clients, including Islamic Insurance Company X. What should X do?
options: Not accept it, though it may request premium discounts
Accept it only if it is below a set limit
Accept it and give it all to charity
Accept it and credit it to participants' account, as it belongs to the insurance fund
explanation: Per 7/3, Islamic insurers should not accept redistributions of insurance surplus from traditional reinsurers, but may request premium discounts.

title: Sale of Debt
q: Why may the seller of an entity holding debts and tangible assets not keep bearing the tangible assets' risk after the sale?
options: It turns the sale into a Hawala between seller and buyer
It requires the debtors' consent
It breaches the 50% tangible asset ratio for the entity
It shows the aim is the debts, not the assets
explanation: Per the Basis for 8/2/1, the seller bearing the risk shows the buyer's intention is the debts, making inclusion of tangible assets superficial (shakli).

title: Mortgage and its Contemporary Applications
q: With Bank A's permission, a mortgagor sells the mortgaged car to Ahmad, who does not agree to keep the mortgage. What happens to the mortgage?
options: It continues, and the sale itself is void
It ceases, due to the permitted transfer of ownership
It continues and binds Ahmad as new owner
It transfers automatically to another asset of the seller
explanation: Per 3/1/6, the mortgage expires on transfer of ownership (sale, gift or will) with the mortgagee's permission, unless the new owner accepts to keep it.

title: Agency and the Act of an Uncommissioned Agent (Fodooli)
q: An investor gives Bank A funds under absolute agency, authorizing it to use any form of investment without naming one. Does this Jahalah affect the agency?
options: Yes, the agency is void for unknown subject matter and cannot be corrected later
No, and the Bank is free of any customary restriction or duty to the investor
No, it is overlooked, but the Bank must serve the investor's interest
Yes, unless the investor names a specific asset later
explanation: Per 3/3/1, Jahalah is overlooked when in absolute agency the principal allows any form of investment; the agent must observe his interest and customs.

title: Syndicated Financing
q: A syndication is in US dollars. Bank B pays its contribution in euros. How is Bank B's contribution measured?
options: Revalued in dollars at the exchange rate on the day of payment
Revalued in dollars at the rate on the day of signing the contract
Revalued at a fixed rate agreed at the outset between the participants
Kept in euros, with profits paid in euros at maturity of the syndication
explanation: Per 9/1, contributions in other currencies are revalued in the syndication currency at the prevailing exchange rate on the day of payment.

title: Monetization (Tawarruq)
q: Bank B, as Monetization beneficiary, has bought a commodity on deferred payment and now needs to sell it for cash. How should it sell the commodity?
options: Through a third-party agent appointed to sell on its behalf
Through the same Institution that sold it the commodity
Through any agent, since proxy is only barred for customers
Through its own staff, though it may use brokers
explanation: Per 5/2, Institutions shall avoid proxy in selling the Monetization commodity, even with a third party, and use their own bodies; using brokers is permissible.

title: Indices
q: Company X's work rules adjust staff wages yearly by the price index. Some wages remain unpaid and become debts. Which rule applies to those unpaid amounts?
options: Continued indexation until paid
The Shari'ah rulings on debts
The rulings on Mudarabah profit
The rulings on wage indexation only
explanation: Per 5/5, wage indexation is permissible, but when unpaid wages accumulate as debt, the Shari'ah rulings on debts should be observed.

title: Syndicated Financing
q: From which contract does the Shari'ah basis derive the permissibility of syndicated financing?
options: Kafalah
Qard
Hawalah
Musharakah
explanation: The basis states that the permissibility of syndicated financing is derived from Musharakah, which encounters no Shari'ah restriction.

title: Waqf
q: A tenant of Waqf land built a new building on it at his own cost, raising the land's normal rent. The superintendent demands a rent increase. What applies?
options: The tenant must accept the increase, as the land's rent has risen
The tenant is not bound to accept the rent increment
The lease is terminated automatically
The building passes to the Waqf free of charge
explanation: Per 6/2, if development and construction are done at the tenant's cost, he is not bound to accept the rent increment; if at the Waqf's cost, he is.

title: Guarantees
q: Per the Shari'ah basis, why may a deferred-sale seller stipulate termination if the price is unpaid?
options: The Hanafis require termination of such sales in every case
A sale on deferment is a trust contract
He agreed to defer only if it causes him no loss
Courts may not hear claims on deferred sales
explanation: Per the Basis, the seller consented to deferment only if it would not lose what is due to him (majority view); Hanafis confine him to litigation unless stipulated.

title: Waqf
q: A Waqf is created to fund a shop that sells alcohol. What must happen under the standard?
options: Its purpose must be changed to a Shari'ah compliant one
It stands unchanged, since Waqf is binding once it is created
It stands if the profits go only to the poor
It is void and the asset returns to the Waqif or his heirs
explanation: Per 2/4/1/7, Waqf for a Shari'ah non-compliant purpose is prohibited; if created, its purpose must be changed to a Shari'ah compliant one.

title: Controls on Gharar in Financial Transactions
q: Company X saw a vehicle a month ago and now buys it without viewing it again. When is this sale permissible?
options: Only if the price is paid after re-inspection
Only if the seller re-describes all its features in writing
Never, the buyer must view it at signing
If the vehicle has undergone no change since it was seen
explanation: Per 5/8/2, it is permissible to sell an asset the buyer has seen before signing, provided it has undergone no change since that time.

title: Payment Cards
q: Bank A's card advertising hides the fee amounts and urges customers to buy more than they need. Which requirements does this breach?
options: Transparency and avoiding tempting excessive consumption
Nothing, as advertising is not regulated by the standard
Only the issuer's internal pricing policy for card products
Only the card network's branding and logo use rules for issuers
explanation: Per 5/9/1, the issuer must comply with transparency and disclosure, especially on fees and profit rate, and avoid misguiding and tempting excess consumption.

title: Sale of Commodities in Organized Markets
q: Why must Bank A state its commodity agent's wages separately rather than merge them into the price, per the Basis?
options: 'Allah has permitted trading and forbidden Riba, so avoid it'
'He who hires a worker must make known to him his wages'
'Muslims shall abide by their conditions, except one that makes lawful the unlawful'
'O you who believe! Fulfil (your) obligations'
explanation: Per the Basis, the hadith 'He who hires a hired worker must make known to him his wages' applies, as a rule of Ijarah, to agency for wages.

title: Stipulations and Ethics of Fatwa in the Institutional Framework
q: A critic says a scholar who knows only financial transactions cannot issue Fatwa. On what view does the basis accept his Fatwa?
options: Financial Fatwas need no Ijtihad
Necessity permits any scholar to issue Fatwa
Ijtihad and Fatwa may be made partially
Only collective Fatwas require full competence
explanation: The basis: accepting Fatwa from a scholar knowing only one branch, like institutional financial transactions, rests on the view that Ijtihad and Fatwa may be partial.

title: Controls on Gharar in Financial Transactions
q: Ahmad makes a gift to a charity of whatever fish his boat catches tomorrow. The quantity is entirely unknown. What is the effect of this Gharar on the gift?
options: The gift is void because it relates to the primary subject matter
The gift is void because the Gharar is excessive
The gift is valid only if the catch is estimated in advance
None; Gharar does not affect donation contracts such as gift
explanation: Per 4/1, Gharar violates only exchange-based contracts (sale, lease, partnership); it does not affect donation contracts such as gift and will.

title: Credit Agreement
q: Bank A issues a letter of guarantee for a client; the client will owe the Bank only if the Bank later has to pay the beneficiary. How is this credit classified?
options: Direct cash credit, since the client's indebtedness arises at the beginning
Incidental credit, since indebtedness is only probable at the end
Financing, since one of the two transacted objects is deferred
Not credit at all, since no funds are presented to the client
explanation: Per 2/1, indebtedness probable only at the end is incidental credit, e.g. bank suretyship, letters of guarantee, bills of acceptance and documentary credits.

title: Online Financial Dealings
q: A hacker trespasses Bank A's commercial website, causing it losses. How does the standard view the website?
options: As its owner's private property, so trespass may need compensation
As public space, so no compensation is due for access
As a mere service, so only criminal penalties may apply
As property of the hosting provider, which alone can claim any compensation
explanation: Per 8/1/1, commercial websites are private properties of their owners, so trespassing them could necessitate compensation.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: An investor undertakes to subscribe all unsubscribed shares of an issue at nominal value and asks a fee for this underwriting. What is the ruling on the fee?
options: Permitted, as a commission for the guarantee he has given
Permitted if the fee is a percentage of the total issue size, not a lump sum
Not permitted for underwriting; fees for other services are allowed
Not permitted, nor are fees for feasibility studies or marketing
explanation: Per 4/1/2/4, underwriting must be without consideration; the shareholder may charge for services other than underwriting, such as feasibility studies or marketing.

title: Payment Cards
q: Why may an issuer not oblige a covered card holder to keep the cover in a current account?
options: Current accounts earn no profit for the holder, so it is unfair
It stipulates a loan within a commutative financing
Current accounts may not hold covers for financing at all
It breaches the holder's privacy over his own funds
explanation: Basis 6/2: a current account is a loan, so obliging it in a financing combines a loan with a commutative contract (loan and sale).

title: Al-Wakalah Bi Al-Istithmar (Investment Agency)
q: Which evidence does the Shari'ah basis cite for the permissibility of investment agency?
options: "Engage in trade with the wealth of orphans" lest Zakah consume it
"Muslims are bound by their conditions" stipulated in their contracts and agreements
"No harm and no reciprocal harm" in all financial dealings
The Prophet's interdiction of Mu'adh and sale of his assets
explanation: Per the basis, permissibility rests on the Hadith "Engage in trade with the wealth of orphans so that it will not be consumed by Zakah" and Verses on seeking sustenance.

title: Syndicated Financing
q: Bank A, Bank B and Bank C join in a syndicated financing through Ijarah. How should the accounts of the syndicated operation be kept?
options: Recorded only in the largest contributor's accounts, as it bears most risk
Split pro rata into each participant's own accounts according to its share
Merged into the accounts of the lead manager for the whole operation
Independent of the participating Institutions' accounts
explanation: Per clause 2, the accounts of the syndicated financing operation are kept independent from the accounts of the participating Institutions.

title: Waqf
q: On which Hadith does the Shari'ah basis rest the rule that the Waqif's permissible conditions must be observed?
options: "There is no misdemeanor on the one in charge of it"
"When a person dies his deeds stop except in three"
"Muslims are bound to the conditions they make"
"Do not sell food until you hold it"
explanation: The basis cites the Hadith "Muslims are bound to the conditions they make", except a condition permitting the prohibited or prohibiting the permitted.

title: Sale of Debt
q: At origination of a Murabaha debt, Bank A and the customer agree that the Bank will sell the debt to the customer at a future date. What is the ruling?
options: Not permitted, nor is a bilaterally binding promise
Permitted, since the debt is sold to the debtor
Permitted, if recorded in a separate deed
Permitted, if the future price is a spot price
explanation: Per 4/2, an agreement at origination to sell the debt to the debtor in the future, or a bilaterally binding promise, is not permitted.

title: Mortgage and its Contemporary Applications
q: A client fully repays his debt, but Bank A wants to keep the mortgaged land as collateral for a new, separate debt. There is no prior agreement. May it?
options: Yes, if the new debt is smaller than the old one
Yes, as the land is already in its possession
No; it was not mortgaged for the new debt
Yes, if the new debt arises within one year
explanation: Per 3/1/7, after repayment the mortgagee may not keep the asset for a new debt, unless both agreed it secures any debt between them within a specific period.

title: Indices
q: Ahmad lends Karim 10,000, agreeing that the repayment amount will rise in line with the consumer price index. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible, to protect the lender against inflation of the currency
Permissible, if the index is set by the state
Permissible, like wage indexation
Prohibited: a cash debt may not be linked to a price index
explanation: Per 6/5, it is prohibited in Shari'ah to connect the amount of a cash debt, at the time of lending, to the price index.

title: Financial Rights and How They Are Exercised and Transferred
q: A shareholder with a pre-emptive subscription right wants to assign it to a third party. Under the standard, how may it be assigned?
options: It may not be assigned at all
Without consideration, subject to law and supervisory rules
Only to another existing shareholder
Only for consideration at market value, as for any financial right
explanation: Per 13/2, it is permissible to assign the right of priority to a third party without consideration, subject to law and the rules of company supervisory bodies.

title: Waqf
q: A Waqif forbade any exchange of his Waqf. The Waqf property has since become ruined. May Istibdal take place?
options: Yes; Istibdal is allowed when the Waqf is ruined
No; the Waqif's prohibition is binding
Only if the beneficiaries unanimously agree
Only if the Waqif's heirs consent
explanation: Per 9/2, Istibdal can take place per the Waqif's condition, or when the Waqf becomes ruined, even if prevented by the Waqif.

title: Istisna’a and Parallel Istisna’a
q: A customer orders ships from a shipyard by Istisna'a through Bank A. The customer owns 40% of the shipyard. The deal was won by competitive bidding. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible, as bidding was competitive
Not permissible, as he owns a third or more
Permissible if the Bank pays the shipyard
Permissible, as he owns less than half
explanation: Per 2/2/4, Istisna'a is impermissible where one third or more of the producing facility belongs to the customer, even if won by competitive bidding.

title: Conversion of a Conventional Bank to an Islamic Bank
q: Bank A, a conventional bank, opens an Islamic window. Does the standard on conversion of a conventional bank govern the window's activities?
options: Only for the deposits of the window
Yes, once the window is licensed
No, Islamic windows are outside its scope
Yes, as a form of partial conversion
explanation: Per the Scope (1), the standard does not cover activities of Islamic windows, departments or units in conventional banks.

title: Salam and Parallel Salam
q: A Salam seller offers to deliver conforming goods one month before the due date. The buyer has no valid reason for refusing. What is the position?
options: The buyer may refuse until the due date
Early delivery voids the Salam
The buyer may accept only at a discount
The buyer will be forced to accept them
explanation: Per 5/5, early delivery of conforming goods is allowed; a buyer with a valid reason is not compelled, otherwise he is forced to accept.

title: Hawalah
q: Ahmad owes Bakr 1,000. With everyone's consent, Bakr will now collect the 1,000 from Zaid instead of Ahmad. What has changed, per the standard's definition?
options: The debtor, so it is a transfer of debt
The debt amount, so it is a set-off
The creditor, so it is a transfer of right
The debt's currency, so it is an exchange
explanation: Per 2, Hawalah of debt transfers the debt from the transferor (Muheel) to the payer (Muhal Alaihi): one debtor replaces another. A transfer of right changes the creditor.

title: Options to Reconsider (Cooling-Off Options, Either-Or Options, and Options to Revoke Due to Non-Payment)
q: A credit sale contract is silent on any option. The buyer misses the payment date, and the seller now claims an option to revoke for non-payment. Is it available?
options: Yes; it arises automatically on any non-payment
No; it is valid only if expressly stipulated
Yes, if the delay exceeds the customary period
Yes, but only by a court order
explanation: Per 3/1, options to revoke for non-payment are not valid unless they are expressly stipulated.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: A service partnership contract states that one partner receives 20,000 from the profit as a lump sum before the rest is shared. What is the ruling?
options: Permitted if he renders more services than the other partners do
Permitted if the partners agree unanimously
Permitted, since there is no monetary capital in a service partnership
Not permitted: no lump sum may be specified from the profit
explanation: Per 3/3/3, profit in a service partnership is shared by the agreed ratio, and the contract should not specify a lump sum from profit for a particular partner.

title: Mortgage and its Contemporary Applications
q: Which evidence does the basis cite for the mortgagor bearing the expenses of the mortgaged asset?
options: The report that the Prophet mortgaged his armor to a Jew for barley
The verse: if one of you deposits a thing on trust with another
The Hadith: one who mortgages gets its benefits and bears its expenses
The verse: if you are on a journey and cannot find a scribe, take a pledge
explanation: Per the basis, the Prophet said: 'The one who mortgages the asset should get its benefits and bear its expenses', since the asset belongs to the mortgagor.

title: Trading in Currencies
q: A trader buys up a currency in a small market, aiming to dominate its supply and dictate its price. All deals are spot. How is this dealing treated?
options: Permissible, if the trader is a licensed Institution
Permissible, if the purpose is hedging devaluation
Permissible, since the countervalues are possessed spot
Not permissible: it aims at establishing a monopoly position
explanation: Per 2/1/4, currency dealing shall not aim at a monopoly position nor entail evil consequences to the interests of individuals or societies.

title: Options to Reconsider (Cooling-Off Options, Either-Or Options, and Options to Revoke Due to Non-Payment)
q: Ahmad pays for a car bought under a 30-day cooling-off option, uses it for the month, then returns it and recovers his money, as planned with the seller. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible, if the seller agreed in advance
Permissible, as he exercised a valid option within its period
Impermissible; a ruse for a lender's benefit on a loan
Permissible, if the car was returned undamaged to the seller
explanation: Per 2/8/4, cooling-off options may not be used as a ruse to synthesise a lender's benefit, as when a buyer pays, uses the item and returns it within the period for a refund.

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: Six months into a lease, the lessee simply wishes to end it as he no longer needs the asset. There is no force majeure, defect or option. May he terminate alone?
options: Yes, by paying the lessor a fixed termination fee
No, the lease is binding; he needs the lessor's consent
Yes, by giving the lessor one month's notice in writing
Yes, as a lessee may always end a lease at his own will
explanation: Per 4/1/1 and 7/2/1, Ijarah is binding; neither party may terminate or alter it without the other's consent, save force majeure, material defect or an option.

title: Sale of Debt
q: A Sukuk entity's tangible assets fall to 40% after issuance, yet trading continues while it is restored. Which maxim does the standard cite for this?
options: What is overlooked in continuance is not at inception
Contracts are valid and permitted by default unless prohibited
The majority is tantamount to the whole in ruling
Muslims act upon their conditions
explanation: Per the Basis for 8/2/3, supervening matters cannot be repelled; what can be overlooked during continuance cannot be at inception.

title: Mudarabah
q: A Mudarib with permission mixes 200,000 of his own funds with 800,000 of Mudarabah funds (ratio 50:50). Profit is 100,000. What does the Mudarib get?
explanation: Per 8/9, profit is split by fund size: 20,000 to the Mudarib's own funds; the remaining 80,000 is shared 50:50, so he gets 20,000 + 40,000.

title: Combination of Contracts
q: Bank A sells a commodity to a customer for 110 on deferred payment and, by agreement in the same set, buys it back at once for 100 cash. What is the ruling?
options: Prohibited: it is Bay' al-'Inah used as a trick for Riba
Permissible, since both sales are valid alone
Permissible, if the commodity is actually delivered
Permissible, if the two sales are on separate dates
explanation: Per 4/2, combination of contracts should not be used as a trick for committing Riba, such as agreeing to practice Bay' al-'Inah or Riba al-Fadl.

title: Settlement of Debt by Set-Off
q: Company X owes Bank A USD; Bank A owes X EUR at a different maturity. They mutually agree to set off the debts. Is this allowed?
options: No, maturities must coincide in any set-off
Yes, contractual set-off needs no similarity of debts
Yes, but only if the two amounts are exactly equal in value
No, debts must be of the same kind and type
explanation: Per 2/2/3, contractual set-off is permissible without the debts being similar in kind, type, description or maturity, as each party relinquishes privileges.

title: Salam and Parallel Salam
q: A Salam for delivery in four months stipulates that Bank A will pay the capital two days after the contract. What is the status of the Salam?
options: Valid only if the seller gives a guarantee to the Bank
Void, as the capital must be paid on the spot, at the session
Valid, as a delay of two or three days is tolerated
Valid only if the delay had not been stipulated
explanation: Per 3/1/3, the capital must be paid immediately, but may be delayed two or three days at most, even if stipulated, if shorter than the delivery period.

title: Documentary Credit
q: Per the Shari'ah basis, why is it not permissible to take compensation for the guarantee aspect of a documentary credit?
options: Guarantees are void in international trade dealings under Shari'ah rules
A guarantee prepares for a loan, which is not compensated
The agency services fee already covers the guarantee given by the bank
The guarantee is a sale of a debt for another debt owed by the bank
explanation: Per the basis, a guarantee is preparatory to extending a loan, which is not compensated; the four Fiqh schools are unanimous on not taking compensation for guarantee.

title: Procrastinating Debtor
q: Bank A sold a machine by Murabahah. The buyer defaulted and later became bankrupt; the machine is still available in the same condition. What may Bank A do?
options: Only claim as one of the creditors in bankruptcy
Sell the machine and keep any surplus above the price as profit
Claim compensation for the delay in payment
Repossess the machine instead of seeking a bankruptcy order
explanation: Per 2/1/7, if the sold asset is available in its sold condition and the buyer defaulted then became bankrupt, the Institution may repossess it.

title: Impact of Contingent Incidents on Commitments
q: A commitment becomes null and void when its fulfillment has become useless. On what principle is this ruling based?
options: A commitment lapses whenever its performance becomes costly
The prohibition of Bay' al-Sinin for agricultural produce
Fulfilling a useless commitment is futility, alien to Shari'ah
Every contract is voidable whenever one party loses interest in it
explanation: Per the Shari'ah basis, implementing a useless commitment is an act of futility, and there is no room for futility in Shari'ah legislation, as Al-Shatibi indicated.

title: Competitions and Prizes
q: A shop offers an unspecified gift with each appliance it sells. Under what condition is this promotional gift permissible?
options: The price is not increased against the gift
The gift's value is disclosed before the sale
The gift is given in kind and never in cash
The buyer pays a separate fee for the gift
explanation: Per 3/6/1/2, a seller may offer an unspecified gift with a good or service provided the price is not increased against the gift.

title: Controls on Gharar in Financial Transactions
q: Bank A relies on a private, not public, need to justify a contract involving Gharar. Per the Shari'ah basis, does a private need count?
options: No; only a public need, not a private one, can justify Gharar
No; only actual necessity, not need, counts
Yes, but only in donation contracts
Yes; need, public or private, is treated as necessity
explanation: The basis cites the Fiqh principle: "Need, whether public or private, enjoys the same status of necessity" (Majallah item 33).

title: Investment Sukuk
q: Investors have subscribed to a Murabahah Sukuk issue, but subscription has not closed and no allotment has been made. When does the issue contract take all the legal effects of its underlying contract?
options: After subscription closes and the certificates are allotted
Only when the Murabahah commodity is delivered to the buyer
As soon as each subscriber pays the subscription amount
When the prospectus is approved by the regulator
explanation: Per 5/1/3, the issue contract has all the legal effects of its underlying contract after closing of subscription and allotment of the certificates.

title: Liability of the Investment Manager
q: Why does the standard prohibit stipulating liability on an investment manager such as a Mudarib?
options: It would void any third-party commitment
It would contradict the rule on doers of good
It would turn the contract into a benefit-bearing loan
It would create Gharar in the profit-sharing ratio
explanation: Per the Basis, stipulating liability on fiduciaries is a means to render an investment contract a benefit-bearing loan.

title: Possession (Qabd)
q: Bank A buys an office building. The seller vacates it and leaves it to Bank A, enabling it to deal in the building freely. Has Bank A taken actual possession?
options: No, until the full price is paid to the seller
Yes, through relinquishment and enabling transactions in it
No, not until Bank A physically occupies and uses the building
No, until Bank A leases the building to a tenant
explanation: Per 3/2, actual possession of immovable property is realised through relinquishment and enabling transactions in it.

title: Debit Card, Charge Card and Credit Card
q: Bank A's charge card terms impose a percentage interest charge if the holder pays after the free credit period. May the Bank issue this card?
options: Yes, if the rate is below that charged on conventional cards
Yes, as interest applies only after the free period
Yes, since charge cards give no revolving credit
No, he must not be obliged to pay interest for delay
explanation: Per 3/2/1, charge cards are permissible only if the cardholder is not obliged to pay interest in case of delay in paying the amount due.

title: Agency and the Act of an Uncommissioned Agent (Fodooli)
q: Broker B is appointed as agent of a seller and, in the same deal, as agent of the buyer, to conclude the sale between them. What is the ruling?
options: Permitted, as long as he discloses both roles to the two principals
Permitted, if the price agreed between them is the market price
Not permitted: an agent may not act for both parties
Permitted, if both principals agree to pay his fee in equal parts
explanation: Per 6/1/3, the agent should not act for both parties to the contract.

title: Waqf
q: Ahmad makes a Waqf whose income goes to his children and grandchildren. Eventually none of them remains in existence. Where does the income go?
options: To a charitable purpose
To the State treasury as ownerless property
To the Waqf superintendent
Back to Ahmad's estate for his heirs
explanation: Per 2/3/2 and 3/3/4, in a family Waqf the income goes to a charitable purpose when none of the specified persons is existent.

title: Credit Agreement
q: Why is charging the client for a credit study also justified, per the Shari'ah basis, even though the financier uses it to assess risk?
options: The client is a borrower and must pay all of the lender's own costs
The study benefits both the financier and the financed party
The benefit of the study is confined to the financier only
The study fee is deducted later from the profit of the deal
explanation: Per the basis, the benefit from the study is shared between the financier and the financed party rather than confined to the former only.

title: Stipulations and Ethics of Fatwa in the Institutional Framework
q: Bank A's board feels that the Bank may use a requested Fatwa to commit an impermissible action. What may the board do?
options: Refer the Bank to another board instead
Issue it anyway, as it must answer every request
Refrain from issuing it or issue it with restrictions
Issue it but keep it secret from the Bank
explanation: Per 7/6, the board issues Fatwa when approached, unless it feels it may be used for an impermissible act; then it may refrain or add restrictions.

title: Mortgage and its Contemporary Applications
q: A client repaid 80% of a debt secured by a mortgaged building and asks Bank A to release 80% of the building. The Bank refuses. Is it entitled to refuse?
options: Yes; it may keep the whole asset for any part of the debt
No; it must release the asset in proportion to repayment
Yes, but only if the debt is now overdue
No; it must release the whole asset once most is repaid
explanation: Per 3/1/7, the mortgagee may keep the whole mortgaged asset for any part of the debt, unless he accepts partial release.

title: Zakah
q: Company X holds conventional bonds bought at 1 million that pay interest. How is Zakah applied?
options: No Zakah, as bonds are prohibited
Zakah on the 1 million cost; all interest donated to charity
Zakah on the interest only
Zakah on the bonds' cost plus the interest, which the company may keep as income
explanation: Per 5/1/4/1, Zakah is paid on the principal of the bond (its cost), while the entire interest is donated for charitable purposes.

title: Hawalah
q: Ahmad transfers his debt to Zaid on terms that the transfer takes effect only if Ahmad's shipment arrives next month. Is this Hawalah valid?
options: Yes, once the shipment has arrived
Yes, provided the arrival date is fixed in the contract
Yes, a Hawalah may be made contingent on a future event
No, a Hawalah must take effect immediately
explanation: Per 4/3, a transfer of debt must take effect immediately; it may not be suspended, temporary or contingent on future events.

title: Gold and Its Trading Parameters in Shari’ah
q: Why does the standard accept holding a gold certificate as constructive possession when ingots are sold for currency?
options: Stored ingots are no longer Ribawi items once held by the bank
It equals physical possession in effect, incl. risk transfer
Spot exchange is not required for ingots held in storage
The seller stays liable for the stored gold
explanation: Per the Basis, a certificate is as good as physical possession in legal effect, transfer of risk and benefits, and ability to dispose.

title: Waqf
q: Ahmad rents a building for five years and declares its usufruct a Waqf, subleasing it for beneficiaries. The owner permits subleasing. How long is this Waqf?
options: Temporary, for the period of the original rent
Permanent, as Waqf is in principle eternal
Until the owner decides to sell the building
For Ahmad's lifetime
explanation: Per 3/4/6, Waqf of a usufruct acquired by rent is temporary according to the original rent period, and needs the owner not to bar subleasing.

title: Waqf
q: Ahmad leases a building for five years. The lessor has prohibited subleasing. Ahmad then creates a Waqf of the building's usufructs. What is the ruling?
options: Valid, as Ahmad owns the usufructs of the building during the lease
Valid if the beneficiaries pay the rent to the lessor
Not valid, as the lessor prevents him from subleasing
Valid if the Waqf is shorter than five years
explanation: Per 2/4/12, a lessee may make Waqf of usufructs only if the lessor does not prevent subleasing and the Waqf term is not longer than the lease.

title: Mortgage and its Contemporary Applications
q: Bank A, as Rab al-Mal in a Mudarabah, requires a mortgage from the Mudarib. In which case is this permissible?
options: If it secures a minimum profit for the Bank
If it secures return of the capital to the Bank in all cases and events
If the Mudarabah term exceeds one year
If confined to indemnity for transgression, negligence or breach
explanation: Per 3/3/2, mortgage may not be stipulated in trust-based contracts (e.g. Mudarabah), unless confined to indemnity for transgression, negligence or breach.

title: Possession (Qabd)
q: An airline hypothecates an airplane to Bank A by valid registration under the law, and keeps operating the airplane. How is Bank A's position regarded?
options: Bank A has no possession, as airplanes cannot be held
Bank A has constructive possession through the registration
Bank A has possession only if the airplane is grounded
Bank A has actual possession by physical delivery
explanation: Per 3/4, hypothecation of mobile movables like cars, trains, steamers and airplanes through valid registration is constructive possession.

title: Conversion of a Conventional Bank to an Islamic Bank
q: A buyer converting Bank C must take over all assets, including interest-based liabilities. What must the buyer do with these liabilities?
options: Dispose of them quickly, even via early repayment at a discount
Refinance them with new interest loans
Transfer them to the bank's depositors in proportion to balances
Keep paying them until their maturity
explanation: Per 9/2, if all assets must be acquired, the buyer must quickly dispose of non-permissible liabilities, even proposing early repayment for a discount.

title: Insolvency
q: After Ahmad's insolvency is revoked, it emerges that before the declaration he had received a gift that was not sequestered. What happens to it?
options: It is shared among all present and future creditors
Ahmad keeps it, since the insolvency has been revoked and his property is free again
It goes to the creditors whose debts arose after revocation
It is sequestered for creditors whose debts predated the declaration
explanation: Per 10/2, such an asset acquired before the declaration without reciprocal consideration is sequestered and distributed among the creditors whose debts predated it.

title: Syndicated Financing
q: A syndication contract states that any exiting participant will be bought out at the nominal value of its contribution. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible, as it protects the exiting party from any loss in value
Permissible, if the syndicate is profitable at the time of exit
Not permissible to agree beforehand on exit at nominal value
Permissible, if all participants accept it at the time of the contract
explanation: Per 10/2, it is not permissible to agree beforehand on transfer of shares at nominal value or on a guarantee of a certain limit of profits.

title: Revocation of Contracts by Exercise of a Cooling-Off Option
q: Under a lease, the lessor adds a supplementary rental for maintenance, insurance and owners' taxes; the lessee refuses. The lessee had promised to purchase the asset. What may the lessor do?
options: Revoke and enforce the promise, adding the supplementary rent to the price
Revoke, and enforce the promise without adding that rent
Enforce the promise only after the lease term ends
Only continue the lease at the original rental
explanation: Per 11/2, the lessor may revoke and demand performance of the promise, provided the supplementary rent for that period is not added to the purchase price.

title: Murabahah
q: A Murabahah customer asks Bank A for six more months to pay an instalment. The Bank agrees but requires an extra payment for the additional time. What is the ruling?
options: Permitted if agreed by mutual consent
Permitted if the extension exceeds 3 months
Not permitted to demand extra payment for time
Permitted if the customer is solvent
explanation: Per 4/8, once the price becomes a debt, no extra payment may be demanded for extra time or for delay in payment, with or without reason.

title: Trading in Currencies
q: Bank A credits purchased USD to a customer's account instead of handing over cash. Why does the Shari'ah basis treat this like actual possession?
options: The parties may waive the possession requirement by mutual agreement
The Bank guarantees the customer against any loss
Currencies are not subject to the rules of exchange
Shari'ah prescribed no particular method of taking possession
explanation: Per the Basis, constructive possession equals actual possession because Shari'ah prescribed no method; custom giving power to dispose and risk transfer governs.

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: Bank A leases a car by specification, not yet owned. Per the Shari'ah basis, which contract is this similar to, and what should the lessor avoid?
options: It is similar to Salam; avoid requesting advance rentals
It is similar to 'Inah; avoid the transaction
It is similar to Murabahah; avoid any mark-up
It is similar to Istisna'a; avoid fixed rentals in advance
explanation: The basis: leasing on specifications does not lead to dispute and is similar to Salam, but the lessor should not request advance rentals per a Shafi'i and Hanbali view.

title: Hiring of Persons
q: An investment agent permitted to utilize a client's money incurs a loss without transgression or negligence. Unlike a shared employee, is he liable?
options: Yes, if the client did not approve the investment in advance
No; he guarantees only for transgression or negligence
Yes, for any loss above 10% of capital
Yes; like a shared employee he is fully liable
explanation: Per 4/6, unlike the shared employee, the investment agent does not guarantee except in case of transgression or negligence.

title: Loan (Qard)
q: Besides the hadith, what reason does the Shari'ah basis give for prohibiting a sale stipulated within a Qard?
options: It is a means to an excess in the Qard, so it is blocked
Sales always require a separate session from loans
The sale price can never be agreed in a Qard
A sale cannot be made between lenders and borrowers
explanation: Per the Basis, stipulating a sale in a Qard may oblige the borrower on the price for the sake of the Qard, creating a stipulated excess (Riba); such means are blocked.

title: Financial Paper (Shares and Bonds)
q: Company X's interest-based loans are 20% of its market capitalization, within the limit. Its CFO argues this makes the borrowing itself lawful. Is he right?
options: No; only loans above 20% of capitalization are prohibited
Yes; loans within the 30% limit are lawful for the company itself
No; interest-based loans are prohibited whatever the amount
Yes, as long as the loans are short-term facilities
explanation: Per 3/4/2, the 30% limit only governs the exemption for investing; raising loans on interest is prohibited whatever the amount.

title: Murabahah
q: After a customer's breach of promise, Bank A claims its lost mark-up. Why does the Shari'ah basis call this claim irrational?
options: The mark-up belongs to the supplier
Mark-up may only be taken as 'Arboun
Mark-up is always refunded to the customer
No mark-up exists without an actual Murabahah
explanation: The basis: a claim for lost mark-up is irrational since there is no mark-up unless there is actually a Murabahah, and here there is none.

title: Payment Cards
q: At check-in, a hotel blocks an amount on Ahmad's card to secure what he may owe at check-out. How is the issuer-cardholder relationship characterized here?
options: Guarantee
Agency for recovery
Novation
Provision of services
explanation: Per 2/2/1/2, the relationship is of guarantee if the card is used to block or deduct an amount to secure what will be outstanding on the cardholder.

title: Distribution of Profit in Mudarabah-Based Investment Accounts
q: Bank A cannot transfer funds to an account holder because he changed his address. After the specified period the funds go to charity, and later he reappears. What happens?
options: He receives them only if he proves need
He loses them, as they were already given to charity
The funds are paid to him from the charity account
The Bank keeps them as income for the period
explanation: Per 2/2/7, such funds are kept in a suspended account then added to the charity account; if the owners' addresses become known, they are paid from the charity account.

title: Controls on Gharar in Financial Transactions
q: Bank A sells a house to a customer who has inspected the house but has not seen its foundation. What is the effect of this Gharar?
options: The sale is voidable at the buyer's option at any time
The sale is void as the Gharar is excessive
The sale is valid only if the foundation is described in writing
No effect; it is minor Gharar that a contract can hardly avoid
explanation: Per 4/2/2, selling a house to a buyer who has not seen its foundation is minor Gharar, which does not affect the contract.

title: Waqf
q: Ahmad creates a Waqf over the yet-to-be-declared dividends on shares he holds in Company X. Is this a valid Waqf asset?
options: Only once the dividends are declared and paid
Yes, as it is appurtenant to an asset he owns
No, due to gharar in the dividend amount
No, since the dividends are not yet owned
explanation: Per 2/4/5/1(b), the Waqf asset may be appurtenant to an asset owned by the Waqif, e.g., yet-to-be-declared dividends on his shares.

title: Murabahah
q: Bank A and a customer amend the mark-up and duration of a promise before the Murabahah is concluded. Why is this not prohibited debt rescheduling, per the Shari'ah basis?
options: A promise is not a contract, so no debt exists yet
Because the customer had already paid Hamish Jiddiyyah
Because the Bank already owned the item being sold
Because the mark-up was only reduced and never raised
explanation: The basis: amending the promise is allowed because a promise is not a contract, so changing profit or duration is not rescheduling of debt.

title: Hiring of Persons
q: A hiring contract gives Company X a conditional option (Khiyar al-Shart) to cancel within 15 days. On day 10, X cancels. What is the ruling?
options: Valid only if X proves a defect
Invalid; hiring cannot be terminated unilaterally
Valid only if the employee also agrees
Valid termination, as it is within the option period
explanation: Per 8/2/2, the contract can be terminated on the basis of Khiyar al-Shart by the party that stipulated it, within its specified period.

title: Distribution of Profit in Mudarabah-Based Investment Accounts
q: Bank A proposes that holders take all profit from Q1 operations while the Bank takes all profit from Q2 operations. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible, if agreed in the account opening form
Impermissible to allocate a period's profit to one party
Permissible, if the two periods are of equal length and the holders agree to it in advance
Permissible, as each party still shares overall
explanation: Per 4/5, allocating the profit of a certain period or transaction to one party and of another period or transaction to the other is impermissible.

title: Sale of Debt
q: Bank A and Bank B agree to swap their portfolios of receivables owed by their respective customers. What is the ruling?
options: Permitted, if the customers consent
Permitted, if the portfolios are equal in value
Not permitted, as a sale of debt for debt
Permitted, as a division of debt
explanation: Per 9/7, selling a debt to a third party for another debt owed to it by another party, e.g., swapping receivable portfolios, is not permitted.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: Per the Shari'ah basis, why may profit be disproportionate to capital contributions?
options: Capital ratios are unknown until liquidation, so profit cannot follow them
Losses are also disproportionate to the capital contributions
Profit belongs only to the managing partner, who alone works for the Sharikah
Profit is deserved through funds, work or risk borne
explanation: Per the basis (Hanafi and Hanbali view), one deserves profit by funds contributed, work done or risk borne, so the ratio may be agreed accordingly.

title: Murabahah
q: Bank A appoints the customer as its agent to arrange insurance cover for goods while the Bank is acquiring ownership. Who must bear the insurance cost?
options: The supplier of the goods
The customer, as agent
Bank A
Bank A and the customer equally
explanation: Per 3/2/7, agency in obtaining insurance at the acquisition stage is permitted, but the Institution must bear the cost of insurance.

title: Zakah
q: A farm owned by Company Y is fully irrigated by pumps at the company's cost. What Zakah rate applies to its produce?
options: 7.5% (three quarters of the tenth)
5% (half of the tenth)
2.5% as for trade goods
10% (one tenth)
explanation: Per 3/3 and 5/4/1, the rate is 10% for non-irrigated lands, 5% for irrigated lands and 7.5% for partially irrigated lands.

title: Options to Revoke Contracts Due to Incomplete Performance
q: A buyer keeps a defective item and seeks Arsh. Per the Hanafi and Shafi'i view adopted in the Shari'ah basis, why is no Arsh due when he keeps it?
options: Descriptions are not treated as part of the price here
Arsh is due only in Ijarah contracts
The seller's good faith cancels any Arsh
The buyer waived all rights by taking delivery of the item and keeping it
explanation: Per the basis, no Arsh is due if the buyer keeps the item, as descriptions are not considered part of the price, and the seller did not consent to a lower price.

title: Financial Paper (Shares and Bonds)
q: Why does the standard exempt trading in shares of permissible-activity companies that sometimes borrow or deposit on interest?
options: Shareholders are not owners of the company's assets
Removal of hardship, general need and predominance
Interest dealings by such companies are lawful
The prohibition of Riba does not apply to companies
explanation: Per the Basis, the exemption rests on removal of hardship, general need, widespread practice, the principles of surplus, shortage and predominance.

title: Protection of Capital and Investments
q: Under the Murabahah and 'Arboun protection method, the fund manager wishes to sell some of the fund's 'Arboun contracts to other investors before settlement. Is this allowed?
options: No; trading in 'Arboun contracts is impermissible
Yes, provided the original sellers consent
Yes, at their market value on the date of sale
Yes, once half of the 'Arboun period has passed
explanation: Per 4/2/7(d), the rules of 'Arboun must be observed, including reserving the assets until settlement and the impermissibility of trading in 'Arboun contracts.

title: Documentary Credit
q: A client asks Bank A to amend a credit by extending its duration (rescheduling). What may Bank A charge for this amendment?
options: Nothing at all, since amendments must always be free
A lump-sum service fee plus a charge for the extra time
A percentage of the credit amount for the extra period
Only actual expenses, as a definite sum, not a percentage
explanation: Per 3/3/1, where an amendment involves rescheduling the duration, the Institution may charge only actual expenses as a definite sum and not a percentage.

title: Credit Agreement
q: Bank A arranges a syndicated Murabahah financing with several banks and charges an arrangement fee. Who should bear it?
options: The arranging bank itself, from its own profit
The client being financed, in all cases
The participants of the syndication
No one; arrangement fees are impermissible
explanation: Per 5/3/1/4/2, in syndicated financing the arranging Institution may charge arrangement fees to be borne by the participants of the syndication.

title: Documentary Credit
q: A client deposits the cash cover for a credit with Bank A and asks that it earn a return until it is used. What does the standard permit?
options: Investing the cash cover on a Mudarabah basis
Lending the cover to others at interest
Paying a fixed interest on the cash cover
Nothing; cash cover must remain idle
explanation: Per 3/4/3, the Institution and the applicant may agree on investing the cash cover of the credit in accordance with Mudarabah partnership.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: Under the standard, Sharikat al-'Aqd (contractual partnership) is defined as an agreement between two or more parties to combine what, for the purpose of making profits?
options: Their assets only, in monetary form
Their debts owed by third parties only
Their labour only, under a fixed wage
Their assets, labour or liabilities
explanation: Per 2/1, Sharikat al-'Aqd is an agreement between two or more parties to combine their assets, labour or liabilities for the purpose of making profits.

title: Islamic Insurance
q: Islamic Insurance Company T must build a statutory reserve. From where should this reserve be deducted?
options: From the policyholders' investment profits
From its share capital, as part of shareholders equity
From the policyholders fund, as a charge on contributions
From the insurance surplus before any distribution
explanation: Per 10/4, the statutory reserve is deducted from share capital and forms part of shareholders equity; nothing is deducted from the policyholders fund for shareholders.

title: Mudarabah
q: A trainee asks how the Sunnah supports a capital provider restricting a Mudarib. Which report does the Shari'ah basis cite?
options: Ibn Umar's sale of camels at Al-Baqi' for dinars at the day's rate
Ali Ibn Abu Talib's saying on sharing profit and loss
Al-'Abbas's conditions to his Mudarib, approved by the Prophet
Umar Ibn Al-Khattab's restriction of an orphan's Mudarabah trade to Iraq
explanation: Per the basis, Al-'Abbas stipulated that his Mudarib not travel by sea, pass valleys or trade in livestock, and the Prophet approved these conditions.

title: Combination of Contracts
q: In a combined set, a subsidiary contract is executed without separate offer and acceptance, to serve a lawful need of the parties. What is the ruling?
options: Void unless both parties later sign a new contract
Void, as offer and acceptance are always required for any contract
Valid only if confirmed later by a written offer
Acceptable, given the lawful need in a subsidiary contract
explanation: Per 5/2/5, subsidiary and implicit contracts may be relieved of some validity prerequisites (such as offer and acceptance) when dictated by need or lawful interest.

title: Islamic Insurance
q: A company seeks Islamic cover against liability claims and breach of trust by staff. Which type of Islamic Insurance is this?
options: Social insurance arranged by the state
Property Insurance, indemnifying actual injury
Life insurance with an investment element
Person Insurance (Takaful)
explanation: Per 6/1, Property Insurance indemnifies actual injury and covers fire, car and airplane accidents, liability, breach of trust, etc.

title: Waqf
q: Bilal is the beneficiary of a Waqf house. The Waqif set no condition on how Bilal benefits. Bilal leases the house to a third party. Is this allowed?
options: Yes, he may benefit through a third party, even by leasing
Only with the prior approval of the relevant authority each time
Only if the lessee is also poor
No, he must live in the house personally
explanation: Per 2/6/5, the beneficiary may benefit personally or through a third party, even by leasing, unless the Waqif stipulated personal benefit only.

title: Waqf
q: Ahmad makes a Waqf for his adult cousin Ali, who is legally competent. Ali rejects it. What happens?
options: The property returns to Ahmad's ownership as a failed Waqf
The Waqf becomes void, as the beneficiary did not accept it
The Waqf stays valid and Ali's share goes to charitable purposes
The Waqf is suspended until Ali changes his mind and accepts
explanation: Per 3/1/1, Waqf needs only offer; if a competent beneficiary rejects it, the Waqf remains valid and his share goes to charitable purposes.

title: Loan (Qard)
q: Ahmad lends money to a trader in City A and stipulates that it be repaid in City B, where Ahmad will be travelling. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible to stipulate repayment at another place
Prohibited unless the trader also lives in City B
Prohibited, as Ahmad gains a benefit that is Riba
Permissible only if no benefit accrues to Ahmad
explanation: Per 4/2, it is permissible to stipulate repayment of Qard at a place other than that where the loan was made.

title: Online Financial Dealings
q: Which aim of Shari'ah does the basis cite to support accepting electronic signatures to verify dealers' identities?
options: Preservation of lineage, one of the five main Maqasid
Removal of Gharar in the subject matter of sale
Preservation of wealth, one of the five main Maqasid
Facilitation of trade through speed of contracting
explanation: Per the basis, Shari'ah encourages technological means to preserve people's wealth, as preservation of wealth is one of the main five aims (Maqasid).

title: Sale of Debt
q: Why does the standard not require the debtor's consent for selling his debt to a third party?
options: Because the debtor is deemed to be the possessor of the debt
By analogy to Hawala; the creditor may claim via another
Because "Muslims act upon their conditions" in all contracts
Because the sale is a separation of rights, not a sale of debt
explanation: Per the Basis for 5/6, analogy to Hawala applies, and the creditor may demand his right himself or through a party acting for him.

title: Controls on Gharar in Financial Transactions
q: Ahmad buys an unseen machine on the basis of the seller's full description. On delivery, the machine differs from the description. What is Ahmad's position?
options: He must accept it and claim a price reduction
He must accept it, as description sales are binding
The sale is automatically void from the start
He is free to conclude the deal or not
explanation: Per 5/8/1, a commodity may be sold on description; the buyer concludes if it is as described, otherwise he is free to conclude the deal or not.

title: Combination of Contracts
q: An investor provides Mudarabah capital to a Mudarib and, in the same set, lends him that same capital. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible, if profit is shared as agreed
Permissible, as the loan protects the investor's capital from loss
Not permissible, as Mudarabah and lending contradict
Permissible, if the loan is interest-free
explanation: Per 4/4, combining Mudarabah with lending the Mudarabah capital to the Mudarib is an example of contradictory contracts that may not be combined.

title: Procrastinating Debtor
q: Ahmad's instalment was due on 1 May. Bank A made a normal demand; he has not proved insolvency and has not paid. Is default in payment established?
options: No, three instalments must be missed
No, a court ruling is needed first
No, unless a penalty clause was agreed
Yes, default is established
explanation: Per 2/6, default is established when, after a normal demand, a debtor who has not proved insolvency fails to settle the debt on its due date.

title: Options to Terminate Due to Breach of Trust (Trust-Based Options)
q: After discovering verbal deception, Ahmad sells the item to a third party. Per the Shari'ah basis, why does his option to revoke lapse?
options: Options lapse whenever the item changes hands
His disposal equals explicit consent to waive the option
The third party acquires the option instead of him, as it passes with the item
The seller can no longer refund the price
explanation: Per the basis, the option lapses on disposal of the item after discovering the deception, because disposal is equivalent to explicit consent to waive the option.

title: Irrigation Partnership (Musaqat)
q: Under a Musaqat, at what point does the worker become entitled to his share of the crop?
options: As soon as the crop materializes, on an indivisible basis
Only after the crop is harvested and sold, when the profit can be known
Upon signing, as an advance on the crop
Only at the end of the agreed contract term
explanation: Per 9/2, the worker is entitled to his share of the crop on an indivisible basis as soon as it materializes.

title: Waqf
q: Ahmad, whose legal competence is restricted because of indebtedness, declares his shop a Waqf. His creditors refuse to confirm it. What is the status?
options: The Waqf is valid but suspended until he pays
The Waqf stays valid; debts are paid from its income
The Waqf becomes invalid
The Waqf is valid for half the shop
explanation: Per 3/2/3, the Waqf of a person restricted for indebtedness depends on his creditors' confirmation; if they refuse, the Waqf becomes invalid.

title: Possession (Qabd)
q: Which text does the Basis cite for requiring ascertainment of movables by customary units of measure before possession is realised?
options: 'He who buys food (wheat) is not to sell it until he has measured it'
'Gold for gold, silver for silver, wheat for wheat... like for like, hand to hand'
'A thing acted upon by the people must be accommodated'
'No ground can there be against those who do good; and Allah is Oft-Forgiving'
explanation: Per the Basis, the hadith 'He who buys food is not to sell it until he has measured it' shows possession in such cases is attained only through measure.

title: Guarantees
