q: In a deferred sale, Bank A stipulates that if the buyer fails to pay within a set period, it may revoke the sale and repossess the asset without court. Ruling?
options: Not permissible, as a concluded sale is final
Permissible, as the seller may stipulate this
Permissible only if the buyer is bankrupt
Not permissible, as revocation needs a court
explanation: Per 5/2, in a deferred sale the seller may stipulate a right to revoke and repossess the asset without recourse to the courts if the price is not paid in time.

title: Liability of the Investment Manager
q: Six months into an investment agency, before any loss has occurred, the agent signs a side letter undertaking to bear any future loss. Is this allowed?
options: Yes, because no loss has occurred so far
Yes, if the undertaking is implicit, not explicit
Yes, since it is outside the original contract
No, he may not assume the risk after the contract
explanation: Per 3/3, the investment manager may not undertake, explicitly or implicitly, assumption of the risk after making the investment contract.

title: Agency and the Act of an Uncommissioned Agent (Fodooli)
q: Ahmad tells his agent to buy a car for up to 100. Its market price is 110. The agent pays 120. How much must the agent compensate Ahmad?
options: 20, the difference between 120 and Ahmad's limit
10, the difference between 110 and Ahmad's limit
10, the difference between 120 and the market price
Nothing, as the agent is a trustee
explanation: Per 6/3/2, if the agent buys above both market and set price, he compensates the difference between the purchase price and the market price.

title: Irrigation Partnership (Musaqat)
q: An orchard owner refuses to allow the Musaqat worker to do his work. What right does the worker have regarding the contract?
options: He has no right of revocation
He must apply to the owner's heirs
He must wait until the term expires
He is entitled to revoke the contract
explanation: Per 13/3, the worker is entitled to revoke the contract if the owner refuses to allow him to work (see 8/5).

title: Distribution of Profit in Mudarabah-Based Investment Accounts
q: Bank A agrees with holders that profit is shared 30:70, but any profit above a 6% index goes to the Bank. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible; profit at or below the index is shared as agreed
Impermissible, as it is a lump sum for the Bank
Impermissible, as profit must always be shared in ratios
Permissible only if the excess goes to the holders
explanation: Per 4/4, a lump sum for one party voids Mudarabah, but agreeing that profit above a limit or index goes to one party is allowed; up to it, profit is shared as agreed.

title: Sale of Debt
q: Company Y buys a debt from Bank A and stipulates that Bank A guarantees it, with recourse for any unrecovered portion. Is this allowed?
options: Only if the debtor was insolvent at sale
Yes, the buyer may stipulate such recourse
No, a seller may not guarantee a sold debt
Only for debts sold to the debtor himself
explanation: Per 7/4, the buyer may stipulate that the seller guarantee the debt, with recourse to the seller for the unrecovered portion.

title: Competitions and Prizes
q: How does Al-Mawardi derive the permissibility of racing from the account of Yusuf's brothers, as cited in the standard?
options: Jacob did not object, and it was not abrogated
The brothers won a prize, showing rewards are allowed
Jacob ordered his sons to race as training
The race was for a known distance without Jahalah
explanation: Al-Mawardi said Jacob did not object to their saying, evidence of permissibility in his code which was not superseded by abrogation.

title: Financial Paper (Shares and Bonds)
q: Company X is being formed with the objective of manufacturing liquor and wants to issue shares to the public. What is the ruling on issuing these shares?
options: Permissible, if half of its income is from lawful sales
Permissible, if the shares are sold only to non-Muslim investors
Not permissible, as the corporation's objective is prohibited
Permissible, as shares are mere evidence of ownership
explanation: Per 2/1, issuance of shares is permissible only if the corporation's objectives are permissible; they should not be prohibited, like manufacturing liquor.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: On the date of distribution, a partner in a Sharikah decides to give part of the profit due to him to another party. What is the ruling?
options: Not permissible, since ratios are fixed at conclusion
Not permissible, as it changes the loss-sharing ratio
Permissible only if agreed in the original contract
Permissible to relinquish part of his profit on that date
explanation: Per 3/1/5/2, a partner may relinquish, on the date of distribution, a part of the profit due to him in favour of another party.

title: Mudarabah
q: Bank A gave funds to a Mudarib under a Mudarabah with no fixed term. Before the Mudarib has started any business, Bank A wants to terminate. May it?
options: No, termination always requires the Mudarib's consent, even before any business starts
Yes, the contract is not binding and may be ended unilaterally
No, a Mudarabah becomes binding on both parties as soon as it is signed by them
Yes, but Bank A must first pay the Mudarib a fixed fee
explanation: Per 4/3, a Mudarabah is in principle not binding and either party may terminate it unilaterally, except after commencement or where a duration was agreed.

title: Waqf
q: Ahmad holds interest-bearing bonds and makes them a Waqf for general charitable causes. When is this Waqf valid?
options: Never, under any circumstances
Always, provided the interest received is paid to the poor
Always, because the yield goes to charity
If the bonds are substituted with assets of permissible yield
explanation: Per 2/4/10, Waqf over assets of prohibited yield (e.g., bonds) is valid if those assets are substituted with assets of permissible yield.

title: Conversion of a Conventional Bank to an Islamic Bank
q: Per the Shari'ah basis, why may premises once used for impermissible services be converted for permissible use rather than sold or destroyed?
options: Premises are owned by the shareholders, not the bank
The prohibition concerns the use, not the location
Real estate is exempt from all Shari'ah rules on use
Destroying property is never permitted under Shari'ah
explanation: Per the Basis, locations used for impermissible services may be transformed because the prohibition relates to the use of the location, not the location itself.

title: Mudarabah
q: A Mudarabah contract stipulates that the Mudarib will receive 50,000 from the profit, the rest going to the capital provider. What is the ruling?
options: The Mudarabah contract is void
Valid if profit exceeds 50,000
Valid, as the Mudarib's share is known
Valid, but the 50,000 is treated as a fee
explanation: Per 8/5, if one of the parties stipulates that he should receive a lump sum of money, the Mudarabah contract is void.

title: Distribution of Profit in Mudarabah-Based Investment Accounts
q: Bank A paid monthly amounts to holders before liquidation. After constructive liquidation, a holder's actual share is lower. What must the Bank do?
options: Cover the difference from its own Mudarib share
Carry the difference into the next period's profit of the investment pool
Deduct the difference so each receives his exact profit share
Nothing; advance payments are final
explanation: Per 5/3, advance payments are permitted; after liquidation the Institution makes necessary additions or deductions so each holder receives his exact share.

title: Gold and Its Trading Parameters in Shari’ah
q: Bank A wants to import gold by way of documentary credit, with the price payable 90 days after shipment. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible, if Bank A holds the title documents until payment
Permissible, if the gold is shipped on spot
Permissible, as the documentary credit acts as a guarantee of payment
Not permissible; the price must be paid without deferment
explanation: Per 5/1/2, gold may not be bought by documentary credit unless item (3) is met, including payment of the price without deferment.

title: Islamic Reinsurance
q: A traditional insurer asks Islamic Reinsurer R, using an Islamic reinsurance contract, to reinsure the risks of a liquor factory. May R accept?
options: Yes, since the client is a traditional insurer
Yes, since the Islamic reinsurance contract is used
No; the reinsurance must not involve a prohibited object
Yes, if the premiums are given to charity
explanation: Per 8/3, reinsurance for traditional insurers is permitted only if it does not involve a Shari'ah-prohibited object, among other conditions.

title: Procrastinating Debtor
q: A solvent customer deliberately delays paying a debt due to Bank A, though he is able to pay. How does the standard classify his conduct?
options: It is Haram (prohibited)
Permissible if he later pays in full
Permissible within a 30-day grace period
Prohibited only if the contract says so
explanation: Per 2/1/1, default in payment by a debtor who is capable of paying the debt is Haram (prohibited).

title: Buyback
q: Under a known market custom of buyback, a seller sells a commodity for 100 spot and on a later date buys it back for a higher spot price of 105. Is this permitted?
options: Yes, since both prices are paid on spot, with no deferment
No, it is a prohibited scenario under such custom
Yes, since the buyback price is higher
Yes, if delivery took place in between
explanation: Per 3/5/1/4, with collusion or custom, selling for spot and buying back later at a higher spot price is a prohibited scenario.

title: Sale of Debt
q: Bank A holds Salam Sukuk and wishes to exchange them with the Salam seller, who is the debtor. Which rules govern this exchange?
options: The rules on sale of debt to a third party
It is not permitted in any form
The rules on sale of debt to the debtor
No debt rules, since Sukuk are securities
explanation: Per 9/3/2, Salam or Istisna' Sukuk may be exchanged with the debtor following the rules of sale of debt to the debtor (4/1, 4/1/1/3).

title: Controls on Gharar in Financial Transactions
q: Two Institutions in different countries disagree whether a certain uncertainty in a contract is excessive Gharar. On what basis is this assessed under the standard?
options: Normal practice ('Urf), which may differ by place and time
The view of the party that bears the greater risk
The amount of profit expected from the transaction
A fixed percentage of the contract value set by the standard
explanation: Per 4/2/1, assessment of excessive Gharar could differ according to place and time and has to be determined in the light of normal practice ('Urf).

title: Stipulations and Ethics of Fatwa in the Institutional Framework
q: Per the basis, why may an Institution not adopt other boards' Fatwas without its own board's permission?
options: Other boards are always less qualified than the Institution's own
To bar fabrication and pursuing exemptions out of context
Fatwas of other boards are secret
Each country forbids foreign Fatwas
explanation: The basis: this bars any tendency to fabrication or pursuing exemptions without their controls or context, which leads to adopting irrelevant Fatwas.

title: Mudarabah
q: A capital provider gives a Mudarib two funds: profit on Fund 1 goes to the Mudarib and profit on Fund 2 to the capital provider. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible if the funds are invested separately
Permissible if losses are also split this way
Permissible if both funds are equal
Not permissible
explanation: Per 8/6, it is not permissible to give two capitals on condition that profit of one goes to the Mudarib and profit of the other to the capital provider.

title: Financial Rights and How They Are Exercised and Transferred
q: With government permission, Ahmad marked a plot of unappropriated land (Tahjir) but has not developed it. He wants to sell the land to Omar. What is the ruling?
options: Waive his entitlement for consideration, but not sell the land
He may neither sell the land nor waive his entitlement in any manner
He may sell the land, as Tahjir confers ownership
He may sell the land after one year of possession
explanation: Per 9/2-9/3, Tahjir gives exclusivity and priority but not ownership; the holder may waive his entitlement for consideration but may not sell the land.

title: Distribution of Profit in Mudarabah-Based Investment Accounts
q: A client transfers funds from his USD account to his EUR account at Bank A. What form of possession suffices for this exchange?
options: Actual possession of cash in each currency
Physical delivery of the euro banknotes
Possession after two working days
Constructive possession is sufficient
explanation: Per 2/2/6, in transfers between accounts, constructive possession is sufficient, for the same or different currencies, as the process involves exchange and transference.

title: Sale of Commodities in Organized Markets
q: Bank A sells part of a stock of sugar it bought before the part sold is distinguished from the rest, so its sugar is mixed with the seller's. What is the ruling?
options: Permitted, if Bank A pays the full price to the seller on the spot
Permitted, if the warehouse holds enough stock to cover both sales
Prohibited, as the liabilities of buyer and seller overlap
Permitted, as long as the total quantity in the stock is known
explanation: Per 4/2/2, selling the commodity before ascertaining it in a distinguishing manner is prohibited, as the liabilities of buyer and seller overlap.

title: Distribution of Profit in Mudarabah-Based Investment Accounts
q: Per the basis, which principle supports the approximation inherent in the scoring method of profit distribution?
options: Exchange dealings tolerate more Gharar and approximation than partnerships
More exemptions are allowed in partnerships than in exchange dealings
Each depositor's exact profit must be traced
Profit is deserved only for contribution of work
explanation: Per the basis, much more exemptions are allowed in Musharakat than in Mu'awadah, and division (Qismah) by approximation of shares rests on mutual consent.

title: Procrastinating Debtor
q: Bank A wants to stipulate that a late payer compensates it for its loss of income, measured by its average profit rate during the delay. Is this permitted?
options: No, opportunity loss compensation is not permitted
Yes, if paid in kind rather than in cash
Yes, if a court determines the amount
Yes, if it is based on the Bank's actual average profit rate
explanation: Per 2/1/2, stipulating compensation for a debtor's delay is not permitted, including compensation for loss of income (opportunity loss).

title: Possession (Qabd)
q: Bank A's staff disagree on how possession of a newly traded type of commodity is achieved. Per the standard, what is the basis for determining the mode of possession in things?
options: Physical transfer by hand in all cases
The rules of the commodity exchange only
The terms set unilaterally by the seller
Custom ('Urf)
explanation: Per 3/1, custom ('Urf) is the basis for determining the mode of possession; hence modes of possession differ with the nature of things and people's practices.

title: Istisna’a and Parallel Istisna’a
q: A manufacturer goes bankrupt while making goods under an Istisna'a, none yet delivered. Does the ultimate purchaser have a prior right over those goods against third parties?
options: Yes, as the goods are being made specially for him
Yes, over the goods and the materials
No, unless they were wholly or partly delivered
Yes, if he paid part of the price
explanation: Per 3/1/3, unless the items are delivered, the ultimate purchaser has no prior right over a third party to items still being produced if the supplier is bankrupt.

title: Distribution of Profit in Mudarabah-Based Investment Accounts
q: A holder exits Bank A's investment pool. Per the Mubara'ah stipulation, what happens to his rights in the remaining reserves for investment risks?
options: They are held for him until the pool is liquidated
He relieves the remaining holders of them
They are transferred to the Bank as Mudarib
He receives his share of them in cash on exit
explanation: Per 5/4, the exiting party relieves the holders of his rights in undistributed profit and the remaining reserves and allocations; holders relieve him of unapparent losses.

title: Salam and Parallel Salam
q: When Salam delivery falls due, the seller offers Bank A cash equal to the wheat's market value instead of the wheat. May the Bank accept this as a replacement?
options: Yes, as the market value is fair
Yes, if paid in the capital's currency
Yes, if the cash is less than the capital
No, replacement by currency is excluded
explanation: Per 4/2, the buyer may exchange al-Muslam Fihi for other goods after the due date, except currency.

title: Banking Services in Islamic Banks
q: Bank A itself underwrites a share subscription and also markets the shares. What may it charge?
options: A fee for underwriting plus the marketing costs it incurred
Nothing at all, for either service
Actual marketing costs, but no fee for mere underwriting
A percentage of the shares it underwrites
explanation: Per 2/3/2, the Institution may underwrite itself without a fee for mere underwriting, but may charge actual expenses for other services like studies or marketing.

title: Zakah
q: Bank A paid Salam capital to a farmer for wheat it bought for trading, not yet received. What Zakah treatment applies?
options: Bank A pays Zakah on the Salam capital
The farmer alone pays and the Bank pays nothing
No Zakah until the wheat is received
Zakah on the wheat's expected market value
explanation: Per 5/3/4/10, the Institution pays Zakah on Salam capital if the goods were purchased for trading; the seller's received capital is Zakatable as his cash.

title: Waqf
q: An overseer appointed by the Waqif breached the conditions of the Waqf deed. Who else may dismiss him?
options: Only the Waqif who appointed him
The judge or the relevant authority
The majority of the beneficiaries
No one, as he was appointed by the Waqif
explanation: Per 3/10/3, for misconduct, negligence or breach, the judge or relevant authority may dismiss the overseer, whoever appointed him.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: A Sharikah owns assets acquired for leasing and distributes rental income to the partners every year. How are these annual distributions treated?
options: As a fixed remuneration of the partners for managing the leases
As final profit that is not subject to any later settlement
On account, subject to settlement at the end of the Sharikah
As a return of capital to each partner in equal instalments
explanation: Per 3/1/5/12, where the subject matter is leased assets or services, the amount distributed annually is on account, subject to settlement and reimbursement at the end.

title: Procrastinating Debtor
q: A Murabahah contract makes all instalments due if one is missed. The customer missed an instalment due to force majeure. May Bank A accelerate the debt?
options: Yes, as the clause was agreed in the contract
No, the clause cannot apply where force majeure caused it
Yes, after giving him notice and allowing a reasonable period
Yes, but only for the next two instalments
explanation: Per 2/1/6, unless the failure was caused by force majeure, all outstanding instalments may be stipulated to fall due when the debtor fails to pay one.

title: Combination of Contracts
q: Bank A offers a money transfer service combined with currency exchange, where spot delivery of the exchanged currency is not observed. What is the ruling?
options: Forgivable, as the exchange is subsidiary to the transfer
Prohibited, as it combines two contracts in one
Permissible only for amounts below a set limit
Prohibited, as spot delivery is always required in currency exchange
explanation: Per 5/2/3, sale-based Riba and violation of exchange rules (e.g. ignoring spot delivery when exchange is combined with money transfer) are forgivable in subsidiary contracts.

title: Islamic Reinsurance
q: Several Islamic insurance companies form a reinsurance fund from contributions out of their insurance funds. What is the nature of this fund?
options: It is owned by the participating companies' shareholders in equal shares
It is a branch of the largest participating company
It is a traditional reinsurer owned by the funds
It has a distinct legal personality and independent liability
explanation: Per 2/1, a reinsurance fund with a distinct legal personality and independent financial liability is formed from contributions made out of insurance funds on donation basis.

title: Agency and the Act of an Uncommissioned Agent (Fodooli)
q: Without any reasonable excuse, the principal forces a paid agent to stop work halfway through the agency period. What fee is the agent entitled to?
options: No fee, since the agency was revoked
Remuneration for the half already performed
The full remuneration agreed upon
The market rate for the work already performed
explanation: Per 4/2/7, when the principal forces the agent to discontinue before the end of the period without reasonable excuse, the agent gets the full agreed fee.

title: Conversion of a Conventional Bank to an Islamic Bank
q: After conversion, Bank B holds impermissible commodities, and some it sold earlier remain unpaid. What is required?
options: Hold them all until the Shari'ah board meets
Sell those held and keep all proceeds
Destroy those held, and waive the unpaid price of those sold
Destroy those held; collect and donate the unpaid price
explanation: Per 8/1/5, the converted bank must destroy impermissible commodities it holds; the unpaid price of those already sold must be received and donated to charity.

title: Concession Contracts
q: Company X builds a toll road on State land; the road and its usufruct belong to Company X for 25 years, then go to the State. What is this?
options: A form of construction concession contract
A survey license, granting the right of preliminary study
A utilization concession contract for extracting natural resources
A management concession contract under which Company X runs the road
explanation: Per 6/1/2/2, a licensee building a project on State land, with the project and usufruct owned by it for a period then passing to the State, is a construction concession form.

title: Sale of Commodities in Organized Markets
q: Bank A stipulates that its commodity agent guarantee the sale price under all circumstances. On what basis does the standard reject this?
options: Guarantees are never allowed in commodity sales, whether by agents or others
An agent is a trustee, liable only for transgression or negligence
The agent's wages would become unknown, which makes the contract invalid
An agent is a debtor for all sums he handles on behalf of his principal
explanation: Per the Basis, the agent is a trustee and gives no guarantee except for transgression, negligence or breach of the constraints of agency.

title: Salam and Parallel Salam
q: Why does the Shari'ah basis say Iqalah is easily applicable to Salam?
options: Salam is not a binding contract until goods are delivered
Salam capital is never paid in advance of delivery
Regret is more likely, as Salam is a low-cost sale
Iqalah applies only to Salam contracts and no others
explanation: The basis: the Prophet encouraged Iqalah; in Salam, a low-cost sale, the parties are more likely to regret it, so Iqalah is easily applicable.

title: Ju’alah
q: Company X announces publicly a reward to anyone who designs a new trade mark meeting its conditions. No specific person is named. Is the Ju'alah concluded?
options: No, the worker must be specified by name in the contract at the time of the offer
Yes, Ju'alah may be concluded by an offer to the general public
Yes, but only once Company X picks and names one worker
No, a worker must first formally accept the public offer
explanation: Per 5/1 and 5/2, the worker need not be specified; Ju'alah is concluded by an offer to the public, and acceptance is not a condition.

title: Mortgage and its Contemporary Applications
q: A client mortgages his current account balance with Bank A to the same Bank. How does the Bank's status over the balance change?
options: It changes from holding it on guarantee basis to holding it on trust
It becomes the Bank's own property until repayment
It changes from holding it on trust basis to holding it on guarantee basis
It does not change; the Bank still guarantees it as a loan
explanation: Per 3/2/5, when an asset held by the mortgagee as a guaranteed asset (e.g. a current account) is mortgaged, its status changes from guarantee to trust.

title: Salam and Parallel Salam
q: A Salam seller delivers wheat of better quality than specified, asking no higher price. The specified grade was not vital to the buyer. What must the buyer do?
options: Cancel the Salam and recover capital
Accept them and pay the extra value
Reject them as non-conforming
Accept the goods
explanation: Per 5/2, the buyer must accept superior goods if the seller seeks no higher price, unless the inferior specified description is itself vital.

title: Investment Sukuk
q: Company X issued certificates of ownership of leased assets and wants to redeem some before maturity. At what price may it redeem them?
options: At market price or a price agreed with the holder at redemption
At nominal value less a fixed early-redemption fee
Only at the nominal value stated in the prospectus
At a price fixed in advance at the time of issue in the prospectus
explanation: Per 5/2/5, the issuer may redeem certificates of leased assets before maturity at market price or at a rate agreed at the date of redemption.

title: Arbitration
q: An Ijarah contract between Bank A and a customer contains an arbitration clause. When a dispute arises, the customer refuses arbitration. What is the position?
options: Arbitration is binding only on the Bank, not the customer
The customer may choose the courts instead at any time
Arbitration is optional until both sign a new agreement
Arbitration is binding as it was stipulated in the contract
explanation: Per 5/1 and 9/3, arbitration is binding when stipulated as a condition in the contract; no further agreement is needed at the time of dispute.

title: Payment Cards
q: Bank A issues a card to Ahmad and keeps it valid for use, but Ahmad has not used it yet. How is the issuer-cardholder relationship characterized at this stage?
options: Novation (Hawalah)
Guarantee
Provision of services
Lending (Qard)
explanation: Per 2/2/1/1, upon issuance the relationship is provision of services to the cardholder: issuing the card and keeping it valid for use.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: A customer wishes to use the balance of his current account with Bank A as his capital contribution in a Sharikah with Bank A. What is the ruling?
options: Not permissible, since current accounts are loans to the bank
Permissible, though current accounts are juristically loans to the bank
Permissible only after the funds are converted into commodities
Permissible only in a Sharikah with a third party, not with Bank A
explanation: Per 3/1/2/5, current account funds, though juristically loans, can be contributed to a Sharikah with the Institution itself or with a third party.

title: Murabahah
q: Under the Murabahah standard, what is the specific purpose of requiring the Institution to take possession of the item before selling it to the customer?
options: So that the Institution may add storage costs
So that the item can be registered for the customer
So that the Institution can inspect it for the customer
So that the Institution assumes the risk of the item
explanation: Per 3/2/2, possession ensures the Institution assumes the item's risk, moving it from the supplier's responsibility to the Institution's.

title: Insolvency
q: The sale proceeds of Ahmad's sequestered assets do not cover his debts. Creditors ask the court to oblige him to work or borrow to pay the shortfall. What is the ruling?
options: He must work until the debts are fully paid
He is not required to earn or take out a loan
He must take a loan to settle the remaining debts
He must do so if a majority of creditors demand it
explanation: Per 7/3, the debtor is not required to earn or take out a loan if the proceeds of sale are insufficient to pay off his debts.

title: Commercial Papers
q: Bilal wants to use a note that is not yet due as the price of goods sold by description as a liability, to be delivered later. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible if the note is first endorsed to the dealer
Permissible if the goods are delivered on maturity
Not permissible for goods sold by description as a liability
Permissible, exactly as with ascertained goods
explanation: Per 6/3, non-due paper may be the price of ascertained goods or usufruct, but not of goods sold by description as a liability.

title: Rules for Calculating Profit in Financial Transactions
q: A Mudarabah contract changes the profit ratio once a hurdle rate is reached. Per the Shari'ah basis, why are different rates permissible?
options: They do not disrupt the sharing of profit by all parties
Profit above a hurdle is not true profit
The capital is guaranteed below the hurdle
The Mudarib's work increases above the hurdle, so he deserves a larger share
explanation: Per the basis, using different rates in Mudarabah is permissible because such a provision does not disrupt the sharing of profits by all parties.

title: Waqf
q: Shares held as Waqf rise in market value from 10 to 15 per share. How is the increase classified?
options: As revenue to be paid to beneficiaries
As a capital gain on the Waqf asset
As a gain returned to the Waqif
As profit due to the overseer
explanation: Per 2/4/14/2, an increase in the market value of Waqf shares constitutes a capital gain on the Waqf asset and not revenue.

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: To secure rentals, Bank A takes an assignment of the lessee's rights to a permissible property insurance indemnity held by a third party. What is the ruling?
options: Not permissible, as insurance is the lessor's
Permissible only for life insurance
Permissible only for misuse, not for rent
Permissible as security for the rentals
explanation: Per 6/1, permissible security of all kinds may be taken, including assignment of rights held by third parties, even a permissible insurance indemnity.

title: Controls on Gharar in Financial Transactions
q: Bank B leases a car to a customer at a set rent per mile; the total rent will be known only after the trip ends. What is the ruling?
options: Valid; the unit price is known though the total is not
Void, since the total rent is unknown at contracting
Void, as the rent is left to one party's choice
Valid only if a maximum mileage is fixed
explanation: Per 5/2/2, renting a car at a rent per mile, with the amount determined after reaching the destination, does not make the contract void.

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: Bank A signs an Ijarah contract for a machine that a third-party supplier still owns, intending to buy it next week. What is the status of the lease?
options: Valid, if the supplier guarantees delivery to the Bank
Valid, if the rent starts only after the purchase date
It may not be executed until the Bank owns the machine
Valid, as the customer already knows the supplier well
explanation: Per 3/1 and 3/1/2, a lease of a specified asset must be preceded by acquiring the asset or its usufruct; it is not executed until the Institution acquires it.

title: Stipulations and Ethics of Fatwa in the Institutional Framework
q: Bank A's board gives an oral ruling on a new product in a meeting. What does the standard require for Institutions?
options: The Fatwa should be written to serve as a document
An oral Fatwa is sufficient for Institutions of small size
It must be recorded only by audio
It needs no record if management attends
explanation: Per 10/1, Fatwa can in principle be issued by uttering, signaling or acting, but for Institutions it should be written as evidence or a reference document.

title: Liability of the Investment Manager
q: Rab Al Maal instructs the investment agent to sell an asset at 100. Without permission, the agent sells it at 90. What is the agent's liability?
options: He is liable for the full price of 100
He must recover the asset from the buyer
He is liable for the difference of 10
He bears nothing, as his possession is fiduciary
explanation: Per 7/2, if the manager sells below the specified price without permission, he is liable for the difference between that price and the price sold.

title: Financial Rights and How They Are Exercised and Transferred
q: Company X holds a call option on shares and wants to sell the option to Bank A for a price. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible, as it is a financial right
Permissible, if the price is fair
Permissible, if the option is not yet due
Not permissible to take consideration for it
explanation: Per 10/1, it is not permissible to take consideration for transfer of put or call option rights, whether by sale or otherwise.

title: Agency and the Act of an Uncommissioned Agent (Fodooli)
q: An agent to sell a mortgaged asset dies before the sale. Per the Shari'ah basis, what happens to this agency?
options: It is suspended until the debtor appoints a new agent in place of him
It does not expire and is pursued by the agent's inheritors
It passes to the mortgagee to sell for himself at the market price
It expires, like any agency, on the agent's death, and cannot be inherited
explanation: The basis treats agency to sell a mortgaged asset as an exception: it does not expire on the agent's death and is pursued by inheritors, to protect the mortgagee.

title: Options to Terminate Due to Breach of Trust (Trust-Based Options)
q: Misled by the seller's false statements, Ahmad buys food and consumes it before discovering the deception. What is the position?
options: The option lapses; the seller is entitled to the full price
The seller must refund the excess over the market price
Ahmad may still revoke and recover the full price
Ahmad is entitled to a partial refund of the price
explanation: Per 2/4/1-2/4/2, Khiyar al-Taghrir lapses if the item is consumed before the deception is discovered; the seller gets the full price and the buyer no refund.

title: Waqf
q: Fatimah donates a farm as Waqf; half the income goes to her relatives and half to an orphanage. Which type of Waqf is this?
options: Charitable Waqf (al-Waqf al-Khayri)
Self-dedicated Waqf (al-Waqf 'Ala al-Nafs)
Joint Waqf (al-Waqf al-Mushtarak)
Family Waqf (al-Waqf al-Ahli)
explanation: Per 2/3/3, a joint Waqf is where the property is donated to family as well as charitable purposes, with the income shared accordingly.

title: Commercial Papers
q: Under the standard, which description fits a bill of exchange?
options: A certificate representing a common share in a stock company
A signed unconditional order to pay a sum to a third person or order
An order from a drawer to a drawee bank to pay a sum at sight
A certificate whereby a debtor promises to pay a creditor a sum
explanation: Per 2/1, a bill of exchange is a written, signed, unconditional order from one person to another to pay a sum at sight or a set date to a third person or order.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: In a diminishing Musharakah, the customer promises to buy Bank A's units at their original value whatever the market value. What is the ruling?
options: Permitted if the units are bought gradually
Permitted if the promise is non-binding on the customer and Bank A
Permitted as the price is known in advance and removes uncertainty for both
Not permitted: it guarantees Bank A's equity value
explanation: Per 5/7, acquisition must be at market value or a price agreed at the time; face or original value would mean the customer guarantees the Institution's equity.

title: Hawalah
q: Per the Shari'ah basis, by analogy with which contract is a Hawalah with deferred payment permitted?
options: A Salam contract with a deferred delivery of the goods
A sale contract with a deferred price payable by instalments
A guarantee contract concluded on a deferred basis
A loan contract with a deferred maturity date
explanation: Per the Basis, deferred Hawalah is analogous to a deferred guarantee: a right due by Hawalah is like one due by guarantee, which may be deferred.

title: Islamic Reinsurance
q: Islamic Insurance Company X earns a Mudarib share from investing premiums retained for a traditional reinsurer. Where is this share credited?
options: To the account of the participants
To X's shareholders as a fee income
To a charity account, as it arises from dealing
To the account of the traditional reinsurer
explanation: Per 6/2, the reinsurer's profit share goes to its account with the Islamic insurer, while the Islamic insurer's share as an independent personality goes to the participants' account.

title: Arbitration
q: How does the Shari'ah basis of the standard characterize the nature of arbitration?
options: A donation by the arbitrator to the parties
A judicial function of the State
A sale of the arbitrator's services to the parties, and nothing more
Like agency for the parties, and like private custodianship
explanation: The Shari'ah basis states that arbitration seems like agency on behalf of the two parties, while also seeming to involve private custodianship.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: A Sharikah reaches its expiry date and all assets are sold at market value. What is paid first from the proceeds?
options: The profit shares of the partners
Liquidation expenses
The partners' capital contributions
The financial liabilities of the partnership
explanation: Per 3/1/6/3, proceeds are used for (a) liquidation expenses, then (b) financial liabilities, then (c) distribution of the remainder to partners.

title: Financial Rights and How They Are Exercised and Transferred
q: A creditor did not claim a debt for many years, and the law sets a limitation period for court claims that has passed. What is the status of the right itself?
options: It is not extinguished, though a court claim may be barred
The right is reduced in proportion to the delay
The right is transferred to the state treasury
The right is extinguished by the mere passage of a long period of time
explanation: Per 12/2 (a), rights are not extinguished by the passage of time, but there can be a limitation period after which a claim cannot be made in court.

title: Combination of Contracts
q: Bank A combines an Ijarah and a Wakalah in one set. Each is permissible on its own and neither is a condition of the other. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible only if both are concluded for a single lump sum value
Prohibited unless one is made a condition of the other
Prohibited, as two contracts may never be combined in one set
Permissible, barring an exceptional Shari'ah restriction
explanation: Per clause 3, combining contracts each permissible on its own, without one as a condition in the other, is permissible unless an exceptional restriction applies.

title: Sale of Debt
q: Why does the standard accept a new Murabaha for an indebted solvent customer, even if its proceeds settle his old debt?
options: The new profit rate equals the old one
It is independent; settling is the customer's choice
A solvent debtor cannot give rise to riba
The old debt is extinguished by set-off against the new financing
explanation: Per the Basis for 4/1/3/4, the rules make it independent financing; any settlement is the customer's own disposition, outside the Institution's authority.

title: Payment Cards
q: What is the basis for an issuer retaining service fees pro rata until a card's cancellation?
options: The fee is earned only on actual usage of the services
The fee is a security for future claims
The fee is earned by enabling use of the usufruct
The fee is earned in full on signing the card agreement
explanation: Basis 5/2/2: the provider is entitled to the fee by enabling possession of the usufruct, estimated by the period elapsed since it was available.

title: Controls on Gharar in Financial Transactions
q: Company Y buys a Juzaf commodity (a heap of unknown quantity). Under the standard, what does actual holding of such a commodity require?
options: Shifting the commodity to another location
Weighing the exact quantity in the seller's store
Signing a delivery receipt at the seller's premises
Obtaining the seller's release letter only
explanation: Per 5/6, actual holding of a Juzaf commodity requires shifting it to another location; for measured goods it is receipt of the exact quantity.

title: Hiring of Persons
q: Per the Shari'ah basis, why must a shared employee guarantee what he works on?
options: He always owns the item that he is working on
His pay is deemed to include an insurance premium
He works in the owner's absence and for many employers
He is a trustee in the same way as a private employee
explanation: The basis cites Sahabah reports: the shared employee does his paid work in the owner's absence and works for many employers, not one.

title: Islamic Insurance
q: Ahmad wants Islamic cover against the risk of disability and death. Which type of Islamic Insurance is this?
options: Social insurance arranged by the state
Person Insurance, sometimes known as Takaful
Property Insurance for actual injury
Liability insurance for breach of trust
explanation: Per 6/2, Person Insurance covers risks of disability and death, is sometimes known as Takaful, and corresponds to conventional life insurance.

title: Commercial Papers
q: Bilal holds a note not yet due and wants to use it as the price to buy a specific, ascertained car from a dealer, who delivers the car at once. What is the ruling?
options: Not permissible, as it is a sale of debt for debt
Not permissible, as the note is not yet due
Permissible only if the car is delivered at maturity
Permissible, with actual or legal delivery of the car
explanation: Per 6/3, a beneficiary may use commercial paper not yet due as price for ascertained goods or usufruct, with actual or legal delivery (commodity-based discounting of debts).

title: Waqf
q: An author creates a Waqf over his book's copyright, intending to appropriate that specific right as it is. Based on the Waqf asset, how is this Waqf classified?
options: Specific Waqf Assets
Joint Waqf
Cash Waqf
Investment Waqfs
explanation: Per 2/2/2/1, Specific Waqf Assets aim to appropriate an asset as it is, and this includes Waqf of usufructs and Waqf of moral rights.

title: Zakah
q: Bank A sold goods in Salam and received the Salam capital, but has not yet delivered the goods. How is this treated in Bank A's Zakah?
options: Only the profit portion is deducted
The Salam capital is fully Zakatable as cash held by the Bank, whatever its obligation
No effect until the goods are delivered
The Salam capital is deducted from Zakatable assets
explanation: Per 6/3/3, goods sold through Salam and not yet delivered are a debt, so the amount of Salam capital is deducted from the Zakatable assets.

title: Buyback
q: Bank A buys a building from Company X, and they exchange promises binding on each of them: the Bank to resell and Company X to buy it back next year. Ruling?
options: Permitted, since promises are not contracts
Permitted, if the prices are both spot
Not permitted, being a binding bilateral promise
Permitted, if recorded in a separate deed
explanation: Per 3/4, there must not be a bilateral promise (muwa'ada) binding on both parties to enter into the second contract.

title: Waqf
q: A superintendent considers a Hikr lease that keeps Waqf land with a tenant as long as he pays the changing normal rent. Which is a condition for Hikr?
options: The Waqif expressly stipulated Hikr
Istibdal of the Waqf is not possible
The tenant pays the whole rent in advance
The Waqf has surplus income
explanation: Per 6/3/1, Hikr requires that the Waqf has no income for development, no one will pay fixed-term rent in advance for it, and Istibdal is not possible.

title: Insolvency
q: Seller S reclaims livestock he sold to an insolvent buyer. While with the buyer, the animals gained considerable weight. Who gets the weight increase?
options: The other creditors, through the value of the increase
The insolvent buyer, whom S must compensate for the fodder and care that produced it
S, since an inseparable increase goes with the reclaimed asset
S and the insolvent buyer, shared equally between them
explanation: Per the basis, if an inseparable increase occurs, like livestock weight, and the seller chooses reclamation, he takes only the asset as is; a separate increase belongs to the insolvent.

title: Guarantees
q: As underwriter of a share issue, Bank A also conducts the feasibility study and markets the shares. May it charge for these?
options: Yes, as a percentage of shares underwritten
Yes, for services other than the guarantee
No, all underwriting must be free
Only if no shares remain unsubscribed
explanation: Per 6/7/2, the underwriter may receive consideration for services other than the guarantee, such as a feasibility study or marketing the shares.

title: Islamic Insurance
q: This year, claims exceed the insurance assets and reinsurance recoveries of an Islamic insurance fund. How may Islamic Insurance Company T cover the deficit?
options: By an interest-bearing loan to the fund, repaid from later contributions
By cutting the indemnities already paid
By keeping next year's contributions as company profit
By Qard Hasan debited to the fund, repaid from surpluses
explanation: Per 10/8, the deficit may be covered by financing or Qard Hasan debited to the fund, from later years' surpluses, or by policyholders if they undertook to.

title: Stipulations and Ethics of Fatwa in the Institutional Framework
q: Bank A plans to launch a new Ijarah product. Must it seek a Fatwa before launching it?
options: Yes, for every operation it intends to pursue
Yes, but only for products above a set size
No, if a similar product exists elsewhere
No, only after a Shari'ah problem arises
explanation: Per 3/4, the Institution must seek Fatwa on incidences occurring or expected, and for every operation it intends to pursue.

title: Loan (Qard)
q: Bank A wants to apply the standard on Loan (Qard) to the deferred price owed by its Murabahah customers. Is that correct?
options: Yes; every deferred amount owed to Bank A is a Qard
No; the price in a credit sale is excluded from its scope
No; the standard covers only loans made by individuals, not institutions
Yes, but only once the customer delays payment
explanation: Per Scope (1), the standard does not cover what is not a Qard, like the price in a credit sale and investment accounts, which have their own standards.

title: Waqf
q: An overseer seeks financing to add a luxury wing to a tangible Waqf building. It would add benefit but is not essential. Neither the Waqif nor the authorities approved. Is it allowed?
options: Yes, since it serves the Waqf's interest
Yes, if the beneficiaries consent
No, as it is not for an essential purpose
Yes, if the profit rate is fair
explanation: Per 5/1, debt against tangible Waqf for non-essential purposes is not permitted, even if beneficial, unless stipulated by the Waqif or authorized.

title: Murabahah
q: Bank A signs a Murabahah sale with a customer today and signs its own purchase contract with the supplier tomorrow. What is the status of the Murabahah?
options: Valid, but binding only after the supplier delivers
Valid, provided the mark-up is disclosed
Valid, since the customer gave a binding promise
Not valid: the Bank must first buy and possess the item
explanation: Per 3/1/1, the Institution may not conclude a Murabahah before it concludes the purchase from the supplier and acquires actual or constructive possession.

title: Ju’alah
q: A broker is engaged under Ju'alah to find a buyer for Company X's building. When is the broker's compensation earned?
options: When the contract he intermediates is concluded
When the buyer pays the last instalment of the price to Company X
When he introduces any interested party to Company X, whether or not a deal follows
When he has spent a set number of days seeking a buyer for the building
explanation: Per 8/4, in brokerage under Ju'alah, entitlement to compensation is contingent upon the conclusion of the contract for which intermediation is undertaken.

title: Online Financial Dealings
q: Company X wants to sell its online customers' data to a marketing firm without their permission. What is the ruling?
options: Permitted if the data are sold at a fair market price
Strictly prohibited without the permission of the data owners
Permitted, since the data were collected by Company X
Permitted if the marketing firm is a Shari'ah-compliant entity
explanation: Per 8/1/3, trespassing dealers' online data is impermissible; it is strictly prohibited to sell or transmit it to others without the owners' permission.

title: Zakah
q: Company X, legally bound to pay Zakah, made a net loss this year, but its assets still exceed its liabilities. Is Zakah due?
options: Yes; losses do not prevent Zakah unless liabilities absorb assets
No; Zakah is due only in a year in which a profit is made on capital
No; Zakah is levied on the income statement, not assets
Yes, but only on the reserves and retained profits
explanation: Per 2/3/2, the Institution need not make profits to pay Zakah; losses do not prevent it, except when liabilities absorb all its assets.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: A diminishing Musharakah contract gives Bank A the right to withdraw its share of capital at any time. What is the ruling on this clause?
options: Permitted if the customer has the same right to withdraw his share at any time
Permitted, as Bank A is the financier and bears the main risk of the venture
Permitted only after the first year
Not permitted under the rules of Sharikat al-'Inan
explanation: Per 5/2, the general rules of partnership, especially 'Inan, apply; the contract may not give any party a right to withdraw his share in the capital.

title: Irrigation Partnership (Musaqat)
q: Without the owner's permission, a Musaqat worker subcontracts his whole work to another irrigator. What option does the owner have?
options: None; the worker may assign the work freely
Only to claim compensation from the subcontractor
To ratify or reject the third-party contract
To void the Musaqat and keep the whole crop
explanation: Per 6/1/2, the worker may not subcontract without the owner's permission; if he does, the owner may ratify or reject the third-party contract.

title: Murabahah
q: Company X sells machinery to Bank A, and the Bank immediately sells the same machinery back to Company X by Murabahah on deferred payment. What is the status of the transaction?
options: Valid but the Bank's profit must go to charity
Valid if the mark-up is disclosed to Company X
Valid if the Bank takes actual possession first
Void, as it is tantamount to 'Inah
explanation: Per 2/2/3, the seller must be a third party other than the customer; a customer selling to the Institution and buying back via Murabahah is void as 'Inah.

title: Irrigation Partnership (Musaqat)
q: After the crop has materialized, the orchard owner prevents the Musaqat worker from continuing. What is the worker entitled to?
options: His share plus a market wage
A market wage only for time worked
His stipulated share of the crop
Nothing, as he did not complete the work
explanation: Per 8/5, if the owner prevents the worker after the crop materializes, the worker is entitled to his stipulated share of the crop.

title: Buyback
q: Why does the standard allow a seller to buy back his commodity in an auction, even below the deferred price?
options: The auction turns the debt into a spot sale
No collusion; the auction sets a market price
The lower price means there is no excess
The seller's bid is a unilateral promise
explanation: Per the Basis, there is no collusion; others may buy it, and the auction mechanism sets a market price rather than a pre-determined one.

title: Sale of Commodities in Organized Markets
q: Bank A buys copper on spot from Company X and sells it on deferred terms to a customer. The customer then sells it back to Company X at a lower spot price. What does the standard require?
options: Such buy-back must be avoided in this application
It is permitted if prices are at market rates
It is permitted as the parties are different
It is permitted if the customer holds it for a day
explanation: Per 4/1/4, in spot purchase and deferred sale by the institution, avoidance of buy-back, like the buyer reselling to the original spot seller at a lower price, is stipulated.

title: Credit Agreement
q: Bank A offers a client a choice between Murabahah and Musawamah to finance a machine. What distinguishes Murabahah from Musawamah?
options: Musawamah is a lease while Murabahah is a sale
Murabahah covers only movable assets, unlike Musawamah
In Musawamah the Bank's cost of obtaining the good must be indicated
In Murabahah the Bank's cost of obtaining the good must be indicated
explanation: Per 3/2/1, both are sale-based financing methods; contrary to Musawamah, in Murabahah the cost incurred by the Institution for obtaining the good must be indicated.

title: Istisna’a and Parallel Istisna’a
q: Why does the Shari'ah basis say a defect exclusion clause, valid in some sales, is invalid in Istisna'a?
options: Only the buyer may stipulate such a clause in a contract
It is valid only for specific, identified goods
Istisna'a goods are always defect-free
Defects in Istisna'a are the buyer's risk
explanation: The basis: Istisna'a sells specified goods for future delivery, and exclusion of defect liability is valid only in the sale of particular identified goods.

title: Salam and Parallel Salam
q: Bank A's Salam requires that the dates delivered must come from the seller's own farm in a named village. What is the ruling?
options: Not permitted to name a specific piece of land
Permitted if the farm's yield is normally large
Permitted, as it improves certainty about the dates
Required, so that the source of the dates is known
explanation: Per 3/2/3, it is not permissible to stipulate that al-Muslam Fihi be from a specific piece of land; the seller may deliver conforming items from anywhere.

title: Insolvency
q: After his assets are sequestered, Ahmad receives a plot of land as a gift from his uncle. How is this land treated?
options: It remains the uncle's property until the declaration is revoked
It is excluded, having been acquired after sequestration, so it is his own free property
Creditors' debts attach to it, as it accrued to him without his dealing
It attaches only to his future liability, not to the creditors
explanation: Per 5/2, debts attach to the debtor's existing property at sequestration and to property accruing to him without his dealing, such as gifts.

title: Monetization (Tawarruq)
q: Bank C holds a large stock of aluminium in one warehouse and sells part of it to a customer in Monetization. How should the sold portion be made distinct from the Bank's other assets?
options: No identification is needed if the price is paid on deferment
By stating the total market value of the sold portion in the contract
By the customer's signature on a general warehouse receipt
By separating it or recording the numbers of its storing certificates
explanation: Per 4/2, the commodity must be well identified, by separating it from the seller's other assets or recording the numbers of identifying documents such as storing certificates.

title: Waqf
q: A Waqf owns an indivisible share in a building jointly with Company X. The Waqf superintendent asks for division; Company X refuses. What applies?
options: The superintendent's request is rejected
The Waqf share is gifted to Company X
Company X must accept a sale; proceeds buy like property
Company X is forced to divide the building physically between them
explanation: Per 3/4/4/2, for an indivisible Waqf, the refraining party is forced to accept selling, and the Waqf's proceeds buy a Waqf property of the same kind.

title: Online Financial Dealings
q: Per the basis, why does downloading purchased software after signing count as possession?
options: The object is released and disposition is facilitated for the buyer
Downloading is a form of registration of the sale
Ownership of software passes only on full payment of the price, whatever the delivery
The seller loses all copies of the software on download
explanation: Per the basis, possession takes place when the sold object is released and disposition is facilitated; its form differs with the object and how it is perceived.

title: Waqf
q: Why does the standard accept a Waqf asset that is not yet known but will become known?
options: Gharar is allowed in all contracts
Ignorance is absolved in gift contracts, and Waqf is one
The overseer can fix the asset at will after the Waqf is created
Waqf is a sale, which requires later disclosure of the asset
explanation: Basis 2/4/5/1(a): ignorance can be absolved in gift contracts, and Waqf is one of the gift contracts.

title: Investment Sukuk
q: The owner of an orchard issues Musaqat Sukuk, and the subscribers assume the obligation of irrigation. What do the realised funds represent?
options: The maintaining cost of the trees
The cultivation cost of new crops
The purchase price of the orchard
The rental for the orchard land
explanation: Per 5/1/5/10(a), where the landowner issues Musaqat Sukuk, subscribers undertake irrigation and the realised funds are the maintaining cost of the trees.

title: Concession Contracts
q: A mining licensee stops extraction without a reasonable excuse, in breach of its duty to continue utilization. What may the State do?
options: Nothing, as the licensee owns the concession
Cancel the license at once, without any notice or grace period
Confiscate the licensee's equipment as a penalty
Give a reasonable grace period, then cancel if not resumed
explanation: Per 5/6, a licensee who ceases without reasonable excuse may be given a reasonable grace period to restart; otherwise the State may cancel the license.

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: A lessee of a large warehouse dies. His heirs prove the lease is now too onerous for their resources and exceeds their needs. What is the position?
options: The heirs must continue to the end
The lease ends automatically on death
The heirs may terminate the Ijarah
Only the lessor may terminate it
explanation: Per 7/2/3, Ijarah does not end with death of a party, but the lessee's heirs may terminate if they prove it is too onerous and exceeds their needs.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: In a Sharikah whose currency is the dinar, one partner pays his capital in US dollars and another in euros. How are their shares determined?
options: By the nominal amounts in each currency, unconverted
By translating both into dinars at current exchange rates
By the exchange rates prevailing at liquidation
By an exchange rate fixed by the managing partner
explanation: Per 3/1/2/2, contributions in different currencies must be translated into the Sharikah's currency at current exchange rates to determine shares and liabilities.

title: Waqf
q: A Waqf's building badly needs maintenance and the Waqf income is insufficient. The Waqif set no condition on borrowing. May the superintendent borrow?
options: Yes, freely, as maintenance precedes any distribution to beneficiaries
No; borrowing needs the Waqif's condition in the Waqf deed
Yes, with the authorities' permission, if the Waqf can repay
No; only beneficiaries may borrow for it
explanation: Per 5/3/6, borrowing is allowed on permission of legal authorities in necessity, e.g. maintenance without sufficient income, considering the Waqf's ability to repay.

title: Settlement of Debt by Set-Off
q: In a contractual set-off, X owes Y 8,000 and Y owes X 5,000. What is the result?
options: The 3,000 balance is waived by agreement
The set-off fails because the two amounts are not equal
The whole 8,000 is extinguished and X owes Y nothing more
5,000 is set off and Y may claim the remaining 3,000
explanation: Per 2/2/3, if the debts are unequal, an equivalent amount is set off and the party owed the larger debt may request payment of the balance.

title: Guarantees
q: Company X paid a primary cash security to join a tender that it lost. The tenderer had mixed the money with its own funds. What applies?
options: It is lost because it was intermingled
It is held on trust and must be returned
It may be retained as a tender fee
It is 'Arboun and may be kept
explanation: Per 6/8/1, tender securities are held on trust, are not 'Arboun, and are recoverable even if intermingled with other money.

title: Buyback
q: Ahmad promised to buy back an asset from Bank A, but the asset is totally destroyed before the buyback date. May Bank A oblige him to perform the promise?
options: No, not after total loss of the asset
Yes, the promise binds him regardless
Yes, but only at a reduced price
No, unless the loss was under half its value
explanation: Per 5/1/6, it is not permitted to oblige the promisor to fulfil the promise in case of total loss of the asset.

title: Salam and Parallel Salam
q: On the due date, a Salam seller delivers goods meeting all contract specifications, but Bank A refuses them as prices have fallen. What is the position?
options: The seller must offer a price discount
The Bank may refuse and recover its capital
The Bank may refuse but must pay a fee
The Bank shall be compelled to accept them
explanation: Per 5/1, the buyer must accept goods that meet the contract specifications; if he refuses, he shall be compelled to do so.

title: Islamic Insurance
q: Per the basis, what is the relationship between insurer and participant in Islamic insurance?
options: In fact the same person, though differing in recognition
The insurer is always the company's shareholders
Totally different persons, as in conventional insurance
The participant is a creditor of the insurer
explanation: The basis: in Islamic insurance the insurer and participant are in fact the same person though differing in recognition; in commercial insurance they differ totally.

title: Impact of Contingent Incidents on Commitments
q: Bank A buys a fleet of vehicles, then discovers that part of the fleet is owned by a third party, not the seller. What is the effect?
options: The whole contract is void and the Bank cannot keep any vehicle
That part is void; the Bank may accept the rest or terminate
The Bank must accept the rest at the full price without any option
The contract stands in full and the Bank must claim from the third party
explanation: Per 5/3, if the object is partly owned by someone else, the commitment in that part is void; the committing party may accept the rest or terminate due to fragmentation.

title: Istisna’a and Parallel Istisna’a
q: Bank A, as manufacturer, wants the ultimate purchaser to supervise the construction to ensure conformity. How may this be arranged?
options: By transferring the work's risk to him
It cannot be arranged, due to conflict
By a separate, independent agency contract
By a clause making him a co-manufacturer
explanation: Per 5/2, the Institution as manufacturer may draw up an independent and separate agency contract appointing the ultimate purchaser to supervise production.

title: Financial Paper (Shares and Bonds)
q: Bank A accepts lawful shares as a mortgage for a customer's debt. Which principle does the Basis rely on to permit this?
options: Gains are based on the bearing of costs, as in shared liability
A thing can be mortgaged if its sale is permissible
Necessity permits the prohibited, so any asset may be mortgaged
The secondary is subservient to the primary, as in mortgages
explanation: Per the Basis, a thing may be mortgaged if its sale is permissible; since shares may be sold, they may be mortgaged to secure and recover a debt.

title: Hiring of Persons
q: Bank A wants its annual hiring contract with a consultant to renew automatically each year. What does the standard require for such spontaneous renewal?
options: A renewal clause, unless a party notifies its disinterest
Approval of the Shari'ah Board each year
A fresh signature at the start of each year
Nothing; all hiring contracts renew automatically each year
explanation: Per 8/2/6, for spontaneous renewal a condition must state that the contract renews at a new period if neither party notifies the other of disinterest.

title: Credit Agreement
q: Bank A sends a client a letter approving a facility with a limit, validity period and conditions on guarantees. No transaction has started yet. What is the letter's effect?
options: It creates a debt owed by the client equal to the whole approved limit
It binds the Bank to finance up to the limit during the period
It binds the client to use the full limit within the period
It is no commitment by the Bank unless transactions actually commence
explanation: Per 2/4, the decision letter indicates it does not constitute any commitment from the Institution unless transactions are actually commenced.

title: Buyback
q: Why does the standard prohibit repurchase at a deferred price exceeding the spot price where there is collusion?
options: It turns the promise into a tradable right
It amounts to a deferred currency exchange
It amounts to 'Inah and two sales in one
It makes the sale contingent on an event
explanation: Per the Basis, it is tantamount to Einah and two sales in one (Bai'tan fi Bai'ah), citing Ibn Omar's and Abu Hurairah's narrations.

title: Gold and Its Trading Parameters in Shari’ah
q: Partners in a Musharakah agree to distribute profit in gold. At what value is the gold to be taken?
options: Its average market value over the whole financial year
Its value when the gold was first acquired by the partnership
Its value agreed at the contract date, to avoid uncertainty
Its market value at the time of profit distribution
explanation: Per 4/2, the parties may distribute profit in gold provided it is at the market value of gold at the time of profit distribution.

title: Financial Paper (Shares and Bonds)
q: Ahmad lends his shares by way of I'arah to his brother so the brother can pledge them for a debt. May the brother sell the shares?
options: No, not even to execute the mortgage
Only to execute the terms of the mortgage
Yes, if he later returns similar shares
Yes, at any time, as he holds them
explanation: Per 3/16, shares may be lent by I'arah for pledging; the borrower has no right to sell them except to execute the terms of the mortgage.

title: Monetization (Tawarruq)
q: Bank A's management wants to use Monetization as its routine way of raising liquidity instead of Mudarabah deposits or Sukuk. When may the Bank resort to Monetization for itself?
options: Only when facing a liquidity shortage that could disrupt operations
Whenever its Shari'ah Supervisory Board approves a budget for it
At any time, as Monetization is a mode of financing
Whenever its cost is lower than issuing Sukuk
explanation: Per 5/1, Monetization is not a mode of financing; the Institution may resort to it only when facing a liquidity shortage that could interrupt operations and cause client losses.

title: Hawalah
q: Ahmad issues a cheque to his creditor Bakr on an account with no balance, and Bank A accepts the overdraft. How is this classified?
options: An agency for collection
A restricted transfer of debt
An unrestricted transfer of debt
Not a transfer, as there is no balance
explanation: Per 12/2, a cheque to a creditor without balance is an unrestricted transfer of debt if the bank accepts the overdraft; if rejected, there is no transfer.

title: Salam and Parallel Salam
q: A Salam seller cannot deliver on the due date because he has become insolvent. How should Bank A treat him?
options: Charge him a penalty for the delay in delivery
Grant him an extension of time for delivery
Sell his debt to a third party
Demand delivery of currency instead
explanation: Per 5/6, if the seller fails to perform owing to insolvency, he should be granted an extension of time for delivery.

title: Al-Wakalah Bi Al-Istithmar (Investment Agency)
q: As investment agent, Bank A sold the principal's goods on credit to Company X, which now delays payment. Who pursues Company X for payment, including litigation?
options: Bank A and the principal jointly
A court-appointed administrator
The principal, as the owner
Bank A, the agent
explanation: Per 8, the results of the contract belong to the principal, but rights and obligations such as pursuing payment or delivery, including litigation, belong to the agent.

title: Irrigation Partnership (Musaqat)
q: After the crop materializes, a Musaqat worker quits. The owner hires a third party for 7,000 to finish. The worker's share later sells for 10,000. What does the worker get?
options: Nothing, as he abandoned the work after the crop materialized and so forfeits his share
5,000, half of his share
3,000, his share after deducting the wage
10,000, his full share
explanation: Per 8/4, a third party's wage is deducted from the worker's share after harvest and sale; any shortfall he makes up, and any surplus he keeps.

title: Investment Sukuk
q: A Sukuk prospectus states that the issuer will compensate holders for loss of capital up to the nominal value. In which situations may such issuer liability be accepted?
options: Only in cases of torts and negligence by the issuer
In all cases, as long as it is stated in the prospectus
Only during the first year after issuance of the Sukuk
Only when the loss exceeds a set percentage of capital
explanation: Per 5/1/8/7, the prospectus must not state that the issuer compensates holders up to nominal value in situations other than torts and negligence.

title: Waqf
q: The Waqf of Mosque A has unspent excess income, while nearby Mosque B lacks funds for its maintenance. What may be done with the excess?
options: It must stay with Mosque A
It must return to the Waqif's heirs
It must go to the poor generally
It may be transferred to Mosque B
explanation: Per 5/4, excess unspent income of a specific mosque's Waqf may be transferred to another mosque lacking enough income for its expenses or maintenance.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: Bank A asks whether the Sharikah standard governs its rules for a building that two heirs jointly own by inheritance, with no partnership contract. What is the position?
options: Covered, as a modern corporation of the allotment (Muhassah) type
Not covered: it excludes ownership partnership in jointly owned assets
Covered only if the heirs later convert it to diminishing Musharakah
Covered, as a form of Sharikat al-'Inan between the two heirs, since both own shares
explanation: Per clause 1, the standard does not cover ownership partnership where the parties jointly own an asset; it covers Sharikat al-'Aqd (contractual partnership).

title: Hiring of Persons
q: A hiring contract says that if Company X defaults on an instalment without excuse after notice, all remaining instalments fall due. If X pays early, when does the employee finally own them?
options: Only once he completes the work of the whole hiring period
At the end of the first year of the hiring contract
Immediately upon receiving the accelerated instalments
Only after a court confirms the employer's default
explanation: Per 5/2/7, an acceleration clause is allowed, but the employee does not own the prepaid instalments finally until he completes the work of the whole hiring period.

title: Buyback
q: Two co-owners hold a building in a joint ownership partnership. One sells his share to the other with a promise to buy it back at a specified price. Ruling?
options: Permitted only at a price set at performance
Not permitted; only market value is allowed
Permitted, subject to the promise rules in 5/1
Not permitted, as it negates risk sharing
explanation: Per 5/4/3, in a joint ownership partnership a promise to buy back at market value, an agreed price or a specified price is permitted, per 5/1.

title: Investment Sukuk
q: An independent third party, unrelated to the issuer, offers to guarantee the Sukuk holders against loss. Under what condition is this permitted?
options: It must also guarantee a fixed rate of profit
It must provide the guarantee free of charge
It must charge a fee equal to market rates
It must be a subsidiary of the Sukuk issuer
explanation: Per 5/1/8/7, an independent third party is permitted to provide a guarantee free of charge.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: A sleeping partner in a partnership in commendum wants to take part in managing the company. What does the standard say?
options: He may manage if the other partners consent by majority
He may manage jointly with a joint-liability partner
Sleeping partners are not entitled to manage or interfere
He may manage if he holds the largest lots
explanation: Per 4/3/1/3-4, sleeping partners may not interfere in operations; management goes to a joint-liability partner or a third party.

title: Irrigation Partnership (Musaqat)
q: A Musaqat worker hires helpers at his own expense. Per the Shari'ah basis, what supports this, and what remains?
options: Analogy with Ijarah; liability is shared equally
Custom alone; liability passes to the helpers, who are paid from the partnership
Necessity; liability passes to the owner
The Khaybar condition; his own liability does not cease
explanation: Per the basis, the Prophet allowed the people of Khaybar to use hired hands at their own expense; the worker's responsibility does not cease.

title: Istisna’a and Parallel Istisna’a
q: After taking possession of Istisna'a goods, Bank A appoints the manufacturer as its agent to sell them to the maker's customers for a percentage fee. When is this permissible?
options: If agency and Istisna'a were not made in connection
Only if the agency is given free of any charge or fee
Never, as the maker is the seller
Only if the fee is a fixed amount
explanation: Per 6/8, after possession the Institution may appoint the manufacturer as selling agent, free or for a fee, if the agency and Istisna'a were not connected.

title: Murabahah
q: In which situation may Bank A take Hamish Jiddiyyah (security deposit) from a customer?
options: Only when the customer suggests the supplier
Only after the Murabahah sale is concluded
Only when the price is payable on spot terms
When the customer has given a binding promise
explanation: Per 2/5/3, the Institution may take Hamish Jiddiyyah in the case of a binding promise by the customer, to secure compensation for any breach.

title: Financial Paper (Shares and Bonds)
q: What does the standard identify as the Shari'ah substitute for bonds?
options: Investment Sukuk
Prize bonds
Preference shares
Tamattu' shares
explanation: Per 6, the Shari'ah substitute for bonds is investment Sukuk.

title: Possession (Qabd)
q: Bank A receives a warehouse receipt issued in its name that identifies specific goods and allows it to deal in them. What does Bank A hold?
options: A debt owed to it by the warehouse keeper
Constructive possession of the goods the receipt represents
Actual possession of the goods, through their physical delivery to it
A mere promise from the warehouse to deliver later
explanation: Per 3/5, holding documents like warehouse receipts in the possessor's name is constructive possession where the goods are ascertained and he can transact in them.

title: Trading in Currencies
q: Ahmad appoints Bakr as agent to sell currency on his behalf but does not authorise him to receive the price. What keeps the exchange valid?
options: The buyer may defer payment since Bakr lacks authority
Bakr must still take possession as contracting agent
Ahmad or another agent takes possession before parting
Possession may follow within the customary settlement cycle
explanation: Per 2/7/2, an agent may sell currency without authority to receive, provided the principal or another agent takes possession before the principals disperse.

title: Buyback
q: An investment deposit agreement gives all profit up to 5% to the depositor and any excess to Bank A as Mudarib. Is this clause permitted?
options: Yes, since the Mudarib takes only the excess
No, it may lead to cessation of profit-sharing
Yes, as a performance incentive for the manager
Yes, if the 5% is only an expected return
explanation: Per 5/6/3/3(d), a clause giving all profits up to a limit to one party is not permitted; an incentive where both share profits first is allowed.

title: Concession Contracts
q: The State fixes the price at which a mining licensee sells its product. What justification does the Basis give?
options: Preventing social injury from unduly high prices
Ensuring the licensee recovers its costs and earns a fixed profit
Avoiding competition among licensees in the mineral market
Making a profit for the State treasury from the licensee's sales
explanation: Per the Basis, the State's right to fix the product price rests on the need to prevent social injury that could result from licensees charging unduly high prices.

title: Islamic Insurance
q: Company X sells insurance as a Mu'awadah contract, aiming to profit from the insurance operation itself. What is its Shari'ah status?
options: Permitted, if its premiums are invested lawfully and the policy is clear
Permitted, as Gharar is overlooked in insurance
Banned, as an exchange contract subject to Gharar rules
Permitted, if the surplus is given to charity
explanation: Per clause 2, conventional insurance is a Mu'awadah contract seeking profit from insurance itself, subject to the rulings on Gharar, and is banned.

title: Istisna’a and Parallel Istisna’a
q: A manufacturer inserts a clause in an Istisna'a contract stating that it is not liable for any defects in the goods. What is the ruling?
options: Permitted for hidden defects only
Permitted if the buyer signs it
Permitted if the price is reduced
Not permitted in an Istisna'a contract
explanation: Per 2/2/3, the manufacturer may not stipulate in the Istisna'a contract that he is not liable for defects.

title: Investment Sukuk
q: Sukuk holders ask the issuer to provide a mortgage and personal guarantees. For what may the issuer permissibly offer such guarantees?
options: For the nominal value of the Sukuk in all cases
For a minimum fixed rate of profit to holders
For its own wrongful acts or negligence
For any fall in the market price of the Sukuk
explanation: Per 5/1/8/7, the issuer may offer some tangible or personal guarantees with respect to its wrongful acts or negligence.

title: Conversion of a Conventional Bank to an Islamic Bank
q: Per the Shari'ah basis, on what contracts does a converted bank's provision of banking services (not interest-based loans) rest?
options: Qard and Hawalah with a fee on each service
Salam and Istisna'a with advance payment
Mudarabah and Musharakah with profit sharing
Ijarah and agency with remuneration
explanation: Per the Basis, providing banking services not related to interest-bearing loans is a practical application of Ijarah and agency with remuneration.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: Why does the Shari'ah basis prohibit a fixed remuneration in the Sharikah contract for a partner who helps manage?
options: Partners may not perform any management work in the company at all
It may guarantee his capital or shield him from loss
