It would make him a sleeping partner who bears no liability for losses
Management work cannot be valued in money, so no wage can be fixed for it
explanation: Per the basis, a fixed remuneration for a partner who assists in management may lead to guaranteeing his capital or to his not bearing loss in proportion to capital.

title: Investment Sukuk
q: Musharakah Sukuk have been subscribed and allotted, but the funds are still in cash and activity has not commenced. Ahmad wants to sell his Sukuk. Which rules must be observed?
options: The rules of Sarf (currency exchange) and the rules for debts
No special rules, as trading in Sukuk is freely permitted at any stage
The rules of Salam applicable to deferred goods
Only the rules on disposal of usufructs
explanation: Per 5/2/1, trading or redemption before commencement of activity requires observing the rules of Sarf (currency exchange) and the rules for debts.

title: Zakah
q: A herder owns 45 free-grazing cows for a full year. What Zakah is due?
options: One Tabee'a (in its second year)
Two Tabee'a
One Musinnah (in its third year)
Nothing, below the Nisab
explanation: Per the cow table in 11/2, 40 to 59 cows require one Musinnah (at the 3rd year of age); 30 to 39 require one Tabee'a.

title: Waqf
q: An overseer leased a Waqf asset at a flagrantly low rent, with no preferred interest. What follows?
options: He pays the difference and seeks termination unless rent rises
The lessee alone pays a penalty to the Waqf equal to a year's rent
The lease stands, and nothing further is due from anyone, as the overseer had discretion
The Waqif must compensate the beneficiaries
explanation: Per 8/5, the overseer is liable for the difference and should demand termination unless the lessee accepts the increase.

title: Irrigation Partnership (Musaqat)
q: A flood destroys 40% of a Musaqat crop; 60% survives. The worker's stipulated share is one half. How is the surviving crop divided?
options: The worker bears the whole loss from his share
The owner bears the whole loss from his share
The owner first recovers the 40% that was lost, and the rest is shared
Half each of what remains, per the stipulated shares
explanation: Per 10/1, if a natural disaster destroys only part of the crop, the parties divide what remains according to their stipulated shares.

title: Zakah
q: Company X's trade goods were worth 10 million on the Zakah due date, and 9 million on the later date it actually paid Zakah. Which value applies?
options: 9 million, the price on the date on which the Zakah was actually paid
10 million, the price at the date of Zakah accrual
The lower of cost or market value
9.5 million, the average of the two
explanation: Per 5/2/2, if prices change between the dates of accrual and payment of Zakah, the price at the date of Zakah accrual is adopted.

title: Combination of Contracts
q: In a combined set, Bank A buys, on deferred payment, the shares of an indebted company. Does the rule against selling a debt for a debt bar this?
options: No, debt for debt may be ignored as a subsidiary contract
Yes, debt may never be sold for another debt, even in a combined set
Yes, unless the company's debts are settled first
Yes, unless the price is paid immediately in cash
explanation: Per 5/2/4, selling a debt for another debt may be ignored in a subsidiary contract, e.g. purchasing (on debt) the shares of an indebted company.

title: Options to Revoke Contracts Due to Incomplete Performance
q: After buying a car, Ahmad notices a tiny mark that custom does not regard as a defect and that does not reduce its value or fitness. Does he have an option to revoke?
options: Yes; any defect at all gives the option
No; the defect must be material
Yes, if he notices it within a week
No, unless the seller hid it deliberately
explanation: Per 2/2/1, a material defect is one that renders the item defective by custom, makes it unfit for purpose or diminishes its value.

title: Islamic Reinsurance
q: Islamic Insurance Company X retains a portion of the premiums due to a traditional reinsurer and invests it by Mudarabah. What are the roles?
options: X and the reinsurer are equal Musharakah partners
The traditional reinsurer is Mudarib and X is Rab al-Mal
X is borrower paying a fixed return to the reinsurer
X is Mudarib and the traditional reinsurer is Rab al-Mal
explanation: Per 6/2, retained funds may be invested through Mudarabah or investment agency, with the Islamic insurer as Mudarib and the traditional reinsurer as Rab al-Mal.

title: Islamic Insurance
q: Participants ask why Islamic Insurance Company T will not guarantee the insurance assets. Per the basis, what is the reason?
options: It is a donor who may withdraw at will
It is a partner bearing loss pro rata to its share in the fund
It is an agent, who does not guarantee save for fault
It is a Mudarib bearing all investment loss
explanation: The basis: the company is an agent, and Fuqaha unanimously agree an agent does not guarantee property except for misconduct, negligence or breach.

title: Liability of the Investment Manager
q: Bank A, as investment agent, breaches a condition of the contract. The contract has no clause on dismissal for misconduct. What is the status of the agency?
options: It continues and Rab Al Maal cannot end it
It continues unless Rab Al Maal dismisses the agent
It ends once the loss is established by evidence
The agent is dismissed automatically by the breach
explanation: Per 7/6, the manager is not automatically dismissed for misconduct, negligence or breach unless stipulated; he is dismissed upon dismissal by Rab Al Maal.

title: Documentary Credit
q: Bank A and a client sign a Musharakah to buy imported goods before any credit is opened and before the client contracts with the supplier. In whose name may the credit be opened?
options: Only in the client's name
Only in Bank A's name
Only in the supplier's bank's name
In the name of either partner
explanation: Per 3/6/1, where the partnership contract precedes the credit and the client's contract with the supplier, the credit may be opened in either partner's name.

title: Mortgage and its Contemporary Applications
q: Per the Shafi'i view cited in the basis, why may a mortgaged asset be kept with a notary?
options: The mortgagee is not trusted to keep the asset, so a neutral third party must hold it
The mortgagor retains ownership of the asset
The right belongs to both parties, so they can agree on it
A notary is required for every valid mortgage
explanation: Per the basis, the Shafi'is permit keeping the mortgage with a notary 'because the right belongs to the two parties, so they can agree on that'.

title: Murabahah
q: Customer C buys goods as Bank A's agent, and the Bank then sells them to C by Murabahah. How are the Bank's liability and C's liability as agent kept separate?
options: By a time interval between the agency and the Murabahah
By signing the agency and the sale in one document
By placing the risk on C from his appointment
By having the supplier insure the goods
explanation: Per 3/1/5, the two risk liabilities are separated by an interval of time between performance of the agency and execution of the Murabahah.

title: Islamic Insurance
q: An Islamic insurance property policy states that it renews automatically unless the participant gives notice within a set period before expiry. What is the ruling?
options: Not permissible, as each year needs a new offer
Permissible only in Person Insurance
Not permissible, as it imposes the contribution
Permissible in property insurance
explanation: Per 13/1, in property insurance it is permissible to stipulate automatic renewal unless the participant informs the company within a specific period.

title: Murabahah
q: A customer asks Bank A to buy equipment from Supplier S. The Bank finds another supplier that is more suitable for it, but the customer refuses that offer. What may the Bank do?
options: Proceed with Supplier S only after charging a commitment fee
Nothing; it is bound to buy from the supplier the customer named
Decline to carry out the transaction
Buy from the other supplier and oblige the customer to purchase
explanation: Per 2/1/2, the customer may name a source of supply, but the Institution may decline if the customer refuses more suitable offers from other suppliers.

title: Islamic Reinsurance
q: Islamic Insurance Company X intends to sign a reinsurance agreement with a traditional reinsurer due to necessity. What must it do before signing?
options: Seek the approval of its Shari'ah Supervisory Board
Notify its Shari'ah Supervisory Board after signing
Obtain consent of each individual participant
Seek approval of the traditional reinsurer's board
explanation: Per 6/4, before signing agreements with traditional reinsurers, Islamic insurance companies should seek the approval of their Shari'ah Supervisory Boards.

title: Indices
q: A report states only that a share index stands at 459 points today. Per the standard, what can be concluded from this single figure?
options: That the market is rising, as the figure is high
Nothing until compared with past or future values
That shares have gained 459% since the base date of the index
That the market is stable, as no change is shown
explanation: Per 3/3/1, the absolute value of an index has no implication as a single figure; it is meaningful only when compared with past and future values.

title: Waqf
q: To which case does the standard draw an analogy when it prevents lending Waqf funds?
options: Lending funds of a Mudarabah
Lending from Zakah funds
Lending a deposit held in trust
Lending the funds of minors
explanation: Basis 7: the prohibition rests on analogy with not lending minors' funds, as lending may cause loss, unless lending is more secure.

title: Obtaining and Deploying Liquidity
q: Why are supervisory bodies, such as central banks, the entities most responsible for ensuring institutions' liquidity is Shari'ah-compliant?
options: They appoint the institutions' Shari'ah boards
They are the institutions' main providers of liquidity and can set the terms of such support
They licensed the institutions to operate by Shari'ah-compliant procedures
They hold the institutions' reserves as custodians
explanation: Per the basis, supervisory bodies are most responsible because they licensed the institutions to operate by Shari'ah-compliant procedures and prohibited what violates Shari'ah.

title: Possession (Qabd)
q: Bank A buys a commodity, and paying the price to the seller involves a transfer charge. The contract and custom are silent. Who bears this charge?
options: The buyer, Bank A
The seller of the commodity
Both parties equally
The bank that executes the transfer
explanation: Per 4/1/1, the expenses of delivering the price, if any, are the responsibility of the buyer unless there is a stipulation or custom to the contrary.

title: Syndicated Financing
q: Bank A prepared the feasibility study and contracts for a syndication. It asks for a commission higher than its actual cost. What is the ruling?
options: Not permissible; preparatory tasks must be free of any charge
Permissible; it may equal, exceed or be below the cost
Permissible only if Bank A is also the lead manager of the syndication
Not permissible; it must equal the actual cost incurred, no more and no less
explanation: Per 7/1, the leading Institution may receive commission for preparatory tasks, equal to, less or more than actual cost, whether or not it is lead manager.

title: Combination of Contracts
q: Bank A wants to apply a concession to an implicit contract in a combined set. How should the concession be judged?
options: By the applicable conventional banking regulations only
By the Bank's management, based on its expected profitability and risk
By the customer's consent alone, with no further review
By tradition and practice, with Shari'ah Board clearance
explanation: Per 5/1, concessions are judged in the light of traditions, practice and professional experience, and subject to clearance by the Shari'ah Supervisory Board.

title: Arbitration
q: A Mudarib managing investment accounts is asked to accept arbitration over a dispute on the Mudarabah funds. When may he accept it?
options: With the capital owners' consent or a Mudarabah clause
Only if the arbitrator is chosen by the other party to the dispute
Only with approval of a court
At any time, since he manages the Mudarabah funds
explanation: Per 8/7, a Mudarib may not accept arbitration except with the capital owners' consent or on the basis of a clause in the Mudarabah conditions.

title: Sale of Debt
q: Bank A holds a USD 1,000 receivable owed by Company X and sells it to Bank B for USD 950 in cash. What is the ruling?
options: Permitted, as Bank B bears the risk of collecting the debt
Not permitted: a monetary debt can't be sold for cash
Permitted, as the buyer is a third party
Permitted, if Company X consents to the sale in writing
explanation: Per 5/1, it is not permitted to sell a monetary debt against cash or for a monetary debt.

title: Zakah
q: Bank A's Shari'ah Board decides to give all of this year's Zakah to the poor and debtors only. Must Zakah cover all eight heads?
options: Yes, in equal shares to all eight heads, as stated in the Qur'anic verse
No, but it must cover at least four
No; it may be confined to some of the heads
Yes, at least one share to each head
explanation: Per 10/8, Zakah should not necessarily cover all eight heads of disbursement; it can permissibly be confined to some of them.

title: Guarantees
q: Investors ask Bank A, acting as Mudarib of their fund, to guarantee their capital in the Mudarabah contract. What is the ruling?
options: Not permitted: the Mudarib may not guarantee the capital
Permitted if the guarantee is written into the Mudarabah contract
Permitted if the Mudarib takes a lower share
Permitted for the capital but not for profit
explanation: Per 2/2/1, a Mudarib, Musharakah manager, investment agent or partner may not be required to guarantee the capital or promise a guaranteed profit.

title: Irrigation Partnership (Musaqat)
q: A Musaqat worker falls seriously ill and cannot work, and the owner revokes the contract. What is the worker entitled to?
options: His full stipulated share of the crop
Nothing, since he did not complete the work
A market wage for the period he worked
A wage, less the owner's actual loss
explanation: Per 13/2/1/1, if the worker cannot work for a reason outside his control, such as illness, he gets a market wage for the period worked.

title: Mortgage and its Contemporary Applications
q: Bank A, as mortgagee, decides to revoke a mortgage it holds before the debt is repaid. What is the ruling?
options: It may do so only with the mortgagor's consent
It may not, as the mortgage binds both parties
It may do so only by a court order
Yes; the mortgagee has the right to revoke it
explanation: Per 3/1/1, the mortgage contract binds the mortgagor, who cannot revoke it, whereas the mortgagee has the right to revoke it.

title: Sale of Debt
q: Bank A wants to sell to a third party a debt that the alleged debtor denies, with no evidence to establish it. What is the ruling?
options: Permitted, if sold for a commodity
Not permitted, due to excessive gharar
Permitted, if the buyer accepts the risk
Permitted at a deep discount for the risk
explanation: Per 5/5/1, selling a debt not established by acknowledgement or evidence involves excessive gharar and is not permitted.

title: Financial Paper (Shares and Bonds)
q: Bank A proposes to swap the dividends of its share portfolio with a counterparty for an agreed return. What is the ruling?
options: Not permitted: swaps on shares and their returns are barred
Permitted, if both parties use one currency
Permitted, if the underlying shares are all Shari'ah-compliant
Permitted, if no cash settlement occurs
explanation: Per 3/14, it is not permitted to conclude swap contracts with respect to shares and their returns.

title: Liability of the Investment Manager
q: Company Y offers to make good any capital loss to Rab Al Maal in a fund managed by Company Z. Company Y owns 60% of Company Z. May Company Y give this commitment?
options: Yes, if Company Y gives it voluntarily
Yes, since Company Y is a separate legal entity
No, one party's holding in the other exceeds 50%
Yes, if it has no recourse to Company Z
explanation: Per 4/1/1, the third party must be independent of the manager; with common shareholding, one party's holding must not exceed 50% of the other.

title: Gold and Its Trading Parameters in Shari’ah
q: In an importer-exporter gold deposit arrangement, the exporter used the deposit, so the gold is sold at market price. What is the stated purpose of this rule?
options: To avoid Gharar in the price of the shipment
To meet spot exchange at the contract's inception
To compensate the importer's opportunity cost
To prevent the deposit becoming a loan with benefits
explanation: Per the Basis for 10/5, selling at market price when the exporter used the deposit aims to prevent rendering the deposit a loan associated with benefits.

title: Concession Contracts
q: Company X holds a survey license for an area and later finds signs of minerals. Does the survey license give it exclusive rights or the right to mine?
options: Yes; it entitles Company X to start mining at once
No; it gives neither exclusive survey nor extraction rights
It gives extraction rights but not exclusivity
Yes; it makes Company X the sole surveyor in the whole licensed area
explanation: Per 5/2/1, a survey license does not grant the right of sole surveyor in the area nor the right to conduct extraction works or build facilities.

title: Sale of Commodities in Organized Markets
q: Bank A buys a specific, ascertained lot of cotton, stipulating that delivery will be in two months and that the price will also be paid in two months. What is the ruling?
options: Not permitted, as the two counter-values are delayed
Permitted, if a portion of the price is deposited as security
Permitted, since the cotton is ascertained
Permitted, if the delivery date is fixed
explanation: Per 3/2/2/2, where the commodity is ascertained but delay in its delivery is stipulated along with delay in the price, the contract is not permitted.

title: Settlement of Debt by Set-Off
q: Bank A pre-stipulates set-off and consolidation of future debts in its deferred sale agreements with customers. What is the stated benefit?
options: It transfers the Bank's receivables to other Institutions
No new agreement is needed if currencies differ or a debt is superior
It allows late payment compensation by set-off
It makes every future set-off compulsory regardless of its conditions
explanation: Per 4/1, pre-stipulating set-off means a fresh agreement may be avoided at the time of set-off when currencies differ or one debt is superior.

title: Guarantees
q: Bakr guarantees whatever Ahmad will come to owe Bank A on future purchases, the amount being unknown today. Is the guarantee valid?
options: Only if Bank A first approves each purchase
No, the guaranteed amount must be known at the outset
No, only existing debts may be guaranteed
Yes, unknown and future debts may be guaranteed
explanation: Per 3/2, a valid guarantee may be given for debts whose exact amount is unknown and for debts that will arise in the future.

title: Financial Paper (Shares and Bonds)
q: Bank A has calculated the prohibited income to be eliminated from its shareholdings and proposes to use it to pay its taxes. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible, as taxes are a public obligation owed by the Bank
Permissible for half of the amount only, the rest going to charity
Not permissible to use it in any way, even for taxes
Permissible, if approved by the Shari'ah board of the Institution
explanation: Per 3/4/6/5, the prohibited component may not be utilised in any way, nor may a legal fiction be created to do so, even through payment of taxes.

title: Sale of Commodities in Organized Markets
q: A broker sells the same lot of metal to two institutions at once, using duplicated title documents. What does the standard require to prevent this?
options: Insurance of the metal by each buying institution
Precision on title document numbers and liability for the cause
Registration of each sale with the regulator only
A guarantee from the broker for the sale price in all circumstances
explanation: Per 4/2/8, selling via fictitious documents or to several institutions is prohibited; title document numbers must be precise and liability fixed on the cause.

title: Mortgage and its Contemporary Applications
q: A client offers Bank A shares of a company whose original activities are permissible and whose dealings are not predominantly Riba-based. May they be mortgaged?
options: No; shares represent common property
Yes, but only shares of Islamic banks
Yes; such shares can be mortgaged
No; only Islamic Sukuk can be mortgaged
explanation: Per 4/1, Islamic Sukuk, shares of Islamic financial Institutions and shares of companies with permissible original activities may be mortgaged.

title: Istisna’a and Parallel Istisna’a
q: A manufacturer delivers items of better quality than specified, for no extra charge. The buyer had not particularly pursued the specified quality. What must the buyer do?
options: Reject them as non-conforming
Accept and pay for the extra quality
Accept only at a discounted price
Accept the items
explanation: Per 6/1/2, the purchaser shall accept better quality offered without extra charge, unless the contract quality was particularly pursued by him.

title: Commercial Papers
q: A payee bank receives a crossed cheque bearing conditions set by the drawer. What is the bank's obligation?
options: It is bound to fulfil the cheque's conditions
It must refuse it as an invalid cheque, since it bears conditions
It may disregard the crossing at will, as it is only the drawer's wish
It must cash it to any bearer who presents it at sight
explanation: Per 3/3(c), it is permitted to use a crossed cheque that binds the payee bank to fulfil its conditions.

title: Murabahah
q: Bank A adds to the cost of a Murabahah item the salaries it paid its own staff for processing the deal. What is the ruling?
options: Permitted if the salaries are disclosed to the customer
Not permitted; only direct third-party costs count
Permitted, as they are customary expenses of the business
Permitted up to a reasonable amount
explanation: Per 4/4, only direct expenses paid to a third party may be included in base cost; payments to the Institution's own staff may not be added.

title: Hiring of Persons
q: Per the Shari'ah basis, why may pay take the form of a common share of the output?
options: It can be known and does not lead to dispute or Gharar
It is in reality a form of Ju'alah, not hiring
The employer bears no risk in this form of pay
It turns the hiring into a partnership contract between the two
explanation: The basis states the pay can be a common share because in this form it can be known and will not lead to dispute or Gharar.

title: Protection of Capital and Investments
q: To protect a fund's capital against currency moves, a manager proposes conventional currency swaps and options. What does the standard say?
options: Permissible if investors consent in advance
Permissible, since currency risk may be protected by any available hedging contract
Permissible if the counterparty is an Islamic bank
Not permissible; conventional hedging contracts are excluded
explanation: Per 5/5, protecting capital by conventional hedging contracts such as futures, options and swaps is not permissible.

title: Investment Sukuk
q: A Murabahah Sukuk commodity has been sold and delivered to the buyer on deferred payment. Why is trading in the certificates now restricted?
options: The commodity can no longer be resold in the market
The profit has already been distributed to holders
They now represent a monetary debt against the buyer
The buyer has not yet issued a promise to purchase
explanation: Per the Basis, after the commodity is sold and delivered, Murabahah certificates represent a monetary debt against the buyer, so only debt-trading limits apply.

title: Payment Cards
q: Bank A, an Institution, plans a revolving credit card whose used amounts are settled in deferred instalments against interest. What is the ruling?
options: Permitted if interest goes to charity
Permitted if the interest is capped
Permitted for non-Muslim customers only
Not permitted for Institutions
explanation: Per 4/4, Institutions may not issue revolving credit cards by extending a loan settled in deferred instalments against interest.

title: Impact of Contingent Incidents on Commitments
q: Supplier X undertook to supply a conference's requirements, but for objective external reasons it could not deliver before the conference was held. What happens to the commitment?
options: It becomes null and void because fulfillment has become of no use
It is converted into a debt owed by the supplier equal to the value of supplies
It is suspended until the next conference of the same organizer
It remains binding and must be delivered after the conference
explanation: Per 5/1, when delivery becomes impossible or useless, e.g. supplies for a conference not delivered before it is held, the commitment becomes null and void under set conditions.

title: Hiring of Persons
q: Ali is a private employee of Bank A. He leaves work for a day without permission, for no recognizable duty. What does the standard say?
options: He may be absent if a colleague covers his work that day
He may not be absent without permission or a recognized duty
He may be absent if he makes up the lost time later
He may be absent for up to three days in each month without pay
explanation: Per 7/1/1, the private employee must render his service and observe the hiring period, not being absent except with the employer's permission or for a recognizable duty.

title: Mortgage and its Contemporary Applications
q: A client who mortgaged his truck to Bank A wants to keep using it for his business. When may he do so?
options: Only after repaying half of the debt
Without any permission, since he is the owner
On the permission of the mortgagee
Never, as long as the truck is mortgaged
explanation: Per 3/2/9, the mortgagor can benefit from the mortgaged asset on permission of the mortgagee.

title: Islamic Reinsurance
q: Islamic Insurance Company X needs traditional reinsurance for one year only, but the reinsurer proposes a five-year agreement. What does the standard require?
options: The period is set by the reinsurer alone
The period should be commensurate with the actual need
Any period may be agreed once necessity to use traditional reinsurance exists
The period must be at least five years
explanation: Per 6/3, the periods of reinsurance agreements with traditional reinsurers should be commensurate to the actual need.

title: Sale of Debt
q: Why may shares of an operating company with many receivables be sold without applying the sale of debt rules?
options: The majority is given the ruling of the whole
Supervening matters cannot be repelled
The debtor is deemed the possessor of the debt
Appurtenance: what can't be sold alone may follow
explanation: Per the Basis for 8/1, the concept of appurtenance (taba'iya): a thing that cannot be sold independently may be sold consequentially.

title: Zakah
q: Company X has set aside 10 million in cash, fully owned and controlled by it, to fund a future investment project. Is this cash Zakatable?
options: Yes; allocation to a project does not affect full ownership
No, not until the investment project starts
Yes, but at half of the normal Zakah rate
No; funds earmarked for a specific purpose are no longer fully owned by the company
explanation: Per 3/2/1, full ownership exists even if the asset is allocated for a purpose other than settling debts, such as implementing investment projects.

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: Bank A's lease states that the lessee may not sublet without the Bank's approval. The lessee sublets without asking. What is the position?
options: Permitted if the sub-lease rent is not higher
Permitted, as the lessee owns the usufruct
Not permitted; he needed the Bank's approval
Permitted if the sub-lessee is a Muslim
explanation: Per 3/3, sub-leasing is allowed unless the owner stipulates that the lessee should not sublet, or not do so without his approval.

title: Waqf
q: A Waqf deed stipulates that the overseers may never be dismissed under any circumstances. What is the effect of this condition?
options: The condition is void, but the Waqf remains valid
The whole Waqf is void because of it
It is valid unless the overseer is negligent
The condition is valid and binding
explanation: Per 2/6/4, a condition prejudicing the Waqf is void while the Waqf remains valid; e.g., stipulating non-dismissal of overseers in all cases.

title: Loan (Qard)
q: Bank A's system splits a single large ATM cash withdrawal by a credit card holder into several smaller ones, charging a fee on each. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible, if the card terms disclose the practice to cardholders
Permissible, as each slice is a separate service
Not permissible: slicing withdrawals to repeat charges is barred
Permissible, if each fee is a fixed amount
explanation: Per 10/3/2, the institution may not slice withdrawals as a device for obtaining repeated charges, nor consider the repayment period in the charge.

title: Rules for Calculating Profit in Financial Transactions
q: Company X earns a return under a sale contract that turns out to be invalid in Shari'ah. How is the return classified under the standard?
options: Permissible profit if the buyer consented to it
Impermissible profit, as it results from an invalid contract
Permissible profit, since it arose from a sale contract concluded with mutual consent
Permissible profit if it was disclosed in advance
explanation: Per 3/2, impermissible profit is that which results from a prohibited transaction such as interest-based contracts, forbidden commodities or invalid contracts.

title: Waqf
q: A Waqf superintendent leases a Waqf apartment to his wife at a rent slightly below the market rent of similar property. What is the ruling?
options: Allowed if the wife pays the whole rent in advance
Allowed, as minor Ghabn is always forgiven in leasing
Allowed if the shortfall is under one third of the rent
Not allowed; even minor Ghabn is not forgiven for relatives
explanation: Per 5/3/2, he may not lease to direct relatives or his spouse for less than the normal rent; minor Ghabn is not forgivable here, though forgivable for nonrelatives.

title: Investment Sukuk
q: Company X has collected subscription money for its Sukuk, but subscription is still open and no funds have been employed yet. Per the definition, when do the Sukuk represent undivided shares in the project assets?
options: Once subscription closes and the funds are employed for the issue purpose
Only on the maturity date when the assets are liquidated
From the moment each subscriber pays the full value of his Sukuk to the issuer
From the date on which the prospectus is published
explanation: Per 2, Sukuk represent shares in assets after receipt of their value, closing of subscription and employment of the funds for the purpose of issue.

title: Syndicated Financing
q: A conventional bank is proposed as lead manager of a syndication in which Bank A participates. When is this acceptable?
options: Never, as the lead manager must always be an Islamic Institution itself
Only if the contracts, projects and modes are Shari'ah-compliant
Only if Bank A guarantees the conventional bank's acts to the participants
Only if the conventional bank holds the largest share of the financing
explanation: Per 5/3, the lead is originally an Islamic Institution, but a conventional bank may lead if the contracts, projects and modes of financing are all Shari'ah-compliant.

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: Land leased for crop cultivation reaches the end of its term, but the harvest is late. What is the position of the lease?
options: It continues at the original rental until the harvest
It ends at once, and the crop must be removed
It continues at the prevailing market rental
It continues free of rent until the harvest
explanation: Per 7/2/6, the lease may remain operative for a good cause such as a late harvest, continuing at a rental based on prevailing market value.

title: Mortgage and its Contemporary Applications
q: With the owner's permission, Ahmad mortgages a borrowed house to Bank A; the house is sold to repay Ahmad's defaulted debt. What right does the owner have?
options: Recourse on Bank A for the full sale price of the house
Recourse on Ahmad for a similar house in kind
No right, since he permitted the mortgage
Recourse on Ahmad for its value, as a house is not fungible
explanation: Per 3/2/6, if a borrowed mortgage repays the debt, the owner has recourse on the mortgagor: in kind for a fungible asset, or in value otherwise.

title: Istisna’a and Parallel Istisna’a
q: Bank A is asked to conclude an Istisna'a for fresh fruit and livestock to be supplied in six months. Is Istisna'a the right contract?
options: No, Istisna'a is for items made or constructed
Yes, if the items are fully specified in the contract
Yes, Istisna'a covers any goods delivered at a later date
Yes, if the price is paid in instalments over six months
explanation: Per 3/1/1, Istisna'a is permissible only for materials transformed by a manufacturing or construction process involving labour.

title: Sale of Debt
q: Bank A sells a monetary receivable to Company Y in return for the use of a specific, identified office for one year. Is this permitted?
options: Yes, but only with the debtor's consent
No, usufructs are always deferred debts, so it is debt for debt
Yes, since the usufruct's delivery is ascertained
No, a debt may be sold only for a commodity delivered on spot
explanation: Per 5/2, a monetary debt may be sold for a usufruct or service whose subject-delivery can be ascertained at the time of sale.

title: Concession Contracts
q: Company X, an exploration licensee, discovers water in its licensed area. The license is silent on later rights. What is Company X's position?
options: It must compete with all other bidders for the concession on equal terms
It is eligible for the exclusive right to the utilization concession
It becomes owner of the water and the land
It has no further rights once exploration ends
explanation: Per 5/2/3, after discovery the exploration licensee becomes eligible for the exclusive right of obtaining the utilization concession, unless the license stipulates otherwise.

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: A lessee pays a rental of 100 dinars on a spot basis and then sublets the asset to the lessor for 110 dinars payable on a deferred basis. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible, as rent may be higher on sublease
Permissible if the deferral is under one year
Permissible if the lessor consents to it
Not permissible, as it leads to 'Inah
explanation: Per 3/4, leasing back to the owner is barred where varying rent or duration leads to 'Inah, e.g. 100 spot followed by 110 deferred.

title: Commercial Papers
q: Per the Shari'ah basis, why is an uncertified cheque not treated as possession of its amount?
options: Receiving the cheque is a sale of a debt owed by the drawee's bank
There may be no or insufficient balance to cover it
The drawer of the cheque may be a non-Muslim who deals in Riba
Cheques can never represent money in Shari'ah, whether certified or not
explanation: Per the basis, an uncertified cheque is not possession due to the probability of no or insufficient balance; possession is based on customary practice.

title: Financial Paper (Shares and Bonds)
q: Company X wants to issue a class of shares that receive profit and liquidation proceeds before ordinary shares. What is the ruling?
options: Not permissible: preference shares with financial priority
Permissible, if the priority applies only at liquidation
Permissible, if approved by the extraordinary general assembly
Permissible, if the holders pay a higher price for them
explanation: Per 2/6, preference shares with financial features giving priority at liquidation or in profit distribution are not permissible.

title: Ju’alah
q: A student asks which Sunnah report supports Ju'alah. What does the Shari'ah basis cite?
options: Al-'Abbas's conditions to his Mudarib
Al-Sa'ib Al-Makhzumi's partnership with the Prophet
Abu Sa'id Al-Khudri's Ju'l for curing a tribal chief
Umar's giving an orphan's funds for trade
explanation: The basis cites Abu Sa'id Al-Khudri's report of stipulating a Ju'l if the tribe's chief was cured through him, and the Prophet's tacit approval.

title: Gold and Its Trading Parameters in Shari’ah
q: A Rab al-Mal wants to contribute gold as the capital of a Mudharabah. What is required for this to be permissible?
options: The gold is pure and in ingot form only
Its value is set by the market price at the time of liquidation
The gold is first sold for cash and the cash contributed as the capital
Its value in the capital's currency is agreed at contract
explanation: Per 4/1, gold may be capital if valued and its monetary value in the capital's currency is determined at the contract date by mutual agreement.

title: Hawalah
q: Ahmad's creditor Bakr agreed to Zaid paying Ahmad's debt, but Ahmad himself was not asked. Per the Shari'ah basis, why is Ahmad's consent required?
options: He must approve the fee paid to Zaid for paying
He might not want a third party to pay his debt
He alone can fix the date of payment to Bakr
He must confirm the amount Zaid owes him and its due date
explanation: Per the Basis, the transferor's consent is required because he might not want a third party to pay the debt on his behalf.

title: Islamic Insurance
q: Without any intent, Ahmad misstated some information about the insured risk. A covered loss then occurs. How is his indemnity determined?
options: It is decided by the policyholders' vote
He receives full indemnity regardless
He is fully deprived of indemnity because of the misstatement
In proportion to the accurate information he gave
explanation: Per 8/1, in case of unintentional misrepresentation, the indemnity becomes proportionate to the accurate information the participant presented.

title: Possession (Qabd)
q: Bank A sells land to Company X. The parties made no stipulation on who pays the conveyancing and registration costs. How is this determined?
options: The party who registers bears them
The seller always bears them
By customary practice
They are split equally by law
explanation: Per 4/1/2, expenses of conveyancing, witnessing, instruments and registration are borne as stipulated; if there is no stipulation, customary practice is relied upon.

title: Mortgage and its Contemporary Applications
q: Through Bank A's negligence, a mortgaged machine is destroyed. What is the treatment?
options: The Bank pays its value on the date of perish; the debt remains
The debt is cancelled entirely, whatever the value of the destroyed machine
The Bank compensates the value at the contract date
The Bank owes nothing, as the asset was a trust
explanation: Per 3/2/4, on perish due to negligence the mortgagee compensates the value on the date of perish; the debt remains and the parties may set one off against the other.

title: Salam and Parallel Salam
q: A farmer owes Bank A 50,000 from a previous transaction. They agree that this debt will be the capital of a new Salam for the farmer's wheat. What is the ruling?
options: Permitted if the farmer agrees in writing
Not permitted to use a debt as Salam capital
Permitted, as the amount is known
Permitted if the debt is already due
explanation: Per 3/1/4, a debt may not be recognised as the capital of Salam, such as loans or debts owed by the seller to the Institution from previous transactions.

title: Concession Contracts
q: Company X leases land from the State and builds a hospital on it, which it must hand over to the State after 20 years. How is this contract adapted?
options: As Ijarah, the rent being the project handed over
As Salam, the hospital being the goods delivered after twenty years
As Ju'alah, the Ju'l being the hospital to be handed over later
As Istisna'a, the price being a money sum paid by the State in instalments
explanation: Per 6/2/2, if the project is built on land leased from the State against handing the project over later, it is Ijarah and the rent is the project itself.

title: Settlement of Debt by Set-Off
q: X owes Y 5,000 and Y owes X 5,000, same currency and maturity, but X's claim on Y is mortgaged to Bank B. Does compulsory set-off occur?
options: Yes, but Bank B then receives the set-off amount from Y
Yes, as the debts are equal in every respect
Yes, if X notifies Bank B in writing
No, the third party's right over the debt prevents it
explanation: Per 2/1/2(c), neither debt may be encumbered by a third party's right, such as a mortgagee's, to protect rights belonging to third parties.

title: Procrastinating Debtor
q: Bakr guaranteed Ahmad's debt on condition that payment is first sought from Ahmad. An instalment is now overdue. How should Bank A proceed?
options: Demand payment from Bakr directly
Demand payment from whichever it chooses
Demand payment from Ahmad before turning to Bakr
Treat the guarantee as void for the condition
explanation: Per 2/2(a), where the guarantor stipulated that settlement be first sought from the debtor, the creditor must start with the debtor.

title: Hiring of Persons
q: Bank A signs a framework agreement with Company X setting general conditions for hiring its consultancy services over three years. How are individual hiring operations concluded?
options: The framework agreement itself is the hiring contract for all operations
By a separate contract, or offer and acceptance, for each operation
Each operation is binding automatically once requested by Company X
Only one hiring contract is allowed under a framework agreement
explanation: Per 3/1, a framework agreement may set general conditions, but each operation needs a separate hiring contract or offer and acceptance referring to those conditions.

title: Zakah
q: Company X bought goods for trade; the goods were earmarked for it after the contract, but it has not yet possessed them by the Zakah date. Who pays Zakah on them?
options: Company X, the buyer, even before possession
Neither, until possession takes place
The seller and the buyer equally
The seller, who remains the owner of the goods until delivery takes place
explanation: Per 5/2/5, Zakah has to be paid on goods earmarked for the buyer after concluding the contract, even if he has not yet possessed them.

title: Investment Sukuk
q: Company X owns a building leased to tenants. It issues equal-value certificates to sell the building to subscribers so that they become its owners. Which type of Sukuk is this?
options: Investment agency (Wakalah) certificates
Certificates of ownership of usufructs of existing assets
Musharakah (participation) certificates
Certificates of ownership in leased assets
explanation: Per 3/1, certificates issued by the owner of a leased asset to sell it, so that holders become owners of the asset, are certificates of ownership in leased assets.

title: Hawalah
q: Bakr, the transferee, dies before collecting the transferred debt from Zaid. What happens to the Hawalah?
options: It is annulled, and Zaid is discharged
It continues only if Ahmad consents
It continues, and Bakr's heirs replace him
It is annulled, and Ahmad becomes liable again
explanation: Per 10/3, Hawalah is not annulled by the transferee's death; his heirs replace him (for an Institution, the liquidator takes its place).

title: Ju’alah
q: In a Ju'alah, the worker ('Amil) undertook not to revoke the contract during a six-month period. After two months he wants to withdraw. What is the ruling?
options: He may withdraw if he returns any advance received
He may withdraw since Ju'alah is not binding
He may withdraw if the offeror has not paid yet
He is bound to abide by his undertaking for that period
explanation: Per 4/1, if the worker undertakes not to revoke the contract during a specified period, it is binding on him to abide by the undertaking.

title: Indices
q: A trader argues that buying and selling an index is like buying shares. Per the basis, why is selling or buying an index prohibited?
options: It involves deferred delivery of shares against a deferred price
It is a sale before taking possession
It is pure gambling: selling an imaginary object
It always involves a usurious loan
explanation: The basis: selling or buying indices is paying or receiving money for a mere reading; the IIFA called it pure gambling, selling an imaginary object.

title: Zakah
q: A herder owns 150 free-grazing goats for a full year. What Zakah is due?
options: One goat
Two goats
One goat for every 40
Three goats
explanation: Per the goat table in 11/3, 40 to 120 goats require 1 goat and 121 to 200 goats require 2 goats.

title: Payment Cards
q: Bank A issues debit cards below their actual direct cost, but only to customers keeping at least 10,000 in their current account. What is the ruling?
options: Not permitted
Permitted, if disclosed in advance
Permitted, as the bank may set criteria
Permitted, as debit cards involve no lending
explanation: Per 4/1/3, offering the card must not be contingent on a set current account balance if it is issued below actual direct cost.

title: Conversion of a Conventional Bank to an Islamic Bank
q: Investors acquired Bank C to convert it. Zakah was not paid for past financial periods. Who bears Zakah for those periods?
options: No one, as conversion cancels the past Zakah
The bank's depositors, in proportion to their account balances
The new owners, for all unpaid past periods
The previous owners; the new owners from the decision date
explanation: Per 11, outsiders acquiring a bank to convert it owe no past Zakah, which is the previous owners' liability; their liability starts from the decision to convert.

title: Buyback
q: A regulator's rules oblige any bank that receives a promise to buy back an asset to accept the buyback. Is such a promise arrangement acceptable under the standard?
options: No, the promisee must not be obliged by regulation
Yes, since a regulation is not collusion
Yes, as the promise is from one party alone and the bank is not bound
Yes, if the promise is recorded in a separate deed
explanation: Per 5/1/4, the promisee must not be obligated to enter into the second contract by regulation, custom, collusion or the like.

title: Zakah
q: Bank A included a full 100 receivable in Zakatable assets; 30 of it is doubtful and covered by an allocation. What may be deducted?
options: The full 100 debt
Nothing, allocations are never deducted
The doubtful part of 30
Half the doubtful part
explanation: Per 5/3/2, when a debt is partially doubtful and an allocation is made, the doubtful part may be deducted if the total debt was initially included in Zakatable assets.

title: Investment Sukuk
q: Bank A issues Wakalah Sukuk and invests the subscription funds as investment agent. What is the status of the subscribers?
options: Owners of capital in a Mudarabah in which Bank A acts as the Mudarib
Principals who own the assets with their benefits and risks
Lenders whose funds Bank A must repay at nominal value
Creditors of Bank A entitled to a guaranteed return
explanation: Per 5/1/5/8, in Wakalah Sukuk the issuer is the investment agent and subscribers are principals who own the assets with their benefits and risks.

title: Loan (Qard)
q: During a loan, a borrower offers his lender a free ride on his animal. Per the hadith of Anas cited in the Basis, what should the lender do?
options: Accept it, since only stipulated benefits are barred and this was not stipulated
Accept it, then deduct its value from the debt when it is repaid
Not accept it, unless such practice existed before the Qard
Accept it, if he reciprocates within the same month
explanation: Per the Basis, the hadith of Anas says the lender is not to accept a gift or free ride from the borrower unless such a practice was prevalent between them before the Qard.

title: Options to Revoke Contracts Due to Incomplete Performance
q: Ahmad bought a car described as automatic but received a manual one. He dies before exercising his option to revoke for breach of description. What happens to the option?
options: It transfers to his successors
It lapses upon his death
It converts into a right to Arsh
It passes to the seller
explanation: Per 4/5, the option to revoke for breach of description can transfer to all types of successors and assignees.

title: Islamic Reinsurance
q: Islamic Insurance Company X presents an individual risk, with a summary of its information, to a reinsurer, which studies it and decides whether to accept. What method is this?
options: Excess risk reinsurance
Comprehensive reinsurance (reinsurance agreement)
Loss reinsurance
Selective reinsurance
explanation: Per 4/1, in selective reinsurance the insurer presents the individual risk with its information; the reinsurer decides whether to accept and is committed to what it accepts.

title: Mudarabah
q: Without the capital provider's consent, a Mudarib donates part of the Mudarabah funds to charity and waives a debt owed to the Mudarabah. What is the ruling?
options: The donation is allowed but not the debt waiver
Neither act is permitted for the Mudarib
Each act is permitted in an unrestricted Mudarabah
The debt waiver is allowed but not the donation
explanation: Per 9/6, the Mudarib may not make a loan, gift or charitable donation from the funds, nor waive a Mudarabah right without the capital provider's consent.

title: Zakah
q: Company X, a private firm, extracts oil it owns under a concession. Mining stops for an abnormally long period and then resumes. What applies?
options: Nisab is assessed afresh from resumption; rate 2.5%
Nisab combines output before and after; rate 10%
No Zakah, as minerals belong to the state
Rate 20% as Rikaz, with no Nisab
explanation: Per 5/5/2, minerals' Zakah rate is 2.5%; if extraction is suspended for an abnormal period, Nisab assessment starts when extraction resumes.

title: Waqf
q: Fair experts value a proposed substitute asset as generating lower revenue than the Waqf asset it would replace. May the substitution proceed?
options: Yes, if the overseer deems it wise in the Waqf's interest
Yes, if its market value is higher than the Waqf asset's
Yes, with the beneficiaries' consent
No, the substitute may not be lower in revenue
explanation: Per 10/1/5/3, the substituting asset shall not be less in value or lower in revenue than the substituted asset per fair experts.

title: Ju’alah
q: Bank A seeks guidance on a clause in an Istisna'a contract requiring the builder to maintain the building for two years. Does the Ju'alah standard cover this?
options: Yes, all maintenance obligations in any contract are a form of Ju'alah
No, maintenance stipulations in other contracts are excluded
No, because Istisna'a is a form of Ijarah for service
Yes, since the extent of the maintenance work is unknown in advance
explanation: Per clause 1, the standard does not cover maintenance contracts or maintenance stipulations in other contracts, such as in a sale or Istisna'a contract.

title: Waqf
q: The hadith "When a man dies, his acts come to an end, but three, recurring charity..." supports which ruling in the standard?
options: That self-Waqf is permissible
That Waqf upon death is a bequest
That Waqf is a recommended act
That temporary Waqf is valid
explanation: Basis 2/3: this hadith, with recurring charity understood as Waqf, is among the bases of Waqf being a recommended act.

title: Indices
q: An index provider publishes its readings at times and places it decides on the day, without prior notice. Which characteristic of a sound index is lacking?
options: Objectivity
Transparency
Accuracy
Weighting
explanation: Per 3/2, transparency entails pre-specifying the time, place and method of announcing index readings so that the process does not involve Jahalah.

title: Commercial Papers
q: In a Salam contract, the buyer wants to pay the capital (Ras al-Mal) by handing over a promissory note. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible, as the note is a certificate of debt
Permissible if the seller agrees to it
Not permissible to use the note as Salam capital
Permissible if the note is payable at sight
explanation: Per 3/2, a bill of exchange or promissory note may not be used as the counter-value for the capital (Ras al-Mal) in the contract of Salam.

title: Irrigation Partnership (Musaqat)
q: A worker knowingly worked usurped trees and is denied any pay. Which Hadith does the Shari'ah basis cite?
options: "Ill-gotten sapling shall have no right therein"
"There should be neither harm nor malice"
"The Pen has been lifted from writing the deeds of three"
"Overcharging a trusting buyer is Riba"
explanation: Per the basis, a worker aware of usurpation is a transgressor, within the Hadith "Ill-gotten sapling shall have no right therein".

title: Guarantees
q: A third party promises to cover losses in a Mudarabah bond issue but fails to pay. May the Mudarib refuse its own obligations on that ground?
options: Yes, as the promise was a contract condition
Yes, if the bonds' prospectus mentioned it
Yes, but only for the uncovered loss amount
No, the promise is independent of the Mudarabah
explanation: Per the Basis (Fiqh Academy), the third party's promise must be independent; the parties may not avoid their obligations because the volunteer failed to perform.

title: Payment Cards
q: A scholar objects that buying gold by credit card lacks immediate possession because settlement is delayed. What is the standard's answer?
options: Possession is not required for gold bought by electronic means
A settlement delay is excused by general public need and custom
Possession occurs when the amount is held for the merchant
Possession occurs only on final settlement between the banks
explanation: Basis 5/4: card payment materializes possession by holding the amount for the acceptor at the time of use; settlement delays do not affect this.

title: Syndicated Financing
q: In a Musharakah syndicate, Bank A contributes 40% and Bank B 60%; profit is agreed 30:70. The operation makes a loss. How is the loss borne?
options: 30% by Bank A and 70% by Bank B
50% by each bank equally
Entirely by the bank that manages the operation
40% by Bank A and 60% by Bank B
explanation: Per 6/2, in Musharakah the Institutions provide funds and bear losses proportionately to their contributions, whereas profits are shared as agreed.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: An Institution arranges a Shari'ah-based syndicated financing and invites conventional banks to join as partners. Under what condition is this permissible?
options: The conventional banks contribute less than half of the funding
The Institution secures the right to manage, under Shari'ah supervision
The conventional banks take over management, with Shari'ah review afterwards
The conventional banks receive a fixed return on their portion of the funds
explanation: Per 3/1/1/3, conventional banks may be included in a Shari'ah-based syndicated financing if the Institution manages it and operations are subject to Shari'ah supervision.

title: Mudarabah
q: Bank A is drafting a Mudarabah memorandum of understanding with a customer. Which item should the memorandum indicate?
options: The type of guarantees from the Mudarib for negligence or misconduct
The Mudarib's fixed fee payable in addition to his profit share
A guarantee by the Mudarib of the capital against any market loss
A fixed annual amount of profit payable to Bank A on its capital
explanation: Per 3/2, the MoU should indicate restricted or unrestricted use, the profit ratio, and the guarantees from the Mudarib to cover negligence, misconduct or breach.

title: Stipulations and Ethics of Fatwa in the Institutional Framework
q: On review, Bank A's board finds that a previous Fatwa was wrong. What must happen?
options: The board retreats only if a court so decides
The board retreats, and the Bank corrects the actions
The Fatwa stands, as Fatwas once issued cannot be reversed
Only new contracts change; past ones need no fix
explanation: Per 11/1, the board must retreat from a wrong Fatwa and inform the Institution, which must correct all actions based on it and stop adopting it.

title: Salam and Parallel Salam
q: A contract says Bank A 'buys' 100 tons of wheat of set specifications for delivery in six months, paying the full price now. The word Salam is not used. Is it a Salam?
options: No, the word Salam or Salaf must be used
Yes, but only if a master agreement exists
Yes, any term indicating such a sale suffices
No, it is an ordinary sale of goods
explanation: Per 2/2, Salam may be concluded using Salam, Salaf, sale or any term indicating sale of a prescribed commodity for deferred delivery against immediate payment.

title: Investment Sukuk
q: In the prospectus for negotiable Sukuk, the issuer undertakes to buy back any certificate offered to it after the issue. At what price may it make this undertaking?
options: At nominal value less a fixed discount
At the nominal value of the certificate
At nominal value plus any accrued profit
At the market value of the certificate
explanation: Per 5/2/2, the issuer may undertake to purchase negotiable Sukuk at market value, but not at their nominal value.

title: Conversion of a Conventional Bank to an Islamic Bank
q: Converting Bank B is entitled to receive certain prohibited non-monetary assets from a counterparty. What may it do?
options: Receive them with the intent to destroy them
Keep them in stock until a buyer appears
Use them in its own operations
Sell them and keep the price
explanation: Per 8/1/4, if the bank has rights to prohibited non-monetary assets, it may receive them with the intent to destroy them.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: Two traders form a partnership to buy goods on credit on their reputation; liability is 50:50 but profit is 70:30. Is it valid for these two ratios to differ?
options: No, the liability and profit ratios must always be equal, as profit follows liability
No, such a partnership is invalid without monetary capital
Yes, but only if the difference between the ratios is small
Yes, the liability ratio may by agreement differ from the profit ratio
explanation: Per 3/2/1, in a partnership of creditworthiness the parties set each partner's profit and liability share; the liability share may differ from the profit share.

title: Islamic Insurance
q: Ahmad, a participant in Person Insurance, dies. He also had investment balances in the scheme. How are those investment balances distributed?
options: Among his heirs per the Islamic rules of inheritance
To charity as decided by the company
To the Islamic insurance fund as a donation
To the beneficiary named in his policy documents or nominee form
explanation: Per 6/2/1/4, Islamic insurance entitlements go as per the documents and board rules, while the deceased's investment balances go to heirs by Islamic inheritance rules.

title: Ju’alah
q: Bank A pays half the Ju'l in advance for a study. The worker fails to achieve the required result. What is Bank A's right?
options: It must pay the remainder to him as reasonable wages
It may reclaim only half of the advance it paid
It may reclaim the advance, which was subject to accounts
It loses the advance, being a non-refundable fee
explanation: Per 5/3/2/4, advance compensation is 'subject to accounts'; the worker is not entitled to it without the result, and the offeror may reclaim it.

title: Hiring of Persons
q: Bank A has hired Company Y, an employee-institution, to provide IT staff support for two years. Company Y is then liquidated. What happens to the contract?
options: It continues with Company Y's liquidator
It is terminated
It is suspended until Company Y is revived
It passes automatically to Company Y's shareholders
explanation: Per 8/1/1, a hiring contract relating to the employee in person is terminated when the employee-institution encounters liquidation, bankruptcy or freezing of activities.

title: Conversion of a Conventional Bank to an Islamic Bank
q: After internal conversion, Bank B still owes interest on old borrowings, in addition to the principal. What does the standard require?
options: Pay the interest amount to charity instead of to the lender
Refuse to repay the principal as well
Avoid paying it by all lawful means, unless in dire need
Pay interest and principal as contracted
explanation: Per 9/1/1, the bank should use all lawful means to avoid paying interest (not principal) and pay interest only on the basis of dire need.

title: Controls on Gharar in Financial Transactions
q: A car showroom sells Ahmad "one of the cars in the showroom" without specifying which, and with no option to specify. What is the effect?
options: The contract is void due to non-specification of the car
The contract is valid with medium, forgivable Gharar
The contract is valid; the seller picks any car
The contract is valid if all cars have the same price
explanation: Per 5/2/1/3, sale of a non-specified car from a number of cars in a showroom involves Gharar that nullifies the contract.

title: Istisna’a and Parallel Istisna’a
q: Costs rise in Bank A's Parallel Istisna'a with a manufacturer. The Bank wants to raise the price in its Istisna'a with the customer accordingly. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible, if the rise exceeds 10%
Not permissible; the two contracts are not linked
Permissible, in proportion to the rise
Permissible, if the customer is duly notified in writing
explanation: Per 7/4, no link may be made between the two contracts; a party may not raise the price due to cost increases in the Parallel Istisna'a.

title: Competitions and Prizes
q: A telecom company runs a prize draw entered by calling a number billed above the normal tariff. What is the ruling on this draw?
options: Permissible, since no direct fee is charged
Permissible, if the prize is Shari'ah compliant
Permissible, if all callers have equal chances
Impermissible, as it is an indirect entry fee
explanation: Per 3/3/3/5, charging a fee to enter a draw, directly or indirectly (e.g., raising call rates above the normal tariff), is impermissible.

title: Agency and the Act of an Uncommissioned Agent (Fodooli)
q: Which narration does the Shari'ah basis cite from the Sunnah as evidence that agency is permissible?
options: The Prophet bought food on deferred payment from a Jew, pledging his armour
The Prophet appointed a collector of Zakah to take it from a tribe
The Prophet gave Urwah Al-Bariqi a dinar to buy a sheep
The Prophet permitted Salam in fruits for a known term
explanation: The basis cites the Hadith of Urwah Al-Bariqi, given one dinar by the Prophet to buy a sacrificial sheep, an incidence involving agency.

title: Loan (Qard)
q: A borrower cannot repay a Qard on time. The lender agrees to extend the period if the borrower adds 2% to the amount due. What is the ruling?
options: Prohibited: an excess stipulated during the delay is Riba
Permitted, as it was not stipulated at the time of the original contract
Permitted if the 2% is given to charity
Permitted, as compensation for the lender's delay
explanation: Per 4/1, a stipulated excess is Riba whether stipulated at the contract, while setting the period of delay or during the period of delay.

title: Mortgage and its Contemporary Applications
q: A mortgaged car held by Bank A is destroyed in a flood with no transgression or negligence by the Bank. What is the effect?
options: The Bank must replace the car with a similar one
The Bank bears no liability and the debt remains valid
The Bank bears the loss and the debt is cancelled
The debt is reduced by the car's value
explanation: Per 3/2/4, the mortgaged asset is a trust owned by the mortgagor; if it perishes without transgression or negligence, no liability arises and the debt remains.

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: Why does the Shari'ah basis reject making a purchase contract contingent on a lease contract?
options: It turns the lease into a loan with a benefit
It makes the rental amount uncertain for the lessee
It delays the transfer of ownership of the asset
It falls under the Hadith barring two sales in one
explanation: The basis: making purchase contracts contingent upon leasing contracts is impermissible, prohibited by the well-known Hadith barring two sales in one sale.

title: Islamic Reinsurance
q: Islamic Insurance Company X keeps all policies whose risks it can easily tolerate and reinsures only those whose risks it cannot tolerate. Which form is this?
options: Risk sharing reinsurance
Comprehensive reinsurance
Excess risk reinsurance
Loss reinsurance
explanation: Per 5/2, in excess risk reinsurance the insurer keeps policies it can tolerate and seeks reinsurance for those involving risks it cannot tolerate.

title: Distribution of Profit in Mudarabah-Based Investment Accounts
q: Bank A uses current account balances to fund its own Murabahah deals. What is the status of these balances and the Bank's use of them?
options: They are Mudarabah funds; holders share the profit
They are trusts; it may not use them at all
They are loans, but any profit earned on them must be shared with the holders
Loans it guarantees, which it may invest at its own risk and benefit
explanation: Per 2/2/1, current accounts are loans the Institution guarantees on demand; it may dispose of and invest them for its own benefit and under its own responsibility.

title: Possession (Qabd)
q: Ahmad owes Company X 10,000. At Company X's request, he deposits that amount by cheque into Company X's bank account. What is the effect?
options: It is constructive possession and Ahmad is absolved of the debt
Ahmad stays liable until Company X actually withdraws the cash amount
It counts only if the deposit is made in cash
It is valid only if Company X signs a receipt
explanation: Per 5/3, depositing an amount into a creditor's account at his demand or consent, by cash, endorsement or cheque, is constructive possession and absolves the debtor.

title: Stipulations and Ethics of Fatwa in the Institutional Framework
q: Bank A's board, of its own initiative, reviews a previous Fatwa and issues a new contrary one. What must Bank A do?
options: Keep following the old Fatwa until it expires
Follow the new Fatwa and rectify the old one's effects
Follow whichever Fatwa management prefers
Ignore the new one, as only the Bank can request review
explanation: Per 11/2, the board may review a previous Fatwa on its own or on request; the Institution follows the new one and rectifies effects of the old.

title: Documentary Credit
q: Under a credit, the bank pays the exporter 20% before documents are presented, against his undertaking to repay if goods are not shipped. What is this credit called?
options: A revocable credit amendable at any time
A back-to-back credit guaranteed by another
A red clause or advance payment credit
A transferable credit for other beneficiaries
explanation: Per 2/3/3, a red clause credit allows the bank to pay a percentage before submission of documents, against the beneficiary's undertaking to repay.

title: Buyback
q: Two banks agree to lend to each other on equal terms when either needs cash (back-to-back loans). On what basis does the standard permit this?
options: The benefit is for both, by analogy to Suftajah
It is a lend-me-and-I-lend-you condition
Each loan is treated as a gift (Hibah) from one bank to the other
It is a promise from one party alone to lend when needed
explanation: Per the Basis, the benefit accrues to both parties, not solely the lender, by analogy to Suftajah; no harm is inflicted on either.

title: Istisna’a and Parallel Istisna’a
q: On what does the Shari'ah basis ground the legitimacy of Istisna'a from the Sunnah?
options: The Prophet's purchase of a she-camel from Abu Bakr
The Hadith on paying with specified scale and weight
The practice of Umar Ibn Al-Khattab on 'Arboun
The Prophet's request to make a pulpit and a finger ring
explanation: The basis: Istisna'a's legitimacy rests on the Prophet's request that a pulpit and a finger ring be manufactured for him, plus Istihsan and Shari'ah objectives.

title: Options to Revoke Contracts Due to Incomplete Performance
q: Ahmad has taken delivery of a car and then discovers a hidden material defect. He wishes to revoke and return it. How is revocation effected?
options: Unilaterally, by giving notice to the seller
By mutual consent or a court order
Only by the seller's free choice
Automatically, upon discovery of the defect
explanation: Per 2/5, if the buyer returns the item after taking delivery, revocation is effected by mutual consent or court order; before delivery he may revoke unilaterally by notice.

title: Payment Cards
q: Ahmad cancels his new card a week after it was issued and asks Bank A to refund the issuance fee. What is the position?
options: Bank A must refund half of it
Bank A must refund it pro rata to the days left in the year
Bank A need not return any part of it
Bank A must refund it in full as the card was barely used
explanation: Per 5/2/1, if the cardholder cancels the card after its issuance, the issuer may not return any part of the issuance fees.

title: Agency and the Act of an Uncommissioned Agent (Fodooli)
q: Ahmad appoints a discriminating minor as his agent to buy goods from the market. What is the ruling?
options: Permitted only if the minor's guardian bears the commitments
Not permitted, as an agent must be an adult of full legal capacity
Permitted, with commitments shared by Ahmad and the minor in equal parts
Permitted; all contractual commitments rest solely on Ahmad
explanation: Per 3/2/1, a discriminating minor may become an agent provided that all the contractual commitments are the sole responsibility of the principal.

title: Payment Cards
q: For a lending-based credit card, which fee must not exceed the actual direct cost?
options: The fee for converting used amounts into instalments
The subscription fee paid by the issuer to the network
An ATM fee charged to other banks' cardholders
The fee the acquirer charges the card acceptor
explanation: Per 5/1/1, fees linked to the loan, incl. converting used amounts into instalments, are capped at actual direct cost; the others fall under 5/1/2.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: A partner wants to lend a large sum of partnership funds to a friend for a year. The other partners have not been asked. What is the ruling?
options: Allowed, as each partner may act for the partnership
Not allowed unless all the partners consent
Allowed if the partner later repays any loss himself
Allowed if the friend gives a mortgage as security
explanation: Per 3/1/3/1, a partner may not give out grants or loans that may damage the partnership unless all partners consent; only minor customary short-term loans are allowed.

title: Salam and Parallel Salam
q: Bank A has bought 500 tons of wheat by Salam for delivery in June. In March, it wants to sell the same wheat to a mill before receiving it. What is the ruling?
options: Permitted, as the Bank already paid
Permitted at a price not above cost
Not permitted before taking possession
Permitted if the mill pays in advance
explanation: Per 4/1, the buyer may not sell al-Muslam Fihi before taking possession of it.

title: Guarantees
q: To secure Ahmad's deferred debt, Bank A blocks an amount equal to the debt in his investment account. How is profit on the account treated?
options: The Bank keeps all the profit earned on the blocked amount as security
He earns no profit on the blocked amount
Profit accrues only on the unblocked portion
He shares profit on the whole balance, after the Mudarib's share
explanation: Per 6/5/1, freezing or blocking is allowed (blocking an equal amount is preferred), but the customer shares profit on the whole balance after the Mudarib's share.

title: Possession (Qabd)
q: A mortgaged, registered house still contains the tenant's household assets. Why does the registration still count as constructive possession?
options: The tenant becomes the mortgagee's agent by law
Custom deems registration possession, even with such assets inside
Registration transfers ownership of the house to the mortgagee by law
The household assets are part of the mortgage
explanation: Per the Basis, custom in registration countries deems registration of a mortgage as constructive possession, even if the property holds the tenant's household assets.

title: Zakah
q: Company X holds real estate prepared for trade, bought at 5 million and now expected to sell for 7 million when Zakah is due. At what value is it assessed?
options: 7 million, its expected cash (selling market) value
5 million, its historical cost, as the gain is not yet realized
The lower of cost or market value
6 million, the average of cost and market
explanation: Per 2/1/2 and 5/2/2, assets prepared for trade are assessed at their expected cash value (selling market value) when Zakah is due, not at cost.

title: Gold and Its Trading Parameters in Shari’ah
q: Gold pledged against a customer's loan is kept in safekeeping, and the fee is capped at actual expenses. What is the reason the standard gives?
options: To keep the pledge in fiduciary possession
Because the pledgee benefits from safekeeping
To ensure fairness in the depositor's absence
To avoid charging Riba in a loan contract
explanation: Per the Basis, the cap at actual safekeeping expenses for gold pledged against a loan is to avoid charging Riba in a loan contract.

title: Distribution of Profit in Mudarabah-Based Investment Accounts
q: Two parties to a Mudarabah defer setting profit ratios until profit is earned. Per the basis, why is this impermissible?
options: It leads to Jahalah, which could lead to dispute
It turns the Mudarabah into a loan with interest
It prevents covering expenses from the profit
It makes the Mudarib a guarantor of capital
explanation: Per the basis, postponing profit ratios leads to Jahalah (ignorance) which could lead to dispute; but agreeing at distribution to change ratios or donate is allowed.

title: Waqf
q: Which maxim does the standard cite on commingling Waqf incomes while observing each Waqf's allocation?
options: Custom is a decisive authority in matters without a text
Repulsion of harm precedes acquisition of interest
Certainty is not removed by doubt, so the first state remains
Hardship begets facility, so rules are relaxed in difficulty
explanation: Basis 9/9: allocation must be observed if ignoring it wastes a specified Waqf, per the maxim daf' al-mafsada muqaddam alā jalab al-maslaḥa.

title: Commercial Papers
q: Ahmad, who neither owes Bank A nor has any balance or claim against it, draws a cheque on Bank A in favour of Bilal. How is the cheque characterised with respect to Ahmad?
options: As a restricted Hawalah
As a contract of Sarf
As an unrestricted Hawalah
As a certificate of debt
explanation: Per 2/3, a cheque is a restricted Hawalah only where a debt exists between drawer and drawee; otherwise it is an unrestricted Hawalah with respect to the drawer.

title: Payment Cards
q: Ahmad uses his charge card at a store, and Bank A pays the store from its own funds. What is the amount Bank A paid?
options: A debt to be claimed from Ahmad
A liability of the store to Bank A
An investment by Bank A in the goods
A gift from Bank A to Ahmad
explanation: Per 2/2/1/2, if the issuer pays the acceptor from its own funds, the paid amount is a debt to be claimed from the cardholder.

title: Buyback
q: An Islamic fund's manager undertakes to buy back investment units from investors upon their exit from the fund. At what price is this undertaking permitted?
options: At the price the investor originally paid
At the face value of the units at issue
At the original price plus expected return
At the unit's market value at exit
explanation: Per 5/5, the fund manager may undertake to buy units on exit provided the purchase is at the market value of the unit at the time of exit.

title: Possession (Qabd)
q: Company X sells 50 tons of rice to Bank A; weighing is needed to ascertain the rice. The contract and custom are silent. Who bears the wages of weighing?
options: Both parties equally
Whoever requests the weighing
The seller, Company X
The buyer, Bank A
explanation: Per 4/1/1, expenses of delivering the sold commodity, including ascertaining it by weight or measure, are the seller's responsibility unless stipulation or custom differ.

title: Zakah
q: Company X harvests wheat twice a year and extracts minerals from a mine. Does the Hawl (Zakah year) apply to these?
options: Yes for minerals, no for the wheat
No; harvesting and extraction are what matter
Yes; a full lunar year must pass for both
Yes for the wheat, no for minerals
explanation: Per 3/2/4, no consideration is given to the Hawl for agricultural products, since harvesting matters; for minerals and Rikaz, extraction is what matters.

title: Salam and Parallel Salam
q: A Salam buyer accepts a substitute worth more than the original al-Muslam Fihi at delivery. Why does the Shari'ah basis forbid this?
options: Because substitution is never allowed in a Salam deal
Because the seller would lose his capital
Because the substitute must be the same genus
To stop the buyer making compound profit on one deal
explanation: The basis: a substitute priced above al-Muslam Fihi's market value at delivery is barred to deter the buyer from making a compound profit on one deal.

title: Revocation of Contracts by Exercise of a Cooling-Off Option
q: A seller holding a cooling-off option decides to revoke the sale when the stipulated situation occurs, but never informs the buyer. What is missing for a valid revocation?
options: Refund of a penalty for revoking the contract
Notification to the buyer as required by custom
Nothing, as the decision alone ends the contract
A court order confirming the revocation
explanation: Per 6/3, a condition of valid revocation is notification of the revocation by the option owner to the other party according to custom.

title: Indices
q: Per the basis, besides the reasons for banning index trading, why are options on indices prohibited?
options: They deal with wills and intentions, not real commodities
They are only traded in foreign markets
They require delivery of foreign currency
Their premiums are always too high compared with the index value
explanation: The basis: options on indices or on the multiplier share the reasons for banning index trading, plus the ban on options, which deal with wills, not real commodities.

title: Guarantees
q: Bakr signed his guarantee for Ahmad's Murabahah debt one week after the Murabahah contract was concluded. Is the guarantee valid?
options: No, it must be signed together with the credit contract itself
Only if it is in the same document
Yes, it may come before, with or after the credit contract
No, it must precede the credit contract
explanation: Per 3/3/3, a personal guarantee may be a separate contract, concluded together with, before, or after the credit transaction.

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: Bank A wants the right to terminate an Ijarah if the lessee fails to pay rent on time. Can it include this?
options: Yes, but only after a court ruling
Yes, it may stipulate termination for non-payment
