No, termination always requires mutual consent of both
No, only force majeure permits termination of a lease
explanation: Per 7/2/2, the lessor may stipulate that the Ijarah be terminated if the lessee does not pay the rent or fails to pay it on time.

title: Sale of Debt
q: Company X sells a debt to Company Y for a car delivered on spot, but neither party knows the amount of the debt. What is the ruling?
options: Permitted, as the car is delivered on spot
Permitted, if the debtor confirms it later
Not permitted, due to jahala of the amount
Permitted, as the debt is established
explanation: Per 5/5/2, lack of knowledge (jahala) of the amount of debt is excessive gharar, so the sale to a third party is not permitted.

title: Murabahah
q: Two partners in a Musharakah with Bank A want one to promise to buy the other's share. Which arrangement is permissible?
options: A promise at the capital originally contributed by the partner
A promise at cost plus a pre-agreed Murabahah mark-up
A promise by Murabahah, payable only on deferred terms
A promise at market price, with a new contract at the sale
explanation: Per 2/2/5, a partner may promise to buy the other's share at market price or a price agreed at the time of sale, provided a new contract is drawn up.

title: Zakah
q: Company X wants to discharge its Zakah by writing off debts owed by its poor debtors. What is the ruling?
options: Not allowed; relieving debtors does not discharge Zakah
Allowed, with the Shari'ah Board's approval
Allowed, if the debtors are eligible recipients of Zakah and cannot pay
Allowed, up to the amount of Zakah due
explanation: Per 10/1, the Zakah payer cannot discharge his Zakah by relieving his debtors, though recipients may repay debts from Zakah absent collusion or precondition.

title: Hiring of Persons
q: Bank A hires a well-defined consultancy service to be delivered in the future. Bank A then hires out an identical service to a client. What is this and is it allowed?
options: Sub-hiring, allowed only with the provider's consent
Sale of a debt, which is not allowed
Parallel hiring, and it is allowed
Two sales in one, which is not allowed
explanation: Per 5/1/3, if the hired service is specifically defined and to be delivered in the future, the employer may hire out an identical service to another (parallel hiring).

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: Bank A leases out a machine it has not yet acquired, as a specified asset. On what ground does the Shari'ah basis reject this?
options: Ijarah sells usufruct; one may not sell what he does not own
The lessee must see and inspect the asset before contracting
Ijarah is a loan of the asset, and loans need collateral
Leasing requires a master agreement to be signed first
explanation: The basis: the Hadith prohibits selling what one does not own, and Ijarah proper is a sale of usufruct.

title: Loan (Qard)
q: Which reason does the Shari'ah basis give for permitting repayment of a Qard in a land other than where it was granted?
options: Necessity overrides the prohibition of Riba
Basic rule in Mu'amalat is permissibility; no text prohibits it
Any benefit to the lender in a Qard is permitted if both parties agree
The lender's benefit from travel is considered Zakat
explanation: Per the Basis, the basic rule in transactions is permissibility; no text prohibits it, it benefits both parties without injury, and Companions' reports allow it.

title: Liability of the Investment Manager
q: Why does the standard allow a third party to commit to make up capital loss, while the same commitment by the Mudarib is barred?
options: The third party is paid a fee for bearing the risk
It is imposed by the regulator as Maslahah Mursalah
The third party acts as a fiduciary like the Mudarib
It is an undertaking to donate, not a manager's guarantee
explanation: Per the Basis, a third party's undertaking is an undertaking to donate; it does not turn into a guarantee by the investment manager.

title: Irrigation Partnership (Musaqat)
q: A Musaqat contract covers a grove of old trees that are no longer productive and cannot bear fruit. What is the status of the contract?
options: Valid, since the trees are clearly identified and owned by the contracting party
Invalid; the trees must be arable and need husbandry
Valid, but the worker gets a wage instead
Valid, if the worker's share is increased
explanation: Per 4/3, the trees must be identified, arable (productive), and in need of irrigation and plant husbandry.

title: Arbitration
q: Per the Shari'ah basis, which of the conditions applied to judges may be dropped for an arbitrator in case of necessity?
options: That the arbitrator be a Muslim
That the verdict conform to Shari'ah
That the arbitrator be non-partial
That the arbitrator have full eligibility
explanation: The basis states that in necessity some judge conditions may be dropped, such as being a Muslim, but a non-Muslim arbitrator must not issue a verdict contradicting Shari'ah.

title: Zakah
q: Bank A wants to send its Zakah from its home country to famine victims abroad. Who judges whether this transfer serves an obvious interest?
options: The board of directors of the Institution, as the governing body
The external auditor
The Shari'ah board of the Institution
The central bank, as the supervisor of the Institution
explanation: Per 10/9, Zakah funds can be transferred from the place of payment to another place due to an obvious interest judged by the Shari'ah boards of the institutions.

title: Agency and the Act of an Uncommissioned Agent (Fodooli)
q: A one-year agency is silent on new operations. In month 11, the agent enters an Ijarah whose effects run beyond the year. What is the ruling?
options: Not permitted, as its effects exceed the agency term
Permitted only with the principal's fresh consent
Not permitted in the last quarter of the term
Permitted, as it was commenced within the agency period
explanation: Per 4/4/3, unless the contract states otherwise, the agent may commence new operations during the period even if their effects succeed the period.

title: Procrastinating Debtor
q: Which Hadith does the Shari'ah basis cite for prohibiting default in payment by a debtor able to pay?
options: Muslims are bound by their contractual conditions
The best of you is the one who is best in the settlement of debt
Default in payment on the part of a solvent debtor is unjust
Take what would suffice you and your child amicably
explanation: Per the Basis, the Prophet (pbuh) said: Default in payment on the part of a solvent debtor is unjust; scholars agreed such a debtor may be punished.

title: Hiring of Persons
q: Company X proposes a hiring contract with no specified period. Per the Shari'ah basis, why must the hiring period be specified?
options: The pay cannot be fixed without a period
An unspecified period makes the employee a partner in the employer's business
Hiring is a donation contract needing a term
An unspecified period causes Gharar and leads to dispute
explanation: The basis: non-specification causes prohibited Gharar and Jahalah leading to dispute; hiring is in essence a sale of service, so must be free of Gharar.

title: Options to Terminate Due to Breach of Trust (Trust-Based Options)
q: A fruit shipment looks fresher than it really is because of unusually cool weather during transport, beyond the seller's control. Does the buyer have Khiyar al-Tadlis?
options: Yes, but only if he returns the fruit the same day
No; the deception did not result from the seller's conduct
Yes, since the buyer was misled about the condition, whatever the cause of the appearance
No, because fruit is excluded from this option
explanation: Per 3/2/1, the deception must result from the seller's conduct or instructions; if caused by circumstances beyond his control, the option is invalid.

title: Distribution of Profit in Mudarabah-Based Investment Accounts
q: Bank A wants to charge investment accounts with the expenses of its investment department and its follow-up and accounting departments. What is the ruling?
options: Not permitted; these are tasks the Mudarib must perform
Permitted, up to half of the gross profit
Permitted, as they relate to the accounts' investments
Permitted, if disclosed in the account terms
explanation: Per 3/1/2/2, investment accounts are not charged with expenses of tasks the Mudarib must perform, e.g. investment departments, follow-up and accounting departments.

title: Financial Paper (Shares and Bonds)
q: Ahmad buys shares of a permissible trading company only to benefit from short-term differences in prices, not for dividends. What is the ruling?
options: Not permissible, as it is speculation rather than genuine investment
Permissible only if bought for dividends and not for price differences
Permissible only if held for at least a year before being resold
Permissible, whether for investment or for dealing
explanation: Per 3/2, buying and selling shares of permissible corporations, spot or deferred, is permissible whether for investment or dealing to benefit from price differences.

title: Ju’alah
q: Bank A hires a collector under Ju'alah and offers him 10% of whatever debt he collects as his compensation. Is this permissible?
options: No, compensation must always be a fixed, known sum
Yes, compensation may be a portion of the object of work
No, since the amount to be collected is unknown
Yes, but only if the whole debt is finally collected
explanation: Per 5/3/2/2, compensation may be a portion of the object of work, e.g. a percentage of a debt agreed upon for collection.

title: Zakah
q: Bank A has a cash debt owed by a solvent client, payable in two years. Is Zakah due on it this year?
options: Yes, annually, whether due or not, as it will surely be paid
No, not until the debt is actually collected, since Zakah is due only on cash in hand
No, not until the debt actually falls due, since the client has no obligation to pay before then
Yes, but only on the profit portion of the debt
explanation: Per 5/3/1, Zakah is due annually on cash debts owed to the Institution, whether due or not, since it will certainly receive them.

title: ’Arboun (Earnest Money)
q: Bank A concludes an Istisna'a contract with a customer for equipment to be manufactured, and the customer pays 'Arboun at the time of contract. Is this permissible?
options: No, 'Arboun is not allowed where the item is described
Yes, but only if the 'Arboun is paid in cash, not in kind
Yes, 'Arboun is permissible in Istisna'a contracts
No, 'Arboun is limited to sales of identified goods
explanation: Per 3/1, 'Arboun is permissible in commutative contracts not requiring spot payment, such as Istisna'a, whether the item is identified or described.

title: Zakah
q: Company X's share capital and share issuance premium are shown under liabilities. Can they be deducted from Zakatable assets?
options: Yes, only the issuance premium
Yes, only the share capital
Yes, as they are sources of funding that the company owes to its shareholders
No; they are not debt obligations of the company
explanation: Per 8/2/2, the capital account and issuance premium fund the company but are not its debt obligations, so they are not deductible from Zakatable assets.

title: Conversion of a Conventional Bank to an Islamic Bank
q: Per the Shari'ah basis, why may a converting bank clear non-permissible previous transactions gradually, for necessity or need?
options: Shareholders may profit from them in the meantime
Gradual conversion is the preferred model
Clearing them all at once is not feasible
Past contracts remain valid until each one matures
explanation: Per the Basis, gradual clearance is allowed because immediate clearance of all non-permissible transactions is not feasible; the bank disposes of their effects.

title: Financial Paper (Shares and Bonds)
q: Company X has 10,000,000 shares and prohibited income of 2,000,000 for the period. Ahmad owns 50,000 shares at period-end. How much must he eliminate?
explanation: Per 3/4/6/4, total prohibited income / number of shares = 0.2 per share; multiplied by the 50,000 shares owned = 10,000.

title: Al-Wakalah Bi Al-Istithmar (Investment Agency)
q: Ahmad appoints Bank A to invest and grow his savings, and the Bank agrees to act without charging any fee. Is this an investment agency?
options: No; investment agency must always be remunerated
Yes; investment agency may be with or without a fee
No; it is a general agency to perform specific tasks
No; without a fee it automatically becomes a Mudarabah
explanation: Per 2/1, investment agency means appointing another person to invest and grow one's wealth, with or without a fee.

title: Combination of Contracts
q: In a Diminishing Musharakah set, the customer pledged to buy Bank A's units in stages. Is this pledge binding?
options: Yes, pledges in such combined sets bind their parties
Only for Bank A, not for the customer
No, pledges in combined sets are morally binding only, not legally
Only if the pledge is repeated at each stage
explanation: Per 7/3, the pledges contained in such combined contract sets are binding to their respective parties.

title: Mudarabah
q: Per the Shari'ah basis, why does a Mudarabah end on the death of the Mudarib?
options: The profit ratio becomes unknown on his death, making the contract uncertain
The capital passes to the Mudarib's heirs, who must continue the Mudarabah
The Mudarib's guarantee lapses on his death, so the capital cannot be protected
It includes agency, which ends on the agent's death
explanation: Per the basis, Mudarabah is similar to, or at least includes, agency, and an agency contract is terminable by the death of the agent.

title: Rules for Calculating Profit in Financial Transactions
q: Bank A sells a commodity in Murabahah at a 40% mark-up over cost, and the customer freely consents. Is there a maximum profit limit that makes this impermissible?
options: Yes; profit is limited to the regulator's standard rate
No upper limit, given mutual consent and the values of kindness
Yes; profit may never exceed one third of the cost price, whatever the customer's consent
Yes; profit may not exceed the market interest rate
explanation: Per 4/1, there is no upper limit for profits, provided the transaction is based on mutual consent, with due consideration for kindness, contentment and clemency.

title: Zakah
q: Bank A sets up a Zakah fund and disburses Zakah directly. Whose clearance is required for this, and what reporting is needed?
options: The board of directors', with no further report
The central bank's, with a monthly report
The Shari'ah Board's, with an annual report on disbursements
The external auditor's, with a quarterly report on the disbursements
explanation: Per 2/2/4, establishing a Zakah fund and disbursing Zakah require Shari'ah Board clearance, with a comprehensive annual report on Zakah disbursements.

title: Financial Rights and How They Are Exercised and Transferred
q: Per the basis, from which Qur'anic indication is the right of retention (lien) derived?
options: The command to fulfil all contracts
The permissibility of reciprocal treatment
The command to record debts in writing
The prohibition of consuming wealth unjustly
explanation: Per the basis, the verse 'And if you punish, then punish them with the like...' indicates reciprocal treatment, so one may retain property until receiving his rights.

title: Unilateral and Bilateral Promise
q: Under a binding bilateral promise in a supply agreement, Company X refuses to conclude the purchase. Bank A sells the goods to a third party at a lower price. What may Bank A recover?
options: Its actual loss plus the profit it expected to make
Only an injunction; it may not claim any indemnity
The full price promised, while keeping the third-party price
Its actual loss from the lower price, excluding opportunity cost
explanation: Per 4/3, the non-defaulting party may seek an injunction; if it mitigates by contracting with a third party at a lower price, the defaulter indemnifies actual loss, not opportunity cost.

title: Distribution of Profit in Mudarabah-Based Investment Accounts
q: Why is earmarking the profit of a specific portion of capital for one party prohibited, per the basis?
options: It could jeopardize profit sharing and lead to oppression
It breaches the rule on equality of investment opportunities for funds
It makes the capital unknown at the outset
It requires the Mudarib to guarantee capital
explanation: Per the basis, earmarking the profit of a specific portion of capital for one party could jeopardize the process of profit sharing and lead to oppression.

title: Salam and Parallel Salam
q: Bank A wants to issue tradable Sukuk representing its Salam receivables (the commodities owed to it by sellers before delivery). What is the ruling?
options: Permitted after half the term has passed
Permitted if the commodities owed are fungible goods
Not permitted to issue tradable Salam debt Sukuk
Permitted if the sellers consent to the transfer
explanation: Per clause 7, it is not permitted to issue tradable Sukuk based on the debt from a Salam contract (see 4/1 on selling before possession).

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: Why does the Shari'ah basis allow tangible assets, after valuation, as Sharikah capital?
options: Cash contributions would involve Riba between partners, so capital must be in kind
Tangible assets carry no risk of loss for the partners, unlike cash contributions
The Hanafi school requires capital to be tangible goods
The aim of free use of funds and profit sharing is still realised
explanation: Per the basis, Sharikah aims to let partners use the money freely and share profit, which is realisable with tangible assets as with cash (Maliki and Hanbali view).

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: A lessor dies mid-lease and his heirs want to end the Ijarah. Why may they not, per the Shari'ah basis?
options: The lessee must consent to any change
Only the lessor himself had that right, and it ended
They suffer no damage, as they receive the rentals
The lease converts into a gift to the heirs on death
explanation: The basis: the lessor's heirs may not terminate because there is no potential damage to them, as they receive the rentals for the rest of the term.

title: Irrigation Partnership (Musaqat)
q: An orchard owner stipulates in the Musaqat that the worker must also repaint the owner's house during the season. Is this permitted?
options: Yes, if the worker's share is raised to compensate him for the extra work
No; the work is restricted to husbandry of the crop and trees
Yes, if the extra work is done after the harvest
Yes, as the owner may set any terms he wishes
explanation: Per 5/2, the work should be restricted to the husbandry of the crop and trees; the owner may not demand additional work from the worker in this contract.

title: Murabahah
q: Customer C is struggling to pay a Murabahah debt. Bank A proposes a new Murabahah with C on the same commodity to refinance the old one. What is the ruling?
options: Not permitted, as it renews Murabahah on the same item
Permitted only if C is proven to be insolvent
Permitted after the Bank re-registers the commodity
Permitted if the new mark-up is lower than the old one
explanation: Per 2/2/8, it is not permitted to renew a Murabahah on the same commodity with the same customer, i.e. to refinance the transaction.

title: Istisna’a and Parallel Istisna’a
q: Midway through an Istisna'a, the ultimate purchaser demands design changes. The manufacturer refuses. Can the purchaser oblige him?
options: Yes, if the changes are minor
No, not without the manufacturer's consent
Yes, as the buyer controls the design
Yes, if he pays for the changes
explanation: Per 4/1/2, the ultimate purchaser cannot oblige the manufacturer to introduce modifications without the manufacturer's consent.

title: Zakah
q: Company X holds promissory notes from a buyer for goods sold on credit at a price including a mark-up. On what amount is Zakah paid?
options: The amount once the notes fall due
The mark-up only
The face amount, including the mark-up
The cost of the goods only
explanation: Per 5/3/4/3, Zakah is paid on the principal of the debt (amount of the paper), including the increment added to the price, whether due or not.

title: Banking Services in Islamic Banks
q: A customer asks Bank A to act as his agent in managing services for his commercial offices. On what basis may the Bank do so?
options: Only for a share of the rental income
Only as a partner in the offices
Only free of charge
For a fee or free of charge
explanation: Per 2/4/2, the Institution may act as an agent of its customers, for a fee or free of charge, in services relating to real estate and movable assets.

title: Waqf
q: A Waqf superintendent uses the Waqf's income to buy an extra building for the Waqf instead of paying beneficiaries. The Waqif set no such condition. Is this allowed?
options: No; it requires a condition stipulated by the Waqif
Yes, if the building yields higher income
Yes, with judicial approval after the fact
Yes, as it increases the Waqf's assets and its future income
explanation: Per 5/3/3, the superintendent shall not use Waqf income to increase Waqf properties, except in fulfillment of a condition stipulated by the Waqif.

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: Bank A leases a car described by accurate specifications that it does not yet own, undertaking to deliver it during the term. Must the rental be paid in advance?
options: No, and the Bank need not deliver to the specs
No, unless the lease is executed as a Salam
Yes, as in every lease of a described asset
Yes, the first year's rent must be paid upfront
explanation: Per 3/5, advance rental is not a requirement in a lease of a described asset as long as the lease is not executed according to Salam (Salaf).

title: Banking Services in Islamic Banks
q: Bank A manages a share issue for the founders of a licensed, Shari'ah-accepted company, and part of the service involves extending credit. How should its fee be set?
options: It must be waived because credit is involved
It may include a return on the credit extended
It must not include any remuneration for the credit
It must equal the interest on the credit
explanation: Per 2/3/1, the Institution may take fees as agent for the issue, but these fees should not comprise any remuneration for extending credit.

title: Mortgage and its Contemporary Applications
q: A seller in a deferred sale stipulates that he retains ownership of the sold item until the price is paid. Per the basis, why is this not allowed?
options: He willingly gave up his right to spot payment of the price
It makes the sale an adhesion contract
Ownership can pass only after full payment anyway in all deferred sales
Retention of ownership is a form of Riba
explanation: Per the basis (Hanbali view), the seller cannot retain ownership until a deferred price is paid, since he willingly relinquished his right to spot payment.

title: Credit Agreement
q: A client paid Company X for a credit study, then wants to use it with another financier. Per the Fatwa cited in the basis, may Company X refuse to hand it over?
options: Yes; the study remains Company X's confidential property
Yes, unless the client also signs a financing deal with Company X itself
No, but it may hand over only a summary of the study
No; the study is the client's once he pays, and must be handed over
explanation: Per the cited Fatwa, the study becomes the client's property once he pays its cost; it must be handed over so he can use it with Company X or any other party.

title: Islamic Reinsurance
q: What distinguishes traditional reinsurance from Islamic reinsurance, according to the definition in the standard?
options: It is formed by agreement among insurance companies
It has a fund with a distinct legal personality
It is based on exchange of premiums and compensation, not donation
It covers only part of the risks that the insurance funds may encounter
explanation: Per 2/2, Islamic reinsurance is the alternative to traditional reinsurance, which is based on exchange of reinsurance premiums and compensation rather than donation commitments.

title: Gold and Its Trading Parameters in Shari’ah
q: Several investors store serial-numbered ingots in one warehouse and have not agreed on joint ownership. One investor's ingots are stolen. Who bears the loss?
options: The investor who stored the most ingots
All the investors in equal shares
All the investors pro rata, as joint owners
That investor, as owner of his allocated ingots
explanation: Per 3/5/4, if ingots have distinguishing serial numbers, each owner owns his allocated ingots and is liable for their loss, unless joint ownership is agreed.

title: Sale of Commodities in Organized Markets
q: What is the Shari'ah basis for permitting international commodity sales that fulfil the elements and conditions of a valid sale?
options: They fall under 'Allah has permitted trading'
Custom of exchanges is sufficient by itself to validate any contract
Public need overrides the general rules of sale in international trade
International conventions bind Muslim parties as a matter of Shari'ah
explanation: Per the Basis, such sales fall within the sale that Allah permitted ('Allah has permitted trading') and trade by mutual consent.

title: Stipulations and Ethics of Fatwa in the Institutional Framework
q: The board declares a type of investment permissible. Customers read it as the board urging them to invest. What should the board make clear when necessary?
options: Permissibility applies only to Muslims
Permissibility does not amount to recommending the act
Permissibility means the act is recommended to customers
Permissibility binds the Bank to offer it
explanation: Per 8/7, it shall be made clear when necessary that declaring an act permissible by no means amounts to recommending it or calling for it.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: A Sharikah contract assigns Partner A a predetermined 50,000 of profit. The clause is never amended and a profit is realised. How is profit divided?
options: Equally among all partners per head
By a ratio chosen by the managing partner
By each partner's respective share in capital
50,000 to Partner A and the remainder to the others
explanation: Per 3/1/5/7, a predetermined amount is void; if not amended before profit comes forth, profit is divided based on each partner's share in capital.

title: Unilateral and Bilateral Promise
q: Relying on a customer's binding promise to buy, Bank A acquires an asset, but then prefers to sell it to someone else. The customer insists on buying. Who is bound?
options: Neither party, as the promise was unilateral
Only Bank A, as the party that bought the asset
Both parties, equally, once the asset is bought on the strength of the customer's promise
Only the customer; Bank A may demand performance or waive it
explanation: Per 3/5, a legally binding promise is enforceable only against the promisor; the promisee has the option either to demand performance or to waive it.

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: Bank A takes an office building on lease from a landlord, so the Bank is the lessee. Does the Ijarah standard apply to this lease?
options: Yes, but only if the lease ends with transfer of ownership
Yes, it applies to the Institution as lessor or lessee
No, it applies only to Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek leases
No, it applies only where the Institution is the lessor
explanation: Per clause 1, the standard covers operating leases and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek whether the Institution is the lessor or the lessee.

title: Mortgage and its Contemporary Applications
q: A client mortgages to Bank A a debt owed to him by Company X. How does possession of this mortgaged debt take place?
options: By possessing the debt's document or attesting the debt
Only by collecting the debt from Company X in cash
It cannot take place, as debts cannot be mortgaged
Only by Company X signing a new debt contract directly with the Bank
explanation: Per 3/2/11-3/2/12, debt may be mortgaged; possession is by possession of the debt's document or attestation of the debt when mortgaged.

title: Arbitration
q: An arbitrator has no proof either way and decides a disputed claim based on his own personal opinion. Is this an accepted method of judgment?
options: Yes, since he need not follow judicial procedure
No; he should not judge on the basis of his own opinion
Yes, if he is a recognized expert in the subject of the dispute
Yes, if the parties do not object later
explanation: Per 10/1, the arbitrator may use legally accepted methods such as confession, attestation, oath or Nukul, but should not judge on the basis of his own opinion.

title: Islamic Insurance
q: Islamic Insurance Company T charges a fee for preparing policies, collecting contributions and paying claims. How must this fee be set?
options: Stated in the agreement for the participant's approval
Decided by the company at year end according to the claims paid
Left to the market rate after each claim
Taken as a share of the insurance surplus
explanation: Per 10/1, the company performs these tasks against a specific fee stated in the agreement so the participant approves it by signing.

title: Options to Terminate Due to Breach of Trust (Trust-Based Options)
q: A seller argues that verbal deception should not allow revocation once the buyer has agreed to the price. Per the Shari'ah basis, why is revocation allowed?
options: The seller must always guarantee the market price
Revocation punishes the seller for his deception
Deception defeats mutual consent, a pillar of valid contracts
Any sale may be revoked within a customary period, without need for a ground
explanation: Per the basis, verbal deception contradicts mutual consent, a basic pillar of valid contracts, since without it the buyer would not have purchased; the same applies to Tadlis.

title: Procrastinating Debtor
q: Per the Shari'ah basis, what makes a clause accelerating all instalments upon a missed instalment valid?
options: A court orders it after the first missed instalment of the debt
The guarantor alone agrees to the clause
Prior notice is given, as a condition of validity
The debtor consented to it when the contract was agreed
explanation: Per the Basis, the Fiqh Academy allows acceleration if the debtor consented at contracting; prior notice is merely a reminder giving him reasonable time.

title: Islamic Insurance
q: Islamic Insurance Company T invests the policyholders' funds as Mudarib. Who bears the expenses normally borne by a Mudarib?
options: The company
The fund and the company equally
The policyholders fund
The participants directly
explanation: Per 10/7, when the company invests via Mudarabah it bears the expenses normally borne by the Mudarib; via investment agency, remunerated agency rules apply.

title: Sale of Debt
q: Bank A sells a USD 1,000 receivable to a third party for exactly USD 1,000 in cash. Why does the standard still prohibit this?
options: The amount of the debt is unknown
The debtor did not consent to the sale
It involves riba al-fadl due to excess
Equal amounts still involve riba al-nasi'ah
explanation: Per the Basis for 5/1, unequal amounts involve riba al-fadl and riba al-nasi'ah; equal amounts still involve riba al-nasi'ah.

title: Arbitration
q: Ahmad, appointed in person as arbitrator by Bank A, falls ill and appoints his colleague to replace him without asking the Bank. What is the ruling?
options: Allowed, if the colleague has the same qualifications
Allowed, if the other party does not object
Not allowed without the appointing party's permission
Allowed, as the arbitrator may delegate his task freely
explanation: Per 8/6, the arbitrator cannot appoint an alternate without permission of the party that appointed him, as he was accepted in person.

title: Combination of Contracts
q: A trainee asks why two lawful acts can become prohibited when combined. Which example does the basis, citing Al-Shatibi, give?
options: Combining sale with a gift of a pen
Combining sale and lending
Combining Ijarah with Wakalah
Combining Murabahah with a promise
explanation: The basis cites Al-Shatibi: combining may create restrictions absent individually, e.g. combining sale and lending, marrying two sisters, or a woman and her aunt.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: Partners hire an outside manager for a fixed salary and also set aside part of the investment profit for him as an incentive. Is this permissible?
options: No, a manager may receive either a salary or a share of profit, not both
Yes, but only if the manager also contributes capital
Yes, a fixed remuneration plus a portion of profit as incentive
No, an incentive from profit makes the salary void
explanation: Per 3/1/3/3, it is permissible to set aside a portion of the investment profit plus a fixed remuneration as an incentive for the manager.

title: Murabahah
q: Why does the Shari'ah basis prefer that the Institution appoint an agent other than the purchase orderer to acquire the item?
options: To avoid a fictitious transaction on paper
Because the customer cannot hold title
Because agency fees would be too high
Because the supplier prefers other agents
explanation: The basis: appointing someone other than the purchase orderer avoids a fictitious transaction, shows the Institution as real buyer and demarcates liabilities.

title: Debit Card, Charge Card and Credit Card
q: A charge cardholder disputes the quality of goods bought from a merchant. Does this affect the issuer's duty to pay the merchant within the card limit?
options: Yes, the obligation lapses if the goods prove to be defective
Yes, payment is suspended until the dispute ends
Yes, the issuer pays only if the holder approves
No, the issuer's obligation is direct and independent
explanation: Per 2/2/6, the issuer's obligation to pay the merchant is direct and independent of the relationship between the merchant and the cardholder.

title: Competitions and Prizes
q: Bank A sponsors a sports competition timed so that participants are unable to perform the obligatory prayer. Is sponsoring it permissible?
options: Yes, since sports competitions are permissible
No, it leads to failure to perform a Shari'ah obligation
Yes, provided no reward is paid to participants
Yes, if the Shari'ah Supervisory Board is told later
explanation: Per 2/3/1/2, a competition must not include or lead to anything prohibited, such as failure to perform a Shari'ah obligation like prayer.

title: Mudarabah
q: A Mudarib sells Mudarabah goods below the market price to a friend, with no benefit to the Mudarabah. What does the standard say?
options: He may sell at any price, being the manager of the funds
He may do so as long as the price still covers the cost
He may do so freely in an unrestricted Mudarabah
He is not entitled to sell below the common or market price
explanation: Per 9/5, the Mudarib may not sell below the common or market price unless it obviously serves an objective in the interest of the Mudarabah.

title: Unilateral and Bilateral Promise
q: Per the IIFA resolution cited in the Shari'ah basis, when can a bilateral promise be made binding on both parties?
options: Whenever the seller already owns the commodity
When a sale cannot yet be concluded and public interest requires it
Whenever both parties sign a written undertaking in the presence of two witnesses
Whenever the subject is a financing transaction
explanation: The basis cites an IIFA resolution: a bilateral promise may bind both where a sale cannot be concluded (seller not owning the commodity) and public interest obliges it.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: Per the Shari'ah basis, why may a partner not promise to buy partnership assets at face value, while a promise at market value is allowed?
options: Face value guarantees the capital; market value does not
Face value involves Riba, as it is in effect a currency exchange between partners
Face value would make the partner a Mudarib rather than a partner in the Sharikah
Market value is known at the contract date, so there is no Gharar in the promise
explanation: Per the basis, a promise to buy at face value constitutes a guarantee of capital, prohibited by Shari'ah; market value does not.

title: Gold and Its Trading Parameters in Shari’ah
q: A customer deposits gold with Bank A as collateral against a loan he borrowed. Bank A wants to charge a safekeeping fee of 2% of the gold's value. What applies?
options: Any lump sum or percentage fee is permissible
The fee must be paid in gold of equal weight
The fee may not exceed the actual safekeeping cost
No safekeeping fee may be charged at all
explanation: Per 5/4/2, safekeeping fees are permissible, but for gold deposited as collateral against the depositor's loan they may not exceed actual cost.

title: Commercial Papers
q: The drawer of a bill refuses to pay. The holder wants to claim from the endorser and the guarantor who signed the bill. What is his right?
options: Recourse only to the last endorser
Recourse to them severally or jointly
Recourse only to the drawer
Recourse only to the guarantor
explanation: Per 8/2, all who signed (drawer, endorser, guarantor) are jointly responsible; the holder may have recourse to them severally or jointly after the drawer's refusal.

title: Salam and Parallel Salam
q: A Salam contract does not state the place of delivery, and delivery at the place of contracting is possible. Where must delivery take place?
options: At the place where the contract was concluded
At a place chosen later by the seller alone
At the buyer's main warehouse, whichever town it is in
At the seller's farm, factory or place of business
explanation: Per 3/2/10, if no place is set, the place of contracting is the place of delivery; if that is impossible, it is determined by customary practice.

title: Financial Paper (Shares and Bonds)
q: Bank A invested in a compliant mixed company, but a year later its interest-based debt rose to 40% of market capitalization. What must Bank A do?
options: Keep it until its market value recovers, then sell it at once
Keep it and eliminate a larger share of the income
Keep it, as it was compliant when it was bought
Give up the investment, as the rules no longer apply
explanation: Per 3/4/8, these rules must be observed throughout the period of participation; if they cannot be applied, it is obligatory to give up the investment.

title: Competitions and Prizes
q: In a hotel loyalty program, a member lacks a few points needed for a stay, so he buys the missing points for cash. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible only if the program has no fee
Not permissible, as points cannot be bought for cash
Permissible; using them pays part of the price
Not permissible, since points are a Tabarru' only
explanation: Per 3/6/3, a member lacking points may buy new points for cash and use them, as using them is deemed payment of part of the price.

title: Hawalah
q: After a valid Hawalah, Zaid delays paying Bakr. There was no solvency condition, and Zaid is neither dead nor bankrupt. Can Bakr go back to Ahmad?
options: No, Ahmad has been discharged
Yes, for half of the transferred debt
Yes, after a formal demand on Zaid
Yes, at any time Zaid delays
explanation: Per 7/1, a valid Hawalah discharges the transferor from the debt and any claims; the transferee has no recourse against him except in stated cases.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: Which evidence does the Shari'ah basis cite for the rule that losses must be borne in proportion to capital contributions?
options: The hadith of Ibn Umar at Al-Baqi'
The hadith of Al-Sa'ib Al-Makhzumi
The saying of Ali Ibn Abu Talib
A resolution of Al Baraka Forum
explanation: The basis cites Ali Ibn Abu Talib: 'Profit distribution is according to agreement of the partners and loss must be borne in proportion to the contribution in the capital.'

title: Mortgage and its Contemporary Applications
q: Under the standard, what does it mean to mortgage an asset?
options: To transfer its ownership to the creditor until the debt is paid
To lease it to the creditor in exchange for deferring the debt
To sell it to the creditor with an option to buy it back later
To tie it to a debt so it or its value repays it on default
explanation: Per 2, to mortgage means to make a financial asset tied to a debt so that the asset or its value is used for repayment of the debt in case of default.

title: Combination of Contracts
q: Ahmad lends Karim 10,000, stipulating in the loan contract that Karim must let him stay free of charge in Karim's house. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible, if it is written in a separate contract
Not permissible: it uses the loan as an excuse for Riba
Permissible, as no extra money is repaid
Permissible, if the stay is for a short period
explanation: Per 4/3, combination must not be an excuse for Riba, e.g. a loan stipulating that the borrower offers accommodation in his house to the lender or a present.

title: Sale of Debt
q: How does the standard's basis characterize selling a debt to the debtor for a new, larger debt owed by him?
options: Riba al-jahiliyah: increase against deferment
Gharar arising from an unknown amount of the new debt
Riba al-fadl only, because the two amounts are unequal
'Inah achieved through a third party who buys the commodity
explanation: Per the Basis for 4/1/3/1, it is riba al-jahiliyah: sale of debt for a new larger debt, i.e., increase of debt against deferment.

title: Zakah
q: Company X's goods in process have no known market value on the Zakah accrual date. How may they be valued?
options: At the raw materials' purchase price only
At the value of the finished goods
At cost
At zero, as they are unfinished
explanation: Per 5/2/6/2, goods in process are valued at current market price on the day of Zakah accrual; if their market value cannot be known, they may be valued at cost.

title: Buyback
q: Bank A buys equipment from Company X; the documents state that ownership reverts to Company X automatically after one year, with no further contract. What is the ruling?
options: Permitted, if Company X pays rent for the asset meanwhile
Not permitted; the buyback needs its own contract
Permitted, as the reversion date is known and the price fixed
Permitted, if the price is paid on spot
explanation: Per 3/2, the subsequent purchase must be by an independent contract; it may not occur automatically upon lapse of a period.

title: Concession Contracts
q: Besides its own share of output, the State wants to buy additional quantities from a licensee's oil output. On what terms may it do so?
options: Only if the licensee chooses to offer them
At a price that the State fixes unilaterally below market rates
Free of charge, as a further share of output
By preemptive right at prevailing prices and contract terms
explanation: Per 5/7/2, the State has a preemptory right to buy the quantities it needs from the output at prevailing prices and contractual terms.

title: Islamic Reinsurance
q: On what basis are contributions made to an Islamic reinsurance fund out of the insurance funds?
options: On the basis of a sale of risk to the reinsurer
On the basis of donation
On the basis of exchange of premium and compensation
On the basis of Qard Hasan to the reinsurer
explanation: Per 2/1-2/2, contributions are made out of insurance funds on the basis of donation, unlike traditional reinsurance based on exchange of premiums and compensation.

title: Conversion of a Conventional Bank to an Islamic Bank
q: Converting Bank A needs liquidity from the central bank. Which approach does the standard give as an example?
options: Repurchase agreements at a fixed rate of return
Interest-bearing overnight borrowing from the central bank
Discounting commercial bills at the central bank for a fee
Opening investment accounts for the central bank
explanation: Per 4/1, the bank should adapt its dealings with the central bank for liquidity, for example by opening investment accounts for the central bank.

title: Murabahah
q: Murabahah is held analogous to a sale at the purchase price without profit, based on the Prophet's purchase of a she-camel from Abu Bakr. What is that sale called?
options: 'Inah
Bay' al-Bara'ah
Tawliyyah
'Arboun
explanation: The basis states Murabahah is analogous to Tawliyyah (sale at purchasing price without profit), as the Prophet took Abu Bakr's she-camel at its acquisition price.

title: Liability of the Investment Manager
q: Funds paid to Bank A for its general pool were never actually added to the pool, yet the pool made a profit. Why is the investor still entitled to his share?
options: He is a partner by contract; commingling isn't required
Bank A volunteered liability after the fact
The profit compensates his opportunity cost
Bank A's breach makes it guarantor of the profit, which it must pay him
explanation: Per the Basis to 7/3, the investor is a partner by virtue of the contract; pooling is not a prerequisite for profit entitlement or bearing loss.

title: Guarantees
q: A successful bidder withdraws, causing actual financial damage of 3,000 in the tender. His final cash security is 10,000. What may be confiscated?
options: The full 10,000 security, as the bidder withdrew
Half the security (5,000) as an agreed penalty
3,000, equal to the damage actually sustained
Nothing, as the security is held in trust for him
explanation: Per 6/8/1, tender securities may not be confiscated except as compensation for an equivalent amount of financial damage actually sustained.

title: Insolvency
q: After distribution of Ahmad's assets, his creditors have recovered only 60% of their debts. What is the position on the remaining 40%?
options: No legal right to demand it, but Ahmad is morally bound to pay it
Creditors may legally demand it immediately
Creditors may have him declared insolvent again to recover it
Ahmad has no obligation of any kind to pay it
explanation: Per 5/8, after distribution creditors have no legal right to demand unpaid debt, but the debtor has a moral obligation in Shari'ah to pay all debts in full.

title: Conversion of a Conventional Bank to an Islamic Bank
q: The central bank requires a cash reserve from converting Bank A. Which alternative to freezing the cash account does the standard suggest?
options: Accepting interest on the frozen reserve and giving it to charity
Buying interest-bearing treasury bills
Borrowing the reserve from another bank
Depositing receivables represented by commercial paper
explanation: Per 4/1, alternatives to the legal reserve include depositing receivables represented by commercial paper instead of freezing the cash account.

title: Banking Services in Islamic Banks
q: A board member asks why Bank A may offer services like custody and collection at all. Per the Shari'ah basis, why are such services permissible?
options: They are allowed only out of necessity for banks
They avoid interest-based lending and serve a lawful interest
They are a guarantee given by the Bank to its clients against loss
They are a form of Mudarabah between the Bank and the customer
explanation: The basis: Institutions may provide banking services not involving interest-based lending and borrowing, as they serve a permissible interest of clients.

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: Bank A wants to raise funds by signing new leases on an asset already leased to Company X for the same period. Why does the Shari'ah basis reject this?
options: The existing lessee did not approve the new lease
The rentals would become a floating amount over the period
The usufruct is already sold; this sells rent receivable
The asset would need fresh insurance for each new lessee
explanation: The basis: after the first lease, the usufruct no longer belongs to the owner; re-leasing amounts to an impermissible sale of the rent receivable.

title: Commercial Papers
q: In a currency exchange (Sarf), Company X offers to pay its side with a bill of exchange due in 30 days. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible, as a bill is a valid form of commercial paper
Permissible if the bill's due date is within thirty days
Permissible if the bill is first endorsed to the bank
Not permissible, as Sarf requires possession of counter-values
explanation: Per 3/2, bills of exchange and promissory notes may not be used in transactions requiring possession, such as counter-values in Sarf or Salam capital.

title: Syndicated Financing
q: The participants in a syndicate arrange their relationship on a Mudarabah basis. What is the role of the syndication manager?
options: He acts as Mudarib and is the exclusive operation manager
He acts as a non-paid agent who receives a fixed bonus at the end
He shares management equally with all participants in the syndicate
He acts as a guarantor of the participants' capital against all loss
explanation: Per 6/1, under Mudarabah the syndication manager acts as a Mudarib and becomes the exclusive operation manager according to the Mudarabah contract.

title: Revocation of Contracts by Exercise of a Cooling-Off Option
q: A leased asset breaks down; the lessee chooses not to revoke and repairs it. Later it breaks down again from the same cause. Can the lessee now exercise his option to revoke?
options: No, his first choice permanently waived the option
Yes, the option is not waived where harm recurs
No, because he repaired the asset at his own cost
Yes, but only with the lessor's fresh consent
explanation: Per item 9, if the harm from the cause triggering the option is recurring or continuous, the option is not waived.

title: Guarantees
q: Bakr guaranteed a 10,000 cash debt and agreed with the creditor to settle it by delivering goods worth 9,000. How much may he recover from the debtor?
options: 9,000, the lesser of the goods' value and the debt
Nothing, since he settled in kind
The goods' value plus a profit margin
10,000, the full amount of the debt originally owed
explanation: Per 3/3/2, if the guarantor settles with a different commodity, he recovers the commodity's amount or the debt's amount, whichever is less.

title: ’Arboun (Earnest Money)
q: A buyer pays 'Arboun for an orchard, and it yields fruit during the option period. The standard treats this yield as part of the sale item. What evidence supports this?
options: The saying of Shurayh on voluntary conditions
The Hadith "Al-Kharaj Bi al-Daman"
The Hadith "Gold for gold, silver for silver"
The narration of Nafi' and Safwan on the Mecca prison
explanation: The Basis attributes separate growth and yields to the sale item on the Hadith "Al-Kharaj Bi al-Daman": entitlement to revenue follows liability.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: A company plans two share classes: Class P gets priority in profit distribution and at liquidation; Class V gets only extra voting rights. Which may it issue?
options: Class P only
Neither class
Class V only
Class P and Class V
explanation: Per 4/1/2/14, preference shares with financial priority at liquidation or profit distribution are not permitted; procedural privileges such as voting are allowed.

title: Arbitration
q: A contract requires each party to appoint an arbitrator. Company X refuses to appoint its own, and the contract sets no other method. What may Bank A do?
options: Appoint Company X's arbitrator itself, as the contract is silent
Treat the arbitration clause as void
Proceed with its own arbitrator as sole arbitrator
Resort to the judiciary to appoint Company X's arbitrator
explanation: Per 8/5, if a party refrains from appointing its arbitrator, the other may resort to the judiciary for that appointment, unless the contract specifies another way.

title: Murabahah
q: On which juristic ground does the Shari'ah basis allow a defaulting debtor's undertaking to donate a sum to charity?
options: The Hanafi rule on penalty clauses
Compensation for the Bank's opportunity loss
The commitment to donate in the Maliki school
A late payment fee due to the creditor
explanation: The basis: it is an instance of the commitment to make a donation, well established in the Maliki school (Ibn Nafi' and Ibn Dinar).

title: Financial Rights and How They Are Exercised and Transferred
q: In a long-term lease, local law allows the tenant to sub-lease for payment without the owner's consent. Per the Shari'ah, may he do so?
options: Yes, if the payment does not exceed the rent
Yes, since local law permits it
Yes, if the new tenant uses it for the same purpose
No, except with the agreement of the owner
explanation: Per 8/3, in long-term leases, contrary to laws in some jurisdictions, Shari'ah does not permit sub-leasing or assigning for payment except with the owner's agreement.

title: Payment Cards
q: Ahmad holds a Bank A debit card. Which of these uses mostly involves a fee to him?
options: Withdrawing cash at another institution's ATM
Paying a local merchant in the card's currency
Withdrawing cash at Bank A's own ATM
Paying online in the card's own currency
explanation: Per 3/1/4, debit cardholders mostly bear no fees except for cash withdrawal at other institutions' ATMs or paying in another currency.

title: Settlement of Debt by Set-Off
q: Company X and Bank A agree by contract to set off their mutual debts. On what Shari'ah basis does a contractual set-off rest?
options: Custom alone determines how debts are settled between parties
Muslims are bound by the conditions they have agreed
The ruler may order mutual debts to be set off in all cases
Necessity overrides the rules on debts between the parties
explanation: Per the Basis, contractual set-off rests on the Hadith: Muslims are bound by their conditions, except one that makes the unlawful lawful or the lawful unlawful.

title: Stipulations and Ethics of Fatwa in the Institutional Framework
q: Bank A's board withholds publication of a Fatwa fearing it may be misused. Per the basis, on which principle does this rest?
options: Istihsan
Maslahah Mursalah
Sadd al-Zara`i'
Talfiq
explanation: The basis: withdrawing or not disseminating a Fatwa for fear of misuse rests on Sadd al-Zara`i', prohibiting a permissible act that leads to blight.

title: Istisna’a and Parallel Istisna’a
q: A manufacturer fulfils an Istisna'a by delivering conforming items produced by another firm before the contract. The buyer set no own-resources condition. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible, as no own-resources condition was set
Permissible only if the buyer is told first
Not permissible; the items existed beforehand
Not permissible; he must make the items himself
explanation: Per 3/1/5, the manufacturer may use items by others existing before the contract if the buyer did not stipulate own resources, but not as a device to defer both counter-values.

title: Murabahah
q: Bank A's Murabahah contract says ownership of the car stays with the Bank until the customer pays the price in full. Which alternative is permissible?
options: Keeping ownership but passing all risk
Transferring ownership only on spot payment
Retaining title until the last instalment
Postponing registration in the customer's name
explanation: Per 5/4, delaying transfer of ownership until full payment may not be stipulated, but registration in the customer's name may be postponed as a guarantee.

title: Waqf
q: Company X, a Shari'ah compliant trading company, is a Waqf. Its managers sell inventory and buy new stock in normal trading. Is this permitted?
options: No, Waqf assets may never be disposed of
Yes, asset turnover is allowed under commercial norms
Only for its real estate assets
Only with the relevant authority's approval each time
explanation: Per 2/4/14/1, Waqf companies are investment Waqfs, and their asset turnover is allowed under the regulations and commercial norms.

title: Commercial Papers
q: In a Salam contract, the buyer pays the capital (Ras al-Mal) with a banker's cheque. What is the ruling?
options: Not permissible, as Salam capital must be paid in physical cash at the session
Not permissible, as all cheques, even a banker's cheque, are deferred debts
Permissible only if it is cashed within one month
Permissible, as a banker's cheque is constructive possession
explanation: Per 7/1, a banker's or certified cheque constitutes constructive possession and may be treated as the capital (Ras al-Mal) of Salam.

title: Unilateral and Bilateral Promise
q: Bank A and Company X sign a binding bilateral promise to sell and buy a commodity, solely to provide financing; no law or custom requires it. Is it legally binding?
options: Yes; all bilateral promises are legally binding
No; it is only a religious obligation in this case
No, and fulfilling it is not even a religious duty
Yes, because both parties signed the document
explanation: Per 4/2, a bilateral promise is legally binding only where a commercial transaction is impossible without it due to law or custom, and the aim is not merely financing.

title: Online Financial Dealings
q: Bank A launches a commercial website to market its permissible Murabahah products, using impermissible advertising means to attract clients. What is the ruling?
options: Impermissible only if the website charges users a fee
Permissible, as the products themselves are fully Shari'ah-compliant
Impermissible, due to the impermissible means of promotion
Permissible, provided the contracts are concluded offline
explanation: Per 2/1, launching commercial websites is permissible unless they involve impermissible acts, such as using impermissible means to promote permissible goods and services.

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: A lessee stops using a leased office and returns the keys to Bank A without the Bank's consent, mid-term. What follows?
options: Rent remains due for the remaining period
The Bank must lease it to someone else
The lease ends on return of the keys
Rent stops, but a penalty is due
explanation: Per 7/1/7, rent continues for the remaining period and the lessor keeps the asset at the lessee's disposal, unless the lessee relinquishes the remaining period.

title: Payment Cards
q: When a card issuer pays the merchant from its own funds, even though the cardholder owes it nothing and holds no money with it, how does the Shari'ah basis classify this?
options: A loan to the merchant
A restricted novation, which is void
An absolute novation, which is permitted
A sale of debt, which is prohibited
explanation: Basis 2/2/1/2: if the issuer pays from its own funds, it is an absolute (unrestricted) novation, permitted even without a debt or funds held.

title: Gold and Its Trading Parameters in Shari’ah
q: Why may a pledgee not stipulate the right to use the pledged gold for its own benefit?
options: To avoid combining loan and sale; it would become a loan
Because the pledge must be sold at market value
Because the pledgor bears the safekeeping costs of the pledged gold
Because gold can be pledged only by certificate, not in physical form
explanation: Per the Basis, this prevents combining loan and sale in one arrangement, as it renders the pledged asset a loan the pledgee is liable for.

title: Agency and the Act of an Uncommissioned Agent (Fodooli)
q: An investment agency contract sets the agent's fee by reference to a published indicator quoted at the beginning of each quarter. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible only if the indicator is fixed for the term
Not permissible, as the fee is unknown at signing
Not permissible, as fees must be a lump sum
Permissible, as the fee will become known in the future
explanation: Per 4/2/3, the fee may be an amount to be known in the future, as when linked to an indicator quoted at the beginnings of different intervals of time.

title: Monetization (Tawarruq)
q: Ahmad buys a commodity from Bank A on deferred payment and wants to sell it to a third party immediately, before receiving it actually or constructively. What is the ruling?
options: He may sell it if the third party pays the price on spot
He may not sell it until he receives it actually or constructively
He may sell it if the Bank agrees to act as his agent
He may sell it, since he already owns it by the purchase contract
explanation: Per 4/4, the commodity shall be actually or constructively received by the buyer, with no further condition or procedure remaining for receiving it.

title: Hiring of Persons
q: A three-year hiring contract links pay after year one to a published wage index. What does the standard require for such variable pay?
options: Known first-period pay and an agreed index with limits
An index chosen by the employer alone at each new period
A fixed amount for all three years with no indexation
Approval of the regulator for the pay of each new period
explanation: Per 5/2/4, pay can be variable if the first period's pay is known and an accurate, agreed indicator with an upper and a lower limit sets later periods.

title: Payment Cards
q: Ahmad holds a charge card and asks to pay this month's purchases in instalments over a year. What does the card arrangement provide?
options: Instalments over a year if he pays a fixed monthly fee
No revolving credit; settlement is within the set period
Instalments over a year, with profit added to the balance
Instalments over a year at no extra cost if he asks the issuer
explanation: Per 3/3/3, the charge card does not provide revolving credit (instalments); the holder must settle within the specified period.

title: Sale of Commodities in Organized Markets
q: Company X enters an exchange contract for copper for a future date. Such contracts are usually closed by cash settlement or counter-contracts and rarely end in delivery. What type of contract is this?
options: A Salam contract, with full advance payment of the price
A spot contract, settled by immediate delivery and payment
An Istisna'a contract, for the manufacture of goods
A futures commodity contract
explanation: Per 2/2/3, futures contracts take effect at a future date through liquidation, cash settlement or counter-contracts, and rarely end in actual delivery and possession.

title: Agency and the Act of an Uncommissioned Agent (Fodooli)
q: An agent told to buy for cash instead buys on deferred payment, which does not serve the principal's interest. What may the principal do?
options: He must accept it, as the agent acted in good faith
He must accept it, but the agent pays any excess
Either maintain the contract or declare it invalid
He can only claim compensation, not reject it
explanation: Per 6/3/1, when the agent breaches in a way not serving the principal's interest (e.g. spot vs deferred), the principal may maintain the contract or declare it invalid.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: In a Sharikah, the customer gives a binding promise to buy all the partnership assets at liquidation. On what price basis is this promise permissible?
options: The face value of the partners' contributions
The original cost of the assets plus a fixed margin
The capital of the other partner, whatever the value
Market value or a price agreed at the date of buying
explanation: Per 3/1/6/2, a partner may promise to buy the assets at market value or as agreed at the date of buying; a promise at face value is not permissible.

title: Sale of Debt
q: After a Sukuk issuance, tangible assets fall to 40% of the entity due to a supervening event acknowledged by the Shari'ah Board. What must the Institution do?
options: Nothing, since the ratio is above 33%
Restore the ratio within a period the Board sets
Delist the Sukuk and stop all trading at once
Redeem the Sukuk at their face value
explanation: Per 8/2/3, if the ratio is lost due to a supervening event, the Institution must restore it within a period specified by the Shari'ah Board.

title: Guarantees
q: In a Murabahah, Bank A stipulates a right to freeze Ahmad's current account until the price is paid. When is such a stipulation allowed?
options: Only if he freely, willingly and absolutely agrees
Always, as the Bank's security for the debt owed to it
Only if the account balance at least equals the debt
Never, under any circumstances, even with consent
explanation: Per 6/5/2, the Institution may not stipulate freezing a current account in a credit transaction, unless the customer freely, willingly and absolutely agrees.

title: Investment Sukuk
q: A Sukuk prospectus is silent on whether it is an offer. Ahmad submits a subscription and the issuer later approves it. How is the contract formed?
options: The prospectus itself is the offer; Ahmad's subscription is the acceptance
No contract arises until the Sukuk are listed and traded
Ahmad's subscription is the offer; the issuer's approval is acceptance
The issuer's approval is the offer; Ahmad's payment is acceptance
explanation: Per 5/1/7, the prospectus is an invitation; subscription is the offer and the issuer's approval is acceptance, unless the prospectus expressly says it is an offer.

title: Options to Reconsider (Cooling-Off Options, Either-Or Options, and Options to Revoke Due to Non-Payment)
q: Ahmad holds a cooling-off option on a car already in his possession. The car is destroyed during the option period. What is Ahmad's liability?
options: He is liable to pay its price
None; the loss falls on the seller
Half the price, shared with the seller
Only its cost, if he was negligent
explanation: Per 2/5/3, if the item is destroyed in the buyer's possession while the buyer owns the option, he is liable to pay its price.

title: Mudarabah
q: Bank A gives funds as a restricted Mudarabah. Which restriction is consistent with the definition of restricted Mudarabah?
options: Requiring Bank A's staff to buy and sell jointly with the Mudarib in the market
Limiting investment to a given location or type of investment
Limiting the Mudarib to a commodity that is out of season
Requiring the Mudarib to guarantee a minimum return on the capital provided
explanation: Per 5/2, the capital provider may restrict the Mudarib to a location or type of investment, but not in a manner that unduly constrains his operations.

title: Possession (Qabd)
q: In a sale of grain, the contract expressly stipulates that the buyer will pay the measuring costs. Who bears them?
options: Both parties equally, despite the stipulation
The seller, as measuring is always his duty
The seller, as the stipulation is void
The buyer, as the stipulation must be followed
explanation: Per 4/1/1, measuring expenses fall on the seller unless there is a stipulation or customary practice to the contrary, which is then binding.

title: Protection of Capital and Investments
q: Under the standard, what is the Shari'ah ruling on protecting capital by permissible means?
options: It is merely permissible, with no preference either way in Shari'ah and no link to wealth
It is obligatory on every capital provider in every investment
It is desirable, as it serves the objectives of Shari'ah regarding wealth
It is disliked, as it conflicts with the sharing of risk and reward
explanation: Per 3/1, protecting capital by permissible means is desirable in Shari'ah as it serves the objectives of Shari'ah with regard to wealth.

title: Commercial Papers
q: Bank A collects the value of a client's bills of exchange for him. How does the standard characterise this collection?
options: As an agency, the client appointing the bank as agent
As a guarantee of the bills given by the bank to the client
As a loan by the bank to the client until the bills are collected
As a purchase of the bills by the bank itself at a discount
explanation: Per clause 5, collection of the amount of commercial papers is an agency, with the client appointing the institution as agent to collect on his behalf.

title: Credit Agreement
q: A client asks Bank A to prepare a feasibility study of his project for his own interest. When may the Bank charge the cost of the study?
options: Never, as it is part of the financing service
Only if the Bank then finances the project
When the cost of the study is agreed upon beforehand
Only if the study proves the project feasible and financeable
explanation: Per 5/3/1/5, the Institution may charge the cost of a feasibility study requested by the client for his own interest, when the cost is agreed upon beforehand.

title: ’Arboun (Earnest Money)
q: During the option period of an 'Arboun sale, the sold car is destroyed in a flood before it is delivered to the buyer. What is the outcome?
options: The buyer must pay the balance since title passed at contract
The buyer loses the 'Arboun as ownership passed to him
The loss is shared in proportion to the price already paid
The contract is void and the 'Arboun is returned to the buyer
explanation: Per item 6, the seller is liable before delivery; if the item is destroyed before delivery, the contract is void and the 'Arboun must be returned.

title: Mortgage and its Contemporary Applications
q: The verse on mortgage mentions travel. According to Ibn Al-Mundhir as quoted in the basis, why is travel mentioned?
options: It is a condition for the validity of mortgage
It is the predominant case of need, not a condition
It limits mortgage to debts in foreign lands
It shows mortgage is obligatory for travellers
explanation: Per the basis, travel is mentioned as the predominant case where mortgage is needed (lack of a scribe); it is not stipulated as a condition.

title: Controls on Gharar in Financial Transactions
q: Company Y sells a pregnant sheep to Ahmad. The condition of the fetus is unknown. What is the effect of this Gharar on the sale?
options: The sale is void as the condition of the fetus is unknown to the buyer
The sale is valid only if the fetus is excluded
The sale is valid only if the fetus is priced separately
No effect, since the fetus is a corollary (Tabi') of the sheep
explanation: Per 4/3, Gharar in a corollary (Tabi') of the primary subject matter, such as a fetus sold with the pregnant sheep, has no effect on the contract.

title: Investment Sukuk
q: Which statement must a Sukuk prospectus explicitly include regarding Shari'ah compliance?
options: That the regulator certifies the profit rate as Shari'ah-compliant at issuance
That a Shari'ah Supervisory Board approved and monitors the issue
That holders waive any claim if the project later breaches Shari'ah rules
That Shari'ah review takes place only once, at the time of the issuance
explanation: Per 5/1/8/4, the prospectus must mention the obligation to abide by Shari'ah and that a Shari'ah Supervisory Board approves the issue and monitors implementation.

title: Combination of Contracts
q: According to the majority of the Hanafi, Shafi'i and Hanbali Fuqaha cited in the basis, how is a set of combined contracts judged?
options: In the light of its individual components
By the largest contract in the set
By the intention of the stronger party
Only as a single indivisible contract
explanation: The basis: per the majority of Hanafi, Shafi'i and Hanbali Fuqaha, a combined set is judged by its components; if each is permissible, the set is too.

title: Debit Card, Charge Card and Credit Card
q: An international card organization raises its service charge to Bank A to cater for credit granted. May Bank A pay the increased charge?
options: Yes, as it is labelled a service charge
Yes, if paid in the organization's currency
No, as it would be an indirect interest payment
Yes, since membership itself is permissible
explanation: Per 4/1/2, fees to card organizations are allowed only if they include no interest, even indirectly, such as raising a service charge to cater for credit.

title: Commercial Papers
q: Per the Shari'ah basis, on which hadith does the payee bank's duty to observe the conditions of crossed and account payee cheques rest?
options: 'The delay of a rich man in paying his debt is oppression'
'Muslims abide by the conditions they stipulate'
'No harm and no reciprocal harm shall be inflicted in Islam'
'Reduce the amount of the debts to hasten the payments'
explanation: The basis relies on the generality of the hadith 'Muslims abide by the conditions they stipulate', as such conditions promote the contract's interest.

title: Irrigation Partnership (Musaqat)
q: After work began, an orchard owner claims Musaqat is non-binding and that he may cancel at will. Which Shari'ah basis supports its binding nature?
options: "O you who believe! Fulfil (your) obligations"
"No harm and no reciprocal harm" in partnerships
"Ill-gotten sapling shall have no right therein"
"Overcharging a trusting buyer is forbidden"
explanation: Per the basis, Musaqat becomes binding once entered into or undertaken under the overarching Verse "O you who believe! Fulfil (your) obligations".

title: Sale of Debt
q: Ahmad owes Bank A 100, due today. Bank A offers to cancel it in return for a new debt of 110 owed by Ahmad in six months. What is the ruling?
options: Permitted, if Ahmad requested the extension
Permitted, if the new debt is a Murabaha
Prohibited as extinction of debt in debt
Permitted, if Ahmad is solvent
explanation: Per 4/1/3/1, selling the debt to the debtor for a larger new debt is extinction of debt in debt (faskh al-dayn), prohibited by Shari'ah.

title: Options to Terminate Due to Breach of Trust (Trust-Based Options)
q: Ahmad discovers he was overcharged excessively. Instead of revoking, he and the seller agree that the seller will pay him an indemnification amount. Is this permissible?
options: No; his only remedy is revocation of the contract
Yes, but only if it equals the full excess price
No; indemnification is permitted only by court order
Yes; they may mutually agree on indemnification instead
explanation: Per 4/4/2, a buyer who accepts the contract has no right to compensation, but the parties may mutually agree upon an indemnification amount instead of revocation.

title: Zakah
q: Company X receives a government cash subsidy for farming and free use of land and equipment. What is included in its Zakah base?
options: The land and equipment only
The cash subsidy only
Both the cash and the land and equipment
Neither of them
explanation: Per 5/4/10, cash subsidies are included in the Zakah base as liquid assets, whereas free-of-charge land and equipment should not be included.

title: Obtaining and Deploying Liquidity
q: Bank A invites investors into a Musharakah to finance its working capital. The venture will use Bank A's office building. How is the building treated?
options: It is used by the venture free of charge, outside the accounts
It is valued and added to the investors' share of the capital
It is contributed as part of Bank A's share of the capital
It is lent or leased to the venture, rent being a venture expense
explanation: Per 4/2/4, the institution contributes its current assets after valuation; fixed assets are not part of the Musharakah but are lent or leased, with rent as an expense.

title: Banking Services in Islamic Banks
q: During a collection request, Bank A realizes that the operation would lead to discounting of a commercial paper. What should it do?
options: Refrain from the collection
Proceed, as the customer bears the sin
Proceed, but charge no fee
Proceed after informing the debtor
explanation: Per 2/5/4, the Institution should refrain from collection when it involves an impermissible practice or leads to discounting of a commercial paper.

title: Islamic Insurance
q: A board member asks for a fiqh precedent for the binding donation in Islamic insurance. To what is it compared in the basis?
options: Ju'alah, a reward promised for completing a task
Hawalah, the transfer of a debt from one debtor to another party
Nihd, a donation pledge among travellers sharing food
Qard Hasan, a benevolent loan
explanation: The basis measures the binding donation by analogy to Nihd (donation pledge), like travellers who pooled food and shared the leftover.

title: Protection of Capital and Investments
q: Bank A, as Mudarib, asks why no reserve deduction is taken from its own profit share. Per the Shari'ah basis, why?
options: Reserves are effectively a fee paid for the Mudarib's own work
The Mudarib's profit share is fixed by contract and cannot change
Any deduction from the Mudarib's share would amount to Riba
Liability for loss is borne by the capital providers, not the manager
explanation: Per the basis, reserves come from investors' profits with consent and in their interest; none is taken from the manager's share as loss is borne by capital providers.

title: Islamic Insurance
q: After an accident, Ahmad receives full compensation from the driver at fault. He also claims indemnity for the same injury from the Islamic insurance fund. What is the ruling?
options: He may receive the indemnity only after a year
He may receive both, as he paid contributions for this very cover
He may not receive both indemnity and compensation
He may receive both if the fund approves
explanation: Per 11/2, the participant should not receive both the indemnity and the compensation from other parties for the injury caused to him.

title: Zakah
q: A herder owns 30 free-grazing camels for a full year. What Zakah is due?
options: One Bint Labun camel (in its third year)
One Bint Makhad camel (in its second year)
Four goats
Six goats
explanation: Per the camel table in 11/1, 25 to 35 camels require one Bint Makhad camel (at the second year of age).

title: Payment Cards
q: Ahmad pays Shop X with his debit card, and Bank A pays the shop out of Ahmad's balance with it. How is this relationship characterized?
options: Ahmad novates the shop to the card issuer
Bank A guarantees the shop's sale
Bank A sells the goods to Ahmad on credit
Bank A acts as the shop's selling agent
explanation: Per 2/2/1/2, upon card usage the cardholder novates the card acceptor to the card issuer, which pays out of the cardholder's balance.

title: Banking Services in Islamic Banks
q: Bank A offers free services to current account holders, but only if they open the account on condition of receiving them. What is the ruling?
options: Not allowed for investment account holders either
Not allowed: they may not be a precondition of the account
Allowed, as free services are always permitted to all
Allowed, if the services are of small value only
explanation: Per 2/6/2, free services to current account owners may not be set as a precondition or a customary prerequisite for opening the account.

title: Guarantees
q: A claimant asks whether the standard on guarantees governs securities for compensation arising from torts. What is the position?
options: No, guarantees against torts are outside its scope
Yes, if the tort arose within a contract
Yes, it covers guarantees of every kind
No, it covers only mortgages, cheques and promissory notes
explanation: Per the Scope (1), the standard covers securities protecting debts and obligations (documents, guarantees, mortgages, cheques) but not guarantees against torts.

title: Waqf
q: Ahmad makes Waqf of his shares in Company X. The company's Memorandum of Association restricts share transfers. How is the Memorandum treated?
options: As overriding Shari'ah rulings on Waqf where they conflict
As binding on the overseer personally only
As irrelevant, since the Waqf rules override any company restrictions
As conditions of the Waqif, unless contrary to Shari'ah
explanation: Per 2/4/14/4, upon Waqf of shares, the company's Memorandum and legal framework are deemed conditions of the Waqif unless they violate Shari'ah.

title: Options to Reconsider (Cooling-Off Options, Either-Or Options, and Options to Revoke Due to Non-Payment)
q: Ahmad, holding a cooling-off option on a property, offers it for sale to third parties to test the market price. When does his option lapse?
