Paid for the part done, with no liability for the loss as he acted in good faith
Entitled to the full fee, with no liability for loss since he did useful work
explanation: Per 4/2/7, the agent gets remuneration for beneficial work done within the contract value, and must indemnify the principal for actual loss from his refusal.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: A Sharikah contract between Bank A (70% of capital) and a customer (30%) stipulates that the customer will bear all losses. What is the status of this term?
options: Not permitted: losses follow each partner's capital share
Permitted if the customer has a higher share of the profit
Permitted if the customer manages the partnership
Permitted since the customer consented to it
explanation: Per 3/1/5/4, losses must be commensurate with capital contributions; it is not permitted to hold one partner liable for the entire loss.

title: Combination of Contracts
q: Before signing, Bank A and a customer agreed a condition that was not repeated in the signed contract. How binding is it?
options: Not binding, as it is not in the contract text
As binding as the normal conditions of the contract
Binding only on the party who proposed it
Binding only if a court later confirms it
explanation: Per 6/2/3, a condition preceding the signing has the same validity and binding nature as normal contract conditions, being the agreed bases of the contract.

title: Distribution of Profit in Mudarabah-Based Investment Accounts
q: Bank A's investment accounts lost money in 2025. Bank A wants to cover the loss from 2026 profits directly. What is the ruling?
options: Allowed, as all periods form one continuing Mudarabah contract between the parties
Allowed, but only from the Mudarib's share
Not allowed, except by covering the loss from reserves
Allowed, if holders do not object
explanation: Per 3/2/1, the loss of one financial period should not be covered from the profits of another period, except in the case of covering losses from reserves.

title: Murabahah
q: Why does the Shari'ah basis forbid one Musharakah partner from promising to buy the other partner's share by Murabahah?
options: Because Murabahah requires a third party as the seller
Because shares in a Musharakah can never be sold to a partner
Because a partner may not buy anything from a partner
It makes the buyer guarantee the other's share, which is Riba
explanation: The basis: such a promise leads to the buying partner guaranteeing the share of the other partner, which is Riba.

title: Controls on Gharar in Financial Transactions
q: Company Y sells a multistory building to Bank A, excepting one floor that it retains, without specifying which floor. What is the ruling?
options: Valid; the buyer may pick the floor later
Valid; the seller may pick the floor later
Void, unless the retained floor is specified
Valid, as Gharar in an exception is forgiven
explanation: Per item 7, Bay' al-Thunya (selling property except an unspecified part) is void; it is permissible only if the retained part is specified.

title: Procrastinating Debtor
q: With no clause in the contract, Bank A sues a solvent defaulter, asking the court to award financial compensation for the delay. Is this permitted?
options: Yes, if the court sets a fair amount
Yes, if the award is in goods, not cash
Yes, since nothing was stipulated in the contract beforehand
No, a judicial demand for such compensation is barred
explanation: Per 2/1/3, it is not permitted to make a judicial demand on a defaulting debtor for financial compensation, in cash or other consideration, for delay.

title: Unilateral and Bilateral Promise
q: Bank A and a client sign a master agreement setting the process and terms for future Murabahah deals. Is the client obliged to enter into a Murabahah upon signing?
options: No; each party keeps the option to enter each deal
No, and its terms cannot apply to later deals
Yes, for at least one Murabahah transaction
Yes; the master agreement is a concluded sale
explanation: Per 4/4, a master agreement is a non-binding bilateral promise; each party has an option, and once a Murabahah is concluded its terms apply as reconfirmed in each contract.

title: Rules for Calculating Profit in Financial Transactions
q: Bank A bought goods for 1,000 and sold them in Murabahah for 1,150. In the context of the standard on calculating profit, how is the 150 described?
options: Interest: a charge for the time value of money
Profit: the amount generated in excess of the cost
Fee: consideration for the Bank's services
Rebate: an amount owed back to the customer
explanation: Per 2, profit means the amount generated in excess of the original capital or of the cost in financing and investment operations.

title: Controls on Gharar in Financial Transactions
q: Company X sells, without any option, goods it will import from abroad; it is not sure an import licence will be obtained. What is the ruling?
options: Valid if the price is paid on delivery
Valid, as medium Gharar does not affect it
Valid, since the goods exist abroad and the price is known
Void, due to Gharar relating to failure in delivery
explanation: Per 5/4, Gharar relating to failure in delivery nullifies the contract, e.g. sale without option of goods to be imported where a licence is uncertain.

title: Financial Paper (Shares and Bonds)
q: A corporation's entire assets consist of debts owed to it. Ahmad wants to trade its shares. What is required?
options: Observing the rules of Sarf only
No special rules, as shares are always tradable
Observing the rules for dealing in debts
Trading only at the nominal value of the shares
explanation: Per 3/18, shares of a corporation whose entire assets are debts may not be traded unless the rules for dealing in debts are observed.

title: Payment Cards
q: Ahmad cancels his card. Bank A cannot recover the prepaid service cost from the actual provider or reassign it. When may Bank A keep those fees?
options: Only if Ahmad used the card at least once
If this was stated in the card issuance agreement
Never; unused service fees are always refunded to the holder
Always, whatever the agreement says, as the fee is earned
explanation: Per 5/2/4, if the issuer cannot retrieve the cost or reassign the service, it may not return the fees, provided this is stated in the agreement.

title: Financial Paper (Shares and Bonds)
q: A government issues prize bonds: no interest is paid, but holders enter periodic draws for prizes. What is the ruling?
options: Prohibited, like other bonds
Permitted, as they are public bonds
Permitted, as no interest is paid
Permitted, if prizes are small
explanation: Per 4, prize bonds are also prohibited, irrespective of the bonds being private, public or governmental.

title: Credit Agreement
q: Bank A prepares the Murabahah contracts to be signed with a client; the contract is silent on who bears the cost of preparing them. Who bears it?
options: Neither party; the cost cannot be charged at all
The Bank alone, as it drafts the contracts
The client alone, as the beneficiary of the financing
The cost is shared between the Bank and the client
explanation: Per 5/3/1/4/1, the contract preparation cost is shared unless the contract says otherwise, and must be fair so it is not an implicit commitment fee.

title: Buyback
q: A Mudarib sells assets to Rab al-Maal with a promise to buy them back at the original price, effectively protecting the capital. What is the ruling?
options: Permitted, as it is a unilateral promise
Not permitted, as it guarantees the capital
Permitted, if both prices are spot prices
Permitted, if documented in a separate deed
explanation: Per 5/1/5, the promise must not come from a partner, Mudarib or investment agent in a way that leads to guaranteeing the capital or part of it.

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: Bank A buys a building from Company X and leases it back to X on Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek. When may the Bank sell the building back to X?
options: Immediately after the lease is signed by both parties
Only at the same price the Bank originally paid to X
After a reasonable period in which value could change
At any time, since the lease itself is a genuine contract
explanation: Per 8/5, a reasonable period must lapse between the lease and the sale to the lessee, long enough for the asset or its value to change, to avoid 'Inah.

title: Options to Terminate Due to Breach of Trust (Trust-Based Options)
q: A dealer paints an old car to hide its age and make it appear new, and Ahmad buys it. On discovering this, what are Ahmad's options?
options: Return the car, or keep it without compensation
Return the car only within three days of purchase
Nothing, since the dealer made no false statement
Keep the car and claim compensation for the difference
explanation: Per 3/3/2 and 3/4, painting an old car is deceptive conduct (Tadlis); the buyer may return or retain it, and gets no compensation if he retains it.

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: Why does the Shari'ah basis allow an Ijarah to take effect from a future date, even though a sale cannot?
options: Ijarah needs no specified duration
Ijarah is a contract that involves time
Rentals are paid only at the end
Ijarah is not a binding contract
explanation: The basis: unlike a sale, Ijarah is a contract that involves time, so it is relevant for it to be contingent on future events.

title: Rules for Calculating Profit in Financial Transactions
q: Bank A's regulator requires a customary accounting method for spreading profit on deferred sales over several periods. May Bank A adopt it?
options: No; all profit on a deferred sale must be booked in full at the date of the sale
Yes, whether or not the method conforms to Shari'ah rules
Yes, if Shari'ah-compliant; AAOIFI standards preferred where possible
No; only methods invented by the Bank itself may be used
explanation: Per 8/1, customary accounting practices required by regulators may be adopted if Shari'ah-compliant; AAOIFI's Accounting Standards should be adopted whenever possible.

title: Controls on Gharar in Financial Transactions
q: On what textual evidence does the standard base the prohibition of concluding a contract or making a condition that involves Gharar?
options: The Hadith that the Prophet forbade aleatory sale
The verse requiring debts for a fixed period to be written
The Hadith forbidding sale of food before holding it
The Fiqh principle that need has the status of necessity
explanation: The Shari'ah basis cites the Hadith that the Prophet (peace be upon him) has forbidden aleatory sale (Bay' al-Gharar).

title: Stipulations and Ethics of Fatwa in the Institutional Framework
q: To make matters easier, a board member picks Shari'ah exemptions from different schools so that two identical cases get different Fatwas. What is this called?
options: Maslahah Mursalah (public interest), which is required
Sadd al-Zara`i', which is permitted
Istihsan (juristic preference), which is encouraged
Talfiq (fabrication), which must be avoided
explanation: Per 8/4, exemptions must not involve acts unanimously prohibited or yield different Fatwas for identical cases; such misuse is called Talfiq.

title: Mortgage and its Contemporary Applications
q: A client defaults and fails to redeem his mortgaged asset. Per the Hadith on foreclosure cited in the basis, what follows?
options: The asset passes to the State Treasury
The mortgagee becomes owner, as was the practice
Failure to redeem does not make the mortgagee owner of the asset
The mortgagee becomes owner after one full year of continued default
explanation: Per the basis, the Hadith 'Mortgage should not be foreclosed from its owner' means failure to redeem does not entitle the mortgagee to the asset, unlike Jahiliyyah practice.

title: Gold and Its Trading Parameters in Shari’ah
q: An item is mostly non-gold metal with a minority gold content, and Bank A does not treat it as gold. Which maxim does the standard rely on for this?
options: A certificate is as good as physical possession of the gold
Gold paid as rent is in lieu of the usufruct, not of the corpus
A promise cannot be the subject of a sale or purchase contract
In ruling (Hukm), majority is tantamount to the whole
explanation: The Basis adheres to the principle of majority: in terms of ruling (Hukm), majority is tantamount to the whole.

title: Financial Rights and How They Are Exercised and Transferred
q: Omar gives his share in a co-owned house as a gift to his nephew, without consideration. The other co-owner claims Shuf'ah. What is the ruling?
options: No Shuf'ah, as the transfer was not a sale
Shuf'ah applies at a price set by the court
Shuf'ah applies at the market value of the share
Shuf'ah applies, since ownership was transferred
explanation: Per 7/2/6, there is no Shuf'ah where ownership is transferred without a sale or similar transaction, e.g. inheritance, bequest or gift without consideration.

title: Online Financial Dealings
q: A client buys gold from Bank A through the Bank's website. What is required regarding the two objects of the contract?
options: Payment may be deferred if the gold is delivered at once
Instant exchange (Taqabud) must be ascertained during the session
Delivery of gold may be deferred if the price is paid at once
Exchange may occur within any period agreed by the parties
explanation: Per 7/3, for currency, gold, silver or any commodity requiring Taqabud, instant exchange of both objects must be ascertained during the contract session.

title: Concession Contracts
q: Which hadith does the Basis cite to support giving the explorer an exclusive right?
options: 'Muslims honor all their obligations except those which permit prohibited deeds'
'A Salaf and a sale are not permitted'
'He who hires a worker must make known his wages'
'Whom who develops a piece of wasteland shall become its owner'
explanation: Per the Basis, offering the exclusive right to the explorer can be based on the hadith: 'Whom who develops a piece of wasteland shall become its owner.'

title: Waqf
q: An overseer prefers to redirect revenue of a Waqf for orphans to a mosque, as he thinks it worthier. No necessity exists. What is the ruling?
options: Not permitted without necessity and authority approval
Permitted if the Waqif's heirs agree
Permitted at the overseer's discretion
Permitted, since a mosque is also a charitable cause
explanation: Per 9/3, the avenue of Waqf disposal may not be changed unless there is a necessity, and after approval from the relevant authorities.

title: Options to Reconsider (Cooling-Off Options, Either-Or Options, and Options to Revoke Due to Non-Payment)
q: Ahmad dies holding an either-or option over three items. Per the standard and its Shari'ah basis, what happens to the option?
options: It lapses, like the option for non-payment, and the sale is cancelled
It passes to the seller, who chooses the item
It passes to his heirs, who must identify their selection
It lapses, and all items return to the seller
explanation: Per 4/3 and the basis, either-or options pass to heirs, since the deceased had established ownership in the items and the heirs need to identify their selection.

title: Islamic Reinsurance
q: In Islamic reinsurance, who owns the contributions paid in, per the basis?
options: The reinsurance company
The reinsurance account
The participants individually
The company's shareholders
explanation: Per the basis (c), in commercial reinsurance the company owns premiums, while in Islamic reinsurance the company does not own the contributions; the reinsurance account does.

title: Istisna’a and Parallel Istisna’a
q: A machine delivered under an Istisna'a does not conform to the agreed specifications. What right does the customer have?
options: To accept it or to refuse it
Only to wait until it is rebuilt
Only to demand a penalty payment
Only to accept it at the full price
explanation: Per 2/2/1, Istisna'a is binding when type, kind, quality, quantity and price are known; if the item does not conform, the customer may accept or refuse it.

title: Hiring of Persons
q: An employee receives 'Arboun when signing a hiring contract. The employer later fails to execute the contract. What is the preferred treatment of the 'Arboun?
options: It is split equally between the two parties
The employee must return all of it to the employer, with no deduction
The employee keeps all of it as profit
The employee keeps only the part covering his actual harm
explanation: Per 4/11, if the contract is not executed the 'Arboun goes to the employee, but he is preferably to take only the portion compensating his actual harm.

title: Murabahah
q: Bank A sold an asset to a customer by Murabahah without stipulating any defect exclusion. A hidden defect that existed before the sale appears after the contract. Who is responsible?
options: The customer, who accepted the asset
Nobody, since the contract is concluded
Bank A, as the seller
The supplier alone, not the Bank
explanation: Per 4/10, the Institution is responsible for pre-existing hidden defects that appear after the contract, unless it stipulated otherwise.

title: Sale of Debt
q: Bank A takes a car from an insolvent customer in place of his debt of 100, then sells the car back to him at 120 on deferred terms. What is the ruling?
options: Permitted, if the customer requested it
Prohibited, being a form of 'Inah raising the debt
Permitted, as the debtor is insolvent and Bank A took the car first
Permitted, as the car is a real commodity and the sale a real sale
explanation: Per 4/1/3/3, anything increasing the debt against longer tenure is prohibited, solvent or not, e.g., substituting a commodity and reselling it higher.

title: Istisna’a and Parallel Istisna’a
q: Bank A sells a building to a customer by Istisna'a on deferred payment, and buys it from a builder by Parallel Istisna'a on immediate payment. What is required?
options: The builder must sign the customer's contract
Both must be on the same payment terms
The two contracts must remain separate
The customer must approve the builder's price
explanation: Per 7/2, the Institution may sell on deferred terms and buy on immediate payment through Parallel Istisna'a, provided the two contracts remain separate.

title: Islamic Reinsurance
q: A traditional reinsurer offers Islamic Insurance Company X a reinsurance commission. What is the correct position?
options: X may take it and credit it to its shareholders
No commission, but it may seek premium discounts
X may take it if the Shari'ah Board approves
X may take it, as it reduces the participants' cost
explanation: Per 7/2, an Islamic insurer may not receive reinsurance commission from a traditional reinsurer, but it has the right to seek premium discounts.

title: Unilateral and Bilateral Promise
q: A shop tells Ahmad: "If you buy this sofa from me, I will give you a lamp as a gift." Ahmad buys the sofa, but the shop refuses to give the lamp. Is the promise legally binding?
options: Yes; it is conditional on Ahmad incurring a liability
No, unless the lamp's value is stated in the sale price
No; benevolent promises are only religiously binding
Yes, but only if the promise was made in writing
explanation: Per 3/6, a benevolent promise is not legally binding unless conditional on the promisee performing an act causing him to incur a liability, e.g. buying an item.

title: Protection of Capital and Investments
q: An investor required the manager to obtain Takaful cover for the investment. The manager did not, and an uninsured loss of capital occurred. Who bears the loss?
options: The investor and manager, in equal shares
The manager, but only for the lost profit
The investor, since protection is merely desirable
The manager is liable for the resulting loss of capital
explanation: Per 4/2/11, if the investor required the manager to adopt certain Shari'ah-compliant protection and he did not, he is liable for any resulting loss of capital.

title: Mortgage and its Contemporary Applications
q: How do the Hanafi scholars justify stipulating a mortgage as a condition in a sale, per the basis?
options: It transfers risk of the goods to the seller
It suits the contract because it entails contract documentation
It is a condition that serves only the seller's profit, not documentation
It is required to make any sale valid
explanation: Per the basis, the Hanafis see it as a condition that suits and conforms to the contract since it entails documentation, like stipulating the quality of the price.

title: Guarantees
q: Bakr, guarantor of a debt to Bank A, incurs actual expenses during the period of his personal guarantee. May he claim them?
options: Only if the debtor later defaults
No, a guarantee must be wholly cost-free
Only if they are below 1% of the debt
Yes, actual expenses incurred may be claimed
explanation: Per 3/1/5, no remuneration is allowed for the guarantee itself, but the guarantor may claim expenses actually incurred during the guarantee period.

title: Zakah
q: Ahmad has a long-term investment account at Bank A from which withdrawals are restricted. Must he pay Zakah on it?
options: Yes, on its balance and profits despite the restriction
No, since he cannot withdraw from the account until the term of the investment ends
Yes, but only on the profits earned in the year
No, not until the deposit term comes to an end
explanation: Per 5/1/3/2(a), account owners pay Zakah on investment balances and profits, short or long term, even if drawing from the account is restricted.

title: Guarantees
q: A notary is asked to witness and certify an interest-based loan between two companies. What is the ruling under the standard?
options: Permitted if he receives no fee for his services
Permitted if he discloses the interest rate in the certificate
Not permitted, as it is an act prohibited by Shari'ah
Permitted, as a witness does not himself take interest
explanation: Per 2/4/3, it is not permitted to scribe or witness acts prohibited by Shari'ah, such as certifying or witnessing borrowing on the basis of interest.

title: Islamic Reinsurance
q: A traditional reinsurer pays Islamic Insurance Company X the amount of insurance coverage for a large claim. May X receive it?
options: No; all amounts from traditional reinsurers are prohibited
Yes; receiving the coverage amounts is permissible
Yes, but it must be given to charity
Only after deducting the interest component
explanation: Per 7/1, it is permissible for Islamic insurance companies to receive the amounts of the insurance coverage from traditional reinsurance companies.

title: Insolvency
q: Company X asks the court to declare its own insolvency. On what basis does the standard permit this?
options: The Maliki opinion that creditors must consent first
The rule that a court may act only on the debtor's own request, never on creditors' claims
The Hanafi opinion that only the debtor may apply
The Shafi'i opinion, and his interest in stabilizing his finances
explanation: Per the basis, the debtor's right to request his own insolvency rests on the Shafi'i opinion and his interest in stabilizing his financial situation, excluding fraud.

title: Concession Contracts
q: Bank A obtains a mining concession for a share of the output and engages an operator to extract, paying it a share of output. Which form applies?
options: Parallel Ju'alah
Parallel Salam
Diminishing Musharakah
Parallel Istisna'a
explanation: Per 7/1, Ju'alah or Parallel Ju'alah may be applied in utilization concessions where the licensee receives a specific share of the output.

title: Stipulations and Ethics of Fatwa in the Institutional Framework
q: After consulting the Qur'an, Sunnah, Ijma' and Qiyas, the board finds no clear answer. What may it then consider as a basis for Fatwa?
options: The practice of conventional banks
The personal preference of the chairman
Istihsan and Maslahah Mursalah
The wishes of the Bank's management
explanation: Per 7/1, after the primary sources, the Mufti's judgment on Fuqaha views, i.e. Istihsan and Maslahah Mursalah, may be considered as a basis for Fatwa.

title: Gold and Its Trading Parameters in Shari’ah
q: A purchase orderer in Murabahah gives Bank A gold as Hamish Jiddiyyah, then breaches his binding promise. How is Bank A's deduction made?
options: Actual loss only, gold valued at the deposit date
Actual loss only, gold valued at the deduction date
The whole gold amount is forfeited as 'Arboun
The bank's expected profit, at market value
explanation: Per 7/2/1, Hamish Jiddiyyah in gold is a trust, not 'Arboun; only actual loss is deducted, with gold valued at market price at deduction.

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: Bank A is asked to lease office premises to be used as headquarters by an institution dealing in interest. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible if the rent is given to charity
Permissible if the lessee is not a Muslim
Not permissible, as the use is impermissible
Permissible, as the Bank only leases the premises
explanation: Per 5/1/1, the benefit from Ijarah must be permissible; e.g., premises may not be leased as headquarters for an institution dealing in interest.

title: Waqf
q: A Waqf deed names a committee, rather than one individual, as the overseer (nāẓir). What is the ruling?
options: Valid only if a judge approves each member
Valid only if the Waqif chairs the committee
Invalid; the overseer must be an individual
Valid; the overseer may be a group or a committee
explanation: Per 3/1, the overseer may be an individual, a group of people, a committee, a ministry or the like.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: A partner in a Muhassah partnership wants to terminate his participation unilaterally. What does the standard require?
options: Notice to the partners and no damage to partners or clients
Consent of the majority of the other partners given in a general meeting
Approval of the company's creditors and clients before he may leave
Sale of his share to an outside buyer first
explanation: Per 4/5/2/4, he may terminate if he notifies other partners and the withdrawal does not cause damage to other partners or clients of the company.

title: Waqf
q: A Waqif from a past century used an ambiguous term in his conditions. How should the overseer interpret it?
options: In light of today's customs in the place where the overseer lives
By the customs of the Waqif's own time and place
By its literal dictionary meaning, ignoring custom and usage
As the beneficiaries prefer
explanation: Per 2/6/1, each Waqif's stipulated conditions must be read in light of the prevailing customs in his time and place.

title: Obtaining and Deploying Liquidity
q: Bank A commissions a project on Istisna'a with immediate payment, then sells the same project to Company X through a second Istisna'a for deferred price and delivery. What condition applies?
options: The two Istisna'a contracts must not be linked
The two contracts must carry exactly the same price
The manufacturer must guarantee Company X's payment
The second contract must be concluded first
explanation: Per 5/4, Istisna'a and parallel Istisna'a are used to deploy liquidity without linking the two contracts.

title: Syndicated Financing
q: A syndicate is asked to finance a hotel project where one floor will house a nightclub serving alcoholic drinks. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible, as the hotel itself is lawful and the nightclub is incidental
Permissible, if the nightclub is a minor part of the whole project
Permissible, if its income is given to charity by the syndicate
Not permissible, even if only part of the funds go to it
explanation: Per clause 3, syndicated financing must go to permissible activities and should not be totally or partially directed to projects with a Shari'ah restriction.

title: Credit Agreement
q: On what basis may an Institution charge a fee for preparing a credit study for a client?
options: The fee compensates the Institution for reserving the facility
The fee is a guarantee return for assessing the client's risk
The study is a remunerable service apart from the financing contract
The study is part of the financing and its cost is priced in the profit margin
explanation: Per the Shari'ah basis, the credit study as such can constitute a remunerable service apart from the financing contract.

title: Protection of Capital and Investments
q: Which of the following is listed by the standard as a permissible method of protecting capital?
options: Conventional futures, options and swaps
The manager's commitment to buy assets at nominal price
A third-party guarantee of the capital against loss, given in return for a fee
A sale with an option to terminate for non-payment (Khiyar al-Naqd)
explanation: Per 4/2/9, a sale with Khiyar al-Naqd is a permissible method; fee-based guarantees, conventional hedging and nominal-price commitments are prohibited under 5.

title: Debit Card, Charge Card and Credit Card
q: A charge cardholder uses his card to pay for things prohibited by the Shari'ah. Which right must Bank A have stipulated when issuing the card?
options: The right to charge interest on such purchases
The right to double the annual membership fee
The right to withdraw the card for this violation
The right to cancel its payment to the merchant
explanation: Per 3/2/3, the Institution must stipulate that the card may not be used for prohibited purposes and that it may withdraw the card if this is violated.

title: Payment Cards
q: In a lending-based card, why may the cardholder not bear the fees the acquirer deducts from the card acceptor?
options: Part goes to the issuer as lender: a loan with benefit
These fees are gharar for the holder as they are unknown
The card network's rules forbid passing them on to holders
The acceptor is the true borrower, so the fee is its cost
explanation: Basis 5/1/2/1: part of these fees goes to the lender (issuer), so making the holder bear them makes it a loan carrying benefit.

title: Sale of Debt
q: Company X holds a bill of exchange due in six months and wants Bank A to pay it now at less than its face value. What is the ruling?
options: Permitted, as a sale of debt to a third party
Not permitted to discount it before maturity
Permitted, if the drawer consents
Permitted, if the discount is modest
explanation: Per 9/1/2, it is not permitted to discount a negotiable instrument, settling it to its beneficiary before maturity for less than its value.

title: Insolvency
q: What is the Shari'ah basis for the obligatory ruling of declaring insolvency and interdiction against a debtor whose debts exceed what he can pay?
options: The Prophet's interdiction of Mu'adh Ibn Jabal and sale of his property
The principle that the deferred period has a share in the price
The Hadith that a sold item found with the buyer reverts to the seller
The Maliki opinion on the three stages of insolvency
explanation: Per the Shari'ah basis, the Prophet (peace be upon him) interdicted Mu'adh Ibn Jabal, sold his property and distributed it among his creditors; this is the majority view.

title: Debit Card, Charge Card and Credit Card
q: Bank A plans a card letting holders pay off purchases in instalments, paying interest for the deferment on a revolving basis. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible if a free credit period comes first
It is not permissible to issue such a card
Permissible if the interest is disclosed upfront
Permissible if issued only to its own depositors
explanation: Per 3/3, an Institution may not issue credit cards with an interest-bearing revolving credit facility where the holder pays interest to pay in instalments.

title: Islamic Insurance
q: Per the basis, why does an insurance policy expire at the end of its stipulated period?
options: The company's agency is non-binding
It is a donation that may be withdrawn
The surplus must be distributed yearly
It is a time-specific contract, like Ijarah
explanation: The basis: the insurance contract is time-specific and expires at the end of its period like Ijarah, and on damage of the property as no object remains.

title: Hawalah
q: Bank A's operations team asks whether the Hawalah standard governs all of the bank's banking remittances. What is the position?
options: It excludes remittances in every case
It covers every type of banking remittance
It covers only remittances taking the form of Hawalah
It covers only remittances made in a currency other than the original
explanation: Per the Scope (1), the standard covers Hawalah involving a change of debtor and excludes banking remittances except those taking the form of Hawalah.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: Ahmad contributes 60% and Bilal 40% of the capital of a Sharikat al-'Inan. They agreed to share profit 50:50. The venture loses 100,000. How is the loss borne?
options: Ahmad bears the whole loss as the larger partner
Each partner bears 50,000 as agreed for profit
Bilal bears 60,000 since he takes a larger profit ratio
Ahmad bears 60,000 and Bilal bears 40,000
explanation: Per 3/1 and 3/1/5/4, profit follows the agreement but losses are borne according to each partner's contribution to the capital.

title: Insolvency
q: After revocation of his first insolvency, Ahmad buys on credit, acquires property through new transactions and is declared insolvent again. What are the first-insolvency creditors entitled to?
options: Priority over the creditors of the second insolvency
No share in the assets of the second insolvency
A share only if the second insolvency is within a year
A pro-rata share alongside the new creditors
explanation: Per 10/3, creditors of the first insolvency are not entitled to share assets of the second insolvency acquired through new transactions (unlike gifts).

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: Sara did not stipulate that she would be a sleeping partner. In fact she did no work, but the agreement gives her profit above her capital share. Is she entitled?
options: No, profit must always match each partner's capital contribution
Yes, but only if she also bears extra losses
Yes, she may stipulate extra profit though she did not work
No, extra profit requires actual work by the partner herself
explanation: Per 3/1/5/3, a partner who did not stipulate being a sleeping partner is entitled to stipulate an additional profit share even if he did not work.

title: Hawalah
q: One of the three parties to a proposed Hawalah lacks legal competence to act independently. What is the effect?
options: The Hawalah is not valid
It is valid if the other two consent
It is valid if the debt is small
It is valid as an unrestricted Hawalah
explanation: Per 6/4, it is a condition that all parties to a Hawalah be legally competent to act independently.

title: Payment Cards
q: Why must a covered card agreement state the issuer is not obliged to lower financing instalments?
options: Lowering instalments is riba, since it changes the price
It protects the card network from the issuer's discount claims
Discounts on financing instalments are always prohibited
An obligation would make the instalments unknown
explanation: Basis 6/2(b): an obligation would make the instalments (the consideration) unknown; it keeps discounts at the issuer's choice without custom.

title: Hiring of Persons
q: Bank A hired a specific, identified service. The service then becomes completely useless. What is the status of the contract?
options: The employee must deliver a similar service
The employer may only claim a discount
The contract becomes null and void
The contract continues and pay remains due
explanation: Per 8/2/1, in specific hiring, when the service becomes completely useless the contract becomes null and void; if partially useless, the employer may terminate.

title: Documentary Credit
q: In brief, how does the standard describe a documentary credit?
options: A bank's undertaking to pay subject to inspecting the goods on arrival at port
A bank's undertaking to pay against conforming documents
A bank's loan to the buyer to settle the price of the goods
A bank's purchase of the goods for resale to the buyer later
explanation: Per 2/1, in brief, a documentary credit is an undertaking by a bank to pay subject to conformity of the documents to the contractual instructions.

title: Guarantees
q: Bank A is asked for a letter of guarantee to back an interest-based loan. Per the Shari'ah basis, why is issuing it prohibited?
options: It aids sin, as the guarantor helps establish the Riba debt
Letters of guarantee are void in all cases under the Shari'ah
The Bank would earn a fee on the guarantee
Guarantees may only cover Murabahah debts
explanation: Per the Basis, it is like assisting in sin; the Hadith cursing the writer and witnesses of Riba applies, as a guarantor has a stronger role than they do.

title: Murabahah
q: Bank A buys goods directly from Supplier S without any agent. The supplier prepares the sale documents in the purchase orderer's name. Is this proper?
options: Yes, either name is equally acceptable
No, the documents should be in the Bank's name
Yes, as the customer will own the goods later
Yes, if the customer signed a promise
explanation: Per 3/1/6, all documents for the sale must be in the Institution's name, not the customer's, unless the customer acts as the Institution's agent.

title: Waqf
q: Ahmad makes Waqf of his share in a jointly owned plot. His partner then takes the share under pre-emption (shuf'a) rights and pays its price. What must Ahmad do?
options: Deploy the price received in a similar type of Waqf
Refuse, as pre-emption cannot apply to a share already made Waqf
Nothing; the Waqf ends and he keeps the price paid by the partner
Give the price to the partner's heirs
explanation: Per 2/4/5/3, Waqf of an asset subject to pre-emption is valid; if it goes to the pre-emptor, the Waqif must deploy the consideration in a similar Waqf.

title: Liability of the Investment Manager
q: A third party commits to make good Rab Al Maal's capital loss, with a right to recover whatever it pays from the investment manager. Is this commitment valid?
options: Yes, if recourse is limited to half the amount
Yes, if the commitment is made voluntarily
Yes, since the third party is independent of both the investor and the manager
No, the obligor must have no recourse to the manager
explanation: Per 4/1/2, the obligor shall have no recourse to the investment manager for what it has undertaken.

title: ’Arboun (Earnest Money)
q: A seller under an 'Arboun sale of an identified car wants to deliver a different car with exactly the same specifications. When may he do so?
options: Never, even if the buyer consents to the substitute
Only if he first refunds the 'Arboun to the buyer
Only with the buyer's consent, and the payment stays 'Arboun
Freely, since the substitute has the same specifications
explanation: Per 9/2, the seller cannot deliver a different item, even of the same specifications, except with the buyer's consent; what was paid remains 'Arboun.

title: Distribution of Profit in Mudarabah-Based Investment Accounts
q: A Mudarabah term makes the Mudarib bear all losses. Which statement does the basis cite against such a term?
options: The Hadith on discounts for calamities
The Hadith of the merchant who profits only after preserving his capital
The IIFA resolution that deposits are loans
Ali's saying: profit as agreed, loss per capital contribution
explanation: Per the basis, Ali Ibn Abu Talib said profit is distributed as agreed, while loss is borne per capital ratios; charging one party with the other's loss is oppressive.

title: Mudarabah
q: A Mudarib hires a worker to perform tasks that, by custom, any similar fund manager does himself. Who pays the worker's wages?
options: The Mudarib, from his own personal funds
The Mudarabah funds, as an operating expense
The capital provider, from his profit share
The Mudarabah funds, then deducted at liquidation
explanation: Per 9/4, work customarily done by a fund manager is part of the Mudarib's duties; if he hires someone for it, wages come from his personal funds.

title: Agency and the Act of an Uncommissioned Agent (Fodooli)
q: Under an absolute agency to sell goods, the agent sells them on deferred payment without asking the principal. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible, since the agency was absolute
Permissible, if the deferred price is above market price
Not permissible without the principal's prior consent
Permissible, as long as the buyer provides a guarantee
explanation: Per 4/1/2, in absolute agency barter and deferred payment sales are not permissible except with the prior consent of the principal.

title: Conversion of a Conventional Bank to an Islamic Bank
q: Converting Bank A's articles of association include objectives that contradict the nature of Islamic banking. What must be done?
options: Keep them unchanged until the next renewal of its licence
Amend the by-laws and cleanse them of anything contrary
Add a Shari'ah clause overriding them
Disclose them in the annual report only
explanation: Per 3/2, by-laws must be amended through the required procedures to include objectives suited to Islamic banking and cleansed of anything contradicting it.

title: Stipulations and Ethics of Fatwa in the Institutional Framework
q: Bank A asks about one product; the board's Fatwa also clarifies a related point not asked. Which Hadith does the basis cite to justify this?
options: Seawater is pure and sea carcasses are permissible
Muslims are bound by their conditions
Whoever cheats is not one of us
Make things easier not harder, as cited for choosing the easier ruling
explanation: The basis cites the Prophet's reply on seawater for Wudu`: "Seawater is pure and sea carcasses are permissible", giving more than asked.

title: Syndicated Financing
q: The lead bank of a syndicated Musharakah asks participants to pay it a commitment commission. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible if disclosed to all participants before they subscribe
It is not permissible to receive commitment commission
Permissible if paid only by the customer and not by the partners
Permissible if it does not exceed the actual cost of the commitment
explanation: Per 7/2, it is not permissible to receive commitment commission.

title: Salam and Parallel Salam
q: Bank A pays the full Salam capital at signing and agrees that the rice will be delivered in four instalments on four different dates. What is the ruling?
options: Not permissible; there must be one delivery date
Permissible only if the capital is also split
Permissible only for goods sold by number
Permissible, as the capital was paid at conclusion
explanation: Per 3/2/9, there is no objection to setting various delivery dates in instalments, provided the capital was paid at the time the contract was concluded.

title: Irrigation Partnership (Musaqat)
q: During a Musaqat, the trees under contract die from disease and can no longer bear fruit. What happens to the contract?
options: The worker must replant the trees
It continues until the term expires
It terminates
It converts into an Ijarah of the land
explanation: Per 12/4, the Musaqat contract terminates upon the death of the trees or their inability to bear fruit.

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: A customer paid Bank A a security deposit for his promise to lease. When the lease contract is executed, what may the parties agree about this deposit?
options: That the Bank keeps it as a fee for arranging the lease
To treat it as an advance payment of rentals
That it becomes 'Arboun owned by the Bank on execution
That it is held until the end of the lease term
explanation: Per 2/4, it is permissible to agree, upon execution of the lease, that the deposit shall be treated as an advance payment of the lease rental instalments.

title: Guarantees
q: In a debtor's liquidation, whose claims for the cost of services provided in the liquidation process have priority over other creditors?
options: The guarantors of the debtor, as they back its debts
The unsecured trade creditors of the debtor company
The shareholders of the debtor, as its owners
The parties in charge of the liquidation
explanation: Per 6/9/4, in bankruptcy or liquidation, those in charge of the liquidation have priority over other creditors for the cost of services they provide.

title: Al-Wakalah Bi Al-Istithmar (Investment Agency)
q: An investment agency contract with Bank A is silent on any fee. Bank A customarily charges fees for such services, as is normal practice. What is Bank A entitled to?
options: The fee prevalent in the relevant markets
A share of the profit as if a Mudarib
Nothing, since no fee was stipulated
Whatever fee Bank A unilaterally sets
explanation: Per 5/2, if the fee was not specified and the agent customarily charges a fee, it is entitled to the fee prevalent in the relevant markets.

title: Concession Contracts
q: The State provides land to Bank A to utilize on a set profit-sharing ratio, and Bank A engages an operator on a similar basis. Which form is this?
options: Parallel Salam
Parallel Istisna'a
Two-step Mudarabah
Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
explanation: Per 7/3, Mudarabah may apply where the State provides land on a predetermined profit-sharing rate; Institutions may act directly or through two-step Mudarabah.

title: Mortgage and its Contemporary Applications
q: A mortgaged asset is sold on default for 70 against a debt of 100 owed to Bank A. What is the status of the shortfall of 30?
options: It becomes a debt only if the mortgagor agrees
It is extinguished, as the mortgage has been executed
It is borne by the notary who held the asset
It remains a normal debt with recourse on the mortgagor
explanation: Per 3/4/1, if the sale value is less than the due debt, the difference is subject to the rulings on normal debt, with recourse on the mortgagor.

title: Agency and the Act of an Uncommissioned Agent (Fodooli)
q: In a paid procurement agency, Bank A's contract with its agent states that the agent shall bear transport, storage and insurance costs of the goods. What is the ruling?
options: Permitted, as the agent is paid a fee that is meant to cover such costs
Not permitted: these expenses are for the principal to bear
Permitted, if the costs are deducted from the fee he is paid for the agency
Permitted only for costs arising after delivery of the goods to the Bank
explanation: Per 5/1/1, in procurement agency the principal bears the price and expenses; in paid agency these may not be stated as payable by the agent.

title: Financial Paper (Shares and Bonds)
q: Shares of a goods-trading company may be traded even though more than half of its assets are cash and debts. Which principle supports this, per the Basis?
options: The secondary is subservient to the primary
Necessity permits what is prohibited
Gains are based on the bearing of costs
What can be sold can be mortgaged
explanation: Per the Basis, cash and debts are secondary to the main activity; the secondary is subservient, as in the hadith on selling a slave who has wealth.

title: Rules for Calculating Profit in Financial Transactions
q: Bank A wants to state the profit in its Murabahah contracts as 5% of the cost price rather than as a lump sum. Is this permissible?
options: Yes, but only if linked to an index benchmark
No; profit must always be a fixed lump sum, since a percentage makes the price unknown
Yes; profit may be a fixed amount or a percentage of cost
No; profit must be a percentage of the sale price
explanation: Per 6/1, Murabahah profit may be stipulated as a fixed amount added to the cost price or as a percentage of the cost price.

title: Conversion of a Conventional Bank to an Islamic Bank
q: Bank B decides on a gradual, partial conversion over ten years instead of an immediate comprehensive one. Can it be licensed as an Islamic bank meanwhile?
options: No, not until the conversion process is completed
Yes, once it announces its conversion plan
Yes, once a Shari'ah board is appointed
Yes, once half of its assets have been converted to Islamic ones
explanation: Per 2/2, a bank adopting gradual or partial conversion is not regarded as converted and may not be licensed as Islamic until conversion is completed.

title: Hiring of Persons
q: A fishing company hires a crew and agrees to pay them 10% of the catch as their pay. What is the ruling on this form of pay?
options: Impermissible, as it turns hiring into Mudarabah
Permissible; pay can be a percentage of the output
Impermissible, since the pay is unknown at signing
Permissible only with a minimum fixed wage
explanation: Per 5/2/6, the pay can be determined as a percentage of the output (e.g., 10%) or as a part of the thing to be made.

title: Salam and Parallel Salam
q: After the delivery date, a Salam seller offers barley instead of the agreed wheat; no such swap was stipulated. On what condition may Bank A accept it?
options: The barley must be of the same genus as the wheat
The barley must be worth more than the wheat sold
The barley must not be worth more than the wheat
The swap must have been stipulated in the contract
explanation: Per 4/2, after the due date the buyer may take other goods (not currency) if not stipulated, if suitable as al-Muslam Fihi and not worth more than it.

title: Sale of Debt
q: In a new Murabaha with an indebted customer, the documents require him to sell the commodity on to a third party at once. Is this consistent with the standard?
options: Yes, if the third party buyer is not Bank A or its affiliate
Yes, if he is a solvent debtor
Yes, since constructive delivery suffices to complete the Murabaha
No, he must be free to keep it, with no duty to sell
explanation: Per 4/1/3/4(b), the customer is entitled to take delivery, retain ownership and dispose of the item as he deems fit, with no obligation to sell.

title: Murabahah
q: A customer defaults on Murabahah instalments that are due, and no donation undertaking exists in the contract. What may Bank A claim?
options: Only the unpaid amount of the selling price
The unpaid price plus a delay charge
The whole price including future instalments
The unpaid price plus its funding cost
explanation: Per 5/8, on default the amount due is just the unpaid selling price; the Institution may not impose any additional payment for its own benefit.

title: Payment Cards
q: On a lending-based card, Bank A adds a lounge access feature and raises the card fee for it. How far may the fee be raised?
options: To any level agreed with the cardholder
Not at all; features must be free
Not beyond the actual cost of the feature
To double the actual cost of the feature
explanation: Per 5/6/2, in the case of a lending-based card, it is not permitted to increase its fees beyond the actual cost of such features.

title: Hawalah
q: A holder offers to transfer a bill of exchange to Bank A before its due date in return for immediate payment of a discounted amount. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible if Bank A is the drawee
Not permissible, as it is a form of Riba
Permissible if the discount is small
Permissible as a successive Hawalah
explanation: Per 12/5/4, discounting bills of exchange by transferring their value before maturity for a discounted immediate payment is not permissible: it is Riba.

title: Agency and the Act of an Uncommissioned Agent (Fodooli)
q: Per the Shari'ah basis, why is the agent treated as a trustee rather than a guarantor of the asset he holds?
options: He has no right to dispose of the asset except by the owner's order
He receives no fee in most agency contracts, so he bears no liability
The principal can revoke the agency at any time before the sale
He works in the principal's interest and was trusted by him
explanation: The basis: the agent works for the principal's interest, trusteeship is normal in such engagements, and choosing him shows the principal's good faith.

title: Possession (Qabd)
q: In a Salam contract, Bank A is the buyer (Rab al-Salam). Absent contrary stipulation or custom, how are the delivery expenses allocated?
options: Bank A bears delivery of both the goods and the capital
Seller bears delivery of both the goods and the capital
Seller: delivery of goods; Bank A: delivery of the capital
Each party bears half of all delivery expenses of the contract
explanation: Per 4/1/4, in Salam the seller bears the expenses of delivering the Salam commodity and the Rab al-Salam bears those of delivering the capital (Ras al-Mal).

title: Combination of Contracts
q: Per the Maliki Fuqaha cited in the basis, which requirement applies before using Sadd al-Zara`i' to bar a Muwata`ah?
options: Resort to the excuse is very frequent and excessive
The deal involves more than two contracting parties
The deal is concluded through a paid agent of either party
The deal is concluded for a single lump sum price
explanation: The basis: per the Maliki Fuqaha, Sadd al-Zara`i' needs very frequent, excessive resort to the excuse and a strong accusation ruling out good intention.

title: Zakah
q: The regulator requires Bank A to keep a legal deposit for its licence; the Bank can neither withdraw nor invest it. It is refunded after five years. What Zakah is due?
options: Zakah every year as it is owned
Zakah for one year, at the time of refund
No Zakah, as it was restricted
Zakah for all five years, due at the time of refund of the deposit
explanation: Per 5/3/4/8, if the Institution was not enabled to invest the legal deposit, it pays Zakah on it for only one year at the time of refund.

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: Bank A argues that, since local law treats its Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek as an instalment sale, the lessee should bear major maintenance. Is this acceptable?
options: Yes, if the rentals resemble sale instalments
Yes, as the lessee will become the owner
Yes, local law governs the parties' duties
No, the rules of Ijarah still fully apply
explanation: Per 8/6, Ijarah rules apply to Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek and may not be breached because local laws or conventional practice treat it as an instalment sale.

title: Distribution of Profit in Mudarabah-Based Investment Accounts
q: A client deposits a large quantity of banknotes over the counter, while another transfers the same amount electronically to the Bank's account. For which deposit may a handling fee be charged?
options: Only the banknotes deposit, for transport, storage and counting
Only the electronic transfer, for the processing and communication costs it involves
Each of the two deposits, at the same rate
Neither deposit, as all deposit fees are prohibited
explanation: Per 2/2/5, the Institution may charge a fee for transportation, storage and counting of cash handed to the cashier; this does not include amounts transferred to it.

title: Irrigation Partnership (Musaqat)
q: A Musaqat worker becomes unable to work for a reason within his control, and the owner revokes the contract. What is the outcome?
options: He gets a market wage and owes nothing
He gets his full share and owes nothing
He gets a market wage but indemnifies actual loss
He gets nothing and must indemnify the owner for the actual loss he suffered
explanation: Per 13/2/1/2, he gets a market wage for the period worked but must indemnify the owner for actual loss suffered, as determined by experts.

title: Murabahah
q: Bank A's promise form, signed by the customer, makes the promise binding on both the Bank and the customer with no option to cancel. Is this acceptable?
options: Yes, as it protects both parties equally
No, a promise binding on both parties is not permissible
Yes, if the Shari'ah Supervisory Board approves the form
Yes, if Hamish Jiddiyyah is taken from the customer
explanation: Per 2/3/1, the promise document may not include a bilateral promise binding on both the Institution and the customer.

title: Online Financial Dealings
q: Bank A's website requires a client to confirm acceptance after clicking the acceptance icon. The client clicks the icon but never confirms. Is there acceptance?
options: Yes; clicking the acceptance icon is acceptance in all cases
No, unless the Bank has already delivered the item
Yes, but the client has an option to rescind within three days
No; acceptance needs the required confirmation
explanation: Per 5/4, clicking the icon is acceptance if no confirmation is required; if the system requires confirmation, acceptance occurs only on confirmation.

title: Distribution of Profit in Mudarabah-Based Investment Accounts
q: To attract customers, Bank A offers to pay a small variable increment on current account balances in addition to full repayment. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible, as it is variable and not fixed in advance, so it is not usurious interest
Permissible, if it is paid from shareholders' profit
Impermissible, as such increment constitutes usurious interest
Permissible, if it is called a gift in the account terms
explanation: Per 2/2/2, the Institution must guarantee current accounts but must not commit to any fixed or variable increment on them, as that constitutes usurious interest.

title: Waqf
q: A Waqf residential building earns little. The superintendent wants to convert it into a commercial building. Which of the following is a condition for this?
options: Approval of the Waqif's heirs
That the Waqif stipulated conversion
Unanimous consent of all beneficiaries
Permission of the concerned authorities
explanation: Per 5/2/5, changing the operational form is allowed if it meets demand, generates more income and is done with the permission of the concerned authorities.

title: Loan (Qard)
q: Ahmad lends 100 kg of ordinary wheat on condition that the borrower returns 100 kg of premium-grade wheat. What is the ruling?
options: Permitted if the borrower agrees in writing
Prohibited: a stipulated excess in quality is Riba
Permitted, since wheat is not a currency
Permitted, as the quantity of wheat returned is exactly the same
explanation: Per 4/1, stipulating an excess for the lender is Riba, whether the excess is in quality or quantity, tangible or a benefit.

title: Ju’alah
q: A Ju'alah offers 'a suitable reward' with no amount stated. The worker achieves the result. What is due?
options: Reasonable compensation becomes binding
Whatever amount the worker demands
Whatever amount the offeror chooses
Nothing, as the contract is void
explanation: Per 5/3/2/1, compensation must be known, lawful and deliverable; if unknown, unlawful or not deliverable, payment of reasonable compensation becomes binding.

title: Payment Cards
q: Ahmad paid a yearly fee for lounge access services on his card, available since issuance. He cancels after four months. What may Bank A stipulate?
options: Refunding the whole yearly fee, since the lounge was never used
Retaining half, regardless of time
Retaining the whole yearly fee, since services were available
Retaining that fee pro rata for the four months
explanation: Per 5/2/2, the issuer may stipulate retaining fees for services other than issuance on a proportionate basis up to cancellation.

title: Gold and Its Trading Parameters in Shari’ah
q: A customer buys gold jewelry from a shop for currency, paying half the price now and half next month. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible, if the full price is agreed now and secured by a pledge
Not permissible; both must be delivered at the session
Permissible, since jewelry is not pure gold and is sold as a commodity
Permissible, since used jewelry is not Ribawi
explanation: Per 3/2/1, in a sale of gold for currencies both countervalues must be delivered at the session, for gold of all purities, used or unused.

title: Hiring of Persons
q: Company X hires Ahmad to do a specific job himself. Ahmad passes the job to an assistant without any contract clause permitting this. What is the ruling?
options: Not allowed; he must do it himself unless the contract allows
Allowed if Ahmad pays the assistant out of his own pay
Allowed, as only the end result matters to the employer
Allowed if the assistant is equally qualified for the job
explanation: Per 7/1/2, the employee is in principle to do the work himself unless the contract stipulates otherwise; for future defined services only the specifications matter.

title: Syndicated Financing
q: Bank A's syndicate finances the power plant of a project via Istisna'a, while other banks finance the rest with interest-based loans. What is the ruling?
options: Not permitted, as the whole project is tainted by Riba, even with separation
Permitted if Bank A shares the conventional lenders' risk
Permitted if accounts and lead manager arrangements are separate
Permitted only if Bank A also leads the conventional loans for the project
explanation: Per 5/5, Institutions may finance parts of a project financed conventionally elsewhere, if accounts and lead manager arrangements of both are separate.

title: Possession (Qabd)
q: Bank A holds a bill of lading in its name, but it does not identify any specific goods, and Bank A cannot transact in them. Is this constructive possession?
options: Yes; holding any bill of lading is always possession
No; documents can never amount to possession
Yes, as long as the bill is issued in Bank A's name
No; ascertainment and ability to transact are required
explanation: Per 3/5, documents are constructive possession of what they represent only if goods are ascertained through them and the possessor is able to transact in them.

title: Sale of Commodities in Organized Markets
q: Bank A will pay a commodity's purchase price only if its agent guarantees that the end buyer will pay the deferred sale price. What is the ruling?
options: Prohibited: payment may not be contingent on such a guarantee
Permitted, if the guarantee is given by a third person, not the agent
Permitted, if the agent receives an extra fee
Permitted, as it protects Bank A's funds
explanation: Per 4/2/11, the institution may not make payment of the purchase price contingent on the agent guaranteeing the sale price himself or through another person.

title: Banking Services in Islamic Banks
q: Bank A rents a safe deposit vault within its premises to a customer against a set fee. On what contract is this based?
options: Wadi'ah, as the Bank owns the stored items
Ijarah, entitling the customer to the vault's usufruct
Kafalah, as the Bank guarantees the items
Qard, as the customer lends the stored items to the Bank for a fee
explanation: Per 2/7/1, leasing safe deposit vaults is based on an Ijarah (hiring) contract that entitles the customer to the vault's usufruct.

title: Possession (Qabd)
q: In a Sarf contract, Bank A exchanges US dollars for euros with Company X. What form of possession is stipulated?
options: Constructive possession through a promise to deliver later
Delivery of the two currencies at any time agreed by the parties
Reciprocal delivery within the contract session, on a spot basis
Delivery of one currency now and the other within a week
explanation: Per 3/7, reciprocal possession in Sarf is delivery and acceptance of delivery within the session of the contract on a spot basis (Yadan bi Yadin).

title: Online Financial Dealings
q: Ahmad buys a car online based on a description and a model shown on the website. On delivery the car differs from the description. What may he do?
options: He has no option, as he did not see the car itself
He must accept it and claim only the price difference
He may only terminate and cannot keep the car
Choose to conclude, terminate, or negotiate a settlement
explanation: Per 8/4, if the delivered object differs from the description, prior sight or model, the buyer may conclude, terminate or negotiate appropriate settlement.

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: Bank A and Company X sign a master agreement setting general terms for many future Ijarah transactions. How may each individual lease then be concluded?
options: Only by signing a new master agreement for each asset
Only by a separate signed lease document, never by offer and acceptance
By a separate contract, or by offer and acceptance under it
By the master agreement alone, with no further contract or step
explanation: Per 2/2, under a master agreement each lease may be a separate signed contract, or the parties may exchange offer and acceptance referring to its terms.

title: Competitions and Prizes
q: A student claims that foot races between people have no precedent in the Sunnah. Which narration cited in the standard's basis answers this?
options: Anas's narration on the she-camel al-Adhbaa'
Ayishah racing the Prophet on foot
Ibn Umar's narration on racing slender horses
Abu Hurairah's Hadith on camel and horse races
explanation: The Basis cites Ayishah: she raced the Prophet on foot and won, later he won and said: "this for that".

title: Payment Cards
q: A Qard Hasan card charges issuance, renewal and cash withdrawal fees. Under which condition is issuing it permitted?
options: Its loan-linked fees may not exceed actual direct cost
Fees may be set freely by agreement between issuer and holder
Fees must be fully waived for all users, as Qard Hasan is free
Fees must be paid by the merchant only
explanation: Per 6/1/2 with 5/1/1, a Qard Hasan card with fees is permitted provided its fees observe 5/1, so loan-linked fees stay within actual direct cost.

title: Waqf
q: Ahmad declares his orchard a Waqf but does not name any beneficiary. What is the ruling?
options: Valid, and its revenue goes to Ahmad's heirs by default
Suspended until Ahmad names a beneficiary
Valid; the overseer or court directs it to charity
Void, as the beneficiary must be specified when the Waqf is created
explanation: Per 2/4/1/6, an unrestricted Waqf is valid and is made available for charitable causes as deemed fit by the overseer or the court.

title: Mudarabah
q: A capital provider hands over 'some funds' without stating amount or currency, and the parties agree to settle the figure later. What does the standard require?
options: The capital may be fixed later at liquidation
Capital must be clearly known in quality and quantity
The Mudarib may determine the capital on his own
The capital need only be stated in the accounts
explanation: Per 7/2, Mudarabah capital must be clearly known and defined in quality and quantity so as to eliminate any uncertainty or ambiguity.

title: Arbitration
q: Bank A must comply with a certain national law in an arbitration it conducts as arbitrator. How should it handle a provision of that law contrary to Shari'ah?
options: It may apply the law if both parties agree
It must stop the arbitration altogether
It must apply the law, since the parties chose it
It should still not violate the rulings of Shari'ah
explanation: Per 9/4, the arbitrator should apply the rulings of Shari'ah; if obliged to apply a certain law, he should still not violate the rulings of Shari'ah.

title: Possession (Qabd)
q: The buyer stipulates that goods located in Port A be delivered at his warehouse in City B at the seller's expense, and the seller agrees. Who bears the transport cost?
options: The seller, who must deliver at the specified place
Both parties equally, as the place was changed
The buyer, as the stipulation is invalid
The buyer, as transport is always his duty
explanation: Per 4/1/3, where the buyer stipulates delivery at another place at the seller's expense, the seller must deliver there and bear the transport expenses.

title: Sale of Debt
q: Before buying a portfolio of receivables, Company Y requires Bank A to arrange Islamic insurance (Takaful) on the debts. Is this condition permitted?
options: No, the buyer must bear all the risk of the debts he buys
Yes, but only after the debt has been sold and delivered
No, Takaful cannot cover sold debts
Yes, a Shari'ah-compliant guarantee may be stipulated
explanation: Per 7/3, the buyer may stipulate that the seller secure the debt by a Shari'ah-compliant third-party guarantee, e.g., Takaful before sale.

title: Salam and Parallel Salam
q: Bank A pays US dollars as Salam capital and wants al-Muslam Fihi to be a quantity of gold delivered in six months. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible if the delivery is under a year
Permissible, as gold is a commodity
Not permissible when the capital is currency
Permissible if the gold is weighed
explanation: Per 3/2/4, al-Muslam Fihi may not be currency, gold or silver if the Salam capital was paid in currency, gold or silver.

title: Investment Sukuk
q: Bank A's Murabahah Sukuk commodity has been purchased and is held awaiting sale to a buyer. What reason does the standard give for allowing the certificates to be traded now?
options: The certificates represent assets that can be traded
Debts may be traded freely before their maturity
The buyer has issued a binding promise to purchase
The Murabahah profit has already been fixed and disclosed to holders
explanation: Per the Basis, if the commodity has been purchased and is yet to be sold, trading is permissible because the certificates represent tradable assets.

title: Controls on Gharar in Financial Transactions
q: For excessive Gharar to be justified by need under the standard, which description of the need is correct?
options: It must be approved by a regulator as a necessity
It causes severe hardship and has no permissible alternative
It must be a public need, not a private one
It must amount to a threat to life or to the survival of the business
explanation: Per 4/4, need (public or private) means refraining leads to severe hardship, though not amounting to mortality, and it must be inevitable with no permissible way.

title: Mortgage and its Contemporary Applications
q: Bank A wants a client to sign a mortgage contract a week before signing the Murabahah that will create his debt. Is this valid under the standard?
options: No; the debt must first be established before any mortgage is signed
Yes, but only if the debt is a Qard Hasan
Yes; the mortgage may be signed before or with the debt contract
No; mortgage may be signed only after the debt is due
explanation: Per 3/3/1, a valid mortgage need not be preceded by establishing the debt; it can be signed before or at the same time as the debt contract.

title: Competitions and Prizes
q: Bank A runs a prize draw for credit cardholders but limits it to cards linked to current accounts, which holders cannot link to investment accounts. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible, if no fee is charged for the draw
Not permissible; prizes can't be confined to such cards
Permissible, since debit and credit cards are alike
Permissible, if card fees during the draw stay ordinary
explanation: Per 3/5/4/3, card prizes must not be confined to cards linked to current accounts where the holder cannot link the card to an investment account.

title: Waqf
q: The board of directors of Company X resolves to declare one of the company's buildings a Waqf. Who should make the Waqf decision for a legal person?
options: The general assembly, not the board of directors
The board of directors, as it manages assets
The chief executive officer alone
Any two directors acting jointly
explanation: Per 3/2/1, if the Waqif is a legal person, the Waqf decision should be made by the general assembly and not the board of directors.

title: Gold and Its Trading Parameters in Shari’ah
q: Bank A agrees to sell gold to a customer, with the sale to take effect only if the gold price rises by 5% next week. Is this permissible?
options: Yes, like a promise contingent on an index
Yes, if the price is fixed at the contract date
Yes, if both sides deliver when it takes effect
No, a gold sale may not be contingent on an event
explanation: Per 3/2/2, a gold sale contract may not be contingent on an event or occurrence, nor be a forward contract.

title: Arbitration
q: An arbitrator's final decision settles only three of five disputed points between Bank A and a customer. What may the parties do?
options: Only take the remaining points to court
Demand a further decision on the remaining points
Treat the whole decision as void and restart the arbitration
Nothing, as the decision is final
explanation: Per 11/2, partial resolution makes arbitration incomplete; the parties have the right to demand a further decision to resolve the remaining points.

title: Mortgage and its Contemporary Applications
q: Ahmad owns a 30% share in a jointly owned building and offers it to Bank A as mortgage. When is this permissible?
options: Only when the co-owners mortgage the whole building
Only when the Bank takes physical possession of the whole
When the share can be identified and sold separately
Never; common property cannot be mortgaged
explanation: Per 3/2/2, a mortgaged object can be a share of common property which can be identified and sold separately.

title: Murabahah
q: Bank A cannot buy an item directly from the supplier and needs an agent. Whom should it preferably appoint?
options: A party other than the purchase orderer
The purchase orderer, if he gave a binding promise
Any party, as the standard sets no preference
The purchase orderer, as he knows the item best
explanation: Per 3/1/3, the Institution may appoint an agent other than the purchase orderer; the customer should not be agent except in case of dire need.

title: Procrastinating Debtor
q: When settling, a defaulting debtor voluntarily pays Bank A more than the debt. There was no condition, custom or agreement on any extra. May the Bank accept it?
options: Only if the excess is given to charity
Only if the extra was agreed verbally
No, any excess over the debt is Riba
Yes, it may accept the extra amount
explanation: Per 2/5/2, the Institution may accept an excess payment from a defaulting debtor if there is no written or verbal condition, custom or agreement on it.

title: Buyback
q: Which Qur'anic basis does the standard cite for permitting buyback free of stipulation, binding Muwa'adah or collusion?
options: "Allah has permitted sale" and trade by mutual consent
The Hadith prohibiting two sales in one and a sale with a loan
The analogy to Suftajah between two cities
Ibn Omar's narration on the 'Inah sale and following the tails of cows
explanation: The Basis: contracts are presumed permissible, citing "Allah has permitted sale" and the verse on trading by mutual consent.

title: Payment Cards
q: With Ahmad's consent, Bank A obtains additional Islamic insurance (Takaful) for his benefit, deducts the contribution and adds a commission. Is this permitted?
options: Yes, but only if Bank A pays the contribution
No, Bank A may not earn a commission
No, insurance may not be linked to cards
Yes, with or without a commission for Bank A
explanation: Per 5/6/3, with the holder's consent, the Institution may obtain additional Islamic insurance for him and deduct the contribution, with or without commission.

title: Gold and Its Trading Parameters in Shari’ah
q: Bank A and a customer exchange promises binding on both sides: Bank A to sell, and the customer to buy, a quantity of gold next month. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible, if the price is fixed today
Permissible, if Hamish Jiddiyyah is paid
Impermissible, as a bilaterally binding promise
Permissible, as no contract is concluded yet
explanation: Per 8/1, a unilaterally binding promise to sell gold is permissible, but bilaterally binding promises for sale of gold are impermissible.

title: Mortgage and its Contemporary Applications
q: A client wants to mortgage to Bank A the future rental income of a specified building he owns, without mortgaging the building itself. What is the ruling?
options: Impermissible, as it involves excessive Gharar
Permissible, as the income-earning principal is specified
Permissible only if the building is mortgaged too
Impermissible, as the income is not yet owned and may never come into existence
explanation: Per 7, mortgaging an income still to be owned is permissible if the principal is specified, whether with the principal or independently.

title: Islamic Insurance
q: Why does the basis require the principles of Islamic insurance to be stated in the company's articles of association?
options: To preserve the donation element and avoid a Mu'awadah
To make the contributions owned by the company
To allow the company to share in the surplus and the profits
To exempt the company from Shari'ah audit
explanation: The basis: stating the principles preserves the donation element and cooperative nature; otherwise the operation becomes a Mu'awadah subject to Gharar.

title: Hiring of Persons
q: Company X hires Ahmad personally to do a specific task. Without any clause or agreement allowing it, Company X hires out Ahmad's service to Company Y. What is the ruling?
options: Allowed, as parallel hiring is always permitted in such cases
Allowed, since Company X owns the hired service
Not allowed unless the contract or the parties permit it
Allowed, if Company Y pays a higher rate for it
explanation: Per 5/1/3, the employer may not hire out a specific person's service to a sub-employer unless the contract permits sub-hiring or the parties agree.

title: Buyback
q: Which of the following falls outside the scope of the standard on buyback?
options: Repurchase from another to whom ownership passed
Selling an asset, then buying it back at spot
Selling a usufruct, then repurchasing it
Return of an item through dissolution (iqala)
explanation: Per item 1, the standard does not cover items returning to the seller other than by sale or rescission, like Wafa Sale and dissolution (iqala).

title: Banking Services in Islamic Banks
q: Per the Shari'ah basis, why may Institutions charge fees for banking services?
options: Customary banking practice requires such fees
Rewarding tasks that bring permissible benefits is allowed
The fees are a return on the funds the Bank lends to its customers
The fees cover the Riba element in the services
explanation: The basis: fees are remuneration the Institutions deserve for their tasks, as reward for tasks with permissible benefits to others is allowed in Shari'ah.

title: Impact of Contingent Incidents on Commitments
q: After Bank A signs a Murabahah contract, the government imposes a new customs duty on the imported goods. Who bears this new obligation?
options: The Bank in all cases, since as seller it imported and priced the goods
Both parties equally, since neither caused the new duty
The party who must bear it by law or as stipulated in the contract
The customer in all cases, as he is the final buyer
explanation: Per 4/1, a new duty or tax affects the commitment of the party who has to bear the new obligation by virtue of law or the stipulations of the contract.

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: An Ijarah is signed on 1 May, but Bank A makes the asset available to the lessee only on 15 May. From when is the Bank entitled to rental?
options: From the end of the first month
From 1 May, the date of signing
From the first payment date in the contract
From 15 May, when the usufruct is made available
explanation: Per 5/2/2, entitlement runs from when the lessee starts benefiting or the usufruct is made available, not necessarily from the signing date.

title: Arbitration
q: Bank A and Company X ask an arbitrator to decide a matter that would establish a ruling against Company Y, which is not party to the arbitration. What is the ruling?
options: Impermissible, as it proves a verdict against a third party
Permissible, if Company Y is notified of the verdict
Permissible if the arbitrator is paid by both parties
Permissible, since the parties consented to the arbitration itself
explanation: Per 7/2/2, arbitration is impermissible in cases that entail proving or disproving a verdict that concerns a third party.

title: Sale of Commodities in Organized Markets
