q: Which of the following is outside the scope of the standard on Sale of Commodities in Organized Markets?
options: Commodity derivatives such as options and futures
Sales concluded outside the organized markets
Spot commodity contracts on an exchange
Commodity swaps and indexes
explanation: Per Scope (1), the standard does not cover financial and commercial paper or currencies, nor sales concluded outside the organized markets.

title: Agency and the Act of an Uncommissioned Agent (Fodooli)
q: Karim, with no authority, sells Ahmad's goods without declaring that he lacks authority. Ahmad refuses to approve the sale. What is the result?
options: The act becomes binding on Karim himself
The sale binds Ahmad despite his refusal
The sale is binding on the buyer and Ahmad equally
The sale remains suspended indefinitely
explanation: Per 8/2, if the owner does not approve, the Fodooli's act binds the Fodooli himself, if he did not declare at signing that he had no authority.

title: Hiring of Persons
q: Bank A, as employee, wants a clause protecting it if the employer defaults in paying. Which clause is permissible?
options: A clause converting the debt into a higher deferred amount
A clause adding a late fee kept by the Bank as income
A pledge by the employer to donate a percentage to charity
A clause increasing the pay by 2% per month of delay
explanation: Per 5/2/8, no condition may increase the agreed pay on default; the contract may include a pledge to donate a percentage of the pay to charity under the Shari'ah Board.

title: Investment Sukuk
q: Under Salam Sukuk, the issuer sells goods for future delivery and the subscribers pay the Salam capital. What are the certificate holders entitled to?
options: A share of the issuer's overall profits for the period
The rental from leasing the Salam goods to the issuer
A fixed return on the Salam capital, paid periodically by the issuer
Sale price of the certificates or of goods sold via Parallel Salam
explanation: Per 5/1/5/3, holders own the Salam goods and are entitled to the sale price of the certificates or of the goods sold through a Parallel Salam.

title: ’Arboun (Earnest Money)
q: A buyer takes delivery of goods under an 'Arboun sale. During the option period, the goods are damaged while with the buyer. What is the effect?
options: The contract is void and the seller refunds the 'Arboun
His option is canceled and he must pay the unpaid balance
The seller bears the loss as the price is not fully paid
He may still revoke, but he forfeits the 'Arboun
explanation: Per item 6, after delivery the buyer is liable; if the item is damaged, his option is canceled and he must pay the balance of the price.

title: Insolvency
q: Creditors of Ahmad ask why they cannot simply declare him insolvent themselves by agreement. What is the Shari'ah basis for requiring a judicial ruling?
options: The case of Mu'adh, and because insolvency needs consideration and Ijtihad
Because a declaration transfers ownership to the creditors
Because the debtor's consent is needed for any sequestration of his property by the creditors
Because creditors of undue debts must be represented
explanation: Per the basis, a judicial ruling is required following the Prophet's act in Mu'adh's case, and because insolvency needs consideration and Ijtihad.

title: Competitions and Prizes
q: A store gives customers a free discount card, with no subscription fee, entitling them to reduced prices, though the exact discounts vary. Is it permissible?
options: No, the varying discounts create prohibited Gharar
Yes, as a Wa'ad to reduce the price on a Tabarru' basis
Yes, but only if a third party issues the card
No, discounts must be fixed in a binding contract
explanation: Per 3/6/2/2/1, a fee-free discount card is a Wa'ad to voluntarily reduce the price (Tabarru'); ambiguity in Tabarru' is forgiven.

title: Financial Paper (Shares and Bonds)
q: Bank A is offered a call option on shares, traded on an exchange. Which reason does the Basis give for prohibiting options on shares?
options: Options are concluded outside the exchange, so they lack transparency
The option premium is always too high compared to the share price
Options are only lawful for commodities, not for shares or currencies
The right of option is not a right that can be sold
explanation: Per the Basis, the right of option is not a saleable right: it is created by the contract and relates to an abstract thing; options also involve Gharar and gambling.

title: Guarantees
q: Bakr asks why he cannot charge Ahmad a fee for guaranteeing his debt. Per the Shari'ah basis, why is it prohibited?
options: Guarantors may not claim any expenses they incur at all
Only Institutions may charge for guarantees, not individuals
A guarantee is charitable, so a fee for it is Riba
Guarantees are invalid whenever any fee is paid for them
explanation: Per the Basis, guarantee is a charitable act implying readiness to lend; taking consideration for giving away a loan amount is Riba, as the Fuqaha agree.

title: Conversion of a Conventional Bank to an Islamic Bank
q: Converting Bank A's current account with the central bank, kept for set-off, earns interest it cannot avoid. What should the Bank do?
options: Retain it in reserves for Zakah
Keep it to cover clearing costs
Distribute it to its depositors
Dispose of the interest earned
explanation: Per 4/1, for set-off the bank should keep current accounts accruing no interest or, if that is impossible, dispose of the interest earned.

title: Hiring of Persons
q: A shared employee hired to design a website within 60 days fails to finish it in that period. What options does the employer have?
options: Keep the work and pay nothing
Only claim a fixed penalty from the employee
Terminate the contract or agree on a new period
Only extend the period without the employee's consent
explanation: Per 4/10, when a shared employee fails to do the work in the specified period, the employer may terminate the contract or a new period can be agreed.

title: Zakah
q: Company X grows two varieties of the same kind of dates on farms in different regions. Neither variety alone reaches 653 kg, but together they do. What applies?
options: No Zakah, since varieties are never added
They are added together, so Zakah is due
Zakah only on the larger variety
No Zakah, since each farm is separate
explanation: Per 5/4/2, different types of the same kind are added together for Nisab; it makes no difference if the produce is in different geographical locations.

title: Commercial Papers
q: Ahmad buys gold from a dealer and pays with a certified cheque drawn on his bank. Is this a valid way to meet the possession requirement?
options: Yes, a certified cheque counts as constructive possession
No, any cheque is merely a deferred promise to pay, even if certified
No, gold may only be bought with physical cash in hand at the time of contract
Yes, but only if the cheque is cashed on the same day
explanation: Per 7/1, receipt of a banker's or certified cheque is constructive possession of its amount, so it may be used where possession is required, e.g. buying gold.

title: Syndicated Financing
q: In a syndicated Mudarabah, the investment agent undertakes to protect the participants against exchange rate fluctuations. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible, if the agent receives a fee for it
Impermissible for the agent or any other party
Permissible, if all participants agree to it
Permissible, if limited to the profit amount
explanation: Per 9/3, the investment agent or any party of the Musharakah or Mudarabah may not commit to safeguard another party against exchange rate fluctuations.

title: Mortgage and its Contemporary Applications
q: A mortgaged asset is insured by Islamic insurance and is damaged; cash compensation is received. What happens to the cash?
options: It is paid to the mortgagor free of the mortgage
It is kept by the insurer until the debt matures
It is mortgaged, with its returns, in a frozen investment account
It is paid to the mortgagee, who becomes owner of the asset's value
explanation: Per 8, cash compensation replaces the asset and is mortgaged with its returns by depositing it in a frozen investment account owned by the mortgagor.

title: Waqf
q: A Waqif creates Waqf by an act clearly indicating it, without the word "Waqf". On what basis does the standard accept this?
options: Silence is treated as an explicit offer
Waqf is valid only when stated in writing before witnesses
Necessity allows exceptions to the form of the Waqf contract
Contracts follow objectives and meanings, not words
explanation: Basis 2/4/1/1: in all contracts, the intended objectives (maqāṣid) and meanings count, not words and forms, and custom is considered.

title: Documentary Credit
q: A client asks Bank A to open a credit to import goods that are prohibited by the Shari'ah, for resale to non-Muslims. What is the ruling?
options: Not permissible for the Institution to deal in such a credit
Permissible, provided the client is not himself a Muslim
Permissible, as the bank deals only in documents, not goods
Permissible, if the bank only notifies and does not issue it
explanation: Per 3/1/3, the Institution may not undertake documentary credit transactions, for itself or others, pertaining to goods prohibited by the Shari'ah.

title: Controls on Gharar in Financial Transactions
q: Bank A sells goods to a customer with the price deferred until the harvest season. What must the parties observe for the Gharar to be forgiven?
options: A date fixed later by the Bank alone
The date of the next market price review
The actual day the customer completes his harvest
The normal date of the season, not the harvest event
explanation: Per 5/3/2, Gharar is forgiven in postponing the price until known seasons; the parties should observe the normal date of the season rather than the event of harvesting.

title: Banking Services in Islamic Banks
q: Bank A reviews its products against the standard on Banking Services. Which of these services falls within that standard's scope?
options: Trading in currencies on behalf of customers
Collecting cheques and promissory notes for customers
Issuing credit cards to the Bank's customers against a fee
Opening and managing investment accounts for customers
explanation: Per clause 1, the standard covers services not involving lending and borrowing; currencies, cards, investment accounts and Sukuk have separate standards.

title: Credit Agreement
q: A client asks Bank A for a facility to buy and sell foreign currency on a deferred basis, as offered by traditional banks. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible if the exchange rate is fixed on signing the contract
Permissible as an incidental facility within the approved limit
Impermissible, as it defers one of the two transacted objects
Permissible if no interest is charged on the deferred amount
explanation: Per 5/1, traditional facilities are impermissible if they involve interest or lead to deferment of one of the two transacted objects, as in currency exchange contracts.

title: Investment Sukuk
q: Company X's draft Sukuk prospectus states that the issuer guarantees holders a fixed 6% annual profit. What is the ruling?
options: Not permissible: the issuer may not guarantee a fixed rate of profit
Permissible if the guarantee is disclosed in the prospectus
Permissible if the Sukuk are of short-term maturity
Permissible if the issuer charges no separate fee for giving the guarantee
explanation: Per 5/1/8/7, the prospectus must not state that the issuer guarantees a fixed percentage of profit.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: Partner X wants to contribute a warehouse rather than cash to a Sharikah. What does the standard require?
options: It is accepted at its historical cost without any valuation
It is rejected because Sharikah capital must be monetary only
Only the rental income of the warehouse may be contributed
All partners must agree and value the warehouse in currency
explanation: Per 3/1/2/1, tangible assets may be capital with all partners' agreement after their monetary value is determined in currency to know each partner's share.

title: Financial Paper (Shares and Bonds)
q: A government issues zero-coupon bonds at a discount, repaying the full face value at maturity. What is the ruling on issuing them?
options: Prohibited, as the loan is repaid with an excess
Permitted, as the issuer is a government, not a company
Permitted, as no periodic interest is paid on them
Permitted, if the discount at issue is small
explanation: Per 4, bonds stipulating return of the loan with any excess are prohibited, including zero-coupon bonds, whether private, public or governmental.

title: Combination of Contracts
q: Bank A relies on a concession that applies to a subsidiary contract within a set. It then wants to apply it to the same contract concluded independently. What is the ruling?
options: It applies if both parties consent to it
It cannot be granted to the independent contract
It applies equally to independent contracts
It applies if the contract value is small
explanation: Per 5/1, concessions granted to implicit and subsidiary contracts when combined cannot be granted to the same contracts concluded independently.

title: Procrastinating Debtor
q: Bank A's Murabahah contract says a late payer must compensate the Bank for any fall in the value of the currency of the debt. Is this clause allowed?
options: Yes, if the amount is not pre-determined
Yes, if paid in goods rather than in cash
No, such compensation may not be stipulated
Yes, as it covers actual loss, not opportunity loss
explanation: Per 2/1/2, no compensation (cash or other, pre-determined or not) may be stipulated for delay, including for loss due to a change in the currency's value.

title: Financial Rights and How They Are Exercised and Transferred
q: Ahmad co-owns a plot with Omar. Omar sells his share to Company X without Ahmad's consent. What right does Ahmad have?
options: To cancel the sale and have the share returned to Omar
To acquire the share at its current market value
Only to claim compensation from Omar
To take the share from Company X at its sale price
explanation: Per 7/1, Shuf'ah is the right of a neighbour or co-owner of real estate to acquire the sold property from the buyer, with or without consent, for the sale price.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: Before any valuation, partners pay themselves amounts 'on account' each quarter. What condition applies under the standard?
options: They undertake to reimburse any excess over their final profit share
The amounts must be fixed as a percentage of each partner's capital
Such payments are prohibited before the partnership is liquidated
The amounts become final profit once paid and are not reviewed
explanation: Per 3/1/5/11, funds may be allocated on account before valuation, provided parties undertake to reimburse any excess over their share after valuation.

title: Financial Rights and How They Are Exercised and Transferred
q: A tenant agrees to pay the owner a lump sum on top of periodic rent for a five-year lease, and the lease ends after two years. How is the lump sum treated?
options: As a non-refundable key money gift to the owner
As an impermissible payment that must be refunded to the tenant in full
As part of the agreed rent, governed by rental payment rules
As a security deposit returned in full
explanation: Per 8/1, the lump sum is permitted if treated as part of the agreed rent for the entire lease; on early termination, the rules on rental payments apply to it.

title: Insolvency
q: After his declaration of insolvency, Ahmad buys a car on credit from Dealer Z. Can Dealer Z share in the sequestered assets with the existing creditors?
options: No, unless Z files his claim before distribution
No; Z's claim attaches to Ahmad's future liability
Yes, with priority as the most recent creditor
Yes, pro-rata with the existing creditors
explanation: Per 5/4, post-declaration purchases attach to the debtor's future liability, not to the sequestered assets; such parties do not share those assets.

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: In an Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek with a gift contingent on paying the remaining instalments, the lessee pays all but one instalment. What happens to ownership?
options: It passes after a new contract is signed
It passes, as the shortfall is minor
It passes pro rata to the paid instalments
It does not pass, as the condition is not met
explanation: Per 8/4, under a gift contingent on paying the rentals, title passes without further procedure on fulfilment; if even one instalment is short, it does not pass.

title: Ju’alah
q: Under a Ju'alah, a collector is to recover a 100,000 debt for a 10,000 reward. He collects only 60,000. What is he entitled to?
options: The full 10,000, as he did the work
6,000, in proportion to the amount collected
Nothing, as the whole debt was not collected
Reasonable wages for his time and effort
explanation: Per 8/2, compensation may be contingent on collecting all the debt, or part of it so that compensation proportionate to the amount collected is due.

title: Islamic Insurance
q: A non-Muslim business owner wants to join an Islamic insurance fund along with Muslim participants. What is the ruling?
options: Non-Muslims may join if they pay double contributions
Only Muslims may join an Islamic insurance fund
Non-Muslims may participate with Muslims
Non-Muslims may join only Property Insurance
explanation: Per 7/1, non-Muslims may participate with Muslims in the various types of Islamic insurance.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: A company limited by shares suffers a loss exceeding its capital. How are the excess losses treated under the standard?
options: They are borne by the managing partners
They are shared by all partners per head
They are borne by the sleeping partners pro rata
They are written off with no partner liable
explanation: Per 4/4/2/4, losses are borne per capital shares and any excess losses are borne by the managing partners.

title: ’Arboun (Earnest Money)
q: Company X signs an agreement to buy a machine next month (a promise to sell, not a contract) and pays the seller 5% of the price with it. How is this payment classified?
options: It is 'Arboun that the seller may forfeit if Company X withdraws from the later purchase
Not 'Arboun, as money paid with a promise is not earnest money
It is 'Arboun to be credited towards the price at conclusion
It is 'Arboun, provided the agreement fixes an option period for the later purchase
explanation: Per 2/2, an agreement to execute a contract in the future is a promise, not a contract; money paid with the promise is not 'Arboun.

title: Mudarabah
q: For constructive valuation at the end of a Mudarabah, how must receivables due in a year be measured?
options: At face value plus a charge for the deferred period at the prevailing rate
At the price a third party would pay to buy the debt
At net realisable value, after a provision for doubtful debts
At present value discounted at the market interest rate for the year of deferral
explanation: Per 8/8, receivables are measured at cash equivalent or net realisable value; neither time value nor discount for the payment period is considered.

title: Combination of Contracts
q: A trainee asks for the textual basis for ignoring currency exchange rules in subsidiary contracts. What does the basis cite?
options: The Hadith forbidding sale and lending
The Hadith on low and high quality dates
The Hadith on the unpollinated palm tree
The Hadith on buying a slave who has money
explanation: The basis cites the Hadith on buying a slave with money: it may be bought with his money without the exchange rules, whether the money is known or not.

title: Mudarabah
q: Parties agree a Mudarabah will run for three years. After one year, the Mudarib alone wishes to end it. What is the ruling?
options: It cannot end before three years except by mutual agreement
He may end it at any time as Mudarabah is non-binding
Only the capital provider may end it before maturity
He may end it if he returns the capital without profit
explanation: Per 4/3/2, where the parties agree a duration, the contract cannot be terminated before the end of that duration except by mutual agreement.

title: Agency and the Act of an Uncommissioned Agent (Fodooli)
q: Bank A is reviewing four agency mandates. Which one falls within the scope of the standard on Agency and the Act of an Uncommissioned Agent?
options: A mandate to handle documentary credits for importers
A mandate to pay the Bank's Zakah on its behalf to the Zakah collectors
A mandate to act as advocate for a client in a court prosecution
A mandate to manage an investment fund for investors
explanation: Per clause 1, the standard covers fund management, real estate and investment agency, but excludes worship (Zakah), legal advocacy and documentary credits.

title: Guarantees
q: Bank A's contract makes future instalments due on default. Ahmad misses an instalment, with no force majeure involved. When does the term take effect?
options: After a reminder notice and a reasonable period
Only after a court order is obtained
At once, on the missed due date, without any notice
Only after three or more consecutive instalments are missed
explanation: Per 5/1, acceleration on default (not caused by force majeure) is permitted, but is not effective until a reminder notice is served and a reasonable time elapses.

title: Gold and Its Trading Parameters in Shari’ah
q: A customer buys gold for currency, with both delivered at the session, and stipulates a three-day option to return the gold and revoke the sale. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible, as the exchange was made on spot and both were delivered
Impermissible; Khiyar al-Shart is barred in gold sales
Permissible, if the customer pays 'Arboun to secure the option
Permissible, if the option period is specified
explanation: Per 3/2/2, stipulation of Khiyar al-Shart (cooling-off option) in the sale of gold is impermissible.

title: Controls on Gharar in Financial Transactions
q: Why, according to the Shari'ah basis, is Rahn allowed to involve Gharar that would not be allowed in a sale?
options: Rahn involves only minor Gharar by definition
Rahn is a form of donation for the creditor's benefit
Rahn is a corollary contract made for documentation
Rahn is always justified by a public need
explanation: The basis states Gharar does not affect Rahn because it is not meant in itself; it is a corollary contract signed for documentation.

title: Waqf
q: An overseer lets his friend, who is not a Waqf beneficiary, use a Waqf flat for free for a year. What is the consequence?
options: It is allowed for short periods without liability
Prohibited; the overseer is liable for fair rent
It is allowed as a charitable act within the overseer's discretion
It is allowed if the friend is poor and the use is temporary
explanation: Per 3/8/4, lending the Waqf asset for no consideration to a non-beneficiary is barred, and the overseer is liable for the fair rent.

title: ’Arboun (Earnest Money)
q: During the option period, the seller of an identified apartment sold under 'Arboun sells it to a third party. The first buyer refuses to ratify this. What is the status of the second sale?
options: It is void, being an unratified Fodooli disposal
It is valid and the seller compensates the first buyer
It is suspended until the option period expires
It is valid and the first buyer recovers his 'Arboun
explanation: Per 9/1, the seller's disposal of an identified item is subject to Fodooli rules; if the first buyer does not ratify it, the second disposal is void.

title: Irrigation Partnership (Musaqat)
q: A hailstorm completely destroys an orchard's crop under a Musaqat. The worker had worked diligently all season. What is he entitled to?
options: A market wage for his work
Compensation from the owner
Nothing
Half of his expected share
explanation: Per 10/1, if the crop is completely destroyed by a natural disaster, the worker is not entitled to anything.

title: Agency and the Act of an Uncommissioned Agent (Fodooli)
q: A Fodooli sells Ahmad's car. Before Ahmad approves, the buyer revokes the contract. Ahmad then approves. What is the effect of the approval?
options: The sale becomes effective from the approval date
The buyer's revocation is void and the sale stands
The sale becomes effective from the date of the act
None; a new contract has to be initiated
explanation: Per 8/2, the owner's approval should precede revocation of the contract by either party; otherwise, a new contract has to be initiated.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: At expiry, after expenses and liabilities, the remaining assets do not cover the partners' full capital. How is the remainder distributed?
options: Equally among the partners per head
Pro rata to each partner's share of capital
According to the agreed profit-sharing ratio
First to the managing partner, then the others
explanation: Per 3/1/6/3(c), if assets fall short of the contributed capital, distribution takes place on a pro rata basis to the shares of capital.

title: Concession Contracts
q: The State leases land to Bank A for a rent equal to a set share of the mine's output, and Bank A leases it to a third party to build the project. What is the ruling?
options: Not permissible, as Bank A may not sublease
Not permissible, as rent must be money
Permissible only as a Ju'alah contract
Permissible as Ijarah with sub-contracting
explanation: Per 7/2, Ijarah may be applied where the State leases land for a rent as a set share of output; the licensee may lease to a third party (sub-contracting).

title: Possession (Qabd)
q: A lender asks why the borrower, not he, pays the delivery and recovery costs of a Qard. What reason does the Basis give?
options: Custom in all markets places such costs on borrowers
The lender earns a return on the Qard that already covers all of these costs
The lender does a good act, and costs are not imposed on one doing good
The borrower owns the loan and so must bear all its risks
explanation: Per the Basis, the lender undertakes a good act, and 'no ground can there be against those who do good'; burdening him would deter lending.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: From the outset, partners engage Omar, a non-partner, to manage their Sharikah solely for 10% of the profit earned. How is Omar classified?
options: As a Mudarib, entitled only to a share in profit, if any
As a partner bearing a share of losses from his own funds
As an employee entitled to a fixed wage plus 10% of profit
As an agent entitled to a fee even if there is no profit
explanation: Per 3/1/3/3, if management is from the outset for a percentage share in profit, the manager is a Mudarib entitled only to profit, if any, with no further remuneration.

title: Indices
q: Company X is developing an Islamic share index. Besides technical controls, what does the standard require?
options: Only a listing of Muslim-owned firms
A Shari'ah Board for the Index with periodic review
Only an annual external financial audit of the index calculation
Only approval from the stock exchange and the securities regulator
explanation: Per 7/1-7/2, an Islamic Index must adhere to Shari'ah precepts and have its own Shari'ah Supervisory Board for periodic review and reporting.

title: Ju’alah
q: A worker in a Ju'alah suffers an accident during the work causing loss, with no tort or negligence on his part. What is his entitlement?
options: Reasonable wages only
Half the agreed compensation
No compensation at all
Full compensation
explanation: Per 5/3/2/3(b), where an accident during work causes loss not due to the worker's tort or negligence, the worker is entitled to full compensation.

title: Financial Rights and How They Are Exercised and Transferred
q: A building's ground floor collapses due to its owner's fault, harming the upper-floor owners. What is the ruling?
options: The ground floor owner is liable to reconstruct it
Each owner bears his own loss
The upper owners must reconstruct and claim later
The court must sell the land and split the price
explanation: Per 6/2/1, if a lower storey collapses due to its owner's fault, he is liable to reconstruct it so the upper-storey owners are not harmed.

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: A customer breaks his promise to take an asset on operating Ijarah. Bank A bought it for 200,000 and sells it to a third party for 185,000. What may the customer be charged?
options: The whole security amount he deposited
Nothing, as a promise to lease is not binding
The rentals for the whole intended lease term
explanation: Per 2/3, in operating Ijarah the breaching promisor is charged the difference between the cost of acquisition and the selling price to a third party.

title: Hiring of Persons
q: Per the Shari'ah basis, why may an Institution not hire out a specific service before owning and possessing it?
options: Because pay must always be in advance
By analogy to selling what one does not own
Because services cannot be delivered constructively
By analogy to the prohibition of 'Inah
explanation: The basis: it is by analogy to the prohibition of selling things one does not own, and Hakim Ibn Hizam's Hadith "Don't sell what you do not have".

title: Financial Paper (Shares and Bonds)
q: Ahmad wants to mortgage his shares of a lawful company whose assets are mostly debts and cash. What is the ruling?
options: Not permissible, since debts predominate
Permissible only if tangible assets predominate
Not permissible, as shares cannot be mortgaged
Permissible, whatever the mix of assets
explanation: Per 3/10, lawful shares may be mortgaged whether the corporation's assets are cash, tangibles, debts or a mix, in line with the rules for selling at liquidation.

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: Bank A and a lessee raise the rentals for future periods not yet due. Why is this not prohibited rescheduling, per the Shari'ah basis?
options: Because the rentals were floating anyway under the contract
Because the lessee freely agreed to the increase in rentals
It creates a new contract for rentals not yet a debt
Because the asset's market value has risen since the lease
explanation: The basis: restructuring future rentals is a new contract for a term whose rentals are not yet due, so they are not a debt; raising due rentals for time is Riba.

title: Sale of Debt
q: Three heirs jointly hold a single debt owed by Ahmad and agree that each will collect his own share of it. Is this permitted?
options: Yes, they may divide it in proportion to shares
Only if the debt is first sold to a third party
Only if Ahmad consents to the division
No, a single debt cannot be divided among its joint creditors
explanation: Per 6/1, claimants in one debt may divide it among themselves in proportion to their shares, each reserving his share.

title: Arbitration
q: Bank A and Company X appoint two arbitrators. What does the standard provide for the case where the two arbitrators' votes are equal?
options: The Bank's arbitrator has the deciding vote
The dispute must then be referred to the competent courts for ruling
The arbitration becomes void as the panel is even
The parties may appoint a chairman with the casting vote
explanation: Per 8/3, the number of arbitrators is preferably odd; otherwise the parties may appoint a chairman whose vote is the casting vote when votes are equal.

title: Guarantees
q: A lessee pays 'Arboun to Bank A and then fails to perform within the option period. The Bank may retain it. What does the standard consider preferable?
options: Keeping the whole amount as profit, as the lessee defaulted
Refunding the balance above the actual damage
Claiming further compensation on top
Donating the whole amount to charity through the Board
explanation: Per 6/8/3, the seller or lessor may retain the 'Arboun, but it is preferable to refund any balance after deducting damage actually sustained.

title: Revocation of Contracts by Exercise of a Cooling-Off Option
q: A seller asks why he cannot stipulate in a sale contract a payment for waiving his right to revoke. What is the Shari'ah basis given?
options: The rule that contracts are generally binding
The maxim that ownership arises at contract
Analogy to Iqalah, done without increase or decrease
The opinion of Abu Hanifah on notifying the other party
explanation: Per the Basis, the prohibition is by analogy to Iqalah, which must be done without any increase or decrease in considerations.

title: Murabahah
q: At the time of payment, a customer wants to pay his Murabahah instalment in a currency other than the Murabahah currency. Bank A agrees. What condition applies?
options: Full payment of the agreed amount, leaving nothing due
The Bank may add a margin for the exchange
The exchange must be stipulated in the original contract
Part of the amount may remain due as a debt for later payment
explanation: Per 5/10, payment in another currency is allowed with the Institution's agreement at payment if paid in full with nothing remaining; it may not be stipulated.

title: Possession (Qabd)
q: Why does the standard refer to custom ('Urf) to determine how possession is realised?
options: Custom always overrides texts specified by the Shari'ah
The Qur'an defines possession expressly as physical transfer by hand
The Lawgiver left 'possession' undefined; jurists agree on custom
Possession is defined precisely in the Arabic language
explanation: Per the Basis, there is consensus of the jurists on custom, as the Lawgiver used possession unqualified and it has no definition in language, so custom is referred to.

title: Murabahah
q: At contracting, Bank A did not disclose transportation and storage expenses it incurred on the item. May it include them in the Murabahah cost?
options: Yes, but only if the customer later agrees
No, undisclosed expenses can never be included
No, unless they are paid to the Bank's staff
Yes, as they are customarily normal expenses
explanation: Per 4/3, undisclosed expenses cannot be included unless customarily normal, such as transport, storage, letter of credit fees and insurance premiums.

title: Indices
q: An investor instructs his Mudarib to sell a commodity at the market price when a commodity index reaches a certain reading. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible to link the Mudarib's deals to the index
Permissible only for agents, not for a Mudarib
Not permissible, as it amounts to trading in the index itself
Not permissible, as it suspends a sale
explanation: Per 5/6, deals of the Mudarib or agent may be linked to an index, to sell at market price or buy a set amount at a specific index reading.

title: Salam and Parallel Salam
q: Bank A wants its Salam contract to stipulate a penalty payable by the seller for each week of delay in delivering al-Muslam Fihi. What is the ruling?
options: Permitted if stated at contracting
Not permitted in respect of delay in delivery
Permitted if the seller is solvent
Permitted if the penalty goes to charity
explanation: Per 5/7, it is not permitted to stipulate a penalty clause in respect of delay in the delivery of al-Muslam Fihi.

title: Zakah
q: A perfume trader's bottles and boxes are not sold separately, but they add to the value of the perfume sold. Are they included in valuing the goods?
options: Yes, but at cost rather than market value
No, packing materials are never part of the goods being valued, whatever their effect on value
No, because they are not sold separately
Yes, because they increase the value of the goods
explanation: Per 5/2/10, packing materials not prepared for trade separately are excluded from valuation, but if such materials increase the value of the goods they should be included.

title: Istisna’a and Parallel Istisna’a
q: Bank A ordered 10 buses by Istisna'a. Before taking any possession, it wants to sell those same buses to a transport firm. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible at a price not above cost
Permissible if the firm pays in advance
Not permissible before actual or constructive possession
Permissible, as the Bank has already paid the maker in full
explanation: Per 6/7, the subject-matter may not be sold before possession; the Institution may instead sell similar items by description through Parallel Istisna'a.

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: Under a lease of a described asset, Bank A delivers a vehicle that does not conform to the agreed specifications. What may the lessee do?
options: Only claim a reduction in the rental
Reject it and demand one that conforms
Keep it, since the lease is already binding
Terminate the lease and claim a penalty
explanation: Per 3/5, if the lessee receives an asset that does not conform to the description, he is entitled to reject it and demand a conforming asset.

title: Mortgage and its Contemporary Applications
q: After concluding a mortgage contract with Bank A, the client wants to revoke it unilaterally before repaying the debt. May he?
options: No; it is binding on the mortgagor once concluded
No, unless the Bank has not yet registered it
Yes, at any time before the asset is delivered
Yes, if he provides a guarantor instead
explanation: Per 3/1/1, the mortgage is binding on the mortgagor once concluded and he cannot revoke it from his side, whereas the mortgagee has the right to do so.

title: Combination of Contracts
q: Which of the following does the standard give as an example of contemporary contract sets agreed beforehand to be executed in successive stages?
options: Traditional hire-purchase
Murabahah on Order of Purchase
Sale combined with lending
Bay' al-'Inah
explanation: Per 7/1, examples include Murabahah on Order of Purchase, Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek and Diminishing Musharakah.

title: Buyback
q: Why must ownership in a buyback pass by a contract made at that time, rather than by the mere lapse of a period?
options: To keep the second price lower than the first in every buyback
To let the seller keep legal registration
Ownership needs a formulation; else the sale is contingent
To stop the asset's value from changing between the two sales
explanation: Per the Basis, ownership transfers only by a verbal or action-based formulation; automatic transfer would be tantamount to a contingent sale.

title: Murabahah
q: Customer C fulfils his promise and the Murabahah contract is executed. What should Bank A do with the Hamish Jiddiyyah C paid?
options: Keep it as earnest money for the Bank once the deal is done
Hold it as security until the last instalment is paid
Keep it as a fee for arranging the deal for the customer
Refund it, or deduct it from the price if so agreed
explanation: Per 2/5/5, once the promise is fulfilled the Institution must refund Hamish Jiddiyyah, or may agree with the customer to deduct it from the Murabahah price.

title: Financial Rights and How They Are Exercised and Transferred
q: A buyer becomes insolvent before paying for a machine, and the seller finds that same machine among the insolvency assets. What right does the seller have?
options: A priority proprietary right to it, if local regulations allow
Ownership of it in all cases, regardless of the law of the jurisdiction
No right, as ownership passed to the buyer
Only an equal claim with all other creditors
explanation: Per 12/2 (c), the seller has a priority proprietary right to the specific item found in the insolvent buyer's assets if the applicable regulations allow it.

title: Islamic Insurance
q: In commercial insurance, the company owns the premiums. Per the basis, who owns the contributions in Islamic insurance?
options: The reinsurance company
The insurance account
The company's shareholders
The managing company
explanation: The basis: in Islamic insurance it is the insurance account, rather than the company, that owns the contributions.

title: Investment Sukuk
q: Thousands of investors accept a single prospectus that expressly states it is an offer. Someone objects that one offer cannot meet many acceptances. On what basis does the standard reject this?
options: Contracts form by anything showing consent; one offer, many acceptances
Each investor's acceptance creates a separate loan contract
Necessity permits what would otherwise be an invalid contract
Acceptance becomes valid only once the regulator approves the whole issue
explanation: Per the Basis, valid contracts occur through anything indicating consent, so an offer from one person and acceptance from many is not objectionable.

title: Zakah
q: Company X inherited land, did not buy it, and now offers it for sale. Is the land an article of trade for Zakah?
options: Yes, but only after a sale contract is signed
No; land is always a fixed asset
No; trade goods must be acquired by purchase
Yes; the intention to offer it for sale suffices
explanation: Per 5/2/1, articles of trade include anything offered for sale, whether acquired by buying or otherwise; the mere intention to offer it for sale is sufficient.

title: Al-Wakalah Bi Al-Istithmar (Investment Agency)
q: An investment agency contract requires Bank A, as agent, to pay storage and insurance of the goods, reimbursed only if the investment yields a profit. Is this valid?
options: Yes, since the agent receives a fee for its work
Yes, if the expected yield is high enough to cover them
No; such expenses are the principal's responsibility
Yes, as long as the agent accepts it in the contract
explanation: Per 6/2, investment expenses are the principal's; the agent may not be required to pay them, nor may reimbursement be deferred or tied to the investment's yield.

title: Hiring of Persons
q: Ali, a private employee of Bank A, accidentally damages office equipment without any transgression, negligence or breach of a condition. Is he liable?
options: No; a private employee is liable only for such faults
Yes; employees are always liable for damage to the employer's property
Yes, for half of the cost of the damage
Yes, unless he was working overtime
explanation: Per 4/5, a private employee is not responsible for damage unless it is due to his own transgression, negligence, or breach of a stipulated condition.

title: Waqf
q: A donor dedicates USD 1 million in cash as Waqf for students. How should this cash Waqf be used?
options: Only interest earned on deposits may be spent
It must be converted into real estate first
The full amount is distributed to students at once
Its income is spent while the principal is retained
explanation: Per 3/4/3/2, Waqf in money is permissible; income from utilizing it (e.g., Shari'ah-based lending or Mudarabah) is spent while retaining the principal.

title: Waqf
q: A Waqf was created for the students of a particular school. The school has since closed permanently. What becomes of the Waqf?
options: Its revenue is kept by the overseer
It remains valid and is used for similar charitable causes
It becomes void from the date of creation
It ends, and the asset returns to the Waqif or his heirs
explanation: Per 2/4/4/3, the Waqf remains valid if the beneficiary is discontinued; it will then be used for similar charitable causes.

title: Islamic Insurance
q: An Islamic insurance policy on Ahmad's life names his nephew as beneficiary. Ahmad is murdered and the nephew is found to be involved. Is the nephew entitled?
options: Yes, but only to half of the benefits
Yes, as the named beneficiary in the policy
No, the policy must deny any compensation to him
Yes, after the heirs approve the payment
explanation: Per 6/2/1/5, the policy should stipulate that a beneficiary or heir involved in the murder of the insured is not entitled to any compensation.

title: Hawalah
q: Ahmad, the transferor, dies after a Hawalah. His creditors ask that the debt Zaid owes under the Hawalah be shared among them pro rata. Is that right?
options: Yes, but the transferee ranks first
No, the transferee is its sole owner
Yes, as the Hawalah is annulled by death
Yes, it forms part of Ahmad's estate
explanation: Per 10/1, Hawalah is not annulled by the transferor's death; the transferee solely owns the debt, which is not distributed among the transferor's creditors.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: Three engineers form a service partnership to render consultancy. One of them performs far more of the services than the others. What is the Shari'ah implication?
options: The partnership is void unless every partner renders an equal share of the services
He must receive a fixed lump sum from the profit first
None; unequal services rendered have no Shari'ah implication
He is entitled to all of the profit of the partnership
explanation: Per 3/3/2, there is no Shari'ah implication regarding any disproportion in the services that the partners or their representatives may have rendered.

title: Combination of Contracts
q: In a combined Murabahah set, the customer fails to honor its commitment, causing Bank A an actual loss. What may Bank A claim?
options: Indemnity for the actual injury it encountered
A pre-agreed penalty linked to the price
Its full expected profit on the deal
Nothing, as the commitments are not binding
explanation: Per 7/6, failure of a party to combined contracts to honor its commitments gives the other party the right to claim indemnity for the actual injury.

title: Financial Paper (Shares and Bonds)
q: Company X rents shares from Ahmad for a fee, to show a stronger financial position at year-end, then returns them. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible, as it is an Ijarah of an asset
Permissible, if the rental is a fixed amount
Permissible, if similar shares are returned
Not permissible, as renting shares is not allowed
explanation: Per 3/15, renting shares is not permissible, whether for pledging, selling and returning similar shares, acquiring profits or showing a stronger financial position.

title: Istisna’a and Parallel Istisna’a
q: Bank A proposes an Istisna'a price set as 'actual cost of construction plus 10%', to be computed on completion. What is the ruling?
options: Permitted, if a ceiling on the cost is added
Permitted, as the 10% margin is known in advance
Not permitted; Istisna'a cannot be cost-plus
Permitted, if the costs are audited by an auditor
explanation: Per 3/2/5, an Istisna'a cannot be drawn up on the basis of Murabahah, e.g. by determining the price on a cost-plus basis.

title: Insolvency
q: Ahmad's debts exceed his assets, but no court has declared him insolvent yet. He plans to give a valuable property to his brother. What is his position in Shari'ah?
options: He may make the gift if at least one creditor approves it
He must first pre-pay his deferred debts, then he may make the gift
He is free to dispose of his property until a declaration is made
He is morally bound to refrain from acts that may harm his creditors
explanation: Per 3/1, a person whose debts exceed his assets has a moral obligation in Shari'ah to refrain from any action that may harm the creditors, even before a declaration.

title: Obtaining and Deploying Liquidity
q: Bank A sells commodities on a Salam basis, receives the price up-front, and obtains a promise to sell from a third-party commodity broker to hedge price fluctuation. Is this permitted?
options: No; any promise connected to a Salam sale is prohibited
Yes; securing a third-party broker's promise to sell is permitted
Yes, but only if the broker is also the Salam buyer
No; Salam may not be used to obtain liquidity, since the price is received before delivery
explanation: Per 4/2/1, selling on Salam and buying for delivery at maturity is permitted; securing a promise to sell from a third-party broker to mitigate price risk is permitted.

title: Commercial Papers
q: Bank A, as drawee, accepts a bill of exchange due in three months. What is the effect of this acceptance?
options: An undertaking to pay the holder the debt at maturity
A purchase of the bill by the bank at a discount
A guarantee for which the bank may take a fee
A mere promise that has no binding effect
explanation: Per 8/1, the drawee's acceptance is an undertaking and obligation to pay the debt in the paper to the holder at maturity, to be fulfilled per Shari'ah.

title: Murabahah
q: Out of dire need, Customer C is appointed as Bank A's agent to buy goods for a Murabahah. How should the price be paid to the supplier whenever possible?
options: By C, who is later reimbursed by the Bank
Half by Bank A and half by Customer C
Bank A pays the supplier directly
Into C's account, as the Bank's agent
explanation: Per 3/1/4(a), the Institution itself must pay the supplier and not pay the price into the customer-agent's account, whenever possible.

title: Irrigation Partnership (Musaqat)
q: A Musaqat worker demands a larger share of the crop for harvesting the fruit, as harvesting is hard work. Is he entitled to an increase?
options: No; customary work is already his contractual duty
Yes, a reasonable increase for the harvesting
No, but the owner must pay him a separate wage
Yes, if the harvest is larger than expected
explanation: Per 8/3, customary work does not entitle the worker to any increase in his share, as he is already contractually obligated to do it.

title: Credit Agreement
q: Bank A requires that a client's credit study be prepared by a third party firm. Per the Shari'ah basis, may it do so?
options: Yes, but then no fee may be charged to the client at all
Yes; the Institution may stipulate preparation by a third party
No; the study must be prepared internally by the Institution
No; a third party may prepare it only if the client chooses
explanation: Per the basis, the Institution can even stipulate a condition that the study be prepared by a third party.

title: Conversion of a Conventional Bank to an Islamic Bank
q: Before converting, Bank B distributed dividends derived from interest to its shareholders. Who should dispose of these earnings?
options: The bank itself, out of its current profits after conversion
The Shari'ah board, out of the bank's general reserves
No one, as the distributions were final and cannot be reversed
The shareholders personally, on ethical grounds
explanation: Per 8/1/2, impermissible earnings distributed before conversion should be disposed of personally by the shareholders and depositors who received them; the bank is not bound.

title: Options to Terminate Due to Breach of Trust (Trust-Based Options)
q: In a Murabahah sale, the seller deliberately tells the buyer that his cost price was 100,000 when it was actually 90,000. What right does the buyer have?
options: Khiyar al-Taghrir: an option to revoke for verbal deception
Only a claim for compensation, not revocation
No option, since the buyer agreed to the price
Khiyar al-Tadlis: an option to revoke for deceptive conduct
explanation: Per 2/1-2/2(a), deliberate misinformation on cost in Murabahah is verbal deception (Taghrir), giving the buyer the option to revoke.

title: Irrigation Partnership (Musaqat)
q: Karim agrees to a Musaqat with a party whom he knows has usurped the orchard. The rightful owner reclaims the trees and produce. What is Karim entitled to?
options: A wage at the fair market rate
Half of his stipulated share
His stipulated share of the produce
No remuneration at all
explanation: Per 11/2, a worker unaware of usurpation gets a fair market wage, but if he knew the trees were usurped he is not entitled to any remuneration.

title: Hawalah
q: Per the Shari'ah basis, what supports the majority view that a transferee who stipulated the payer's solvency has recourse if the payer is insolvent?
options: The report of Uthman Ibn Affan on the payer's bankruptcy
The Hanafi rule on unrestricted Hawalah
The Hadith that Muslims are bound by their conditions
The analogy with a deferred guarantee
explanation: Per the Basis, the majority rely on the Hadith that Muslims are bound by their conditions; the solvency condition serves the contract's purpose.

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: An Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek contains an undertaking by the lessee to donate a percentage of late rentals if he delays without good reason. How must the amounts be used?
options: Used to reduce the Bank's maintenance and insurance costs
Paid to charity under the Shari'ah Board's coordination
Returned to the lessee at the end of the lease
Added to the Bank's rental income for that period
explanation: Per 6/4, such a donation should be paid to charitable causes under the co-ordination of the Institution's Shari'ah Supervisory Board.

title: Murabahah
q: Customer C pays his Murabahah debt early, and Bank A wishes to give up part of the price. The contract was silent on this. What is the ruling?
options: Not permissible, as it resembles Riba
Not permissible; the full price is owed
Permissible, as it was not part of the contract
Permissible only if stipulated in the contract
explanation: Per 5/9, the Institution may give up part of the selling price on early payment provided this was not part of the contractual agreement.

title: Ju’alah
q: An offeror promises a reward to a person for doing a task that this person is already obliged to do. Is this a valid Ju'alah?
options: No, the work must not be obligatory for the worker
Yes, if the reward is known and deliverable
Yes, any task may be the subject of Ju'alah
No, unless the worker accepts the offer first
explanation: Per 5/3/1/5-6, it is a condition that the work involves some effort and that the work not be obligatory for the worker.

title: Revocation of Contracts by Exercise of a Cooling-Off Option
q: Before delivery, the buyer, who holds a cooling-off option, damages the sold item so it is destroyed. He then seeks to revoke the contract. What is the ruling?
options: He may revoke only if the option period remains
He may revoke but must compensate the seller
He may revoke, as the seller is liable before delivery
He cannot revoke, even though it was before delivery
explanation: Per 7/2, destruction of the sale item caused by the buyer, whether before or after delivery, prevents revocation.

title: Unilateral and Bilateral Promise
q: Bank A tells Company X of its resolute intention to lease it a building next year, leaving X free to take up the offer or not. What is this arrangement and X's role?
options: A unilateral promise; Company X is the promisor
A unilateral promise; Company X is the promisee
A concluded Ijarah contract effective next year
A bilateral promise binding both parties
explanation: Per 2/1, a unilateral promise is informing another of a resolute intention to act in the future in its interest; the receiving party, the promisee, has the option to avail itself.

title: Al-Wakalah Bi Al-Istithmar (Investment Agency)
q: Bank A, an investment agent experienced in equity investing, wants to appoint a sub-agent to manage the principal's equity portfolio, without the principal's permission. Is this permitted?
options: Yes, at the agent's full discretion, since an agent may always delegate to a sub-agent
Yes, if the sub-agent is its own subsidiary
No; the activity is within its expertise and capacity
Yes, if Bank A pays the sub-agent's fee
explanation: Per 9/1, the agent may not appoint a sub-agent except for activities outside its expertise or capacity, or where the principal permits it.

title: Protection of Capital and Investments
q: Bank A, as Mudarib, proposes a capital protection reserve funded by deductions from both the investors' profit share and its own Mudarib share. What does the standard allow?
options: Deductions only from the investors' share of profits
Deductions only from the Mudarib's share
Deductions from both shares in proportion
Deductions from the capital before profit is computed
explanation: Per 4/2/6, reserves to protect capital are created through deductions from the investors' share of profits but not from the manager's share as Mudarib.

title: Online Financial Dealings
q: On which view is the ruling based that an offeror may not retract an offer within its stated validity period?
options: The general rule that every promise is binding in law
The view of some Maliki scholars that a timed offer stays valid
The view that silence of the offeree counts as acceptance
The Hanafi view that an offer can be revoked before acceptance
explanation: Per the basis, it rests on the view of some Maliki scholars (Al-Hattab quoting Abu Bakar Al-Arabi), supported by an International Islamic Fiqh Academy resolution.

title: Sale of Debt
q: A customer owes Bank A a financing receivable. Bank A proposes using that receivable as the capital of a Salam with the same customer. Is this permitted?
options: Yes, if the commodity is delivered at maturity
Yes, as the money is already with the customer
Yes, if the receivable has already fallen due
No, a debt may not be made the Salam capital
explanation: Per 4/1/3/2, it is not permitted to make a debt, such as cash loans or financing receivables owed by the customer, the Salam capital.

title: Protection of Capital and Investments
q: A critic says splitting a fund's capital between Murabahah and Musharakah is a prohibited combination of contracts. Per the Shari'ah basis, why is it not?
options: The Shari'ah board has waived the prohibition
Combining contracts is always permitted in funds, whatever the link between them
Each part is invested independently in a separate contract
Musharakah and Murabahah are one type of contract
explanation: Per the basis, diversification is not combining contracts in one, as each contract is conducted independently, each part of capital invested in a different contract.

title: Insolvency
q: Company X suffers a temporary liquidity shortfall and delays some payments, but no declaration of insolvency follows. Is this situation governed by the Insolvency standard?
options: No, because the standard covers individuals only, not companies
Yes; any delay in payment of a due debt is treated as insolvency (Iflas) by the court
Yes, once the delay exceeds the agreed grace period
No; delays not leading to a declaration of insolvency are outside its scope
explanation: Per 1, the standard does not cover financial difficulties, liquidity shortfalls or delays in payment that do not lead to a declaration of insolvency.

title: Islamic Reinsurance
q: An Islamic insurance company asks whether the standard on Islamic reinsurance governs the Islamic insurance policies it issues directly to individuals. What is the answer?
options: No; direct policies are governed by conventional law
No; Islamic insurance is covered by a separate standard
Yes, but only policies issued to companies
Yes; it covers all Islamic insurance and reinsurance
explanation: Per 1, the standard covers Islamic reinsurance and participation with traditional insurers or reinsurers; it does not cover Islamic insurance, covered separately.

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: Bank A already owns a fleet of trucks. A customer agrees with the Bank on leasing two of them. When may the Ijarah contract be executed?
options: As soon as the two parties reach agreement
Only after a master agreement is signed
Only after the trucks are insured by the customer
Only after the customer pays rent in advance
explanation: Per 3/1/1, if the asset or its usufruct is owned by the Institution, as it should in principle be, the Ijarah may be executed as soon as agreement is reached.

title: Agency and the Act of an Uncommissioned Agent (Fodooli)
q: A collection agency contract lets the agent keep "whatever share it deems fit" from the amounts it collects for the principal. What is the ruling on this fee?
options: Permissible, if customary practice supports it
Permissible, as the agent's share is linked to output
Permissible, if the principal may revoke at any time
Not permissible, as the remuneration is left undetermined
explanation: Per 4/2/3, it is not permissible to leave the agent's fee undetermined and allow him to take an unspecified share from the principal's entitlements.

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: Ahmad, a lessee, invites two friends to share the usufruct he owns, and they then sub-lease the asset. When must the friends have joined?
options: Before the sub-lease, then share rental pro rata
Never; a lessee may not share his usufruct with others
Only after the sub-lease, sharing the rental equally
At any time, even after the sub-lease has been made
explanation: Per 4/2/4, a lessee may make others co-owners of the usufruct only before a sub-lease; each then shares the sub-lease rental pro rata to his share.

title: Insolvency
q: All creditors of Company X sign an agreement declaring X insolvent and sequestering its assets without going to court. Is this a valid declaration of insolvency?
options: Yes, if Company X itself countersigns the declaration
Yes, if the central bank is notified of the agreement
No; the court has the sole authority to declare insolvency
Yes, provided every creditor has signed the agreement
explanation: Per 4/5, the court has the sole authority to declare a person insolvent.

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: A lessee who paid 'Arboun withdraws, so the Ijarah is not executed for a reason attributable to him. What is preferable for Bank A to do?
options: Keep the full 'Arboun and claim lost rent
Forgo any amount above its actual damage
Refund the full 'Arboun without deduction
Keep the 'Arboun and charge a penalty
explanation: Per 4/1/4, the lessor may retain the 'Arboun, but it is preferable for the Institution to forgo any amount in excess of the actual damage it suffered.

title: Zakah
q: Bank A owns its head office, computer software, and spare parts kept in its warehouse for operations. Which of these are Zakatable?
options: Only the spare parts kept in the warehouse
All three, at their market value
None of these operational assets is Zakatable
Only the software, as an intangible asset
explanation: Per 4/1, Zakah is not due on operational fixed assets, intangible assets like software, or operational movable assets such as spare parts, even if warehoused.

title: Conversion of a Conventional Bank to an Islamic Bank
q: A buyer converting Bank C offers creditors early repayment of Riba loans in return for a discount. Which principle supports this, per the Shari'ah basis?
options: Muqassah, if the two debts are of equal amount and maturity
Da' Wa Ta'jjal, if the discount was not agreed earlier
Hawalah, if the creditor consents in advance
Ibra', if the discount is fixed in the loan
explanation: Per the Basis, early repayment for a discount rests on Da' Wa Ta'jjal, endorsed by the Fiqh Academy, provided the discount was not agreed upon earlier.

title: Revocation of Contracts by Exercise of a Cooling-Off Option
q: A sale contract states that the buyer "may cancel the deal" if a stated event occurs, without using the word "revocation". Is this a valid cooling-off option to revoke?
options: Yes, but only if confirmed later by a court
No, the option must be agreed in a separate contract
No, the technical word "revocation" must be used
Yes, any form indicating the option suffices
explanation: Per item 3, a cooling-off option to revoke can be stipulated in any form that indicates it; no specific word meaning revocation is required.

title: Agency and the Act of an Uncommissioned Agent (Fodooli)
q: Company X, as Bank A's agent, buys goods for the Bank. Company X then wants to buy the same goods from the Bank. What is the ruling?
options: Allowed by new offer and acceptance, guarantees kept separate
Allowed automatically, with no new offer and acceptance and no change of risk
Allowed, with the goods staying at the Bank's risk after sale
Not allowed, as an agent can never buy from his principal, even by offer and acceptance
explanation: Per 6/1/4, an agent may buy what he bought for the principal by offer and acceptance; guarantees stay separate and after the sale goods are at the agent's risk.

title: Mudarabah
q: A Mudarabah contract omits the profit ratio and there is no customary practice on it. The Mudarib has worked for a year. What is the outcome?
options: Void; and the Mudarib gets nothing for his year of work
Void; the Mudarib gets a common market price for his work
Valid; the profit is then shared equally by default between the two parties
Valid; all of the profit goes to the capital provider, as the Mudarib took no share
explanation: Per 8/4, absent a ratio and custom, the Mudarabah is void ab initio and the Mudarib receives a common market price for the services he provided.

title: Waqf
q: Ahmad acquired a building through prohibited means. He makes it a Waqf for general charitable causes and plans to live in one of its flats. Is that allowed?
options: Yes, if he pays fair rent to the Waqf for the flat he lives in
Yes, up to one-third of its usufruct
No, he may not benefit from this Waqf in any manner
Yes, since a Waqif may be his own beneficiary under the Waqf deed
explanation: Per 2/4/9, one holding assets taken by prohibited means may make them Waqf for general charitable causes, but may not benefit from it in any manner.

title: Investment Sukuk
q: What is the Shari'ah basis for permitting the issue of investment Sukuk?
options: Public need overrides the rules that would otherwise govern debt trading
They are a permissible form of benevolent loan
Market custom has accepted them like bonds
They are issued on the basis of Shari'ah-nominated contracts
explanation: Per the Basis, Sukuk are usually issued on Shari'ah-nominated contracts, so issuance on the basis of any of these contracts is acceptable.

title: Zakah
q: Bank A's board of directors decides the Bank should pay Zakah, but there is no Zakah law, no clause in the articles, and no general assembly resolution. Is the Bank committed to pay Zakah directly?
options: No; the duty then lies with shareholders and account holders
Yes; a board decision is sufficient to commit the Bank directly
Yes; every Islamic bank must pay Zakah directly
Yes, if the Shari'ah Board approves it
explanation: Per 2/2/1 and 2/2/5, the Institution pays Zakah directly only under an enforceable law, its articles, or a general assembly resolution; otherwise the shareholders pay.

title: Investment Sukuk
q: Ahmad leases a warehouse and issues equal-value certificates to sublease its usufruct, so that the holders own the usufruct and receive the rental. What type of Sukuk are these?
options: Certificates of ownership in leased assets
Certificates of ownership of usufructs of existing assets
Certificates of ownership of usufructs of described future assets
Certificates of ownership of services of a specified party
explanation: Per 3/2/1/2, certificates issued by the lessee (owner of the usufruct) of an existing asset to sublease it are certificates of ownership of usufructs of existing assets.

title: Sale of Commodities in Organized Markets
q: Company X, as agent, reports to Bank A only an inclusive purchase price that silently includes its brokerage fee. What does the standard require instead?
options: The fee must be stated separately from the purchase price
The fee must be paid by the end buyer only and not by the principal
The fee may stay merged in the price if it is below the market rate
The fee must be an undivided share of the profit from the sale
explanation: Per 4/2/9, merging the agency compensation into the price is prohibited; the fee must be mentioned and deducted from, or added to, the price.

title: Gold and Its Trading Parameters in Shari’ah
q: Bank A charges a fee for a service that involves exchanging a customer's gold for other gold. How must the fee be set?
options: No fee may be charged for such a service
As a percentage of the gold's market value
At any amount the parties agree upon
Based on the actual expenses of the service
explanation: Per 10/7, fees for safekeeping, allocation, minting and delivery are permissible; if the service involves gold-for-gold exchange, the fee is based on actual expenses.

title: Zakah
q: Bank A gives Zakah to a poor debtor, who then voluntarily uses it to repay his debt to the Bank, with no prior condition or collusion. Is this acceptable?
options: No, a debtor who receives Zakah may never use it to repay the payer
Yes, even if it was a stated condition
Yes, absent collusion or a pre-stated condition
No, unless a court approves it
explanation: Per 10/1, Zakah recipients may repay their debts out of the Zakah they receive from their creditors, provided there is no collusion or pre-stated condition.

title: Monetization (Tawarruq)
q: A trainee asks why the standard forbids linking the deferred purchase and the spot sale in Monetization. What reason does the Shari'ah basis give?
options: It turns the transaction into a Salam contract
It prevents the Institution from earning a profit margin
It makes the deferred price unknown at the time of contracting
It commits the client to sell at once, before receiving it
explanation: The Shari'ah basis: joining the contracts imposes a commitment on the client to sell right away, so the immediate transfer may not enable him to receive the commodity.

title: Guarantees
q: Company X deposits goods with Bank A for safekeeping and requires a mortgage from the Bank to cover any loss of the goods from any cause. Is this allowed?
options: No, no security may ever be sought in deposits
Yes, if the Bank charges a safekeeping fee
No, unless limited to misconduct, negligence or breach
Yes, as a guarantee may be stipulated in any contract whatsoever
explanation: Per 2/2/1, stipulating a guarantee or mortgage in trust contracts (agency, deposits) is not allowed, except to cover misconduct, negligence or breach.

title: Islamic Reinsurance
q: Islamic Insurance Company X wants to hold back part of the premiums due to a traditional reinsurer to keep liquidity, without paying interest. What arrangement is allowed?
options: Withhold all premiums until claims are settled
Agree to retain a portion of the premiums due to the reinsurer
Lend the premiums to the reinsurer as Qard Hasan until claims are settled
Hold reserves for the reinsurer and pay it interest
explanation: Per 6/2, the Islamic insurer and the traditional reinsurer may agree that a portion of premiums payable to the reinsurer be retained by the Islamic insurer.

title: Unilateral and Bilateral Promise
q: Ahmad tells a shop he will buy a phone from it next month. The shop does nothing in reliance on this. Ahmad then changes his mind without excuse. What is the position?
options: He breached a religious obligation, but is not legally bound
He is legally bound to buy the phone, since a promise to buy always binds the promisor
He must pay the shop its expected profit
He committed no wrong at all, legal or religious
explanation: Per 3/4, fulfilling a promise is a religious obligation and breaking it without excuse is a sin, but it is legally binding only when it causes the promisee to incur a liability.

title: Al-Wakalah Bi Al-Istithmar (Investment Agency)
q: Bank A, as unrestricted investment agent, invests the agency funds in its Mudarabah portfolio. Per the Shari'ah basis, why is it entitled to the agency fee and not Mudarabah profit?
options: The principal acts as Mudarib in the portfolio
Agency funds cannot generate any profit
Its contract with the principal is agency, not Mudarabah
Mudarabah profit is always given to charity when the funds come from an agency
explanation: Per the basis, the agent's contract is agency, not Mudarabah; even if funds go into a Mudarabah portfolio, it earns the agency commission, not Mudarabah profit.

title: Irrigation Partnership (Musaqat)
q: Before the crop materializes, an orchard owner bars the worker from the trees and, when asked, still refuses to let him complete the work. What is the worker entitled to?
options: A wage at the market rate for similar work
Double his share, as a penalty on the owner
Nothing, as no crop has materialized yet
His stipulated share of the expected crop
explanation: Per 8/5, if the owner does not enable the worker before the crop materializes and refuses when asked, the worker is entitled to the market wage for similar work.

title: Online Financial Dealings
q: Ahmad buys computer software from Company X's website. When does possession in the strict Shari'ah sense take place?
options: When he pays the price by bank card online
When he clicks to accept the offer shown on the seller's website
When Company X sends him an invoice by e-mail
When he downloads it to his computer after signing
explanation: Per 7/2, for software and the like, possession occurs when the purchaser, after signing, downloads it from the website to his personal computer.

title: Payment Cards
q: Under Bank A's Qard Hasan card with fees, how is the amount owed from card usage settled by Ahmad?
options: In instalments with a profit margin added to the principal
In equal monthly instalments, with no increase
In one lump payment at the end of the card year, with no increase
In instalments with interest after a grace period
explanation: Per 6/1/1, the owed amount is settled in equal monthly instalments on set dates, without increase in the loan principal for instalments.

title: Procrastinating Debtor
q: Bank A argues that a late payment compensation clause is valid since the customer freely agreed to it. Why is it null and void per the Shari'ah basis?
options: Any increase in the amount of a debt is Riba
Courts cannot reliably assess such losses
It is unfair to debtors who are insolvent
It conflicts with the acceleration clause
explanation: Per the Basis, compensation for delay in a debt is Riba and void; conditions that make the impermissible permissible are not binding.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: The rules of Sharikat al-'Inan apply to a stock company except in which respects?
options: Agency of the managers and trust in holding assets
Shareholders' limited liability and no unilateral termination
Use of capital in monetary form and the valuation of non-monetary contributions
Profit sharing and loss bearing in proportion to the capital shares held
explanation: Per 4/1/1/1, the 'Inan rules apply except the limited liability of shareholders and that the company cannot be unilaterally terminated by one party or a minority.

title: Possession (Qabd)
q: A seller asks why he is discharged by relinquishing ascertained movables rather than placing them in the buyer's hands. What reason does the Basis give?
options: Movables have no value until they are physically moved by the buyer or seller
Custom forbids sellers from touching sold goods once the price is agreed
Physical taking is the taker's act, beyond the seller's ability
The buyer always bears the delivery expenses, so the seller is discharged
explanation: Per the Basis, the obligor must be able to discharge himself; relinquishing is within his ability, while physical taking is a voluntary act of the taker.

title: Sale of Commodities in Organized Markets
q: Bank A is offered a commodity swap as practised in exchanges. What reason does the Basis give for prohibiting such swaps?
options: They are concluded for overly long periods with no fixed end date
They are concluded only between banks
Commodity prices in swaps are unknown
No real exchange occurs; they usually involve interest, 'Inah
explanation: Per the Basis, in swaps no actual exchange of counter-values takes place, and they usually constitute interest payment, 'Inah and deferment of one counter-value.

title: Agency and the Act of an Uncommissioned Agent (Fodooli)
q: A debtor agrees that, if he defaults, his own assets will be placed under the management of his creditor. What form of agency is this?
options: Future agency
Act of an uncommissioned agent
Conditional agency
Immediate agency
explanation: Per 2/2/3/2, conditional agency makes validity subject to a condition, e.g. a debtor placing his assets under his creditor's management on default.

title: Sale of Commodities in Organized Markets
q: An agent buys a commodity and resells it before taking delivery, either actually or legally. What does legal delivery include?
options: Transfer of liability by ascertaining the commodity sold
Receipt of the deferred price from the end buyer
Payment of the full purchase price to the seller of the commodity
Signing a general memorandum of agency
explanation: Per 4/2/4, selling before actual or legal delivery is prohibited; legal delivery includes transfer of liability by ascertaining the commodity from other things.

title: Protection of Capital and Investments
q: Investors question why Takaful cover may protect capital while conventional insurance may not. What is the basis given by the standard?
options: Takaful cover is issued only by government-owned institutions
Takaful is an undertaking to donate, not an exchange of counter-values
Takaful contributions are lower than conventional insurance premiums
Takaful covers only those losses caused by the manager's negligence
explanation: Per the basis, Takaful is an undertaking to make donations among participants, not Mu'awadah, aiming at cooperation; prohibitions on commercial insurance do not apply.

title: Al-Wakalah Bi Al-Istithmar (Investment Agency)
q: Bank A, as investment agent, negligently left the principal's funds uninvested for six months. The capital is intact. What is Bank A liable for?
options: The expected profit stated in the contract
Half of the expected profit for the period
Market-rate profit for the six months
Nothing for expected profit; only for capital
explanation: Per 7/1, where the agent is liable, liability is limited to the capital; it is not liable for expected profit whether capital was invested late or not at all.

title: Ju’alah
q: Ahmad offers a reward for finding his lost car. Bilal starts searching. Ahmad now wants to revoke the offer unilaterally. What is the ruling?
options: It became binding on Ahmad as soon as he made the offer
It became binding on Ahmad once the worker started work
Ahmad may revoke freely as Ju'alah is never binding on the offeror
Ahmad may revoke without any liability to Bilal for the search so far
explanation: Per 4/1, Ju'alah is in principle not binding, but it becomes binding for the Ja'il (offeror) when the worker commences work.

title: Distribution of Profit in Mudarabah-Based Investment Accounts
q: Bank A wants to change the profit sharing ratios of its investment accounts but finds individual correspondence too costly. What may it do?
options: Apply the new ratios immediately to the current period
Change them without any notice, as Mudarib
Notify or advertise it; if no protest, it applies from next period
It may never change ratios once the account is opened, even with consent
explanation: Per 2/2/8, the Institution may notify or advertise on its website; implicit acceptance arises if no protest within a period, effective from the beginning of the next period.

title: Protection of Capital and Investments
q: A Mudarabah agreement drafted by Bank A states that the Mudarib is liable for any loss of capital, whatever its cause. Is this stipulation permissible?
options: No; liability is limited to misconduct, negligence or breach
Yes, if the Mudarib freely agrees to it when signing the contract
Yes, if the Mudarib's profit share is raised in return for it
Yes, but only in a restricted Mudarabah with a specified activity
explanation: Per 3/6 and 5/1, it is not permissible to stipulate that the manager is unconditionally liable for loss of capital beyond wilful misconduct, negligence and breach.

title: Waqf
q: A Waqf superintendent wants to lease the Waqf shop to his dependant son at a rent above the market rent. What is the ruling?
options: Allowed if the lease is for one year only
