It breaches the debtor's right to consent
It may raise or cut the debt, harming either party
Past exchange rates are unknown to the parties
explanation: Per the Basis for 4/1/1/2(c), other rates may increase the debt against deferment (harming the debtor) or reduce the creditor's right.

title: Zakah
q: Bank A owns 70% of Subsidiary S, which does not pay its own Zakah. How is Zakah on Subsidiary S handled?
options: Bank A pays nothing; S's managers pay it
Bank A pays Zakah on 70% of S's share price
Bank A pays all of S's Zakah, since it controls the subsidiary
S's Zakah is computed alone; Bank A pays 70% of it
explanation: Per 4/2/5, the subsidiary's Zakah is calculated independently; the mother pays its proportion and the rest falls on the other parties (minority rights).

title: Murabahah
q: What evidence underlies the ban on deferred Murabahah in gold, silver and currencies?
options: The Hadith of Hibban Ibn Munqidh on the option of cancelling
The Hadith 'Do not sell what you own not' about absent goods
The Hadith requiring such exchange 'hand to hand'
The practice of Umar Ibn Al-Khattab among the Companions
explanation: The basis cites the Prophet's saying that exchange of gold with silver be 'hand to hand', without delay; currencies take the ruling of gold and silver.

title: Islamic Reinsurance
q: A new Islamic reinsurance company is being established. Which body should supervise its establishment and verify its contracts and documents?
options: A Shari'ah Supervisory Board formed for it
Its external auditor only
The Shari'ah board of the largest participant
The board of directors acting alone
explanation: Per 8/2, a Shari'ah Supervisory Board is formed to supervise establishment, verify contracts and documents, review applications and report on activities.

title: Hawalah
q: A Hawalah takes effect today, but the parties agree that Zaid, the payer, will pay the transferred debt on 31 December. Is this permitted?
options: Yes, if Zaid pays an added profit
Yes, payment of the transferred debt may be deferred
No, deferring payment makes the Hawalah itself contingent
No, payment must be made on the spot
explanation: Per 4/3, the transfer itself must be immediate, but it is permissible to defer payment of the transferred debt until a future specified date.

title: Istisna’a and Parallel Istisna’a
q: During an Istisna'a, a force majeure event sharply raises the cost of materials. How may the contract price be amended?
options: It may never be changed once it has been agreed
Only upwards, by the manufacturer acting alone
Only by adding a charge for the extra time needed
By agreement, arbitration or court, up or down
explanation: Per 4/2/1, the price may be amended upwards or downwards for force majeure by agreement, arbitration or judicial procedure, read with 4/1/3.

title: Monetization (Tawarruq)
q: A customer needing cash asks Bank B to arrange Monetization using gold bars held in the Bank's vault as the commodity. What is the ruling?
options: Not permitted: gold, silver or currency cannot be the commodity
Permitted if the gold is identified by vault certificates
Permitted if the customer receives the gold constructively
Permitted, as gold is a real commodity owned and held by the Bank
explanation: Per 4/1, in Monetization the commodity sold shall not be gold or silver or any type of currency.

title: Murabahah
q: Supplier S is 60% owned by Customer C. C asks Bank A to buy goods from S and sell them to him by Murabahah. What is the ruling?
options: Permitted, as C's share in S is below 75%
Permitted if the Bank takes Hamish Jiddiyyah
Permitted, since S is a separate company
Not permitted, since S is majority owned by C
explanation: Per 2/2/3, the supplying party may not be wholly or majority (more than 50%) owned by the customer; such a deal is tantamount to 'Inah.

title: Islamic Insurance
q: Which principle does the basis cite as the ground for indemnity in Islamic insurance?
options: What matters is intentions and meanings, not words and forms
Gain accompanies liability for loss, so the insurer takes the profit
One should neither tolerate harm nor cause it
Necessity makes the prohibited permissible
explanation: The basis grounds indemnity on the principle that one should neither tolerate harm nor cause it to others, with fair, non-obsessive indemnification.

title: Zakah
q: According to the Shari'ah basis of the standard, why is it impossible to imagine a debt arising from commodities purchased through Salam?
options: The goods are delivered at the time of contract
The capital (price) has to be paid in advance
The seller bears all the risk until delivery
Salam goods are always exempt from Zakah
explanation: The Shari'ah basis states it is impossible to imagine a debt from commodities bought through Salam, because the capital (price) has to be paid in advance.

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: Part of a leased building collapses, impairing the expected benefit. The lessee is not at fault. What options does the lessee have?
options: Only sub-lease the remaining part of the building
Only continue the lease at the full agreed rent until term
Terminate, or waive it and agree an amended rent
Only claim the cost of repairs from the lessor
explanation: Per 7/1/5, on partial destruction impairing benefit, the lessee may terminate; or he and the lessor may agree to amend the rent if he waives termination.

title: Liability of the Investment Manager
q: Rab Al Maal claims that the Mudarib's negligence caused a loss; the contract is silent on the evidentiary burden. Initially, who must prove the claim?
options: Whoever holds the larger share of the capital
Rab Al Maal, as the party making the claim
The Mudarib, who must prove he was not negligent
Both parties equally, before an arbitrator
explanation: Per item 6, as an initial presumption, the burden of proving misconduct or negligence lies on the claimant, not the investment manager.

title: Revocation of Contracts by Exercise of a Cooling-Off Option
q: Bank A's contract allows it to accelerate all installments. A solvent customer has missed one installment. Under the standard, may Bank A accelerate now?
options: No, it requires failure to pay two or more instalments
Yes, without notifying the customer beforehand
Yes, any single missed installment is sufficient
No, acceleration is never allowed for solvent debtors
explanation: Per 11/3, a creditor may stipulate acceleration, after notifying the debtor, if a solvent debtor fails to pay two or more instalments.

title: Irrigation Partnership (Musaqat)
q: A Musaqat contract gives the worker the first 1,000 kg of dates harvested and the owner the rest. Is this share arrangement valid?
options: Yes, if the owner guarantees the 1,000 kg
Yes, provided the harvest exceeds 1,000 kg
Yes, since the worker's quantity is fixed and known, which removes any Gharar
No; each party needs a defined, indivisible share of produce
explanation: Per 5/1, the contract should stipulate for each party a predetermined, defined, indivisible share of the produce.

title: Payment Cards
q: Bank A allows prepaid cardholders to spend beyond their balance, charging a fee proportional to the excess. What is the ruling?
options: Permitted, if the fee is fixed in the terms
Permitted, as a prepaid card is not a loan
Not permitted, as it leads to lending on interest
Permitted, if the excess is settled within a month
explanation: Per 4/2/1, a prepaid card should not lead to lending on interest, e.g., allowing use beyond the balance (overdrawing) against a consideration.

title: Financial Paper (Shares and Bonds)
q: Shareholders object to a proposed class of shares with priority in profit. On what basis does the standard prohibit such preference shares?
options: They sever participation in profit and wrong others
They turn the corporation into a Qard with its holders
They make the market price of the shares unknown
They prevent the shares from being traded on markets
explanation: Per the Basis, preference shares lead to severance of participation in profit and imposition of injustice on other shareholders.

title: Zakah
q: Company X holds cash in US dollars while its financial statements are in a local currency. How is Zakah on this cash determined?
options: At the historical rate when the dollars were bought
In local currency at the exchange rate on the due date
At the average rate of the year
Only in US dollars, without conversion
explanation: Per 5/1/1, Zakah on foreign currency cash is paid from its local currency equivalent at the prevailing exchange rate on the date Zakah is due.

title: Documentary Credit
q: A client's credit is only partly covered. Bank A proposes to pay the uncovered part to the beneficiary as a loan to the client bearing interest. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible if the client agreed in advance
Permissible if the interest equals actual cost
Permissible, as the loan arises from a guarantee
Not permissible, as the credit would include interest
explanation: Per 3/1/3, the Institution may not deal in credit that includes interest, explicitly as in a loan on payment of amounts not covered, or impliedly.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: Partners terminate a Sharikah on the basis of constructive liquidation; some assets are valued but not sold. How are these unsold assets treated?
options: As property of the partner with the largest share
As assets that must be sold within one year
As the capital of a new partnership between the parties
As a debt owed by the managing partner to the other partners after liquidation
explanation: Per 3/1/6/3, in constructive liquidation the Sharikah is regarded as ended and a new partnership begun, with the valued unsold assets as its capital.

title: Competitions and Prizes
q: Which text does the standard cite as evidence for the permissibility of prizes in competitions?
options: The account of Yusuf's brothers going racing
Ayishah's foot race with the Prophet: "this for that"
The race of the she-camel al-Adhbaa'
No prizes except on camelback, horseback or spear
explanation: The Basis cites the Hadith: no prizes on racing except on camelback, horseback (or the like) or spear throwing; Sabq involves prizes.

title: Stipulations and Ethics of Fatwa in the Institutional Framework
q: A new financial product has no explicit text in the Qur'an and Sunnah and is not discussed in Fiqh literature. Should the board refrain from issuing Fatwa?
options: Yes, Fatwa needs an explicit text in the Qur'an or Sunnah
No, it may issue Fatwa by Shari'ah-sanctioned deduction
No, it should permit it by default
Yes, until Fiqh literature discusses the same product
explanation: Per 7/3, absence of explicit texts or Fiqh literature does not justify refraining from Fatwa; it may be derived via Shari'ah-sanctioned methods.

title: Impact of Contingent Incidents on Commitments
q: In an Ijarah, an incidental excuse arises causing the lessee abnormal harm, but the acceptability of his excuse is doubtful. How is the issue resolved?
options: By mutual agreement or by resort to law
By automatic termination of the Ijarah at the lessee's request
By the lessor's sole decision, as owner of the leased asset
By continuing the lease with no possibility of termination
explanation: Per 5/4, the harmed party may terminate for abnormal harm, and an obvious excuse permits termination; a doubtful excuse is resolved by mutual agreement or by law.

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: In an Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek, which of these is a recognised method of transferring title to the lessee?
options: A sale contract signed now, effective at lease end
A transfer clause inside the Ijarah contract itself
Transfer on registration under local law
A promise to give it as a gift for no consideration
explanation: Per 8/1, methods include a promise to sell (token, market value or accelerated rental), a promise of gift, or a gift contingent on paying remaining instalments.

title: Guarantees
q: Bakr guarantees Ahmad's future debt, with liability starting on 1 July. On 1 June, before any debt arises, Bakr wants to withdraw. Can he?
options: No, a guarantee once given can never be withdrawn by the guarantor
Yes, by notifying the creditor before the debt arises
Yes, even without notifying the creditor
Only with the debtor's written consent
explanation: Per 3/1/4 and 3/2, a guarantee contingent on a future date may be withdrawn by notifying the creditor before the guaranteed obligation arises.

title: Murabahah
q: Bank A already owns a stock of goods that it can readily sell to other buyers. Must it obtain a promise to purchase before selling them by Murabahah?
options: Yes, whenever the price is paid on deferred terms
No, but it must then take 'Arboun from the buyer
No, the promise is not integral to Murabahah
Yes, a Murabahah is invalid without a promise
explanation: Per 2/3/2, the promise is not integral to Murabahah; it only assures completion, so if the Institution has other ways to sell, it may not need it.

title: Monetization (Tawarruq)
q: At the time of signing a Monetization purchase contract, the commodity is not available at Bank A's premises. What must the Bank give the customer?
options: A full description or sample, with quantity and storage place
A written undertaking to deliver the commodity within a week
Only the invoice issued by the original supplier
A guarantee that the commodity will be resold at a fixed price
explanation: Per 4/3, if the commodity is not available at signing, the client shall be given a full description or a sample indicating its quantity and place of storage.

title: Commercial Papers
q: Company X wants to exchange currencies with Bank A, paying with an ordinary (uncertified) cheque drawn on its account. What is the ruling?
options: Permitted if Bank A collects the cheque some days later
Permitted, since all cheques are payable at sight, which equals possession
Permitted if Company X's account is usually well funded with sufficient balance
Not permitted: it is not constructive possession of the amount
explanation: Per 7/2, an ordinary cheque that is not banker's or certified is not constructive possession; it may not be used where possession is stipulated.

title: Ju’alah
q: The period of a Ju'alah expires; the worker has done part of the work, which benefits the offeror, but the result is not near. What is the worker entitled to?
options: Reasonable wages (Ujrat al-Mithl)
Nothing, as the result was not achieved
The full agreed Ju'l
A share of the offeror's profits
explanation: Per 5/3/1/3, when the period is over and the worker has done part of the work that will benefit the offeror, he is entitled to reasonable wages (Ujrat al-Mithl).

title: Loan (Qard)
q: At repayment, a borrower voluntarily gives the lender a better camel than the one borrowed. Which evidence supports the permissibility of this?
options: The hadith of Anas on refusing gifts and free rides from the borrower
Abu Rafi': 'The best people are those who do better in repayment'
The hadith: 'A Salaf and a sale are not permitted'
The maxim: 'Gains are based on bearing of costs'
explanation: Per the Basis, the hadith of Abu Rafi', where the Prophet repaid a young camel with a better one, supports an unstipulated excess at repayment.

title: Islamic Insurance
q: Ahmad pays his contribution to an Islamic insurance fund and later suffers a covered loss. What is the nature of the relationship between Ahmad and the fund?
options: Loan on paying, repayment of the loan on loss
Mudarabah on paying, profit share on loss
Donation commitment on paying, indemnity commitment on loss
Sale of cover on paying contributions, gift of the indemnity on loss
explanation: Per 4/3, the policyholder-fund relationship is a donation commitment when contributing and an indemnification commitment when compensating injury.

title: Mudarabah
q: Under a separate agreement independent of the Mudarabah, the Mudarib is hired for a fee to do work not customarily part of Mudarabah operations. If this agreement ends, what happens?
options: The Mudarib loses his profit share
The fee converts into a share of profit
The Mudarabah contract terminates as well
The Mudarabah contract is not affected
explanation: Per 8/2, such a separate agreement is permissible; its independence means that terminating it will not affect the Mudarabah contract.

title: Waqf
q: Which evidence does the standard cite for the validity of a Waqf of movable assets, such as weapons or equipment?
options: Umar's Waqf of his land in Khaybar, a fixed real property
Banū Najjār's Waqf of their orchard, offered to the Prophet
Khālid kept his armour and weapons for Allah's Cause
Sa'd's orchard given on his mother's behalf
explanation: Basis 2/4/7: the Prophet said Khālid kept his armour and weapons for Allah's Cause; this is also the majority view and IIFA Res. 181.

title: Guarantees
q: Bank A manages a Mudarabah in foreign currency and offers to guarantee investors against exchange rate fluctuations. What is the ruling?
options: Prohibited, as it amounts to guaranteeing the capital
Permitted if limited to major currencies
Permitted, as it covers only currency risk and not the capital
Permitted if disclosed in the prospectus
explanation: Per 3/3/4, a Mudarib, partner or investment agent may not guarantee currency fluctuations, as this amounts to guaranteeing others' capital.

title: Insolvency
q: Bank A's deferred Murabahah receivable from Ahmad is not yet due when he is declared insolvent. What happens to this receivable?
options: It is extinguished by the declaration of insolvency
It becomes due and Bank A shares the assets with due creditors
It stays deferred and Bank A must wait until maturity, being paid after all due creditors
It becomes due but ranks after all originally due debts
explanation: Per 5/5/1, all the debtor's undue debts become due, and their creditors share the sequestered assets with the creditors of due debts.

title: Murabahah
q: Bank A has paid a supplier but has not yet taken possession of the goods at the delivery location. Under the standard, when does the risk of the goods transfer to the Bank?
options: Upon the Bank's taking possession of the goods
Upon the Bank's payment of the price
Upon the signing of the Murabahah contract
Upon the customer's promise to purchase
explanation: Per 3/2/5, responsibility for the risk attached to the item is transferred to the Institution upon its taking possession of the item.

title: Banking Services in Islamic Banks
q: A customer asks Bank A to keep his Shari'ah-accepted share certificates and title deeds in safe custody. May the Bank charge for this?
options: No, custody must be offered free of charge
No, as custody is a form of lending
Yes, but only as a share of the papers' profits
Yes, it may act as custodian against a fee
explanation: Per 2/1, Institutions may receive Shari'ah-accepted documents and financial papers as custodian and may charge fees for such services.

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: Bank A links later rentals to a benchmark. To which principle does the Shari'ah basis liken this method?
options: Hamish Jiddiyyah (security deposit taken from the customer)
Ujrat al-Mithl (prevailing market rate of rental)
Bay' al-Bara'ah (sale on an 'as is' basis without liability)
Muhaya'ah (time-sharing of usufruct between co-owners)
explanation: The basis: using a benchmark for later rentals makes them known, is similar to Ujrat al-Mithl and does not lead to dispute.

title: Revocation of Contracts by Exercise of a Cooling-Off Option
q: A buyer with a cooling-off option revokes the sale of a sheep after delivery. Between delivery and revocation, the sheep gave birth to a lamb. Who owns the lamb?
options: The seller, as the lamb is part of the sale item
The seller, as revocation operates retroactively
The buyer, as the growth occurred after delivery
Both parties, shared in proportion to the price
explanation: Per item 8, revocation nullifies the contract at the moment of revocation; separate growth after delivery belongs to the buyer, before delivery to the seller.

title: Salam and Parallel Salam
q: Bank A wants to buy 'this car parked in the dealer's yard' by Salam, for delivery in three months. What is the ruling?
options: Permitted, as the car is clearly identified and seen
Not permitted, as Salam is not for a specific item
Permitted if the price is paid on the spot
Permitted if the dealer gives a guarantee
explanation: Per 3/2/3, Salam is not permitted for anything specific like 'this car'.

title: Hiring of Persons
q: A hiring contract's pay instalments are payable monthly. The parties now consent to raise the pay for months not yet served. Is this permitted?
options: Yes, but only for past unpaid months
No; the agreed pay can never be changed once the contract is signed
Yes; pay for future periods can be amended by consent
No; changes need a new framework agreement
explanation: Per 5/2/5, it is permissible, with both parties' consent, to amend the pay of future periods in which the service has not yet been benefited from.

title: Agency and the Act of an Uncommissioned Agent (Fodooli)
q: An agent sells the principal's goods to his adult son, who is not under his guardianship, at a fair price. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible unless it involves injustice or favoritism
Permissible only if the price exceeds market price
Not permissible without the principal's consent
Not permissible in any case, as the son is a relative
explanation: Per 6/1/1, deals with ascendants or descendants not under the agent's guardianship (and not his spouse) are permissible unless they involve injustice or favoritism.

title: Hawalah
q: Per the Shari'ah basis, why must the transferee in a restricted Hawalah take no more than the amount of his own debt?
options: To protect the payer's other creditors
To preserve the transferor's recourse
To keep the two debts in one currency
To avoid Riba
explanation: Per the Basis, the required similarity in amount means the transferee must not take more than his actual debt, the intention being to avoid Riba.

title: Mortgage and its Contemporary Applications
q: The mortgagor permits Bank A to use a mortgaged apartment free of charge during the mortgage. What is the ruling?
options: Impermissible; the Bank may use it only against normal pay
Permissible, if the use is for a short period
Permissible, since the mortgagor gave permission
Impermissible, as the mortgagee may not use it at all, even for a fee
explanation: Per 3/2/9, the mortgagee may not enjoy free benefit of the asset with or without permission, but may use it with permission against the normal pay for similar assets.

title: Istisna’a and Parallel Istisna’a
q: Bank A's actual cost of completing an Istisna'a proves much lower than estimated, thanks to a discount in its Parallel Istisna'a. Must it pass a discount to the customer?
options: Yes, if the saving exceeds 10%
Yes, the full amount of the saving made by the Bank
Yes, in proportion to the saving
No, the customer has no claim to the saving
explanation: Per 3/2/6, the Institution need not give a discount when costs are substantially lower; likewise it cannot charge more if they are higher.

title: Islamic Insurance
q: An Islamic insurance company drafts its documents. What must be stipulated about each participant's contribution?
options: He sells it to the company against the cover
He keeps ownership of it until a claim arises
He donates it and its returns to the insurance account
He lends it to the company until the policy ends and then recovers it
explanation: Per 5/1, it should be stipulated that the participant donates his contribution and its returns to the insurance account for paying indemnity.

title: Al-Wakalah Bi Al-Istithmar (Investment Agency)
q: Company X used investment agency financing from Bank A for working capital and no longer needs it. How may the relationship be ended?
options: By a buy-out of Bank A's share at face value fixed at the outset
By Takharuj: pro-rata division or a buy-out at a price then agreed
By Bank A keeping its share until the original term ends
By Company X repaying the amount plus a fixed return
explanation: Per 12/2, the relationship may be terminated by Takharuj: the joint account is distributed pro-rata or one party buys the other's share at a price agreed at that time.

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: Why does the Shari'ah basis bar a lessor from excluding liability for defects in the leased asset?
options: Rent for impaired usufruct is unjust enrichment
Defects are always caused by the lessee's own use
Such clauses are allowed only in sales, not in leases
The lessee bears all major maintenance of the asset
explanation: The basis: such a condition defeats the purpose of exchanging usufruct for rentals; if usufruct is impaired, receiving rentals becomes unjust enrichment.

title: Investment Sukuk
q: In Muzara'ah Sukuk, the certificate holders act as workers who undertake the agricultural work. When may they trade their certificates?
options: At any time, as with Mugharasah certificates
Immediately after closing of subscription
As soon as activity commences after allotment
Not before the maturity of the fruits and plants
explanation: Per 5/2/17, where Muzara'ah or Musaqat holders act as workers, trading is not permissible before the maturity of the fruits and plants.

title: Hawalah
q: After a restricted Hawalah, Ahmad, the transferor, asks Zaid to pay him directly the amount Zaid owes him. Is Ahmad entitled to it?
options: Yes, because Zaid's debt is still legally owed to Ahmad
No, that right has passed to the transferee
Yes, if Bakr has not yet claimed it
Yes, but only for half of the amount
explanation: Per 8, after a restricted Hawalah the transferor may not reclaim from the payer the amount transferred, as the right to receive it has passed to the transferee.

title: Istisna’a and Parallel Istisna’a
q: Bank A contracts by Istisna'a to sell a specific, identified car it does not own. Which Hadith does the Shari'ah basis cite against this?
options: 'Give a worker his wages before his sweat dries'
'Write off a portion of your debt'
'Do not sell what you own not'
'Muslims are bound by their conditions'
explanation: The basis: Istisna'a is a sale by specification; selling a specific identified item not owned violates the Hadith 'Do not sell what you own not'.

title: Islamic Reinsurance
q: Islamic Insurance Company X reinsures 25% of every policy it issues, whether within or beyond its own capacity. Which form of reinsurance request is this?
options: Loss reinsurance
Risk sharing reinsurance
Selective reinsurance
Excess risk reinsurance
explanation: Per 5/1, in risk sharing reinsurance the insurer seeks reinsurance for a percentage (e.g. 50% or 25%) of its policies, within or in excess of its own capacity.

title: Hawalah
q: Zaid, the payer, dies solvent before paying the transferred debt. What is the effect on the Hawalah?
options: It is annulled; the debt is extinguished
It stands, but payment waits for the heirs' consent
It stands; the transferee claims from Zaid's estate
It is annulled; the transferee claims from Ahmad
explanation: Per 10/2, the payer's death does not annul Hawalah; the transferee has recourse against his estate or guarantor, and to the transferor only if he died bankrupt.

title: Irrigation Partnership (Musaqat)
q: The agreed Musaqat term ends, but the crop has not yet materialized. What options does the worker have?
options: Stop, or continue without a wage until the crop appears
Continue and claim a market wage for the extra time
Demand that the owner extend at a higher share
Stop and claim a market wage for the full term
explanation: Per 10/2, if the crop does not materialize within the term, the worker may stop working or continue without a wage until it materializes and then take his share.

title: Gold and Its Trading Parameters in Shari’ah
q: A customer leases gold ingots from Bank A, and the parties agree that the rent will be paid in gold. What is the ruling?
options: Not permissible, being gold for gold with excess
Permissible only if rent equals the ingots' weight
Not permissible unless the rent is paid on spot
Permissible, even though the leased asset is gold
explanation: Per 5/3/3, the rent (Ujrah) may be paid in gold even if the leased asset is gold.

title: Indices
q: Bank A compares the returns of its fund managers with a market index to judge their performance. What is the ruling?
options: Not permissible unless the index is Islamic
Permissible
Not permissible, as it is trading in an index
Permissible only for sectoral indices
explanation: Per 5/1, it is permissible to use indices to judge the performance of specialized managers by comparing their returns to the indices.

title: Agency and the Act of an Uncommissioned Agent (Fodooli)
q: Company X asks Bank A to act as its agent in extending interest-bearing loans to third parties for a fee. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible, if the Bank's fee is fixed in advance and not a share of interest
Permissible, since the Company could lend such funds personally with interest
Permissible, as agency covers all financial contracts that clients request
Not permissible: the subject matter is a Shari'ah-banned practice
explanation: Per 3/3/3, the subject matter of agency should not involve a Shari'ah-banned practice, like trading in impermissible commodities or usurious lending.

title: Sale of Debt
q: A customer asks Bank A to buy Shari'ah non-compliant bonds for him and hold them for later sale. What is the ruling?
options: Permitted, if held until maturity
Permitted, if sold for a commodity
Not permitted to trade in such bonds
Permitted, if bought at a discount
explanation: Per 9/2/1, trading in Shari'ah non-compliant bonds, by sale, purchase, assignment or otherwise, is not permitted.

title: Istisna’a and Parallel Istisna’a
q: Bank A offers two prices depending on whether a plant is delivered in 12 or 18 months. To which ruling does the Shari'ah basis liken this?
options: Giving a labourer wages that differ by finishing time
Taking 'Arboun to secure performance
Charging more for extending a debt's due date for payment
Setting the profit as a percentage of cost
explanation: The basis: Istisna'a is analogous to Ijarah, where a labourer may be offered two dinars if he finishes in one day or one dinar if in two days.

title: Trading in Currencies
q: A customer alone gives Bank A a binding promise to buy USD from it next month; the Bank makes no promise in return. What is the ruling?
options: Forbidden, as any binding promise in currency trading is void
Permissible only if the promise is non-binding
Permissible: a one-party promise is allowed even if binding
Permissible only if the Bank also promises to sell
explanation: Per 2/9/1, while a binding bilateral promise is forbidden, a promise from one party is permissible even if it is binding.

title: Waqf
q: Why, per the Shari'ah basis, does a beneficiary's rejection of a Waqf not nullify it?
options: Acceptance is needed only from the Waqif
He may drop his own rights but cannot nullify the Waqf
Rejection is valid only after the Waqif's death and not before it
A Waqf can only be nullified by a court
explanation: Per the basis (Hanafi view), the beneficiary can drop his own rights in the Waqf, but he cannot nullify the Waqf itself.

title: Agency and the Act of an Uncommissioned Agent (Fodooli)
q: Which Qur'anic passage does the Shari'ah basis cite for the permissibility of agency?
options: The verse on recording debts in writing when dealing for a specified term
The verse permitting trade and prohibiting Riba in all dealings
The verse on fulfilling contracts and obligations in all transactions
The sending of one with a silver coin to buy food in Al-Kahf
explanation: The basis cites Al-Kahf: 19, where one was sent to town with a silver coin to buy food, as the agent of the others.

title: Protection of Capital and Investments
q: A fund places part of its capital in Murabahah with strongly rated parties so that principal plus profit protects the initial capital, and invests the rest in Musharakah. Ruling?
options: It is a permissible diversification method to protect capital
It is permissible only if the Murabahah buyer guarantees the rest
It is prohibited as it amounts to guaranteeing the capital
It is a prohibited combination of two contracts in one
explanation: Per 4/2/7(b), dividing capital between Murabahah with strong-rated parties and Musharakah is a permissible diversification method to protect capital.

title: Waqf
q: A Waqf deed is silent about maintenance. The Waqf building now needs repairs. What does the standard provide?
options: Repair needs the Waqif's express stipulation in the Waqf deed
Repair takes priority even without the Waqif's stipulation
Beneficiaries are paid first, then repairs from what remains
Repair needs consent of all beneficiaries
explanation: Per 4/1, maintenance or repair takes priority over other expenditures, and it is not subject to express stipulation from the Waqif.

title: Procrastinating Debtor
q: Bank A's financing is secured by a mortgaged asset. May the contract require the debtor to mandate the Bank to sell the asset without recourse to the courts?
options: Yes, such a mandate may be stipulated
Yes, but only after the debtor's death
No, any sale must be ordered by a court
No, the Bank may only retain the asset
explanation: Per 2/1/5, the creditor may apply for sale of the mortgaged asset and may stipulate a mandate from the debtor to sell it without recourse to the courts.

title: Guarantees
q: Bank A sells by Murabahah on condition that it may freeze the buyer's current account. Per the Shari'ah basis, why is this barred?
options: It makes the Murabahah price uncertain
Current accounts cannot be pledged at all
It deprives the buyer of the profit he would earn on the account
It combines a deferred sale with a condition of a loan
explanation: Per the Basis, freezing a current account is like a deferred sale conditioned on a loan, which Shari'ah prohibits; freezing investment accounts is a pledge of funds.

title: Zakah
q: A family Waqf (al-Waqf al-Ahli) pays income to Ahmad's children; part of the income remains unspent at year end. Who pays Zakah on it?
options: The Waqf itself, on the whole property and all of its income at year end
The Waqf superintendent, on the gross income
The beneficiaries, on the unexpended income at year end
Nobody, as all Waqf is exempt from Zakah
explanation: Per 3/1/6, charitable Waqf is exempt; for family Waqf, the beneficiaries pay Zakah at year end on the portion of Waqf income that remains unexpended.

title: Waqf
q: A Waqif set a sequence: orphans of Town X, then students of Town X. No orphans remain in Town X. Where does the revenue go?
options: To the students, as the next body in the sequence
To general charitable causes chosen by the overseer
Back to the Waqif's heirs
To orphans of any similar town, as the Waqif's first choice
explanation: Per 10/2, on discontinuation of a beneficiary body, the Waqf goes to the next body if the Waqif arranged a sequence; otherwise to similar bodies.

title: Mudarabah
q: Per the Shari'ah basis, besides the capital not being available, why is a debt owed by the Mudarib barred as Mudarabah capital?
options: Debts carry no risk at all for the capital provider, who is the creditor
Debts cannot be valued in any currency at all while they remain unpaid
The creditor may seek extra return for extending the debt
The Mudarib would become a sleeping partner with no right to manage
explanation: Per the basis, it involves potential Riba: the creditor may be suspected of extending the debt tenure for extra consideration under the name of Mudarabah.

title: Murabahah
q: A Murabahah contract stipulates that all instalments fall due early if the customer delays payment without valid reason. How may Bank A apply this condition?
options: Only if a court approves the acceleration in advance
After notice and lapse of the time specified in it
It may not apply it at all, as the condition is invalid
Immediately on the first day of any delay in payment
explanation: Per 5/1, acceleration may be stipulated for refusal or delay without valid reason, after lapse of the time in a notice sent within a reasonable period.

title: Controls on Gharar in Financial Transactions
q: A trader sells Ahmad a commodity he does not have and will have to purchase from the market later. Which contracts are exceptions to the nullity of such a sale?
options: Any sale if the price is deferred
Ijarah and Ju'alah, subject to known rent
Murabahah and Musawamah, subject to disclosure
Salam and Istisna'a, subject to their conditions
explanation: Per 5/5, Gharar from sale of a non-owned commodity nullifies the sale; Salam and Istisna'a are exceptional cases subject to their conditions.

title: Ju’alah
q: Ahmad offers a Ju'alah reward and Bilal accepts but, before starting any work, Bilal revokes the contract. Is Bilal entitled to compensation?
options: No, revocation before work gives no compensation
Yes, half of the agreed reward, as he accepted the offer
Yes, the full reward as agreed, since he had accepted the offer
Yes, reasonable wages for his readiness to work during the period
explanation: Per 6/1, if the offeror or the worker revokes the contract prior to commencement of work, the worker is not entitled to compensation.

title: Payment Cards
q: Bank A, an Institution, issues charge cards. Ahmad delays settling his balance beyond the specified period. May Bank A stipulate interest on the delay?
options: Yes, once the grace period has lapsed
Yes, at a rate below the market rate
No, that would lead to lending on interest
Yes, as pre-agreed in the card terms
explanation: Per 4/3/1 (and 3/3/4), dealing with a charge card must not lead to lending on interest, including stipulating interest if the holder delays.

title: Impact of Contingent Incidents on Commitments
q: Company X is committed to deliver goods to Bank A. The goods are totally destroyed in Company X's warehouse before delivery to the Bank, with no act of the Bank. Who bears the loss?
options: Bank A, because ownership passed to it upon signing the contract
An insurer only; neither party bears any loss in such a case
Both parties equally, since the loss was not caused by either of them
Company X, the committed party, as delivery had not yet taken place
explanation: Per 5/2, if the object of commitment is damaged before delivery to the committing party, the loss is borne by the committed party.

title: Murabahah
q: Bank A buys goods on a 'sale or return' basis with a 10-day option. It presents them to the customer, who declines to buy. May the Bank still return them within the 10 days?
options: No, presenting the goods to the customer ends the option
Yes, mere presentation to the customer does not end the option
Yes, but only with a new consent from the supplier
No, the option ended when the customer signed his promise
explanation: Per 2/3/5, the option between the Institution and the supplier does not expire by mere presentation of the item to the customer, but by the actual sale to him.

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: A leased machine is destroyed due to the lessee's negligence. The machine is replaceable. What is the lessee's liability?
options: He pays its value fixed by the lessor
He has no liability, as he is a trustee
He pays only the remaining rentals
He must replace the machine
explanation: Per 7/1/4, the lessee holds the asset in a fiduciary capacity and is liable only for misconduct or negligence; then he replaces it if replaceable, else pays valued damage.

title: Impact of Contingent Incidents on Commitments
q: A supplier fails to deliver on time and the delivery becomes useless. Which condition must exist for the commitment to become null and void?
options: The failure is caused by an act of the supplier's own staff
The failure originates from objective rather than personal reasons
The failure originates from the supplier's own personal choice
The failure could have been avoided with reasonable effort
explanation: Per 5/1/1-5/1/3, failure must be absolutely inevitable, arise from objective rather than personal reasons, and be caused by an external party.

title: Islamic Reinsurance
q: For a large claim, Islamic Insurance Company X bears the first USD 20,000 and the reinsurer bears the rest of the compensation. Which form is this?
options: Loss reinsurance
Excess risk reinsurance
Selective reinsurance
Risk sharing reinsurance
explanation: Per 5/3, in loss reinsurance the reinsurer bears losses beyond an agreed limit, e.g. the insurer bears the first 20 thousand dollars and the reinsurer the rest.

title: Competitions and Prizes
q: Bank A offers prizes to investment account holders and proposes to fund them from the profits of those investment account holders. Is this allowed?
options: Yes, if the charity account bears part of the cost
Yes, since the prizes go back to the same holders
No, they may be paid from shareholders' funds instead
Yes, if holders consent in the account terms
explanation: Per 3/5/2/1, prizes are not paid from investment account funds, their holders' profits or charity accounts, but may be paid from shareholders' funds.

title: Financial Rights and How They Are Exercised and Transferred
q: Ahmad's house neighbours a house that is sold, but the two share no common easement rights. Does Ahmad have Shuf'ah as a neighbour?
options: Yes; every adjacent neighbour has Shuf'ah, whether or not they share common easements
Yes, if his house is larger than the sold one
Yes, if he offers a higher price than the buyer
No; a neighbour's Shuf'ah applies only with common easements
explanation: Per 7/1/2, the right of Shuf'ah enjoyed by a neighbour is applicable only when the two properties share common easement rights.

title: Irrigation Partnership (Musaqat)
q: An orchard owner signs a Musaqat with a 12-year-old boy as the worker. Which Shari'ah basis is cited for requiring legal competency?
options: "O you who believe! Fulfil (your) obligations", the verse on contracts
"Muslims are bound by their conditions"
"The Pen has been lifted from writing the deeds of three"
"There should be neither harm nor malice"
explanation: Per the basis, legal competency rests on the Hadith "The Pen has been lifted from writing the deeds of three", including the child until puberty.

title: Al-Wakalah Bi Al-Istithmar (Investment Agency)
q: An agent breached a 12% minimum-yield restriction while the market average was only 7%. Per the Shari'ah basis, why is he not liable up to the stipulated 12%?
options: That would be acquiring another's wealth by illegitimate means
The stipulated rate is void in every agency contract, so no restriction can be enforced
The principal should have consulted the market first
The agent's breach was advantageous to the principal
explanation: Per the basis, the agent compensates up to the market average for breach, but not a stipulated rate above it, as that would be acquiring another's wealth illegitimately.

title: Syndicated Financing
q: Which narration does the Shari'ah basis cite for paying syndication contributions in another currency at the day's exchange rate?
options: Urwah buying two sheep with one dinar and selling one of them
Ibn Umar selling camels at Al-Baqi' in dinars for dirhams
The Hadith forbidding two sales in one
Hakim Ibn Hizam buying sacrificial animals with the Prophet's money for a dinar
explanation: The basis cites Ibn Umar's Hadith on selling camels at Al-Baqi' in dinars and taking dirhams at the same day's rate before parting.

title: Credit Agreement
q: A client asks Bank A to extend the repayment date of his Murabahah debt by six months. What may the Bank charge for the rescheduling?
options: Only the actual expenses of the rescheduling transaction
A share of the client's profits during the extension
An additional return for the period of extension
A fixed fee proportional to the extension period
explanation: Per 5/3/2/4/1, the Institution should not obtain returns for extending the repayment date of debts; it charges only actual expenses of the rescheduling.

title: Loan (Qard)
q: Bank A proposes to lend to a customer on condition that the customer buys goods from it. Which hadith does the Shari'ah basis cite against this?
options: 'Gold for gold... like for like, from hand to hand'
'A Salaf and a sale (in one contract) are not permitted'
'The best people are those who do better in repayment'
'He who buys food is not to sell it until he measures it'
explanation: Per the Basis, the hadith 'A Salaf (loan) and sale are not permitted' shows that combining a Qard and a sale in one contract is impermissible.

title: Guarantees
q: Bank A acts as investment agent for a client and, within the same agency contract, guarantees the client's capital. Why is this prohibited?
options: Agency contracts may not contain conditions
Agents are never liable for anything, even for negligence
Guarantees must always be paid for by the client as a fee
It turns the transaction into an interest-based loan
explanation: Per 2/2/2, combining agency and guarantee conflicts with their nature; guaranteeing capital plus returns is like a loan repaid with an increase (Riba).

title: Gold and Its Trading Parameters in Shari’ah
q: A customer exchanges 21K gold jewelry for 18K gold jewelry at a shop, on spot. What must be equal for the exchange to be valid?
options: The market value of the two pieces at the time of the exchange
The karatage of the two pieces
The weight of pure gold in each countervalue
The total weight of the two pieces, including any other metals
explanation: Per 3/3/1/2, substances added for karatage are not intended per se; exchange must be spot and the pure gold weight in each countervalue equal.

title: Zakah
q: Islamic Insurance Company T asks whether Zakah is payable by its policyholders' insurance portfolio, which has an independent financial liability. What is the answer?
options: Yes, at 2.5% of its surplus, as the portfolio is treated as a separate company
Yes, but only on investment income
Yes, on contributions received
No Zakah is payable by the insurance portfolio
explanation: Per 5/3/5, the contributions form a fund with independent liability given as donation, not returnable; so no Zakah is payable by the insurance portfolio.

title: Conversion of a Conventional Bank to an Islamic Bank
q: To raise funds, converting Bank A enters Istisna'a contracts as manufacturer. Which condition does the standard attach for this purpose?
options: The price is paid on delivery of the asset
The price is deferred over instalments
The Istisna'a price is paid to the bank in advance
The price is paid by a third-party guarantor on delivery
explanation: Per 6/2/3, the bank may act as manufacturer in Istisna'a for funding, on condition the price is paid in advance, though deferment is generally allowed.

title: Stipulations and Ethics of Fatwa in the Institutional Framework
q: Bank A asks its board to issue all Fatwas strictly by the Madhab officially followed in its host country. What does the standard say?
options: It should not demand Fatwa by a specific Madhab
It must follow the Madhab of the board chairman
It may demand any Madhab it prefers
It must demand Fatwa by the official Madhab
explanation: Per 6/4, the Institution should not demand Fatwa per a specific Madhab, even the official one, though a school followed by the courts deserves attention.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: Partnership goods held by the managing partner are destroyed by a fire with no misconduct, negligence or breach on his part. Is the managing partner liable?
options: Yes, for half the loss as a shared responsibility
No, partners hold Sharikah assets on a trust basis
Yes, the managing partner always guarantees the assets
Yes, if he receives a larger profit share
explanation: Per 3/1/4/1, partners maintain the assets on a trust basis; no one is liable except for misconduct, negligence or breach of contract.

title: Settlement of Debt by Set-Off
q: Bank A is offered a currency swap in which interest-based securities are set off against interest-based securities. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible because the currencies differ
Permissible if the parties mutually consent
Not permissible, as it is based on Riba
Permissible as a contractual set-off
explanation: Per 5, currency swaps concluded on the basis of Riba are not permissible, since interest-based securities are set off against interest-based securities.

title: Arbitration
q: An Institution concluded an arbitration verbally. According to the Shari'ah basis, what is needed for the arbitration to be legally accepted?
options: It must be approved by the Shari'ah Supervisory Board
It must be written and signed by arbitrators and parties
Nothing; verbal arbitration alone is enough to be legally accepted
It must be attested by two witnesses only
explanation: Per the basis, arbitration may be verbal in Shari'ah, but to be legally accepted it needs to be written and signed by the arbitrators and the parties.

title: Insolvency
q: Proceeds from selling an insolvent debtor's assets are available. Which claim should be paid first?
options: Fees of the administrators who manage the sale and distribution
Claims of unsecured creditors on a pro-rata basis
Claims of the creditor holding the largest debt
Claims of secured creditors, as they hold a security over specific assets of the debtor
explanation: Per 8/3/1, priority goes to the fees of the administrators and their assistants who manage the sale and distribution, then secured creditors (8/3/2).

title: Buyback
q: In a joint enterprise, Partner A gives Partner B a binding promise to buy back B's share at a price fixed today, regardless of market value then. What is the ruling?
options: Permitted, as a normal feature of Diminishing Musharaka
Permitted, if documented in a separate deed
Permitted, since the promise is unilateral and the price is known
Not permitted; it contradicts sharing risk and reward
explanation: Per 5/4/2, such a promise at a specified price is not permitted; it is permitted at market value or a price agreed at performance.

title: Gold and Its Trading Parameters in Shari’ah
q: Company X sells gold bars to a car dealer in exchange for cars to be delivered in three months. What is the ruling?
options: Not permissible; both must be delivered at the session
Permissible; spot exchange is not required here
Permissible only if the cars arrive within a month
Not permissible; gold may be sold only for currencies
explanation: Per 3/1/4 and 3/2/1, gold sold for commodities other than gold, silver or currencies may be sold at any price with deferment of one countervalue.

title: Guarantees
q: Bank A is asked to guarantee a client's debt without any right of recourse to the client. When may it do so?
options: Only if shareholders and investors authorised such donations
Whenever its management finds the guarantee commercially useful
Never, as non-recourse guarantees are void
Only if it charges a fee for the guarantee
explanation: Per 3/1/3, an Institution may not be a non-recourse guarantor unless its shareholders and investors have authorised it to make donations or acts of benevolence.

title: Possession (Qabd)
q: Ahmad lends 100 tons of wheat to Company X as Qard. Measuring is needed both on delivery and on recovery. Who bears these expenses?
options: Both parties equally
Ahmad on delivery; Company X on recovery
The borrower, Company X
The lender, Ahmad
explanation: Per 4/2/1, the expenses of delivery and recovery in a loan, including ascertainment by customary units of measure, are borne by the borrower.

title: Sale of Debt
q: Company X sells its trade invoices to a factor for an immediate cash payment below their value. What is the ruling?
options: Permitted, as the factor bears collection risk
Permitted, if the invoices are not yet due
Permitted, if the debtors are notified
Not permitted: it sells monetary debt for cash
explanation: Per 9/6/2, factoring is not permitted unless the invoices are bought for a commodity, usufruct or service with ascertained delivery.

title: Procrastinating Debtor
q: A defaulting debtor claims that Bank A's warning to other companies about him is slander. Per the Shari'ah basis, how is the warning viewed?
options: As advice which it is a duty to give
As slander, allowed only with his consent
As a right arising only from the contract
As slander, tolerated for large debts
explanation: Per the Basis, a public complaint about a solvent debtor's default is not prohibited slander; warning others is advice that it is a duty to give.

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: Why may a lessor sell the leased asset to a third party without the lessee's consent, per the Shari'ah basis?
options: Because the buyer pays the lessee compensation for the loss
Because the lessee has no rights at all in the asset
He acts within his ownership and does not harm the usufruct
Because the lease ends automatically upon any sale of it
explanation: The basis: the lessor owns the asset and acts within his ownership without affecting the lessee's right, which is the usufruct attached to the asset.

title: Distribution of Profit in Mudarabah-Based Investment Accounts
q: Bank A plans to give its shareholders' funds better investment opportunities than the funds of its participatory Mudarabah account holders. What must it do?
options: Compensate holders with a fixed return on their capital
Obtain each holder's written consent after the investment
Nothing; shareholders always have priority in investments
Disclose that policy before disposition
explanation: Per 2/1/3, equality in investment opportunities should in principle be ensured; a different policy must be disclosed before disposition.

title: Online Financial Dealings
q: In an online auction run by Bank A, Ahmad is currently the highest bidder and wants to withdraw his bid before the auction ends. What is the ruling?
options: He may retreat if he pays a cancellation fee to the Bank
He may not retreat from his bid until the bidding is over
He may retreat at any time before the auction closes
He may retreat if another bidder matches his bid
explanation: Per 4/3, in online bidding the highest bidder should not retreat from his bid until the bidding process is over.

title: Combination of Contracts
q: Bank A and Company X agree to finance a machine, leaving it to be decided later whether the deal will take the form of Murabahah or Ijarah. How does the standard treat this?
options: As one of the forms of combination of contracts
As a Muwata`ah to form up a Riba trick
As a single sale with a deferred price payable in instalments
As an act of an uncommissioned agent
explanation: Per 2/1/4, agreement to conclude the deal through any of different contractual forms to be finally decided in the future is a form of combination of contracts.

title: Zakah
q: Company X paid a bid security to a ministry and could not invest it. It was refunded after three years. How much Zakah does Company X owe on it?
options: Zakah for all three years
Zakah for one year
No Zakah at all
Zakah for two years
explanation: Per 5/1/5/2, the owner pays Zakah annually unless he was not enabled to invest it before refund; when several years elapse before refund, Zakah for one year is paid.

title: Financial Paper (Shares and Bonds)
q: An underwriter of a share issue also prepares the feasibility study and markets the shares, charging for this work. What is the ruling on this charge?
options: Permissible only if equal to the underwriting risk
Permissible only if done by a separate company
Not permissible, as the underwriter may take no fee
Permissible, if it is not in lieu of the guarantee
explanation: Per 2/4, compensation for work like feasibility studies or marketing is permissible, by the underwriter or another, if it is not in lieu of a guarantee.

title: Sale of Commodities in Organized Markets
q: Bank A buys ascertained assets, paying part of the price as 'Arboun, with the right to revoke within 30 days and forfeit the 'Arboun. Can Bank A sell this right to another?
options: Yes, if the seller consents to the transfer
Yes; it is a valid option that may be traded to another investor
No; the contract is valid but the right may not be traded
No; the 'Arboun contract itself is invalid
explanation: Per 5/2/3/1, a contract with 'Arboun and a right of revocation in a set period is permitted, but trading the right relating to the earnest money is not.

title: Waqf
q: Company X's owner declares today that his warehouse will become a Waqf starting from next year. What is the status of this declaration?
options: Valid; a Waqf may be effective from a future date
Void; a Waqf must take effect immediately upon declaration
Valid only if made in a will
Valid only for family Waqf
explanation: Per 3/1/3, Waqf can be declared effective from a future date, as when the donor declares his property to become Waqf starting next year.

title: Documentary Credit
q: A credit expires before the seller presents the documents. The seller still delivered the goods under the sale contract. What can the seller do?
options: Nothing, as the sale is revoked with the credit
Claim payment only from the issuing bank
Claim payment directly from the buyer
Claim the price plus compensation for delay
explanation: Per 2/4/2, if the credit expires before submission of documents, the seller may claim payment directly from the buyer, as expiry does not revoke the sale.

title: Loan (Qard)
q: Company X is about to lend money to Ahmad. Which legal capacities does the standard stipulate for the two parties?
options: Both: only the capacity to receive gifts
Lender: capacity to donate; borrower: capacity to transact
Both: capacity to donate
Lender: capacity to transact; borrower: capacity to donate
explanation: Per 3/2 and 3/3, the legal capacity for donation is stipulated for the lender and the legal capacity to undertake transactions for the borrower.

title: Waqf
q: Which evidence does the standard cite for Waqf over a common share of an asset?
options: Sa'd's orchard given on behalf of his deceased mother
Khālid's armour and weapons kept for Allah's Cause
Ḥakīm b. Ḥizām's charity during the pre-Islam period
Banū Najjār's Waqf of their jointly owned orchard
explanation: Basis 2/4/11: Banū Najjār instituted Waqf over an orchard they owned as a common share; Umar also made Waqf of shares in Khaybar.

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: In an Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek, Bank A promises to transfer ownership, and the lessee also binds himself to acquire it. What is wrong with this?
options: Only one party may be bound; the other has an option
Nothing, as both binding promises protect both parties
A promise must be made by the lessee only, not the Bank
The Bank's promise may never be binding on the Bank
explanation: Per 8/2, the lessor's promise is binding on one party only; the other must have the option not to proceed, to avoid an impermissible bilateral promise.

title: Financial Rights and How They Are Exercised and Transferred
q: Ahmad learned of the sale of his co-owner's share but delayed claiming Shuf'ah for months, beyond what custom allows. What is the effect?
options: His right passes to his heirs
His right of Shuf'ah lapses
His right remains, but he pays a higher price
His right remains valid for one year
explanation: Per 7/2/4, Shuf'ah must be claimed immediately on becoming aware of the sale in accordance with custom or law, failing which it lapses.

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: In a floating-rental Ijarah, Bank A ties later rentals to a benchmark with a clear formula but sets no limits on its movement. What does the standard require?
options: A floor on the minimum level only, not a maximum
No limits, as a clear formula is enough
A ceiling on the maximum level only, not a minimum
A ceiling on both maximum and minimum levels
explanation: Per 5/2/3, the benchmark must use a clear formula not subject to dispute and should be subject to a ceiling on both maximum and minimum levels.

title: Options to Revoke Contracts Due to Incomplete Performance
q: A car delivered as described is in good working order. Two months later, its condition changes so that it no longer meets the description. Does the buyer have an option for breach of description?
options: No, unless the seller caused the change
Yes, if the description was in writing
No; the breach must occur at or before delivery
Yes, within the customary return period, whenever the change occurs after delivery
explanation: Per 4/2/4, the breach of description must occur at or before the time of delivery (actual or constructive) and must not be a subsequent occurrence.

title: Islamic Insurance
q: An Islamic insurance fund's regulations state that surplus goes only to policyholders who received no indemnity during the period. Is this a permitted method?
options: No, surplus must be split by contributions only
No, surplus may only be given to charity
No, all participants must share the surplus equally
Yes, it is one of the forms listed in the standard
explanation: Per 12/2/2, distributing the surplus among policyholders who have not received indemnity during the period is a permitted form, if stated in the regulations.

title: Documentary Credit
q: A client asks why Bank A may charge him a percentage fee for credit services. What basis does the Shari'ah basis give?
options: It is compensation for guaranteeing the payment, upheld by most Fuqaha
It is a wage for agency services, upheld by most Fuqaha
It is a charge for the time until payment
It is a share of the profit on the imported goods sold to the client
explanation: Per the basis, the fee is in lieu of services by the Institution as the client's agent; the majority of Fuqaha upheld charging wages for agency.

title: Online Financial Dealings
q: Per the Al Baraka Seminar resolution cited in the basis, when is an online contract between parties in different places one between absent parties?
options: When neither party can hear the voice of the other
When the contract is concluded outside working hours
When either party uses a third-party website
When the parties are in different countries
explanation: The cited Al Baraka resolution treats an online contract as between absent parties if neither can hear the other's voice, so message contracting rules apply.

title: Investment Sukuk
q: An investor asks why Salam certificates may not be traded while certificates of leased assets may. What reason does the standard give?
options: Salam goods are always perishable commodities that cannot be stored
Salam certificates have no fixed maturity date for delivery of goods
Salam certificates represent a share in the Salam debt
Salam capital must remain held by the issuer until delivery
explanation: Per 5/2/14 and its Basis, a Salam certificate represents a share in the Salam debt, so it is subject to the rules of debt trading.

title: Murabahah
q: Customer C, acting as Bank A's agent, asks that the price be paid into his account. Why does the standard require the Bank to pay the supplier directly, per the basis?
options: To let the Bank earn a fee for transferring the payment
To make C liable for the risk of the goods
To pass the risk of the goods over to the supplier
To avoid the deal becoming interest-based financing
explanation: The basis: requiring the Institution to pay the supplier directly avoids the risk of the contract degenerating into mere interest-based financing.

title: Obtaining and Deploying Liquidity
q: The central bank wishes to provide liquidity support to Islamic Bank A during a market squeeze. How must this support be provided?
options: Through a commission-based overdraft facility
Through an interest-bearing facility, as central banks are exempt from the Riba prohibition
Only through Shari'ah-compliant modes, e.g. Mudarabah or investment agency
Through any mode, since the support is only temporary
explanation: Per 4/1, liquidity support from supervisory or regulatory bodies such as central banks must be provided only through Shari'ah-compliant modes, e.g. Mudarabah and investment agency.

title: Islamic Insurance
q: A brewery asks Islamic Insurance Company T to insure its stock of alcoholic drinks against fire. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible, as the cover is against fire only and not against theft
It must refrain from covering Shari'ah-banned items
Permissible, if the claim is paid to charity
Permissible, if the contribution is higher
explanation: Per 5/8, the company must adhere to Shari'ah, especially refraining from providing coverage for Shari'ah-banned items, activities or purposes.

title: Sale of Commodities in Organized Markets
q: A general agency memorandum for commodity purchases denies the buyer (principal) any right to take delivery. Why is this prohibited, per the Basis?
options: It negates transfer of ownership and the right to deal in the goods
It makes the agent's wages unknown to him
It turns the commodity sale into a deferred currency exchange (Sarf)
It creates two deferred liabilities
explanation: Per the Basis, stipulating no delivery negates the requirements of sale: transfer of ownership to the buyer and his right to transact in the sold commodity.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: A shareholder in a stock company wants to dissolve the company with respect to his own shares and take back his capital. What is the ruling?
options: He may dissolve it for his own shares after giving due notice to the board
He may withdraw his capital at nominal value
He may not dissolve it for his shares but may sell them
He may dissolve it for his shares if he holds more than 10% of the capital
explanation: Per 4/1/2/1, the stock company contract is binding; no one may dissolve the company in respect of his shares, but he may sell or relinquish them.

title: Guarantees
q: Bakr agrees to guarantee Ahmad's debt to Bank A, but asks Ahmad for a fee of 1% of the amount in return for the guarantee. What is the ruling?
options: Not permissible to take remuneration for a guarantee
Permissible if Ahmad offered the fee himself without being asked
Permissible if the fee is modest and fixed
Permissible if based on the amount at risk
explanation: Per 3/1/5, no remuneration whatsoever may be taken for a personal guarantee per se, nor commission paid for obtaining one.

title: ’Arboun (Earnest Money)
q: A buyer pays 'Arboun for equipment. The option period expires without him paying the remaining price, and the seller has not agreed any extension. What follows?
options: The contract stands and the seller may claim the balance
The contract is revoked and the seller keeps the 'Arboun
The option period is automatically extended by custom
The contract is revoked and the 'Arboun is refunded
explanation: Per 5/2, the contract is considered revoked and the buyer is not entitled to recover the 'Arboun.

title: Possession (Qabd)
q: A seller gives Bank A access to a warehouse holding 1,000 tons of wheat, of which Bank A bought 100 tons, but the 100 tons have not been measured or set aside. Has constructive possession occurred?
options: Yes, provided the price has already been paid in full
Yes, if Bank A insures the whole stock in the warehouse
Yes; giving access to the whole warehouse is sufficient by itself
No; the 100 tons must first be ascertained by a known method
explanation: Per 3/3, constructive possession of movables takes place after their ascertainment by a known method, through relinquishment enabling delivery without obstacle.

title: Options to Revoke Contracts Due to Incomplete Performance
q: Ahmad buys a laptop, then spills coffee on it, causing a hidden circuit fault. He seeks to revoke the sale due to defect. What is the ruling?
options: No option, since the defect was caused by the buyer
He may revoke if he reports it promptly
He may revoke, as the defect is hidden and was not known to him when he bought
He may claim Arsh but not revoke
explanation: Per 2/2/5, a condition of the option to revoke due to defect is that the hidden defect was not caused by the buyer.

title: Islamic Insurance
q: Which Hadith does the basis cite to show the obligatory nature of the donation contract?
options: The Prophet prohibited sales involving Gharar
One who withdraws his gift is like a dog that withholds its vomit
One should neither tolerate harm nor cause it, whether in sales or in gifts
Muslims are bound by their conditions, save one that permits the prohibited
explanation: The basis derives the binding nature of donation from the Hadith: "A person who withdraws his gift is like a dog that withholds its vomit".

title: Sale of Debt
q: Bank A places debts and tangible assets in a registered special purpose company and sells units in it. What minimum share must tangible and like assets form?
options: No minimum, as commingling has occurred
At least one-third of the asset value
At least 25% of the asset value
More than 50% of the entity's asset value
explanation: Per 8/2/2, the ratio of tangible and like assets must exceed 50% of the value of the entity's assets.

title: Irrigation Partnership (Musaqat)
q: An orchard owner and a worker sign a Musaqat. Before any work starts, and with no agreement not to terminate, the owner wishes to withdraw. Can he?
options: Only if he pays the worker the market wage
Only with the approval of a court
Yes; it binds only on commencing work or by agreement
No; Musaqat is binding on both parties as soon as it is signed, before work starts
explanation: Per 3, Musaqat is permissible and becomes binding on commencement of the work or if the parties mutually agreed not to terminate before expiry.

title: Murabahah
q: A supplier gives Customer C a price list that is not addressed to any named customer. C plans to use it for a Murabahah with Bank A. How is this price list treated?
options: As an offer of sale made to Bank A as the buyer
As an invitation to negotiate, not an offer of sale
As a binding offer of sale made to Customer C by the supplier
As a sale already concluded with Customer C on those prices
explanation: Per 2/1/4, a general offer with no named addressee is considered an invitation to negotiate and not an offer of sale.

title: Indices
q: Company X's staff ask why wage indexation in their contracts is acceptable. Per the basis, what is the justification?
options: Indexation is a form of permissible gambling
Wages are a debt that may grow over time
A fair wage policy protecting income against inflation
Employers must share their profits with staff as a matter of justice
explanation: The basis: wage indexation pursues a fair wage policy and protects employees' income against inflation; conditions between parties are permissible in principle.

title: Zakah
q: Company X keeps laying hens to sell their eggs. How are the hens treated for Zakah?
options: Like Mustaghallat: no Zakah on them, only on unexpended income
As articles of trade, valued at market price at the end of the Zakah year
Fully exempt, together with all of their income, as they are a means of production
As livestock, at the rates applicable to goats, since hens are kept for their produce
explanation: Per 5/6/7, Zakah is not due on chickens acquired for production; they are treated like Mustaghallat (productive assets) under item 4/2.

title: Financial Rights and How They Are Exercised and Transferred
q: Company X wants to sell its patent to Company Y for a price. When is this transaction permissible?
options: Never, as patents are not financial rights
Only if the patent is transferred without consideration
Only if the patent is attached to a tangible asset
When it is free of Gharar, deception and fraud
explanation: Per 3/3/3/2, rights to intangible assets are financial rights and may be disposed of or transferred for consideration if free of Gharar, deception and fraud.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: Company G offers to guarantee the capital of Partner P in a Sharikah, free of charge. Company G owns 60% of Partner P's capital. Is this third-party guarantee acceptable?
options: No, the guarantor must not own more than half of the guaranteed entity
Yes, since the guarantee is given without any consideration or fee
Yes, provided Company G is not itself a partner in the Sharikah
No, unless Company G owns the whole of Partner P's capital
explanation: Per 3/1/4/3(III), the third-party guarantor should not own more than half of the capital in the entity to be guaranteed.

title: Gold and Its Trading Parameters in Shari’ah
q: Bank A buys a manufacturing company whose assets include some gold. Gold is not its primary asset and it does not trade in gold, silver or currencies. Must al-Sarf rules be met?
options: Yes, unless the gold is under half of the assets
Yes, spot exchange is required for the gold portion
Yes, the gold must first be sold separately
No, the sale is not subject to the rulings of al-Sarf
explanation: Per 3/1/2, selling such an entity along with its non-primary gold is not subject to the rulings of al-Sarf.

title: Procrastinating Debtor
q: Bank A suspects a defaulting debtor is hiding assets and wants to investigate his financial status and activities. What does the standard allow?
options: No investigation, as it intrudes on his private affairs
Investigation by all permissible and legitimate means
Investigation only of assets mortgaged to it
Investigation only under a court order
explanation: Per 2/5/1, the Institution may monitor and investigate the financial status and activities of a defaulting debtor through all permissible and legitimate means.

title: Istisna’a and Parallel Istisna’a
q: An Istisna'a customer asks Bank A for six more months to pay the price. The Bank agrees if the customer pays an extra amount for the extension. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible if the price was left unpaid by him
Permissible as an agreed contract amendment
Not permissible to charge for an extension
Permissible if the work is already complete
explanation: Per 4/1/3, amendments may not provide an additional sum for extending the payment period; a rebate for pre-payment is allowed if not stipulated at conclusion.

title: Possession (Qabd)
q: Ahmad has been leasing a car from Company X and holds it. He then buys the same car from Company X. Is a fresh delivery needed for him to take possession under the sale?
options: No; his prior possession stands in place of the possession due
Yes, since his prior possession as lessee was not one of ownership
Yes; he must return the car and receive it again
No, but only if the sale contract is officially registered
explanation: Per 3/6, prior possession of a tangible thing stands in place of subsequent lawful possession due to a cause acknowledged by the Shari'ah.

title: Waqf
q: A tangible Waqf building has validly incurred a debt for urgent repairs. The financier asks for a mortgage over the building. What is the ruling?
options: Permitted for up to half of its value
Permitted, as the debt was validly incurred for urgent repairs
Not permitted, even though the debt itself is allowed
Permitted with the relevant authority's approval of the pledge
explanation: Per 6/1, it is not permitted to pledge tangible Waqf assets even when availing a debt against the Waqf.

title: Commercial Papers
q: A client gives Bank A a cheque to collect on his behalf, but no commission was agreed. What is the bank entitled to?
options: A share of the amount collected by the bank as its agent's profit
Nothing, as collection is a free service that a bank owes its clients
Interest on the amount until it is credited to the client's account
Commission per prevalent practice among institutions
explanation: Per clause 5, collection is an agency; the institution gets the agreed commission or, absent agreement, the practice prevalent among institutions applies.

title: Stipulations and Ethics of Fatwa in the Institutional Framework
q: A board member wants to prohibit a new digital payment habit merely because he dislikes new customs, though it violates no Shari'ah rule. What does the standard say?
options: He may prohibit it if most members agree
Fatwa should not hastily prohibit for mere condemnation
New habits should be prohibited until they are proven safe by experts
He may prohibit it if the Bank is uncertain
explanation: Per 8/6, Fatwa shall not hastily prohibit an act out of mere condemnation of new habits unless they contradict Shari'ah rules and principles.

title: Combination of Contracts
q: Which of the following is one of the meanings of Muwata`ah stated in the standard?
options: Unrevealed prior agreement on a permissible deal as a Shari'ah exit
A written guarantee given by the agent to the principal against loss of the goods
A sale whose price is later fixed by a third party chosen by both sides
A unilateral promise made after signing the contract
explanation: Per 6/1/2, one meaning of Muwata`ah is an unrevealed prior agreement between the parties to perform a permissible act or deal to find a Shari'ah-accepted exit.

title: Options to Revoke Contracts Due to Incomplete Performance
q: How does the Shari'ah basis characterise the option to revoke owing to deal fragmentation?
options: As a form of price gouging
As a cooling-off option
As a type of defect
As a type of deception
explanation: Per the basis, deal fragmentation is a type of defect; some Fiqh references categorise it under the option to revoke due to defect.

title: Syndicated Financing
q: Bank A wants to sell its share in a syndicate whose physical assets and usufructs exceed its cash and debts. On what terms may it sell?
options: Only after the syndicate is fully liquidated and its assets are sold
Only at face value plus a fixed profit agreed by the participants
Only at the nominal value of its contribution, whatever the assets are worth
At the value agreed with the buyer, per the contract conditions
explanation: Per 10/2, an Institution may dispose of its share at the agreed value if physical assets and usufructs exceed cash, debts and financial rights.

title: Financial Paper (Shares and Bonds)
q: Why does the Basis prohibit the issuance of interest-bearing bonds?
options: They are Salam contracts with deferred capital
They are loans, and every loan yielding a benefit is Riba
They are sales of goods that are not yet owned by the issuer
They give holders no voting rights
explanation: Per the Basis, bonds by nature are loans; as each loan yielding a benefit is Riba and bonds rest on interest-bearing loans, their issuance is prohibited.

title: Competitions and Prizes
q: Bank A offers a limited number of prizes to one subcategory of its investment account holders. How must the winners be chosen?
options: Through a draw open to every holder in the subcategory
By the length of each holder's relationship with the Bank, longest first
At the discretion of the Bank's management
By the size of each holder's investment, the largest holders being served first
explanation: Per 3/5/2/3, every holder of an investment account or a subcategory must have a chance; if prizes are limited, winners are determined by draw.

title: Hiring of Persons
q: Per the Shari'ah basis, why is pay due even if the employer did not benefit from an employee who placed himself at his disposal?
options: The pay is in reality a donation from the employer, not a price
The employee met the condition; the employer has no excuse
The employee bears no duties at all under hiring
Pay in hiring is always due in full at signing
