title: Loan (Qard)
q: To attract current account balances, Bank A offers current account holders full exemption from credit card fees and transfer charges. What is the ruling?
options: Not permitted: these benefits are given in lieu of the accounts
Permitted, if the exemption is only partial and not a full exemption
Permitted, as current accounts are deposits
Permitted, as they are only service exemptions
explanation: Per 10/2, the institution may not give current account holders, in lieu of the accounts, benefits unrelated to deposits and withdrawals, including fee exemptions.

title: Waqf
q: A Waqif did not specify the overseer's remuneration, and the relevant authorities have set none. What is the overseer entitled to?
options: Whatever the beneficiaries agree to pay
Nothing, as he is presumed a volunteer
Remuneration at the prevailing market rate
A fixed 10% of the Waqf asset
explanation: Per 3/9/2, absent the Waqif's specification and any authority's determination, the overseer receives remuneration at the prevailing market rate.

title: Possession (Qabd)
q: Without the creditor's demand or consent, Ahmad deposits the amount he owes into an account maintained for Company X. What condition for constructive possession is missing?
options: The deposit must be upon the creditor's demand or with his consent
The deposit must be made at the creditor's branch
The deposit must be witnessed by two persons
The deposit must be made in cash only, never by cheque or endorsement
explanation: Per 5/3, a deposit into a bank account maintained for a person is constructive possession when made upon his demand or with his consent.

title: Mudarabah
q: At liquidation, a Mudarabah's total expenses exactly equal its total revenues. What do the parties receive?
options: The Mudarib gets his profit ratio applied to the total revenues
The capital is reduced by the Mudarib's fee, which is due whether or not profit exists
The Mudarib gets a fair wage for his work, paid out of the capital
Capital back to the provider, nothing to the Mudarib
explanation: Per 8/7, if expenses equal revenues, the capital provider receives his capital back without profit or loss, and there is no profit for the Mudarib.

title: Commercial Papers
q: A bill of exchange is endorsed by its holder to a third party, meeting all legal conditions for endorsement. What is the effect of the endorsement?
options: It is a mere promise with no legal effect
It is binding in its legal effects
It is void, as debts cannot be transferred
It is binding only if the drawer consents
explanation: Per clause 4, all forms of endorsement are binding with respect to their legal effects provided they fulfil the legal conditions and regulations set for them.

title: Competitions and Prizes
q: Which narration cited in the standard's basis shows that the Prophet himself established racing competitions?
options: Anas's account of the camel al-Adhbaa'
Abu Hurairah's Hadith on prizes in races
Ayishah's account of racing on foot
Ibn Umar's report of races between horses
explanation: The Basis cites Ibn Umar: the Prophet established a race between slender horses and another between ordinary horses, and Ibn Umar raced.

title: Waqf
q: A Waqf owns vacant land but has no funds. Bank A leases the land, builds on it, and leases the building to the Waqf, which owns it at the end. Which mode is this?
options: Hikr, with the tenant paying a changing normal rent
Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek of a property to be built
Istibdal of the Waqf land in exchange for a building
Diminishing Musharakah in which the land is shared too
explanation: Per 7/2/3, under IMB the Waqf land is leased to the financier who builds and delivers the building to the Waqf; at term end the Waqf owns the building.

title: Islamic Reinsurance
q: Islamic Reinsurer R is asked to provide reinsurance to a traditional insurance company. Which condition applies?
options: The Islamic reinsurance contract must be used, with no linkage
It is never allowed for an Islamic reinsurer
R must first convert the traditional insurer into an Islamic insurance company
The traditional insurer's contract may be used if fair
explanation: Per 8/3, it is permissible subject to: use of the Islamic reinsurance contract, no linkage, and no Shari'ah-prohibited object.

title: Payment Cards
q: Bank A's ATM charges other banks' cardholders 2 per withdrawal. It wants to charge its own credit cardholders 3 per withdrawal. What is the ruling?
options: Permitted, if the higher fee is stated in the card agreement
Permitted, as it owns the ATM and sets its own fees
Not permitted to exceed the fee charged to others
Permitted, since credit cards cost the issuer more to serve
explanation: Per 5/1/2/4, an Institution that issued the card observes 5/1/1 and may not charge more than it charges other institutions' cardholders.

title: Documentary Credit
q: The seller presents conforming documents on time, but the buyer tells the bank he has heard the goods may be of poor quality. What must the bank do?
options: Pay, as credit dealings are on documents alone, not the goods
Cancel the credit at the buyer's request and notify the seller
Pay half now and hold half pending the goods' arrival
Withhold payment until the goods are inspected on arrival
explanation: Per 2/4/1, documentary credit deals with documents alone without reference to the goods; the bank must execute when conforming documents are presented in time.

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: Midway through a lease, Bank A sells the leased asset to the lessee himself. What happens to the Ijarah contract?
options: It continues at a reduced rental for the lessee
It continues unchanged until the original term ends
It becomes a sub-lease granted back to the Bank
It terminates, as the lessee becomes the owner
explanation: Per 7/1/1, if the lessor sells the leased asset to the lessee, the Ijarah terminates due to transfer of ownership of the asset and usufruct to him.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: Partners ask why they may not leave their profit ratios undetermined until profit is realised. What reason does the Shari'ah basis give?
options: Ratios must always match capital shares
Profit belongs to the Institution until then
It involves uncertainty that may lead to dispute
It would make the capital a debt
explanation: Per the basis, deferring the profit ratio until profit is realised involves uncertainty which may potentially lead to dispute.

title: Arbitration
q: The arbitration document set a 60-day period. The period ends without a verdict, and the parties have not agreed to extend it. What is the arbitrator's status?
options: He must issue whatever verdict he has reached
He becomes terminated
He may continue until he issues the verdict
He may extend the period on his own
explanation: Per 9/6, when the period specified for arbitration expires without a verdict, the arbitrator becomes terminated unless the parties agree to extend it.

title: Liability of the Investment Manager
q: A partial loss occurs in a Mudaraba. The Mudarib, of his own free will, then offers to make good the loss to Rab Al Maal. Is this permitted?
options: No, any liability on the Mudarib is prohibited
No, unless the loss resulted from his negligence
Yes, volunteering after a loss occurs is permitted
Yes, but only if agreed at the time of contract
explanation: Per 3/4, after a total or partial loss occurs, the investment manager may volunteer to assume the liability of his own free will.

title: Concession Contracts
q: Company X's exploration period ends without it discovering the minerals for which the license was obtained. Is it entitled to a utilization concession?
options: Yes, as it bore the costs and risks of exploration during the period
Yes, for a reduced area of the license it originally held
Yes, if it pays an additional fee to the State for the concession
No, it is not entitled at the end of that period
explanation: Per 5/2/4, if the licensee does not discover the minerals or water by the end of the exploration period, it is not entitled to a utilization concession.

title: Revocation of Contracts by Exercise of a Cooling-Off Option
q: Why does the standard say cooling-off options to revoke are stipulated only in binding contracts?
options: Nonbinding contracts are revocable by their nature
Binding contracts cannot otherwise be ended
Only binding contracts involve a price or rent
Nonbinding contracts are void under the Shari'ah
explanation: Per the Basis, cooling-off options apply only to binding contracts because nonbinding contracts are by nature revocable by one or both parties.

title: Waqf
q: An overseer records the Waqf's income and expenses inside the general ledger of his own trading company. What does the standard require?
options: Nothing, as the overseer owns the revenue
Waqf accounts must be prepared separately
Only an annual report to the beneficiaries
Nothing, if the totals are disclosed yearly
explanation: Per 3/6/7, the overseer must prepare the accounts of Waqf separate from other accounts, under prevailing accounting principles.

title: Hiring of Persons
q: Ahmad is hired and puts himself at Bank A's disposal from day one, but the Bank has not yet assigned him any task. Is his pay payable?
options: Yes; making himself available makes the pay payable
No, until the first task is completed
No, until the Bank actually assigns him some task to perform
Only half until a task is assigned
explanation: Per 5/2/3, pay is payable on delivery of the work or making it available, i.e. when the employee is at the employer's disposal even if no task is assigned.

title: Combination of Contracts
q: A trader wants high-quality dates for his low-quality dates. Per the Hadith in the basis, what should he do?
options: Exchange equal amounts with a cash top-up
Sell the low-quality dates, then buy the high-quality ones
Sell and buy back the dates in one pre-agreed contract
Exchange more low-quality dates for less of the high-quality dates
explanation: The basis cites the Prophet's direction to sell low-quality dates first and then buy the high-quality ones, as two separate unrelated contracts.

title: Monetization (Tawarruq)
q: Bank A is asked by a conventional bank to perform Monetization for it. Bank A discovers the liquidity will be used for interest-based lending. What should Bank A do?
options: Proceed, since the use of the cash is the other bank's concern
Proceed, but only through a broker rather than directly
Decline to perform Monetization for that bank
Proceed, provided the commodity is not gold, silver or currency
explanation: Per 3/2, the Institution should not perform Monetization for conventional banks when it discovers they will use the liquidity for interest-based lending.

title: Rules for Calculating Profit in Financial Transactions
q: A Mudarabah contract sets a 60:40 profit split for a one-year tenor and 70:30 for a three-year tenor. Is setting different ratios by tenor permissible?
options: No; one ratio must apply throughout the Mudarabah
No; ratios may change only on a hurdle rate
Yes, but only if the capital is guaranteed
Yes; different ratios may be set for different tenors
explanation: Per 7/1, in Mudarabah different profit ratios or rates may be set as per different tenors or triggered by a hurdle rate, without totally depriving any party.

title: Guarantees
q: The holder of an asset mortgaged to Bank A is using it in a way that may cause losses to be borne by the Bank. What may the Bank do?
options: Nothing until the debt falls due
Charge the debtor a misuse penalty
Take legal action against the misuse
Take the asset into full ownership
explanation: Per 6/9/2, the Institution may protect the integrity of the subject of a guarantee, such as a mortgaged asset, and pursue legal action against its misuse.

title: Competitions and Prizes
q: Which of the following does the standard cite from the Qur'an as evidence for the permissibility of competitions?
options: The Bedouin's camel outrunning al-Adhbaa'
Yusuf's brothers telling their father they went racing
The Prophet's horse race to Thaniyyat Al-Wada'a, as narrated by Ibn Umar
Ayishah's foot race with the Prophet
explanation: The Basis cites Yusuf (Joseph): 17, where Yusuf's brothers told their father they went racing; the others are cited Sunnah narrations.

title: Financial Rights and How They Are Exercised and Transferred
q: Ahmad holds a commercial license from the authorities and wants to transfer it to Company X for a price. The law does not prohibit this. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible only without consideration
Permissible only with the consent of a court
Not permissible, as a license is personal to its holder
Permissible, for or without consideration
explanation: Per 3/3/3/3, a license holder may dispose of a commercial license for or without consideration unless specifically prohibited by law.

title: Irrigation Partnership (Musaqat)
q: A Musaqat worker dies mid-season. The contract does not stipulate that the work is non-assignable. What option do his heirs have?
options: To complete the work on the same terms, personally or by hiring
None; the contract terminates on his death, as it rests on his personal work
To claim his full share without further work
To renegotiate a higher share with the owner
explanation: Per 12/3, absent a non-assignability stipulation, the successor may complete the work on the same terms, himself or by hiring workers, for the deceased's share.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: A partner in a joint-liability company wants to bring in his brother as a substitute partner in his place. The other partners object. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible, as shares in such a company are freely transferable like stock
Permissible if the brother is at least equally wealthy and creditworthy
Not permissible without the other partners' agreement
Permissible after giving due notice
explanation: Per 4/2/2/3, a partner in a joint-liability company may not bring in a substitute for himself without the agreement of the other partners.

title: Gold and Its Trading Parameters in Shari’ah
q: A customer buys gold, and a latent defect appears later. The seller had not expressly absolved himself of defects. What right does the customer have?
options: Option to revoke for defect and return the gold
None, as the gold was exchanged on spot
Only a price reduction, as the sale is final
None, as options are barred in gold sales
explanation: Per 10/2, unless the seller expressly absolves himself of latent defects, the buyer has the Option to Revoke Due to Defect and may return the gold.

title: Mudarabah
q: A Mudarib has already bought goods with the Mudarabah capital. The capital provider now wants to terminate unilaterally. What is the ruling?
options: He may terminate it if he pays the Mudarib a fair wage for the work already done
The contract becomes binding only from its maturity date
He may terminate at once and reclaim the full cash value of the capital provided
The contract is binding until actual or constructive liquidation
explanation: Per 4/3/1, once the Mudarib has commenced the business, the Mudarabah becomes binding up to the date of actual or constructive liquidation.

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: Bank A has bought a building under a sale contract, but the title is not yet registered in its name. Can the Bank lease it?
options: Yes, but only as an agent of the seller
Yes, ownership exists under the sale contract
No, title must be registered in its name first
No, until the seller vacates and registers it
explanation: Per 3/1/2, ownership is possible under a sale contract even if title is not registered in the purchaser's name; the purchaser may obtain a counter-deed.

title: Financial Paper (Shares and Bonds)
q: Why does the Basis reject the claim that holders of Tamattu' shares have been fully redeemed?
options: Their shares were originally issued at a discount
They never paid in full for their original shares
Redemption is only in form; they remain owners
Their new shares carry no voting rights of any kind
explanation: Per the Basis, Tamattu' holders still claim profit rights and liquidation rights; their redemption is only in form, as they continue to be owners.

title: Possession (Qabd)
q: A merchant receives payment from a customer through a credit card. Per the standard, how is this payment regarded?
options: As a debt with no possession until settlement
As constructive possession of the payment
As actual possession of banknotes
As possession only when cash is withdrawn
explanation: Per 5/2, payments made through a credit card are deemed constructive possession of such payments.

title: Mudarabah
q: Bank A manages its joint investment accounts on a Mudarabah basis and also issues Mudarabah Sukuk. Which of these does the Mudarabah standard cover?
options: The joint investment accounts, but not the Mudarabah Sukuk
Neither, since the standard covers bilateral contracts only
Both, since each is based on the Mudarabah contract
The Mudarabah Sukuk, but not the joint investment accounts
explanation: Per clause 1, the standard covers joint and special purpose investment accounts run on Mudarabah, but not Sukuk of Mudarabah, which have a separate standard.

title: Salam and Parallel Salam
q: Bank A and a Salam seller agree to cancel delivery of 40% of the cotton. What is the correct treatment?
options: Return the capital plus a profit margin
Partial cancellation is not allowed
Return the cotton's current market value
Return 40% of the capital to the Bank
explanation: Per 4/3, Iqalah of the whole Salam for full return of capital, or partial cancellation for return of a corresponding part of the capital, is permissible.

title: Payment Cards
q: Which evidence does the standard cite for allowing a lender to charge the actual direct cost of a loan?
options: The hadith on accepting a transfer of debt (Hawalah)
The verse forbidding riba and consuming wealth wrongfully
The verse that the debtor should dictate the debt
The hadith on a sale combined with a loan contract
explanation: Basis 5/1/1: the verse "And the one who owes should give the dictation" shows the cost of writing the debt deed falls on the debtor.

title: Hiring of Persons
q: Ahmad is a private employee working full-time under the supervision of Company X. He wants to take a second job with Company Y during the same hours. What is the ruling?
options: Allowed, since he may serve several employers
Not allowed without Company X's permission
Allowed, as long as his work quality is unaffected
Allowed, if Company Y pays him more
explanation: Per 4/3, a private employee working for a single employer may not work for anyone else at the same time, except with his employer's permission.

title: Controls on Gharar in Financial Transactions
q: In Country Z there is no Takaful provider, and Bank A must insure its assets to avoid severe hardship. May it use commercial insurance despite its Gharar?
options: Yes, as a Shari'ah-recognizable need justifies the Gharar
No, need only applies when life is at risk
No, excessive Gharar is never permitted in exchange contracts
Yes, because insurance is a donation contract
explanation: Per 4/4, need (severe hardship with no permissible alternative) justifies Gharar; commercial insurance in the absence of Takaful is cited as an example.

title: Sale of Debt
q: The basis for selling a registered entity of commingled debts and assets relies on a Maliki analogy of assemblage (tarkib). What is it?
options: Camels sold for dinars with payment collected in dirhams
Usurped property sold to the usurper at its value
Salam over livestock sold before the buyer takes possession
Jewellery fixed on an ornament sold for that metal
explanation: Per the Basis for 8/2, the entity meets the Maliki assemblage condition for selling ornaments fixed with gold or silver for the same metal.

title: Insolvency
q: After his declaration of insolvency, Ahmad exercises an option to terminate a purchase contract he concluded before the declaration. What is the effect?
options: It has no legal effect, like all his post-declaration acts
It is effective, since it relates to a previous transaction
It is effective only with the creditors' unanimous approval
It is effective only if the court later ratifies it
explanation: Per 5/3, post-declaration sales, gifts and endowments have no legal effect, except acts relating to previous transactions such as exercising an option to terminate.

title: Liability of the Investment Manager
q: An investment agent, without intending to, exceeds the limits agreed in the contract when disposing of the funds. Does this count as misconduct (ta'addi)?
options: No, unless it causes a loss above a set limit
Yes, but only if custom treats it as intentional
Yes, whether the excess was intentional or not
No, misconduct requires a deliberate breach
explanation: Per 5/2, misconduct is exceeding the limit authorized by Shari'ah and agreed by the parties, whether the exceeding was intentional or not.

title: Stipulations and Ethics of Fatwa in the Institutional Framework
q: On a controversial issue with several Fiqh opinions, Bank A's board adopts one view. What must the Fatwa state?
options: The opinion it subscribes to and the bases of its choice
Only the final ruling, without any opinion or basis for it
All opinions, leaving the Bank to choose
The opinion of the majority of boards only
explanation: Per 9/2, the board shall declare the opinion it subscribes to and, if the issue is controversial, explain the specific bases of its choice.

title: Islamic Insurance
q: Ahmad delays paying his agreed Islamic insurance contribution. What right does the company have?
options: To pay him half indemnity until he pays
To charge him a late interest on the contribution
To cancel all his past contributions
To terminate the contract or pursue legal enforcement
explanation: Per 8/2, if the participant refrains from or delays payment of his contribution, the company may terminate the contract or pursue legal enforcement.

title: Sale of Debt
q: An investor buys shares of an operating Islamic bank whose assets are mostly Murabaha receivables. Do the sale of debt rules apply to the debts?
options: Yes, unless tangible assets exceed one-third of its asset value
Yes, so shares must trade at face value
No, the debts are ancillary to its ongoing activity
Yes, since debts exceed half of its assets, as in a debt portfolio
explanation: Per 8/1, an ongoing permissible entity may be sold whatever its debt ratio, as business debts are ancillary, unless it is entirely debt.

title: Financial Paper (Shares and Bonds)
q: Bank A buys shares in a conventional bank in order to work to convert it. Which principle does the Basis cite for allowing this?
options: The rule that the secondary is subservient to the primary
Enjoining good and forbidding evil (al-Amr bil-Ma'ruf)
Gains are based on the bearing of costs
What can be sold can be mortgaged
explanation: Per the Basis, participation by one able or striving to convert is a means to alter the rejected and falls under enjoining good and forbidding evil.

title: Documentary Credit
q: Bank A opens a documentary credit not on a client's order but to import equipment for its own use. Does the Documentary Credit standard cover this?
options: Yes, it covers both client-ordered credits and own-use credits
No, an Institution may never open credits for its own use under Shari'ah rules
Yes, but only if the credit is also confirmed by another bank
No, it covers only credits opened on the order of a client of the Institution
explanation: Per clause 1, the standard covers documentary credit extended by an Institution on the basis of client orders or for the use of the Institution itself.

title: Loan (Qard)
q: Ahmad lent wheat to a farmer in City A, and the contract says nothing about the place of repayment. Where must the farmer return the similar wheat?
options: At any place chosen by the farmer
Wherever Ahmad happens to demand it
At the farmer's place of residence
In City A, where the loan was delivered
explanation: Per 3/4/2, the applicable rule is the return of an amount similar to the loan amount at the place where it was delivered.

title: Murabahah
q: Customer C accepted a supplier's offer addressed to him personally but has not paid yet. He then asks Bank A to finance the same goods through Murabahah. What is the Bank's position?
options: It may not do Murabahah, as the sale is concluded with C
It may proceed if the supplier assigns C's contract to it
It may proceed because C has not yet paid the price
It may proceed if C signs a binding promise to purchase
explanation: Per 2/2/1, once the customer accepts the supplier's offer, the sale is concluded with him and the Institution may not carry out Murabahah on the same item.

title: Sale of Commodities in Organized Markets
q: Bank A buys a commodity on spot from Company X and sells it on deferred terms to Company Y, which owns 80% of Company X. How does the standard treat this?
options: As permitted, since Company Y is not the seller
As a buy-back ('Inah) sale, which is prohibited
As a valid sale, since the parties are separate entities
As a valid Murabahah, if the profit is disclosed
explanation: Per 4/2/6, a spot purchase then deferred sale to the same seller or to its holding institution with majority ownership or effective control is 'Inah.

title: Hawalah
q: Ahmad owes Bakr 10 dinars and is owed 20 dinars by Zaid. He transfers Bakr to Zaid in a restricted Hawalah. What is the ruling?
options: Invalid, as the debts are unequal
Valid, and Bakr may collect all 20
Valid, but Bakr may receive only 10 dinars
Valid if Bakr pays Ahmad the difference
explanation: Per 6/6, a lesser debt may be transferred against a larger one, on condition the transferee is entitled only to the equivalent of his own debt.

title: Revocation of Contracts by Exercise of a Cooling-Off Option
q: Midway through an Ijarah, the lessee asks the lessor to waive his rights for the remaining lease period, and they agree a consideration at the time of waiver. Is this allowed?
options: No, any consideration must be fixed in the contract
Yes, but only for debt transfer, not for Ijarah
No, waiver of revocation rights is never compensated
Yes, in term contracts like Ijarah this is allowed
explanation: Per 10/1, in contracts with specified terms such as Ijarah, a party may waive rights to the remaining period for a consideration agreed at waiver.

title: Syndicated Financing
q: Bank A manages a syndicate as a partner. Participants ask it to guarantee them against default by the syndicate's debtors. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible, if the debtors are its own customers
Permissible, if limited to the profit portion
Not permissible for the managing Institution
Permissible, as it selected the debtors
explanation: Per 8/2, the Institution managing the syndication as Mudarib, partner or agent may not guarantee the debtors of its partners or FX fluctuations of contributions.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: Company X issues shares and adds a percentage to their actual value on the subscription date to recover issuing costs. Under what condition is this allowed?
options: The percentage is paid as an extra dividend to the old shareholders of the company
The percentage does not exceed 10% of nominal value, whatever the expenses are
The percentage is approved by the licensed stockbroker
The percentage reflects an appropriate estimate of actual expenses
explanation: Per 4/1/2/2, the issuer may add a percentage to recover issuing expenses provided it is appropriately estimated to reflect the actual expenses incurred.

title: Liability of the Investment Manager
q: A central bank requires investment managers to bear the burden of proving losses and the absence of negligence. How does the standard justify complying with this?
options: As an undertaking to donate by the manager
As Maslahah Mursalah enforced by the authorities
As the manager's waiver of his right by consent
As the norm that the manager is presumed not liable
explanation: Per the Basis, a burden imposed by a regulatory or supervisory authority is deemed Maslahah Mursalah enforced by ruling authorities and must be heeded.

title: Payment Cards
q: What is the Shari'ah basis for prohibiting revolving credit cards as conventionally structured?
options: They give a revolving loan against a riba-based increment
They are a sale of debt for debt between issuer and merchant
They involve gharar in the card limit set by the issuer
They involve a prohibited form of Tawarruq
explanation: Basis 4/4: the contract gives a revolving loan over time against a riba-based increment, prohibited by Quran, Sunnah, consensus and reason.

title: Istisna’a and Parallel Istisna’a
q: Per the Shari'ah basis, why can animals, fruits and vegetables not be the subject of an Istisna'a?
options: They cannot be described by specification
They perish before the delivery date
They are sold only by weight
They are not transformed by human manufacture
explanation: The basis: Istisna'a means a sale of materials to be transformed by manufacture or construction; natural things like animals, fruits and vegetables are not covered.

title: Procrastinating Debtor
q: Bakr guaranteed Ahmad's debt to Bank A, with no condition on the order of claims. Ahmad defaults. From whom may the Bank demand payment?
options: From either Ahmad or Bakr
From Bakr only, once Ahmad defaults
From Ahmad first, then Bakr if he refuses
From Ahmad only, until he is insolvent
explanation: Per 2/2(a), a creditor may demand settlement from the debtor or the guarantor, unless the guarantor stipulated that it be sought from the debtor first.

title: Gold and Its Trading Parameters in Shari’ah
q: Bank A holds a customer's gold as Wadi'ah and, without his permission, commingles it with its own gold without allocation. Is this allowed?
options: Yes, if it later returns gold of equal weight
Yes, since gold is fungible by nature
No, it may not commingle it without allocation
Yes, if the deposit is recorded by weight
explanation: Per 5/4/1, gold deposits are held in trust; the depository may not use them or commingle them without allocation unless the depositor permits.

title: Insolvency
q: Creditors of Company X, whose debts exceed its assets, want to act before going to court. What does the first stage of insolvency involve?
options: Filing a petition for an immediate declaration of insolvency
Demanding pro-rata payment and no donations, loans or preferences
Selling the debtor's tools of trade by public auction
Seizing the debtor's assets directly without any authority
explanation: Per 4/1, in the first stage creditors demand pro-rata payment and that the debtor refrain from donations, loans and preferential dealings.

title: Waqf
q: Ahmad made a perpetual Waqf of investment Sukuk. The Sukuk are now cancelled (redeemed). What happens to the cancellation proceeds?
options: They are returned to Ahmad or to his heirs after redemption
They are distributed to the beneficiaries as Waqf revenue at once
The Waqf ends upon the cancellation
They are reinvested in other Sukuk, units or income assets
explanation: Per 2/4/15/1(a), on cancellation of perpetual Waqf Sukuk or fund units, the proceeds are reinvested in other Sukuk, fund units or revenue assets.

title: Sale of Debt
q: Bank A sells a receivable secured by a pledge. The buyer did not stipulate the pledge, and custom does not include it. Does the pledge pass to the buyer?
options: Yes, a pledge always follows the debt
No, the pledge does not transfer
Yes, once the debt falls due
Yes, if the pledgor does not object
explanation: Per 7/2, a pledge or guarantee transfers with the debt only if the buyer stipulated it or custom admits it, absent a non-assignability term.

title: Payment Cards
q: Bank A lets a covered card holder spend beyond the cash cover limit. Which fee rulings apply to that excess?
options: The rulings of the lending-based card
No fee rules apply to the excess
The rulings of the debit card
The rulings for non-lending cards
explanation: Per 6/2/2/3, if the issuer lets the holder use the card beyond its cash limit, the excess takes the lending-based card ruling, observing 5/1/1.

title: Waqf
q: Ahmad created a Waqf for his grandchildren. Years later, none of the designated beneficiaries exist any more. What happens to the Waqf?
options: It ends and the asset returns to Ahmad's heirs
It becomes void from the time of its creation
It turns into a Charitable Waqf
It passes into the ownership of the overseer
explanation: Per 2/2/1/2, if the designated beneficiaries of a Private (Dynasty) Waqf no longer exist, it turns into a Charitable Waqf.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: Two partners sign a Sharikah and agree to set their profit-sharing percentages later, once the profit is realised. What is the ruling?
options: Permitted if losses are fixed by capital shares
Not permitted: ratios must be set when the contract is concluded
Permitted, since profit belongs to the partners
Permitted, as long as they agree on the ratios before distribution
explanation: Per 3/1/5/2, the profit percentage of each partner must be determined at conclusion of the contract and may not be deferred until profit is realised.

title: Zakah
q: Ahmad and Ali each own 25 goats that share the same facilities. How does the standard treat them for Zakah?
options: As one herd of 50 owned by one person
As two herds, each paying half a goat
As one herd only if in the same place
As two herds, each below Nisab
explanation: Per 5/6/1, mixed ownership is recognized: animals owned by several persons are treated as owned by one when they share the same facilities.

title: Conversion of a Conventional Bank to an Islamic Bank
q: Converting Bank A sells some premises for liquidity and leases them back by Ijarah. Which requirement applies?
options: The sale must be made conditional on the signing of the lease
The rental must equal the sale price
The sale contract must be independent of the lease
The lease must be signed before the sale
explanation: Per 6/2/4, sale-and-leaseback must follow the Ijarah standards; the contract of sale must be independent and separate from the contract of lease.

title: Distribution of Profit in Mudarabah-Based Investment Accounts
q: Bank A invests the liquidity portion of unrestricted investment accounts in short-term instruments without holders' consent; a loss arises without negligence. Who bears it?
options: The Bank, as it invested without consent
The central bank holding the reserve
The Bank and holders equally
The account holders as Arbab al-Mal
explanation: Per 4/10/2, the Bank may invest liquidity funds without consent in unrestricted Mudarabah; returns join the investment base and losses without fault are borne by the holders.

title: Mortgage and its Contemporary Applications
q: Bank A incurs costs for safekeeping and documentation of a mortgaged asset. The contract is silent on these costs. Who bears them?
options: Both parties equally
The mortgagor, as owner of the asset
Bank A, the mortgagee
The notary, if one is appointed
explanation: Per 3/2/10, the mortgagee bears expenses of safekeeping, documentation and selling of the mortgaged asset, unless the parties agree the mortgagor bears them.

title: Arbitration
q: The parties require the arbitrator to consult two named experts before ruling. The experts' views differ from the arbitrator's own assessment. What applies?
options: He must consult them but is not bound to accept their views
He must adopt the experts' views in his verdict, whatever his view
He may ignore the requirement to consult them
He must refer the dispute back to the parties
explanation: Per 9/5, the parties may require consultation with named experts, but the arbitrator is not bound to accept the experts' viewpoints.

title: Agency and the Act of an Uncommissioned Agent (Fodooli)
q: Per the Shari'ah basis, why is a Fodooli's act suspended pending the owner's approval rather than treated as void?
options: Gharar is always tolerated in sale contracts, so no sale is ever void
A Muslim's act should be preserved from cancellation if possible
The buyer's rights override those of the owner of the goods sold
The Fodooli is considered a guarantor of the owner for the value of the goods
explanation: The basis: a Muslim's act should be preserved from cancellation where possible; Ibn Al-Humam reconciled Gharar and benefit by permissibility with suspension.

title: Investment Sukuk
q: In a Murabahah Sukuk, subscription funds are used to buy a commodity which is then sold on Murabahah. What do the certificate holders own and receive?
options: They own shares in the issuer and receive its dividends
They own a debt on the issuer and receive fixed interest
They own the usufruct of the commodity and receive rentals
They own the commodity and are entitled to its sale price
explanation: Per 5/1/5/5, Murabahah certificate holders own the Murabahah commodity and are entitled to its sale price.

title: Credit Agreement
q: Bank A provides capital to Company X under a Mudarabah within a credit facility. When would Company X owe the capital as a debt to the Bank?
options: Whenever the Mudarabah operation ends with any loss
Always, since every cash facility creates a debt on the client
Only in case of transgression or negligence by Company X
Once the facility period expires, whatever the outcome
explanation: Per 2/2/1, Musharakah and Mudarabah are cash facilities but do not result in a debt owed by the client except in case of transgression or negligence.

title: Waqf
q: An overseer appointed by the Waqif wishes to step down. What is the ruling?
options: He may, with reasonable notice to the Waqif or authorities
He cannot, since he was appointed by the Waqif himself and accepted
He may only with a court's approval after showing a valid excuse
He may only after finding a replacement
explanation: Per 3/10/1, the overseer can dismiss himself, even if appointed by the Waqif, and should inform the Waqif or the authorities within a reasonable period.

title: Istisna’a and Parallel Istisna’a
q: Why does the Shari'ah basis forbid pricing an Istisna'a on a Murabahah cost-plus basis?
options: Istisna'a prices must be paid in cash
Cost-plus profits are always excessive
Murabahah is valid only for sales of gold and silver
Murabahah needs an existing owned item of known cost
explanation: The basis: Murabahah requires an existing owned item of known cost, while Istisna'a precedes ownership, its actual cost is known only on completion, and its price must be known at signing.

title: Arbitration
q: Company X refuses to implement an arbitration verdict, and the only available courts do not observe the rules of Shari'ah. What may Bank A do?
options: Seize Company X's assets on its own
Approach those courts to execute the verdict
Nothing; it may only use Shari'ah courts
Restart the arbitration with a new arbitrator
explanation: Per 13/1 and 13/2, if a party refuses, the other may present the verdict to judiciary; it is permissible to approach courts not observing Shari'ah for execution.

title: Online Financial Dealings
q: Why does the basis classify online contracts by audio or audiovisual communication as contracts between present parties?
options: Both parties are deemed to be present in the same place
The contract is written down on screen during the call
The parties are present at the same time, though not in one place
The communication is recorded and can later be used as evidence in court
explanation: Per the basis, both parties are present at the same time though not in one place, so simultaneous presence in time is fulfilled when offer and acceptance are exchanged.

title: Gold and Its Trading Parameters in Shari’ah
q: A trader sells 100 grams of gold for 1,500 grams of silver, with both delivered in the contracting session. Is the sale valid despite the weight disparity?
options: No, gold and silver must be equal in weight, as in gold for gold
Yes, disparity is allowed when gold is sold for silver
Yes, and delivery of the silver may be deferred until the next day
No, unless each is first valued in currency
explanation: Per 3/1/3, gold for silver is permissible regardless of disparity in weight, provided the countervalues are exchanged as required (spot).

title: Sale of Debt
q: A farmer owes Company X 1,000 kg of dates, and they agree he will settle it with dates of another type. Which conditions apply?
options: Any agreed quantity, delivered at maturity
Possession in the session; quantity may differ
Equal quantity; delivery may be deferred
Equal quantity, with possession in the session
explanation: Per 4/1/1/1(b), where the consideration is of the same Ribawi kind as the debt, equality (tamathul) and possession in the session are required.

title: Loan (Qard)
q: Ahmad hands Company X 1,000 dinars, transferring ownership to it on condition that Company X returns 1,000 dinars similar to them. How is this contract classified?
options: Qard
Wadi'ah (deposit)
Mudarabah
Hibah (gift)
explanation: Per 2, Qard is the transfer of ownership in fungible wealth to a person on whom it is binding to return wealth similar to it.

title: Guarantees
q: Two parties conclude a deferred sale. Under the standard, what is the status of documenting it in writing?
options: Unnecessary, as attestation always suffices
Obligatory, so that failing to write it down is a sin
Recommended; custom governs form and evidential value
Valid only in official, not private, documents
explanation: Per 2/4/1, written documentation is recommended (private or official); customary practice governs drawing up documents and their evidential value.

title: Stipulations and Ethics of Fatwa in the Institutional Framework
q: Two departments of Bank A ask the board the same question separately. The board answers each differently to suit them. Which ethic is breached?
options: Avoiding different Fatwas on one issue by request source
Avoiding Fatwa on matters outside the board's specialization
Being slow and cautious in explaining the Fatwa to the requester
Avoiding Fatwa when mentally preoccupied or physically tired
explanation: Per 12/2, Fatwa issuers should avoid issuing different Fatwas on the same subject and issue depending on who requested the Fatwa.

title: Waqf
q: Ahmad pledged his land to Bank A, then made the land a Waqf. A year later he settled the debt in full. From when is the Waqf enforceable?
options: From the date the debt was settled
From the time of its creation
It is not enforceable; it must be re-created
From the date Bank A releases its title
explanation: Per 2/4/5/4, Waqf by the pledgor is valid; once enforced (e.g., by settlement of the debt), its enforceability is from the time of its creation.

title: Mortgage and its Contemporary Applications
q: A creditor argues that the Qur'anic verse makes taking a mortgage obligatory in every debt. What does the basis say?
options: Mortgage is obligatory only on deferred sales
Mortgage is obligatory whenever the creditor asks for it in the contract
Mortgage is obligatory when there is no scribe
Mortgage is not obligatory; the verse indicates guidance
explanation: Per the basis, mortgage is not obligatory, without known dispute; the emphasis in the verse indicates guidance rather than obligation.

title: Waqf
q: A Waqf's revenue this year is less than the overseer's remuneration, and the roof urgently needs repair. What is the correct treatment?
options: The unpaid remuneration is forfeited
Repair first; unpaid remuneration stays a liability on the Waqf
The Waqif must pay the shortfall personally
Pay the overseer's remuneration first and defer the repair
explanation: Per 3/9/5, priority goes to maintenance and necessary expenses; the outstanding remuneration remains a liability against the Waqf.

title: Murabahah
q: A Murabahah customer undertakes to donate a percentage of the debt if he pays instalments late. How must Bank A handle these amounts?
options: Keep them to offset its funding costs for the period
Add them to its own income as fees for late payment
Spend them on charitable causes, not for itself
Return them to the customer later
explanation: Per 5/6, the undertaking to donate is allowed, and the Shari'ah Supervisory Board must know the amounts go to charity, not to the Institution itself.

title: Gold and Its Trading Parameters in Shari’ah
q: Ahmad wants to exchange his old gold bracelet for a heavier new gold bracelet at a jeweller, on spot, paying nothing else. Is this permissible?
options: Yes, since the exchange is made on spot
Yes, since the new bracelet is unused
Yes, if the jeweller agrees to the difference
No, gold for gold must be equal in weight
explanation: Per 3/1/1, gold for gold is permissible only if equal in weight, regardless of being new or old, with exchange as required by Shari'ah.

title: Zakah
q: Bank A's Zakah is due, but it wants to distribute it over a set schedule. For how long may it delay payment?
options: For not more than one year
Not at all; it must pay at once
Indefinitely, at its discretion
For up to three years
explanation: Per 10/2, Zakah is to be paid when due but may be delayed for not more than one year for shortage of funds, a distribution schedule, or obvious interest.

title: Ju’alah
q: A Ju'alah requires a mining result within one year. The year ends with the minerals almost reached. What happens to the worker's entitlement?
options: The contract converts into an Ijarah
The period is automatically extended
He receives half of the compensation
He loses any right to compensation
explanation: Per 5/3/1/2, a period may be stipulated, after which there is no compensation, except when the period ends and the result is close: the period is then extended.

title: Trading in Currencies
q: Ahmad pays Bank A local currency for a USD remittance abroad. What is the Shari'ah basis for combining the exchange with the transfer?
options: The transfer fee replaces the need for possession
The exchange may be completed after the funds arrive
Constructive possession via a bank draft, exchange first
Remittances are exempt from currency exchange rules
explanation: Per the Basis, the combination is allowed because a bank draft achieves constructive possession; the exchange takes place before the transfer.

title: Conversion of a Conventional Bank to an Islamic Bank
q: Converting Bank A must terminate all its previous interest-based transactions. Which verse does the Shari'ah basis cite for this?
options: Give up what remains of your demand for usury
Render back your trusts to those to whom due
No ground of complaint against those who do right
And get two witnesses out of your own men
explanation: Per the Basis, terminating previous impermissible transactions rests on: Give up what remains of your demand for usury (Al-Baqarah 278).

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: At the end of an Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek, the lessee is to acquire the asset by sale under Bank A's earlier promise. What must be done?
options: The original lease is simply re-signed
Nothing; title passes under the promise
The lessee only needs to notify the Bank
A new contract of sale must be drawn up
explanation: Per 8/3, in transfer by gift or sale, a new contract must be drawn up on fulfilling the promise; ownership does not pass automatically under the promise document.

title: Credit Agreement
q: Bank A charges a client a credit study fee higher than the study's actual cost of preparation. Per the Shari'ah basis, is this acceptable?
options: Yes, but only if the facility is then granted
No; only actual expenses may ever be charged to clients
Yes; the fee need not equal the actual cost of preparation
No; the fee must equal the actual cost of preparation
explanation: Per the basis, the study fee need not equal the actual cost, since it is a service that can be performed independently within the contract.

title: Combination of Contracts
q: Ahmad tells Karim: "I sell you my house for 10,000 dinars on condition that you rent it back to me for two years at 1,000 a year." What form of combination is this?
options: Two contracts for separate values with no link
Two contracts for a single lump sum value
A prior agreement with no condition at all
One contract stipulated as a condition in the other
explanation: Per 2/2/3, some combined contracts may be stipulated as conditions in the others, e.g. selling a house on condition the buyer leases it back to the seller.

title: Gold and Its Trading Parameters in Shari’ah
q: Company X pays gold as capital of Salam for wheat. Why does the standard find no Riba in this, unlike gold for silver?
options: The gold capital is constructively possessed
Each countervalue has a different Illah
Salam is exempt from the rules of Riba
Wheat is a non-fungible identified item
explanation: Per the Basis, gold as capital of Salam (or as its subject) is allowed where the other side is not gold, silver or currency: different Illah, so no Riba.

title: Documentary Credit
q: A supplier ships to Company X monthly and, within the credit's limit and validity, submits new documents for each new shipment under the same credit. What type of credit is this?
options: A revolving or renewable credit
A syndicated credit with several banks
A standby credit conditional on failure
A back-to-back credit backed by another
explanation: Per 2/3/3, under a revolving or renewable credit the beneficiary can repeatedly submit new documents for new operations within the credit limits and validity.

title: Competitions and Prizes
q: Bank A announces a reward-based competition but leaves its timing, location, tools and mode of operation undetermined. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible if a third party pays the reward
Permissible, as long as the activity is cultural
Permissible, since the reward amount is known
Not permissible, due to Jahalah in the competition
explanation: Per 2/3/2/1, a reward-based competition must be clearly defined to remove Jahalah as to timing, location, type, particulars, tools and mode of operation.

title: Indices
q: In an Ijarah, Bank A uses an index to set the variable part of the Ujrah that represents its return. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible
Not permissible, as Ujrah must be fixed for the whole term
Not permissible, as it is trading in an index
Permissible only for the first rental period
explanation: Per 5/4, it is permissible to use the index to determine the portion of the variable Ujrah (rent) that represents the return.

title: Irrigation Partnership (Musaqat)
q: After harvest, the dates of a Musaqat are stored awaiting sale. Absent any other term, who is responsible for taking care of them now?
options: The worker alone, until they are sold, as he worked on them
Owner and worker, each in proportion to his share
Whoever holds the storage keys at the time
The owner alone, from the moment of harvest
explanation: Per 8/1, after harvesting the worker and owner take care of the crop in proportion to their shares; before harvest the worker does unless custom or contract differ.

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: A customer buys a building jointly with Bank A, owning 30% while the Bank owns 70%. He then leases the Bank's share. On what is the Bank's rental based?
options: Any amount the two parties freely agree
The whole building less a 30% discount fee
Only its 70% share of the building
The whole building, as the customer uses it all
explanation: Per 3/6, the rental receivable by the Institution is only in proportion to its ownership share, since the lessee pays rent only on the share he does not own.

title: Financial Paper (Shares and Bonds)
q: A trading company's tangible assets, benefits and rights are 40% of total assets; the rest is cash and debts. May its shares be traded without the rules of Sarf or debts?
options: No, its shares may be traded only at nominal value
Yes, but only with spot payment and immediate delivery of the price
No, as cash and debts exceed one-half of its assets
Yes; tangible assets are not below 30%, so the rest is secondary
explanation: Per 3/19, where the activity is in tangible assets and benefits, shares may be traded freely if those assets are not less than 30% of total assets.

title: Gold and Its Trading Parameters in Shari’ah
q: An online platform sells customers unallocated gold ingots for currency, without the buyer taking physical possession. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible, if the gold's weight is specified
Permissible, since the price is paid on spot
Not permissible without physical possession
Permissible, if the platform stores the gold
explanation: Per 3/4, it is not permissible to sell an unspecified (unallocated) ingot without physical possession.

title: Distribution of Profit in Mudarabah-Based Investment Accounts
q: An operation of Bank A's unrestricted investment pool spans two financial periods. How is its profit allocated?
options: Over the whole period of the operation, by each period's duration
Entirely to the period in which it started
Entirely to the period in which it is completed
Equally between the two periods, regardless of the time in each one
explanation: Per 3/2/2, profit from operations extending to succeeding periods is distributed over the whole period of such operations in proportion to the duration of each operation.

title: Combination of Contracts
q: A Shari'ah board examines a Muwata`ah that might be an excuse for Riba. The intention is doubtful and there is a clear lawful need. Should it be prohibited?
options: Yes; a lawful need does not affect the ruling
No; prohibition needs obvious intent and no lawful need
Yes; any possible excuse for Riba is prohibited, even where intent is doubtful
No; only Bay' al-'Inah can ever be prohibited
explanation: Per 6/3/2/1, prohibition requires that the intent to reach a banned deal be obvious beyond doubt and that no obvious need or lawful interest justify it.

title: Waqf
q: Ahmad created a Waqf over his shop last month. He now regrets it and wants the shop back. What is the ruling?
options: He may resile, as Waqf is only a recommended act
He may resile until the beneficiaries take possession
He cannot resile, as Waqf binds him from its creation
He may resile if he compensates the beneficiaries
explanation: Per 2/3, Waqf is binding upon the Waqif from the instance of its creation, and he cannot resile from it.

title: Mudarabah
q: A Mudarib asks for a fixed monthly management fee in addition to his profit share for managing the Mudarabah. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible if the fee is below the profit share
In principle not permissible to take both
Permissible if paid from the capital provider's share
Permissible if agreed in the Mudarabah contract
explanation: Per 8/2, in principle it is not permissible to earn a share of profit in addition to a fee in a Mudarabah contract.

title: Options to Reconsider (Cooling-Off Options, Either-Or Options, and Options to Revoke Due to Non-Payment)
q: An option holder offers the item to third parties, then actually sells it to one. Per the Shari'ah basis, why does the option lapse only upon the actual sale?
options: An offer is a sale under all schools of Fiqh
The seller's consent is needed for any offer made during the option
Offering is permitted only after the option period has ended, never during it
Offering probes the price; selling is disposal as an owner
explanation: Per the basis, offering for sale probes the fairness of the price, but an actual sale testifies to acceptance, as the disposal is considered a disposal by owners.

title: Waqf
q: Which report supports allocating a Waqf to some children, such as divorced daughters, for a valid purpose?
options: Al-Zubayr's Waqf of houses for his divorced daughters
Sa'd's orchard given for his mother
Uthmān's Waqf of the well of Rūma for all Muslims
Umar's Waqf of his Khaybar land for the poor and relatives
explanation: Basis 2/4/4/5: al-Zubayr (RA) held his houses in charity for use by his divorced daughters, ending if a daughter remarried.

title: Islamic Reinsurance
q: After expenses and compensations, part of the contributions and their returns remain in an Islamic reinsurance account. Per the basis, where does it go?
options: To the traditional reinsurers as a rebate
To the policyholders' account as surplus for participants
To the company's shareholders as dividend
To the company as revenue and profit, as compensation for managing the reinsurance account
explanation: Per the basis (d), the remaining contributions and returns go to the policyholders' account as distributable surplus, unlike commercial reinsurance where they are revenue.

title: Gold and Its Trading Parameters in Shari’ah
q: Why does the standard allow gold jewelry to be leased?
options: The lease is of usufruct; the corpus stays intact
The lessee owns the gold at the end of the lease term
Rent paid in gold is in lieu of the corpus, so the lease is a sale
Gold leased as jewelry is not a Ribawi item
explanation: Per the Basis, leasing gold is permitted as the lessee uses its usufruct while its corpus remains intact; the subject is the usufruct.

title: Al-Wakalah Bi Al-Istithmar (Investment Agency)
q: An investor appoints Bank A as unremunerated investment agent for a fixed three-year term. After six months, the investor wishes to terminate unilaterally. What is the position?
options: He may terminate if he pays the fee for the full term
He may terminate at will, as unremunerated agency is a non-binding contract in all cases
The contract is binding; he cannot terminate it unilaterally
It is binding only if Bank A receives a fee
explanation: Per 4/1, investment agency contracts, remunerated or not, are binding on institutions as fixed-term contracts in which both parties agree not to terminate.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: Why does the Shari'ah basis permit a third party's promise to guarantee partners' capital?
options: It is a guarantee given against a commission to the partners
The third party shares in the profit of the partnership
The third party acts as an agent of the partners in the venture
It is a charitable act independent of the partnership contract
explanation: Per the basis, a third party's promise to guarantee is a mere charitable act and an undertaking independent of the partnership contract.

title: Zakah
q: A farm owns 50 camels used only for ploughing and irrigation. Are they part of its Zakatable assets?
options: Yes, at the camel livestock rates
No; working animals are not Zakatable
Yes, as articles of trade
Yes, if they reach the Nisab
explanation: Per 5/6/3, working animals, such as those used in land plowing, irrigation and carrying, are not part of Zakatable assets.

title: Concession Contracts
q: The State grants a utilization concession directly to Company X without any prior survey or exploration licenses. Is this permissible?
options: Yes, but only for water, not minerals
No; a survey license must always come first
No; an exploration license must come first
Yes; the State may offer concessions directly
explanation: Per 5/2/5, notwithstanding the procedural order, the State may offer exploration or utilization concessions directly without those procedures.

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: Why does the Shari'ah basis require a lapse of time before selling a sale-and-leaseback asset back to the original seller-lessee?
options: It gains a different asset's traits, avoiding 'Inah
To let the Bank earn enough rental income on the asset
To allow registration of the asset in the Bank's name
To allow the lessee time to save up the price
explanation: The basis: the time lapse prevents 'Inah, as physical changes or value changes during it give the asset the economic characteristics of a different asset.

title: Agency and the Act of an Uncommissioned Agent (Fodooli)
q: Ahmad, who has no right over a property, tries to authorize an agent to sell it. Per the Shari'ah basis, why is this agency invalid?
options: Agency is not allowed in the sale of real estate or other fixed property
Only paid agency can cover the sale of property owned by others
The agent derives his right from a principal who has none
The agent has not yet taken possession of it from the principal
explanation: The basis: the principal must have the right to dispose because the agent derives that right from him; he cannot delegate a right he does not own.

title: Distribution of Profit in Mudarabah-Based Investment Accounts
q: Per the basis, on what ground is distributing profit on constructive liquidation permissible?
options: Valuation is accepted in Shari'ah only where the assets are all in cash
Mudarabah profit is a lump sum fixed in advance
Expected returns are binding on the Institution
Shari'ah accepts valuation in several applications, such as Zakah
explanation: Per the basis, it rests on acceptance of valuation in Shari'ah in applications such as Zakah and theft, with the Hadith on valuing a co-owned liberated slave.

title: Agency and the Act of an Uncommissioned Agent (Fodooli)
q: Why does the Shari'ah basis limit a breaching agent's compensation to the gap from the market price, not a pre-set profit?
options: Because the agent is never liable for any loss
To compensate loss without a pre-fixed return on capital
Because the market price is always the fairest price
Because the principal may otherwise revoke the deal
explanation: The basis: compensating the market-price gap establishes justice without accepting capital on pre-fixed return, which entails a suspicion of Riba.

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: Bank A drafts an Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek with the clause on transferring title placed inside the lease contract itself. What does the standard require?
options: It must be stated in the master agreement only
It must be inside the lease contract itself, as a clause
The transfer method must be in a separate document
It may be oral if both parties agree to it beforehand
explanation: Per 8/1, the method of transferring title must be evidenced in a document separate from, and independent of, the Ijarah contract.

title: Salam and Parallel Salam
q: A Salam seller delivers goods of lower quality than the contract specifications. What are the buyer's options?
options: Reject them, or accept them, possibly at a discount
He must wait for the seller to replace them
He must accept them and pay the full price agreed
He must accept them and also claim a penalty from the seller
explanation: Per 5/3, the buyer may reject or accept inferior goods; acceptance is ethical, and the parties may settle on acceptance even at a discounted price.

title: Ju’alah
q: Per the Shari'ah basis, why is reasonable compensation due when the named Ju'l is vitiated (e.g. unlawful)?
options: By analogy with a bequest when the bequeathed item is later revoked
By analogy with Mudarabah when the profit share is unknown or vitiated
Because the offeror must pay a penalty for the unlawful stipulation
By analogy with Ijarah when the named wage is vitiated
explanation: Per the basis, recourse to reasonable compensation is by analogy with Ijarah, where reasonable wages apply upon vitiation of the named wages.

title: Controls on Gharar in Financial Transactions
q: Ahmad appoints an agent for a fee under a Wakalah whose subject matter is vague. How does the standard treat the Gharar in this paid agency?
options: It is treated like Ijarah and is affected by Gharar
It is treated as a donation, so Gharar is ignored
It is valid as a general agency in all cases
Agency is never affected by Gharar
explanation: Per 6/3, agency may involve Gharar when free of charge; if paid, it is treated like Ijarah (hiring) and is affected by Gharar.

title: Hawalah
q: Zaid owes Ahmad nothing but, on Ahmad's order, agrees to pay Ahmad's creditor from his own funds and recover later from Ahmad. What is this?
options: A transfer of right to Zaid
A permissible unrestricted Hawalah
A restricted Hawalah on Zaid's funds
An invalid Hawalah, since Zaid owes nothing
explanation: Per 5/1/2 and 6/3, where the payer is not the transferor's debtor and pays from his own funds with recourse, on the transferor's order, it is unrestricted Hawalah.

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: Bank A is asked to lease a house to a non-Muslim for residential purposes. The Bank has no reason to presume any impermissible use. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible only with a guarantor
Not permissible to lease a residence to a non-Muslim
Permissible, as the intended use is permissible
Permissible only for commercial purposes, not residential
explanation: Per 5/1/3, an Ijarah may be executed with a non-Muslim if the use is permissible, unless the lessor knows or has reason to presume an impermissible use.

title: Debit Card, Charge Card and Credit Card
q: Bank A requires a deposit before approving a card and forbids the cardholder from investing it. Why does the Shari'ah basis reject this?
options: It amounts to a loan that draws extra benefit
It makes the deposit a gift to the Bank
It turns the card into a revolving credit card
It breaches the card's approved credit limit
explanation: Per the Basis (9), barring the holder from investing the deposit is like a loan drawing extra benefit; it should be invested for him on a profit and loss basis.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: A third party voluntarily promised to cover Partner A's capital loss in a Sharikah, then fails to do so. Partner A claims the Sharikah is void and stops meeting his obligations. Is he entitled?
options: Yes, but only for the portion of capital that was lost
No, he cannot void the Sharikah or refuse his obligations
Yes, since he relied on the guarantee when contracting
No, but the other partners must then cover his loss
explanation: Per 3/1/4/3, the beneficiary may not claim the Sharikah is void or refuse his obligations if the guarantor fails to meet his voluntary promise.

title: Conversion of a Conventional Bank to an Islamic Bank
q: Converting Bank A buys a commodity on deferred payment and sells it for cash to raise liquidity through Tawarruq. To whom may it sell?
options: Only the bank's own subsidiary
Any party, including the original seller
The original seller, at a lower price
A third party other than the original seller
explanation: Per 6/2/5, Tawarruq means buying a commodity on deferred payment and selling it for immediate payment to a third party other than the previous seller.

title: Murabahah
q: After the Murabahah contract is drawn up, the supplier grants Bank A a discount on the same item. What happens to this discount?
options: It is shared equally by Bank and customer
It is paid to charity under Bank supervision
The customer's price is reduced in proportion
The Bank keeps it, as the contract is concluded
explanation: Per 4/5, even after the contract, the customer should benefit from such a discount by a proportional reduction of the total Murabahah price.

title: Procrastinating Debtor
q: A customer of Bank A stops paying Murabahah instalments because he has become insolvent. Does the standard on the procrastinating debtor govern his case?
options: No, insolvent or bankrupt debtors are outside its scope
Yes, it governs every debtor who fails to pay
Yes, once the delay exceeds a reasonable period
No, it governs only guarantors who are in default, not debtors
explanation: Per the Scope (1), the standard covers solvent debtors and guarantors in default, not insolvent or bankrupt debtors or those delaying for a Shari'ah reason.

title: Combination of Contracts
q: Which Hadith does the basis cite to show that Gharar may be forgiven in implicit aspects of a contract?
options: The sale of a slave together with his money
Ibn Umar's sale of camels at Al-Baqi' for dinars against dirhams
The prohibition of two sales in one deal
The buyer of an unpollinated palm may stipulate its fruits
explanation: The basis cites the Hadith on buying an unpollinated palm: the buyer may stipulate its fruits; the Gharar is forgiven as it is an implicit aspect.

title: Payment Cards
q: On a lending-based card, the acquirer charges Shop X 2% per sale and passes part of it to the issuer. Bank A wants to recover this fee from cardholders too. Is this allowed?
options: Yes, if the card is non-revolving
No, the cardholder shall not bear such fees
Yes, as the fee follows the agreement in the card contract
Yes, if the amount charged is capped at the actual cost
explanation: Per 5/1/2/1, the acquirer may charge the acceptor as agreed, with part to the issuer, provided the cardholder does not bear it in lending cards.

title: Financial Paper (Shares and Bonds)
q: Company X lets subscribers pay 25% of the share value now and defer the rest in instalments. What conditions does the standard set?
options: Deferred instalments must carry a fixed profit for the company
Instalments may apply to some shareholders only, at the company's choice
Instalments apply to all shares; liability limited to subscribed value
Subscribers get full rights in all shares before full payment
explanation: Per 2/5, share value may be paid in instalments provided they apply to all shares and the corporation's liability is restricted to the value of the shares subscribed.

title: Liability of the Investment Manager
q: When concluding a Mudaraba contract, the Mudarib offers on his own initiative to guarantee Rab Al Maal's capital in full. Is this permitted?
options: Yes, since it is voluntary and not stipulated as a condition of the contract
Yes, if it is limited to part of the capital
Yes, if Rab Al Maal accepts it in writing
No, volunteering liability at contract is not permitted
explanation: Per 3/2, absolute liability may not be stipulated on the investment manager, nor may he volunteer to assume the risk at the time of the contract.

title: Conversion of a Conventional Bank to an Islamic Bank
q: Converting Bank A asks whether it may take a commission for providing a mere credit facility to a customer. What is the ruling?
options: Yes, as a percentage of the facility
No, and no charge may be made even for actual expenses
No, but a charge may be linked to expenses incurred
Yes, provided no interest is charged
explanation: Per 5, no commission may be taken for providing a mere facility; however, the commission may be linked to expenses incurred in executing it.

title: Payment Cards
q: A card network offers Bank A incentive amounts for issuing cards managed by the network. May Bank A accept them?
options: Only if all of it is passed on to the cardholders as rebates
Yes, receiving such incentives is permitted
No, as they amount to riba paid by the network to the issuer
Only if paid in kind, not in cash
explanation: Per 5/3/3, Institutions may receive incentive amounts from the card network for issuing cards managed by such corporations.

title: Waqf
q: Which analogy does the standard use for spreading a revenue shortfall proportionally among specific beneficiaries?
options: The 'awal reduction in inheritance shares
Equal division in a partnership loss
The priority of a first-named heir
Preference of a secured creditor
explanation: Basis 9/10/3: by analogy with the 'awal reduction of inheritance portions and with the creditors of a bankrupt.

title: Zakah
q: Bank A holds a bad debt for four years and finally collects it. How much Zakah is due on it?
options: No Zakah, as it was doubtful
Zakah for one year after collection
Zakah for all four years, paid at once after collection of the debt
Zakah for two years
explanation: Per 5/3/1, for bad and doubtful debts the Institution does not have to pay Zakah except for one year after their collection.

title: Distribution of Profit in Mudarabah-Based Investment Accounts
q: Why does ignorance about the profit share nullify a Mudarabah contract, per the basis?
options: Profit must equal the expected rate of return
Ignorance makes the capital guaranteed
Profit is the object of contracting and must be known
Profit belongs only to the Mudarib, so the capital provider need not know its share
explanation: Per the basis, profit has to be known because it constitutes the object of contracting, so ignorance about it nullifies the contract.

title: Controls on Gharar in Financial Transactions
q: A restaurant obtains supplies regularly from a supplier, and the price is fixed later per an index, even after the goods are consumed. How does the standard treat this?
options: Valid, as Bay' al-Istjrar with forgivable Gharar in price
Void, as two sales are combined in one sale
Void, because the goods are consumed before pricing
Valid only if the price is fixed before each delivery
explanation: Per 5/2/2, Bay' al-Istjrar, where the buyer obtains goods regularly for a price set by normal price or an index, even after consumption, does not become void.

title: Conversion of a Conventional Bank to an Islamic Bank
q: Bank B received revenues believed permissible under a position of an authoritative school, though now doubtful. Must it dispose of them on converting?
options: Yes, all revenues of doubtful permissibility must be donated
Yes, if received in the conversion period
Yes, half of them must be donated
No, they are not subject to compulsory disposal
explanation: Per 8/1/3, received revenues of doubtful permissibility, believed permissible per a qualified Ijtihad, an authoritative school or eminent scholars, need not be disposed of.

title: Zakah
q: Company X trades in cattle, buying and selling them for profit. Which Zakah treatment applies to these cattle?
options: Both livestock and trade Zakah
Zakah on articles of trade only
Zakah on livestock only
No Zakah, as they are not grazing
explanation: Per 5/2/3 and 5/6/2, when articles of trade are livestock or produce, they are subject to Zakah on articles of trade only, valued at selling market price.

title: Sale of Debt
q: A solvent customer owing Bank A asks for a new, larger Murabaha and may use its proceeds to settle the old debt. When is this permitted?
options: If the profit rate is raised for the rollover
If the contract requires settling the old debt
If the Bank keeps the sale proceeds as security
If it is independent financing with credit approval
explanation: Per 4/1/3/4(a), the new Murabaha must be independent, not stipulated or required to settle the first debt, and given credit approval.

title: Hiring of Persons
q: On what does the Shari'ah basis rely for the permissibility of taking 'Arboun in hiring of persons?
options: What Umar did before the Sahabah, adopted by Ahmad
The Hadith "Don't sell what you do not have"
The consensus of the four schools
The analogy with Salam payment in advance, as a pledge of performance
explanation: The basis derives 'Arboun permissibility from what Umar did in the presence of the Sahabah, adopted by Ahmad, and a Fiqh Academy of Makkah resolution.

title: Murabahah
q: Bank A arranges a syndicated financing for a large Murabahah and claims an arrangement fee. Who pays this fee?
options: Nobody, as such a fee is not allowed
The customer, as a facility fee
The participants in the syndicate
The supplier of the financed goods
explanation: Per 2/4/4, in syndicated Murabahah the arranger Institution is entitled to an arrangement fee paid by the participants in the syndicate.

title: Waqf
q: Why, per the Shari'ah basis, must the Waqif have full legal competence?
options: Because the beneficiary must accept the Waqf when it is declared
Because the Waqf needs judicial registration
Because Waqf is an exchange contract
Because Waqf in its essence is a donation (Tabarru')
explanation: The basis states the Waqif must have full legal competence because Waqf in its very essence is a donation (Tabarru').

title: Possession (Qabd)
q: Why does the seller bear the costs of presenting and measuring the sold commodity, per the Basis?
options: Delivery is his duty, and what an obligation requires is also obligatory
The seller benefits more from the sale than the buyer
The buyer has no duty to bear any cost of the sale
The seller is a trustee who must bear all expenses relating to the goods
explanation: Per the Basis, delivery is obligatory on the seller by the contract, and a thing without which an obligation cannot be fulfilled is also obligatory.

title: Syndicated Financing
q: Bank A agrees to manage a syndicate for no reward, and the financing Institutions share the profit. What arrangement is this?
options: Paid agency
Non-paid agency
Mudarabah
Musharakah with a management fee
explanation: Per 6/4, in non-paid agency the lead manager undertakes to manage the operations for no reward, and the financing Institutions share the profit.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: A Sharikah contract gives Bank A a profit of 8% of its capital each year, with the rest of the profit to the customer. What is the status of this clause?
options: Valid, as the percentage is fixed at the outset
Valid if Bank A also bears losses by its capital share
Not valid: profit must be an undivided percentage of profit
Valid if the customer is the managing partner
explanation: Per 3/1/5/1, each partner must get an undivided percentage of profit, not a sum of money or a percentage of the capital.

title: Liability of the Investment Manager
q: To protect Sukuk holders, an investment manager sets up a new company specifically to give a commitment covering capital losses. What is the ruling?
options: Permitted, if the commitment is voluntary
Permitted, since the company is a separate entity
Permitted, if the manager holds under 50% of it
Not permitted, as it is an artifice (hila)
explanation: Per 4/1/1, as an artifice to the independence condition, setting up a company or legal entity specifically for this purpose is not permitted.

title: Investment Sukuk
q: Murabahah Sukuk funds have been used to purchase a commodity, which has not yet been sold to the buyer. May the holders trade their certificates?
options: Yes, but only at their nominal value
No, only after delivery to the buyer
Yes, trading is permissible at this stage
No, Murabahah certificates may never be traded
explanation: Per 5/2/15, trading Murabahah certificates is permissible after purchasing the commodity and before selling it, but not after delivery to the buyer.

title: Hiring of Persons
q: A provider delivers a future, well-described IT service that does not conform to the agreed specifications. What right does the employer have?
options: Reject it and insist on a conforming service
Only terminate the contract with no other remedy
Accept it, since delivery has occurred
Only accept it with a reduced pay
explanation: Per 5/1/6, if the delivered service does not conform to what was agreed, the employer may reject it and insist on a service conforming to specifications.

title: Insolvency
q: Supplier S sold machinery to Company X on credit and received 20% of the price. X is declared insolvent and the machinery is among the sequestered assets. Does S have the right of claw-back?
options: Yes, upon returning the 20% he has received, since the rest of the price remains unpaid
No; the right is for a seller who has received no part of the price
Yes, because the machinery is still identifiable
Yes, if X's other creditors give their consent
explanation: Per 6, the right of claw-back is established for the seller who has not received any part of the selling price.

title: Murabahah
q: Customer C asks Bank A to prepare a feasibility study for C's own benefit before a Murabahah and agrees to pay for it. What is the ruling?
options: The fee is allowed, but the study stays with the Bank
The fee is allowed only if the Murabahah is executed
