No fee; the study is part of the Murabahah cost
The Bank may charge the fee, and C may get a copy
explanation: Per 2/4/5, the Institution may receive a fee for a feasibility study requested by and for the benefit of the customer who agrees to pay; he may obtain a copy.

title: Arbitration
q: Bank A operates in a country where an acute need arises to appoint a non-Muslim arbitrator for a dispute. What is the ruling?
options: Never permitted; the arbitrator must always be a Muslim
Permitted, provided the verdict conforms to Shari'ah
Permitted only if the other party is also non-Muslim
Permitted, and he may apply any law he chooses
explanation: Per 8/2 and 11/1, an arbitrator is in principle a Muslim, but a non-Muslim may be appointed when acute need requires, to reach a Shari'ah-accepted verdict.

title: Financial Rights and How They Are Exercised and Transferred
q: Company X copies the registered trademark of Company Y for its own products, claiming trademarks have no value in Shari'ah. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible, if Company X's products are better
Permissible, as trademarks are not tangible property
Not permissible; trademarks are protected rights
Permissible, unless Company Y sells the trademark
explanation: Per 3/3/3/1, rights to trade names, trademarks, copyrights and patents have recognised monetary value and are protected by Shari'ah; violating them is not permissible.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: In a diminishing Musharakah for a house, Bank A requires the customer to bear all insurance and maintenance costs since he will eventually own the house. What is the ruling?
options: Not permitted to stipulate this
Permitted if his profit share is raised
Permitted as he will become the owner
Permitted for insurance but not maintenance
explanation: Per 5/3, it is not permitted to stipulate that one partner bears all insurance or maintenance costs on the ground that he will eventually own the subject matter.

title: Murabahah
q: Why does the Shari'ah basis accept constructive possession as fulfilling the possession requirement?
options: Because physical delivery is always impractical for a bank
Because the customer bears the risk anyway
Shari'ah sets no form for possession; custom decides
Because possession is not needed in a Murabahah sale
explanation: The basis: Shari'ah did not state a particular form of possession; it is left to custom, and any procedure giving control counts as possession.

title: Protection of Capital and Investments
q: A Rabb al-Mal claims compensation for opportunity cost after the Mudarib's negligence. Per the Shari'ah basis, why is unrealised profit not compensated?
options: The Rabb al-Mal waived profit by entering the contract
Compensation of any kind is Riba in Mudarabah
Profit belongs entirely to the Mudarib until distribution
It is non-existent wealth that has not yet been realised
explanation: Per the basis, opportunity cost is not compensated because it is non-existent wealth not yet realised; realised profit after liquidation is treated like capital.

title: Waqf
q: A tenant pays a lump sum (Kardar) at signing for developing the Waqf, plus a rent below that of similar property, gaining Haqq al-Qarar. When is this permissible?
options: In necessity, if no tenant pays normal rent plus a lump sum
Whenever the lump sum exceeds one year's normal rent
Whenever the Waqif did not expressly prohibit it
Only if the Waqf already has sufficient income of its own
explanation: Per 6/3/2, Haqq al-Qarar (al-Khulu) is permissible when dictated by necessity and no tenant will pay the normal rent along with a lump sum for development.

title: Competitions and Prizes
q: Which of the following falls outside the scope of the standard on competitions and prizes?
options: Competitions sponsored by the Institution
Incentives to improve employees' performance
Promotional gifts given upon purchases
Prizes offered to investment account holders
explanation: Per item 1, the standard does not cover incentives to improve performance of clients, employees and directors, job-related competitions or reverse auctions.

title: Insolvency
q: Bank A, which manages, as a paid agent, an investment fund it does not own, is declared insolvent. How is the fund treated?
options: It is not part of Bank A's insolvency assets
It is part of the insolvency assets up to the agency fee
It is shared equally between fund investors and creditors
It is part of the insolvency assets as Bank A manages it
explanation: Per 9/2, investment vehicles independent of the institution, not owned by it and managed on a paid agency or Mudarabah basis, are not part of the insolvency assets.

title: Investment Sukuk
q: Investors trade certificates of ownership of leased assets on an exchange. Which reason justifies the permissibility of this trading?
options: The issuer guarantees the nominal value of the certificates
The trading is in fact on the assets, which may themselves be traded
Market need permits trading in all kinds of certificates
Sukuk are negotiable instruments of debt, just like conventional bonds
explanation: Per the Basis, trading Sukuk representing tangible assets or usufruct is in fact trading the assets and usufructs; since these may be traded, so may the Sukuk.

title: Irrigation Partnership (Musaqat)
q: A Musaqat on mango trees sets a two-month term, although the crop normally needs six months to be ready. What is the problem?
options: Musaqat must always be for a full calendar year
The term must be at least three years for trees
The term must run to harvest or a period normally enough for it
None; the parties may set any term they wish, however short for the crop to mature
explanation: Per 5/3, the contract is valid until harvest or for a defined period in which the crop is normally enough for harvest.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: Per the Shari'ah basis, why is underwriting a share issue without consideration permissible?
options: It is a gift from the company to the underwriter
The underwriter becomes a sleeping partner in the company for the unsubscribed shares
It is a form of interest-free loan to the company, repaid at its nominal value
It involves no impermissible act like a fee for a guarantee
explanation: Per the basis, underwriting without consideration is an undertaking not involving an impermissible act, such as taking a commission for a guarantee.

title: Waqf
q: A scholar asks why family Waqf is permissible though it benefits relatives. What reasons does the Shari'ah basis give?
options: Umar's Waqf Hadith, and it finally becomes charitable
It is a form of inheritance before death
Relatives are always poor by presumption, so it is charity
The Waqif retains ownership of the asset through his family
explanation: The basis: family Waqf is permissible on the basis of the Hadith about Umar's Waqf, and because it is in fact charitable since it will finally become so.

title: Istisna’a and Parallel Istisna’a
q: An Istisna'a links payments to completion of each construction stage. On what condition is this permissible?
options: The stages are fixed by the contractor alone
The total price is left open until completion
The buyer pays the full price in advance at signing
Stages are customarily specified, without dispute
explanation: Per 3/2/2, payment may be tied to stages of completion if, by custom, such stages are subject to specification and identifying them will not lead to dispute.

title: Agency and the Act of an Uncommissioned Agent (Fodooli)
q: Why does the Shari'ah basis allow agency to be tied to a condition or a future date?
options: Customary practice overrides Shari'ah rulings on conditions in contracts
Agency is a binding contract like Ijarah, so conditions may be attached
Agency is delegation of power, not a transfer of ownership
Gharar is always tolerated in non-paid contracts such as agency
explanation: The basis: agency can be linked to a condition or future date because it is delegation of power rather than an act of ownership transfer required immediately.

title: Mortgage and its Contemporary Applications
q: Bank A appoints its subsidiary as agent to possess a mortgaged asset on its behalf. What rights of disposition does the agent have?
options: Wider rights than the Bank, as the actual possessor
The same rights of disposition as the Bank as principal
Only the rights the mortgagor separately grants it
Only the right to hold the asset, without disposition
explanation: Per 3/1/3, the mortgagee may appoint an agent to possess the mortgage; the agent has the same rights of disposition as the principal.

title: Documentary Credit
q: Per the Shari'ah basis, why may sight documents and bills of exchange not be negotiated for less than their nominal value?
options: It breaches the rules of agency contracts
It is a guarantee given in return for a fee
It takes the form of a prohibited sale of debt
It is a form of Bay' al-'Inah arrangement
explanation: Per the basis, negotiating documents payable on sight, including bills of exchange, for less than nominal value adopts the form of the sale of debt, which is prohibited.

title: Hiring of Persons
q: A contractor refuses to deliver the agreed service and fails to provide the suitable alternative agreed in the contract. What may the employer do?
options: Claim the full contract value as a penalty
Terminate and claim indemnity for the actual harm
Only terminate, with no indemnity for any harm he has suffered
Only wait until the contractor performs
explanation: Per 8/1/2, if the employee refrains from delivering the service and fails to present the agreed alternative, the employer may terminate and claim indemnity for actual harm.

title: Concession Contracts
q: A State follows the Fiqh view that the landowner has the right to utilize minerals against a fee to the State. Can it grant a mining concession over privately-owned land?
options: Yes, but only if the land is vacant
Yes, if the landowner is paid a fair fee for the use of the land
Yes; concessions may cover all types of land
No; privately-owned lands are not subject to concession
explanation: Per 5/4/2, under the view giving utilization of minerals to the landowner, privately-owned lands, vacant or built on, are not subject to concession contracts.

title: Combination of Contracts
q: Per the Shari'ah basis, why is combining several permissible contracts in one transaction permissible?
options: Freedom of contracting is acknowledged in principle
Combined contracts are never subject to Riba
Necessity makes all combined contracts permissible
Customary practice overrides the rules of contracts
explanation: The basis: freedom of contracting and honoring commitments is acknowledged in principle unless it leads to violation; Ibn Al-Qayyim affirmed this.

title: Islamic Reinsurance
q: On what ground does the basis hold commercial reinsurance impermissible?
options: It involves deferment of both of the objects of exchange in the contract
It rests on commercial insurance and involves prohibited Gharar
It is a donation contract lacking possession
It gives the reinsurer no right of option
explanation: Per the basis, commercial reinsurance depends on commercial insurance and involves prohibited Gharar; the Prophet prohibited Bay' al-Gharar.

title: Mortgage and its Contemporary Applications
q: Per the basis, why is freezing a current account balance as mortgage at the same Institution permissible?
options: The balance becomes the Institution's own property
Current accounts are trust deposits with no guarantee by the Institution
It is a form of Mudarabah from the outset
It is like mortgaging an asset already under the mortgagee's guarantee
explanation: Per the basis, it is similar to mortgaging assets previously held under the guarantee of the mortgagee (in the mortgagee's hands), which is permissible.

title: Zakah
q: A customer paid Hamish Jiddiyyah to Bank A to confirm his binding promise to purchase in Murabahah. Who pays Zakah on this amount?
options: Bank A, as holder of the amount
The two parties equally
The customer
Neither party, as it is a security
explanation: Per 5/1/5/1, Hamish Jiddiyyah is the advance paid by the client to confirm his binding pledge; Zakah on such amount shall be paid by the client.

title: Hiring of Persons
q: Bank A wants to sign a contract providing a specific, identified hospital service to a client, but it has not yet acquired that service. What is the ruling?
options: Impermissible until the Bank owns and can deliver the service
Permissible since the client has promised to hire
Permissible if the Bank pays the hospital in advance for the service
Permissible if the price is fixed in the contract
explanation: Per 5/1/5, for a specific service the Institution must own it and be able to deliver it; it may not sign with the client before possessing it.

title: Istisna’a and Parallel Istisna’a
q: Company X has a construction contract with Builder B but cannot pay him. It asks Bank A to step in purely to pay B on X's behalf, calling it Istisna'a. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible, as long as work has not started
Not permissible to be a mere financial intermediary
Permissible, if B agrees to the arrangement
Permissible, if X repays the Bank later in instalments
explanation: Per 2/1/3, the Institution may not be a financial intermediary between a buyer and a third party, especially if the buyer cannot pay, before or after work starts.

title: Zakah
q: An expert estimates (Khars) Company X's ripe grapes. What may be deducted and left to the owner before Zakah is assessed?
options: Nothing at all
One tenth, which is the Zakah rate for rain-fed crops
One half of the estimated produce, left to the owner
One fourth or one third
explanation: Per 5/4/3, Khars can be used when produce is ripe; one fourth or one third can be left to the owner, the rest being Zakatable after drying.

title: Debit Card, Charge Card and Credit Card
q: Per the Shari'ah basis, how is the percentage commission that Bank A charges merchants accepting its card justified?
options: As a penalty for the merchant's late settlement
As a share of the profit on the merchant's sale
As brokerage, marketing and a debt collection fee
As compensation for the credit given to the merchant
explanation: Per the Basis (5), the commission is partly a brokerage and marketing fee and partly a service charge for collecting the debt.

title: Controls on Gharar in Financial Transactions
q: Which Fiqh principle underlies the rule that Gharar in a corollary of the sold item does not nullify the sale?
options: "What can be forgiven in corollaries is not so elsewhere"
"Hardship begets facility in all contracts"
"Any property not existing nor ensured should not be sold"
"Need, public or private, has the status of necessity"
explanation: The Shari'ah basis grounds the corollary rule on the Qa'idah: "What can be forgiven in corollaries is not so elsewhere" (Majallah item 45).

title: Zakah
q: Bank A manages investment accounts as Mudarib. On what does the Bank itself pay Zakah regarding these accounts?
options: The full balances of all accounts, as they are liabilities of the Bank towards the holders
Only its share of profit or commissions, as cash assets
The balances plus profits of all accounts
Nothing at all
explanation: Per 5/1/3/2(a), investment accounts are a trust (Amanah) for the managing Institution, which pays Zakah only on its share of profits or commissions.

title: Al-Wakalah Bi Al-Istithmar (Investment Agency)
q: The agency requires investments yielding at least 10%. Bank A, without consulting the principal, invests at 5%, while the market average is 8%. What must Bank A compensate?
options: 3%, the gap between the earned and average market profit
5%, the gap between the profit earned and the stipulated 10%
Nothing, as profit is never guaranteed and the agent only owes his best effort
2%, the gap between market and stipulated profit
explanation: Per 10/2, the agent compensates the difference between profit earned and the average market profit (if below the stipulated rate), not the stipulated minimum.

title: Arbitration
q: Ahmad, a paid arbitrator, accepts a case and then withdraws mid-way, causing the parties actual harm. What is the ruling?
options: He may not withdraw, and his withdrawal is ignored
He has no liability, as arbitration is never binding on him
He may be liable for the actual harm caused
He loses his fee but bears no other liability
explanation: Per 5/2, arbitration is binding on a paid arbitrator; if he terminates himself after accepting, he bears any actual harm resulting from his act.

title: Mortgage and its Contemporary Applications
q: Bank A stipulated that the mortgagor appoint it as agent to sell the mortgaged asset on default without resort to judiciary. The mortgagor later wants to revoke this agency. Can he?
options: Yes, but only before any default occurs
Yes, since agency is a non-binding contract
No, unless he deposits cash equal to the debt
No; he cannot retreat from such agency once agreed
explanation: Per 3/1/4, the mortgagee may stipulate this agency to sell without judiciary, and the mortgagor has no right to retreat from it once agreed upon.

title: Financial Rights and How They Are Exercised and Transferred
q: A workshop repaired a client's machine, and the client has not paid. May the workshop retain the machine?
options: Yes, it may retain the machine until it is paid
Yes, and it may sell it immediately to recover its fee, without notice to the client
No, it must return it and sue for payment
No, unless the client signed a mortgage
explanation: Per 12/2 (b), a creditor has a right of lien; e.g. a manufacturer or worker may retain the product of their work until they receive the payment due.

title: Payment Cards
q: Why does the standard forbid raising card fees in return for a cash-back feature?
options: It breaches the card network's rules on rewards and incentives
It is gharar akin to gambling, with possible riba al-fadl
Cash back is a prohibited gift from the issuer to the holder
Cash back is always a form of riba, whatever its basis
explanation: Basis 5/6/2: this is gharar, comes under a form of gambling, with the probability of riba al-fadl if the benefits are redeemed or decreased.

title: Islamic Insurance
q: Islamic Insurance Company T can settle with a party who caused damage to an insured car, for less than the full claim, in the participants' interest. What is the ruling?
options: Not permissible; the full claim must be pursued
Not permissible, as the company is only an agent
Permissible if in participants' interest and compliant
Permissible only with each participant's written consent
explanation: Per 10/10, there is no restriction on reconciling with the injuring party if it serves the participants' interest and conforms to Shari'ah rulings.

title: Sale of Debt
q: A customer owes Bank A compensation for damage caused by his negligence to a leased asset. Is this amount a 'debt' as defined in the standard?
options: No, debt arises only from a loan contract
Only if it is acknowledged before a court
No, debt arises only from commutative contracts
Yes, debt includes amounts arising from negligence
explanation: Per item 2, debt is an established owed asset whatever its cause, including (i) a loan, (ii) a commutative contract, or (iii) misconduct or negligence.

title: Credit Agreement
q: Bank A charges a client a commission for a credit study of his creditworthiness, and then rejects his request. What is the ruling?
options: The commission is permitted only if the facility is granted
The commission is permitted, but the study remains the Bank's
The commission is permitted, and the study belongs to the client
The commission must be refunded because the request was rejected
explanation: Per 5/3/1/1, the commission is due as the client benefited regardless of acceptance or rejection; the study becomes the client's property.

title: Mortgage and its Contemporary Applications
q: A buyer on deferred terms promised to give a mortgage as a condition of the sale but refuses to provide it. Per the Hanafi view in the basis, what does the seller have?
options: The right of option
The right to charge a late payment fee
No right, as the condition is void
The right to keep the price and the goods
explanation: Per the basis, refraining from honoring a valid condition like the mortgage condition gives the concerned party the right of option (Hanafi view).

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: How does the Shari'ah basis distinguish permissible Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek from conventional hire-purchase?
options: The lessee bears ownership risk from the start
Ijarah rules apply until the end, then title passes
Sale and lease rules apply together throughout the term
Title passes at the start, as in a sale
explanation: The basis: in hire-purchase, sale and lease apply at the same time and title passes on the last payment; in Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek, Ijarah rules apply until term end.

title: Documentary Credit
q: Company X leases machinery from a foreign owner, who requires the rent to be paid through a documentary credit. Can a lease be the contract preceding the credit?
options: Yes, but only if the lease is first converted into a sale
No, the preceding contract must always be a sale contract
No, rent can only be secured by letters of guarantee
Yes; it may be a lease, agency or other contract
explanation: Per 2/2/1, the preceding contract is usually a sale, but it may be a lease contract, agency with commission or any other contract.

title: Liability of the Investment Manager
q: An investment agent claims a loss on a portfolio, while peer investments in the same market were profitable. Who bears the evidentiary burden in this case?
options: The agent, to prove the loss and no negligence
The regulator, which must investigate the claim
The investor, as the party claiming negligence
No one, since losses fall on the investor
explanation: Per 6/3, circumstantial evidence (qara'in) contradicting the manager's claim, e.g., peers being profitable, shifts the burden to him.

title: Guarantees
q: Bakr stipulated that Bank A must first claim from the solvent debtor. Per the Shari'ah basis, what supports such a stipulation?
options: A Hadith requiring creditors to sue debtors first
The consensus of the Fuqaha that guarantors are never claimed first
The rule that guarantees are trust contracts
Maliki and Hanafi views: claiming the guarantor is then pointless
explanation: Per the Basis, the sequence condition rests on Maliki and Hanafi opinions: if the debtor is solvent, claiming the guarantor is pointless unless the debtor refuses.

title: Protection of Capital and Investments
q: An investor argues a Mudarib should bear a market loss because he held the money. Per the Shari'ah basis, why is the manager not liable absent misconduct or negligence?
options: Losses in Mudarabah are always borne by the state as guarantor
A manager's liability exists only where the investor is a bank
He holds it with the owner's permission, as if it were with the owner
The Mudarib's possible loss is offset by his expected profit share in other operations
explanation: Per the basis, by consensus the manager takes capital with the owner's permission as his representative; loss in his hands is like loss in the owner's possession.

title: Murabahah
q: Bank A bought an asset from the supplier on a deferred price and now intends to sell it to a customer by Murabahah. What must it do?
options: Nothing, the payment terms are its own affair
Disclose that it bought the asset on deferred terms
Pay the supplier in full before it sells the asset on
Sell it only on spot terms to the customer, not deferred
explanation: Per 4/3, when the Institution purchased an asset for a deferred price for sale by Murabahah, it must disclose this to the customer.

title: Irrigation Partnership (Musaqat)
q: A Musaqat refers vaguely to "some trees on the farm" without identifying them. Per the Shari'ah basis, why must the trees be identified and productive?
options: To determine the Zakat due before the contract
To calculate the worker's market wage in advance if the crop fails to appear
To allow the owner to change trees during the term
To avoid Gharar; non-productive trees defeat Musaqat's purpose
explanation: Per the basis, identifying the trees and requiring them to be arable avoids Gharar; non-productive trees do not fit the purpose of Musaqat.

title: Mortgage and its Contemporary Applications
q: On what evidence does the basis rely to show that mortgage is permissible even when the parties are not travelling?
options: The verse on depositing a thing on trust with another
The verse requiring a scribe to record every deferred debt in writing
The Prophet mortgaged his armor to a Jew in Al-Madinah for barley
The consensus that travel is a condition of mortgage
explanation: Per the basis, Anas reported that the Prophet mortgaged his armor plate to a Jew in Al-Madinah and took barley for his family.

title: Guarantees
q: Per the Shari'ah basis, what is the authority for taking 'Arboun (earnest money) to secure performance of a contract?
options: The Hadith that the guarantor is liable
The practice of Umar Ibn Al-Khattab, permitted by Imam Ahmad
The Hadith on the seller who finds his goods with a bankrupt buyer
The consensus of all four schools of law
explanation: Per the Basis, taking 'Arboun is based on the practice of Umar Ibn Al-Khattab before companions, permitted by Imam Ahmad, and a Fiqh Academy resolution.

title: Possession (Qabd)
q: Bank A takes a mortgage over a customer's house, registered in the official register as valid under the law, while the customer continues to live there. What is the effect of the registration?
options: It is constructive possession, standing in place of actual possession
It is a mere record without legal effects of possession
It transfers ownership of the house to Bank A
It has no effect at all until Bank A takes physical possession of the house
explanation: Per 3/4, registration of a mortgage of immovables valid under the law is constructive possession and stands in place of actual possession in its rules and effects.

title: Options to Reconsider (Cooling-Off Options, Either-Or Options, and Options to Revoke Due to Non-Payment)
q: Which Hadith does the Shari'ah basis cite as the basis for the cooling-off option?
options: "No yield without risk taking"
"Do not sell what is not with you, and no profit from what is not guaranteed"
"Muslims are bound by their conditions, except a condition that makes lawful unlawful"
"Say: 'There shall be no Khalabah', then you have a 3-day option"
explanation: Per the basis, the Hadith of Habban Bin Munqidh: "If you are concluding a deal say: 'There shall be no Khalabah', then you shall have a 3-day option".

title: Salam and Parallel Salam
q: Why does the Shari'ah basis prohibit penalty clauses for delay in delivering al-Muslam Fihi?
options: It is a debt, so nothing above the principal is allowed
Penalties go only to the Institution, never to charity
The buyer bears the risk of delay
Delay is always caused by force majeure, never by the seller
explanation: The basis: al-Muslam Fihi is considered a debt, and it is not permitted to stipulate payment in excess of the principal amount of debts.

title: Insolvency
q: Seller S meets all conditions for reclaiming goods from an insolvent buyer and verbally cancels the sale. Is a court decision needed for the reclamation?
options: Only once the competent authority is informed
No; it takes place immediately without a judge's decision
Only once the goods can be delivered to him
Yes; reclamation requires a judicial order, as it affects the rights of other creditors
explanation: Per the basis, reclamation is cancellation of the sale, verbal or otherwise, taking place immediately without a judge's decision, the authority's knowledge or ability to deliver.

title: Conversion of a Conventional Bank to an Islamic Bank
q: A customer owes converting Bank B for a non-permissible service supplied before conversion and argues he need not pay. What applies?
options: He pays only half, the rest being waived
He pays and the bank keeps it as income
He must pay; the bank donates it to charity
He is released, as the service was prohibited
explanation: Per 8/1/4, the bank receives such consideration to donate it; the customer may not avoid paying, or he would get both the service and its price.

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: Ahmad leases a shop from Bank A. The lease says nothing about subletting. Ahmad sublets the shop to Karim for a higher rent. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible, at the same, a lower or a higher rent
Not permissible, as Ahmad does not own the shop itself
Permissible only with the Bank's approval
Permissible only at the same or a lower rent than his own
explanation: Per 3/3, a lessee may sublet to a party other than the owner for the same, lower or higher rent, unless the owner stipulated against it or required approval.

title: Gold and Its Trading Parameters in Shari’ah
q: Selling a gold-silver alloy for heavier pure gold is allowed, the excess pure gold being in lieu of the silver. Whose view does the standard follow here?
options: The Shafi'i School
The Maliki School
The Hanbali School
The Hanafi School
explanation: The Basis states that treating the excess pure gold as in lieu of the silver in the alloy is the view of the Hanafi School.

title: Islamic Reinsurance
q: Per the basis, the Islamic reinsurance contract is a binding donation by analogy to which practice?
options: Bay' al-Gharar, the aleatory sale
Munahadah: travelers' contribution to a pool of food
Hamish Jiddiyyah paid with a promise
Mudarabah between the reinsurance company and the reinsurance fund
explanation: Per the basis, the contract is a binding donation, analogous to Munahadah (travelers' contribution to a pool of food victuals) or to a pledge of donation.

title: Waqf
q: While suffering from a terminal illness, Ahmad creates a Waqf over his apartment building. How is this Waqf treated?
options: It is a perpetual Waqf binding immediately
It is a Joint Waqf with his heirs
It is deemed to be a bequest
It is void for lack of legal capacity
explanation: Per 2/4/3/4, Waqf during terminal illness is deemed to be a bequest.

title: Sale of Debt
q: A customer delays paying a matured USD Murabaha debt for three months, then settles it in euros. Which exchange rate must be used?
options: The rate on the actual settlement day
The rate on the Murabaha contract date
The higher of the maturity and settlement rates
The rate on the debt's maturity date
explanation: Per 4/1/1/2(c), the settlement-day rate applies if the debtor delayed settling the debt when it matured.

title: Loan (Qard)
q: Nothing is written in a Qard contract, but local customary practice is that borrowers repay 5% more than they borrowed. What is the ruling?
options: Permitted, since nothing was stipulated in writing in the contract
Permitted, as the excess is paid at repayment
Prohibited, as a stipulation by custom is like a written one
Permitted if the borrower is satisfied with it
explanation: Per 4/1, the excess is Riba whether the stipulation is in writing or is part of customary practice.

title: Possession (Qabd)
q: A bailee holds a car, and the owner sells it to him. Why does the Basis treat his prior possession as sufficient for the sale?
options: The owner's liability for the car ends at once
His bailment is converted automatically into a loan, which counts as possession
Possession is irrelevant to the validity of a sale
Possession aims at control and ability to transact, which he already has
explanation: Per the Basis, the purpose of possession is control over and ability to transact in the thing; if that state exists, possession exists too.

title: Protection of Capital and Investments
q: Company Y owns 60% of an investment manager and voluntarily undertakes to indemnify the fund's investors against any capital loss, without recourse to the manager. Is this undertaking valid?
options: Yes, provided Company Y charges no fee for it
No; the ownership relationship exceeds one half
Yes, since it has no right of recourse to the manager
Yes, if Company Y acts in the public interest
explanation: Per 4/2/4, a valid third-party undertaking requires administrative independence and no direct or indirect ownership relationship of more than a half with the manager.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: In a diminishing Musharakah, Bank A's equity falls from 80% to 50%, but the parties keep the original profit ratio. Is that allowed?
options: Yes, if losses still follow the ratio of equity ownership
No, the profit ratio must fall with Bank A's share
No, profit must always match the equity ratio as it changes after each unit sale
Yes, and losses may also stay at the original ratio if the parties so agree
explanation: Per 5/5, partners may keep the profit ratio despite changes in equity, or amend it, provided losses are allocated according to the equity share of ownership.

title: Impact of Contingent Incidents on Commitments
q: What is the Shari'ah basis for amending a commitment to absorb the impact of contingent incidents rather than ending it?
options: Contracts are binding only until conditions change after signing
Muslims should seek appropriate disposition, not rush to termination
A commitment may always be ended once either party suffers any harm at all
Termination is the only way to remove harm under all Fiqh schools
explanation: Per the Shari'ah basis, amendment rests on striving for appropriate disposition without rushing to termination, a rule adopted by the various schools of Fiqh.

title: Commercial Papers
q: Company X holds a 100,000 bill due in six months and offers to sell it to Bank A today for 95,000. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible if the drawer has a good credit rating
Permissible if Bank A charges no extra fee
Permissible, as the discount reflects the time value
Not permissible: it is discounting of commercial paper
explanation: Per 6/1, it is not permissible to discount commercial papers.

title: Syndicated Financing
q: In a Musharakah syndicate, the partners delegate Bank A to manage the operation. How may Bank A be rewarded for managing it?
options: By a share of profits stated within the Musharakah contract only
By a fixed percentage of the total capital stated in the Musharakah contract
By a higher profit share or a lump sum under a separate contract
By a guaranteed return on its contribution, whatever the syndicate earns
explanation: Per 6/2, partners may delegate one of them to manage against an increase in its profit share or a lump sum, with a separate management contract signed.

title: Mortgage and its Contemporary Applications
q: Bank A holds a client's documents of title to goods as mortgage. Per the basis, why is this permissible?
options: Documents are a debt owed by the shipper to the Bank, which the Bank may collect on demand
Documents are cash and thus valid as mortgage, like any other monetary instrument
Documents give the Bank ownership of the goods
Possession of the documents counts as possession of the goods
explanation: Per the basis, holding documents representing ownership of goods as mortgage is permissible because their possession is considered possession of the goods.

title: Ju’alah
q: Which Qur'anic evidence does the Shari'ah basis cite for the permissibility of Ju'alah?
options: The verse on partners who oppress one another, except the righteous
The verse on travellers seeking Allah's bounty while travelling through the land
The camel load promised for returning the King's beaker
The verse commanding the fulfilment of contracts
explanation: The basis cites the story of Yusuf: 'For him who brings it is the (reward of) a camel load; I will stand surety for it.'

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: A rental has two parts: one paid to Bank A, and one held by the lessee for approved costs such as major maintenance. The held part exceeds the actual costs. How is the excess treated?
options: As the lessee's own money to keep
As an advance to the lessor on account
As a penalty payable to charity
As a reduction of the asset's price
explanation: Per 5/2/4, the excess of the second part is treated as an advance to the lessor on account, while the lessor bears any shortage.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: At year end, partners propose a final allocation of profit based on the profit projected for the venture, without any valuation. What is the ruling?
options: Not permitted: final allocation must rest on actual profit earned
Permitted if the partners later waive any difference that arises
Permitted only where the Sharikah holds assets acquired for leasing
Permitted if the projection is made by independent valuation experts
explanation: Per 3/1/5/10, final allocation of profit may not be based on expected profit; it must be based on actual profit through actual or constructive valuation.

title: Murabahah
q: Bank A wants to apply the Murabahah standard to a deferred payment sale that is concluded on a basis other than Murabahah. Does the standard govern that sale?
options: Yes, provided the sale is preceded by a promise to purchase
No, such deferred payment sales are outside its scope
Only if the Institution takes Hamish Jiddiyyah in the sale
Yes, it covers every deferred payment sale of the Institution
explanation: Per clause 1, the standard does not cover deferred payment sales on a basis other than Murabahah, nor other trust and bargaining sales.

title: Hawalah
q: Which of the following brings a Hawalah liability to an end under the standard?
options: Write-off of the debt by the transferee
Liquidation of the transferee Institution
Death of the transferor
Unilateral notice by the transferor
explanation: Per 11, a Hawalah liability ends by settlement of the debt, mutual agreement to terminate it, or write-off of the debt by the transferee.

title: Payment Cards
q: Ahmad returns a defective item bought by card. The seller did not know of the defect. Bank A asks Ahmad for the exchange rate difference, per their agreement. What applies?
options: It is split equally between Ahmad and the seller
The seller must bear it, as the item was defective
Ahmad bears it and cannot claim it from the seller
Bank A must bear it as the issuer
explanation: Per 5/7, the issuer may claim such fees per the agreement; the holder may not revert to the acceptor, even for a defect, unless it was concealed.

title: Istisna’a and Parallel Istisna’a
q: Bank A concludes an Istisna'a with a customer for a ship before the Bank owns the ship or any of the materials to build it. Is this permissible?
options: No, the Bank must first own the finished ship itself
Yes, but only after a binding bilateral promise
No, the Bank must first own the materials
Yes, Istisna'a may precede owning the materials
explanation: Per 2/1/1, the Institution and customer may conclude Istisna'a before the Institution has title to the subject-matter or the materials it will be made from.

title: Rules for Calculating Profit in Financial Transactions
q: A Murabahah contract contains a clause obliging Bank A to grant a rebate if the customer pays early. Is this clause acceptable?
options: Yes, provided the rebate equals the unearned profit
No; a rebate may be granted but not stipulated in the contract
No; rebates for early payment are prohibited outright
Yes; early-payment rebates must always be stipulated in the contract to be valid
explanation: Per 11, the institution may grant a rebate for early payment provided it was not stipulated in the contract, taking regulatory directives into account.

title: Conversion of a Conventional Bank to an Islamic Bank
q: A board member asks why training staff and redesigning contracts can become obligatory during conversion. Which principle does the Shari'ah basis cite?
options: Necessity renders prohibited things permissible in such cases
Harm is removed to the extent possible
A means needed to fulfil an obligation is itself obligatory
Custom is an arbiter in commercial dealings
explanation: Per the Basis, conversion is obligatory; if it can be realised only by certain procedures and tools, using them also becomes an obligation.

title: Revocation of Contracts by Exercise of a Cooling-Off Option
q: The standard requires the revoking party to notify the other party. On what is this requirement based?
options: Abu Hanifah and Muhammad Ibn Al-Hasan, to avert harm
The agreed opinion of the majority of jurists
Analogy to Iqalah, done without increase or decrease
The maxim that contracts follow intent, not words
explanation: Per the Basis, notification follows Abu Hanifah and Muhammad Ibn Al-Hasan, contrary to the majority, to avert harm to the unaware party.

title: Islamic Insurance
q: Islamic Insurance Company T wants to add cases in its policy where the participant is deprived of indemnity. Under what condition is this permissible?
options: The deprivation cases are set by the company alone
The participant pays a higher contribution for them
The cases are first approved by the reinsurer
Justice and rights are preserved, with no abusive terms
explanation: Per 9/2, special cases of deprivation from indemnity may be stipulated provided justice, preservation of rights and avoidance of abusive conditions are observed.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: Company Z, independent of a Sharikah, offers to guarantee the capital of one partner against loss in return for an annual fee. Is this third-party guarantee acceptable?
options: No, a third party may never guarantee a partner's capital
Yes, provided the fee is paid out of partnership expenses
No, a third-party guarantee must not be for consideration
Yes, a third party may guarantee capital on any terms
explanation: Per 3/1/4/3, a third party may guarantee capital loss, but the guarantee should neither be for consideration nor linked in any manner to the Sharikah contract.

title: Monetization (Tawarruq)
q: According to the Shari'ah basis of the standard, why is 'Inah prohibited while Monetization is permitted?
options: 'Inah requires actual receipt, while Monetization does not
'Inah involves a deferred price, while Monetization does not
'Inah always involves gold or silver as the commodity
'Inah is a trick for Riba between a real lender and borrower
explanation: The Shari'ah basis states that 'Inah is a trick for practicing Riba: two parties who are in fact borrower and lender sell and buy back the commodity.

title: Murabahah
q: The owner selling a house to Bank A for a Murabahah is the customer's brother. What must the Bank do before entering into the Murabahah?
options: Require the brother to guarantee the customer's debt to the Bank
Verify it is not a fictitious sale or stratagem for 'Inah
Refuse the deal, since sales between close relatives are barred
Nothing, since family ties have no effect on Murabahah
explanation: Per 2/2/4, where the supplier has a blood or marital relationship with the customer, the Institution shall verify the sale is not fictitious or a stratagem for 'Inah.

title: Investment Sukuk
q: Company X, a manufacturer, issues Istisna'a Sukuk to produce equipment. In this structure, what do the funds realised from subscription represent?
options: The cost of the product to be manufactured
A loan to the manufacturer repayable on delivery
A deposit held in trust until the product is sold
The rental for the use of the manufacturing plant
explanation: Per 5/1/5/4, the issuer is the manufacturer, the subscribers are buyers of the product and the subscription funds are the cost of the product.

title: Distribution of Profit in Mudarabah-Based Investment Accounts
q: Bank A and its investment account holders agree to give a part of the profit to a charitable third party. What is the ruling?
options: Impermissible, as profit belongs only to the parties
Permissible only if the third party contributed work
Permissible only from the Bank's share
Permissible by agreement of the two parties
explanation: Per 4/8, in principle profit belongs to the Institution and the holder, but they can agree to allocate a certain part of it to a third party.

title: Murabahah
q: Bank A buys goods on the international market and its agent receives the bill of lading while the goods are at sea. What is the Bank's status?
options: It has constructive possession of the goods
The customer has possession of the goods
It has actual possession of the goods
It has no possession until the goods arrive
explanation: Per 3/2/4, the receipt of a bill of lading by the Institution or its agent when buying on the international market is considered constructive possession.

title: Salam and Parallel Salam
q: Bank A and a farmers' cooperative sign a memorandum of understanding setting quantity, specifications and pricing basis for successive Salam deals. When is each Salam concluded?
options: Automatically, at the start of each harvest season
Separately, when each contract is executed
All at once, upon signing the memorandum of understanding
Only when the goods are delivered
explanation: Per 2/1/1, a memorandum may set the framework for successive Salam contracts; the execution of each Salam then takes place separately at the appropriate date.

title: Islamic Reinsurance
q: A traditional reinsurer asks Islamic Insurance Company X to keep cash reserves for ongoing risks that belong to the reinsurer, on which X pays interest. What is the ruling?
options: Permitted, as the reserves belong to the reinsurer
Permitted, if the reserves are held for under a year
Not permitted; X should not keep such interest-bearing reserves
Permitted, if the interest is paid only from the shareholders' own funds
explanation: Per 6/2, Islamic insurers should not keep cash reserves for ongoing risks belonging to traditional reinsurers on which interest has to be paid.

title: Sale of Debt
q: An investor wishes to sell his Murabaha-based Sukuk to another investor for cash. What is the ruling?
options: Permitted, since Sukuk are securities
Not permitted for a cash price
Permitted once the Murabaha matures
Permitted at their face value
explanation: Per 9/3/1, it is not permitted to trade in Sukuk based on Salam and Murabaha for a cash price.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: Of the four categories of partnership classified by the Fuqaha, which does the Shari'ah basis describe as the most important?
options: Sharikat al-Wujuh
Sharikat al-Mufawadah
Sharikat al-'Inan
Sharikat al-Abdan
explanation: The Shari'ah basis lists 'Inan, Abdan, Mufawadah and Wujuh, and states that Sharikat al-'Inan is the most important of all.

title: Financial Paper (Shares and Bonds)
q: A broker offers Ahmad an interest-bearing loan to buy shares on margin, with the shares mortgaged for the loan. What is the ruling?
options: Not permissible, nor is mortgaging the shares for that loan
Only the mortgage is prohibited, while the interest-bearing loan is permitted
Permissible, if the shares bought are themselves Shari'ah-compliant
Permissible, if the interest rate is low and the shares are mortgaged
explanation: Per 3/5, buying shares with interest-bearing loans (margin sales) is not permissible, nor is mortgaging the shares for such a loan.

title: Syndicated Financing
q: Bank A, an Islamic Institution, is invited to join a syndicated financing with two conventional banks. All funds are subscribed and used through Murabahah. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible only if the conventional banks convert to Islamic banks
Not permissible, as syndication is only among Islamic Institutions
Not permissible unless the conventional banks contribute less
Permissible, since subscription and use of funds are Shari'ah-compliant
explanation: Per 5/2, conventional banks may join Islamic Institutions in syndicated financing as long as subscription and utilization of funds follow Shari'ah-compliant forms.

title: Insolvency
q: Upon Ahmad's insolvency, his undue debt of 100,000 is accelerated. Creditors approve reducing it to 80,000. A guarantor had guaranteed the original debt. What is the guarantor liable for?
options: Only the 20,000 difference waived by creditors
Nothing, as the reduction discharges the guarantee
80,000, the reduced amount
100,000, the amount originally guaranteed
explanation: Per 5/6, with creditors' approval the accelerated undue debt may be reduced, and guarantors are liable for the reduced amount, not the amount originally guaranteed.

title: Waqf
q: A tangible Waqf building has no revenue to pay its utility bills and employees' dues. May the Waqf incur debt for this?
options: Yes, via Shari'ah compliant financing at a fair profit rate
Yes, but only by borrowing from the Waqf beneficiaries
Yes, by pledging the building
No, Waqf may never incur debt
explanation: Per 5/1, tangible Waqf may incur Shari'ah compliant debt at a fair rate for necessary costs, e.g., fees, utility bills and employees' dues.

title: Online Financial Dealings
q: Bank A posts an e-mail message stating all rights and commitments of a sale without retaining any right of withdrawal if accepted. How is this message treated?
options: As a concluded contract in itself
As an offer
As a mere announcement to the public
As an invitation for contracting
explanation: Per 5/2, a message containing all the rights and commitments, without retaining the right of withdrawal if accepted, is considered an offer.

title: Guarantees
q: Bank A wants to market its Musharakah investment product to customers as a guaranteed investment. Is this allowed?
options: Yes, if only the profit, not the capital, is described as guaranteed
Yes, if all the partners agree to it
Yes, if the product is low risk
No, it may not be marketed or operated as guaranteed
explanation: Per 2/2/1, it is not permissible for Musharakah and Mudarabah contracts to be marketed or operated as a guaranteed investment.

title: Mortgage and its Contemporary Applications
q: A client mortgages his investment account managed by Bank A on an investment agency basis. The account earns profit. What is the status of the profit?
options: It is mortgaged along with the principal unless agreed otherwise
It is mortgaged only if the relationship with the Bank is Mudarabah
It is free of the mortgage because of the agency basis
It belongs to the Bank as compensation for the debt
explanation: Per 6/2, income and growth of the units or account are mortgaged with the principal whether the relationship is Mudarabah or investment agency, unless agreed otherwise.

title: Financial Paper (Shares and Bonds)
q: A broker earns commission on trades in shares of a mixed company. Must the broker eliminate part of its commission as prohibited income?
options: Yes, the whole commission must be eliminated
No; the commission is its right for the work done
Only if the broker also holds the shares
Yes, in proportion to the company's prohibited income
explanation: Per 3/4/6/3, elimination is not obligatory for the intermediary, agent or manager out of their commission or wages, which are their right for their work.

title: Sale of Debt
q: Why may a monetary debt be sold to a third party for a specific asset or the usufruct of a specific asset?
options: Possession of any debt is constructive, so the sale is a spot sale
The debtor's consent is presumed
It is treated by analogy to Hawala, the assignment of debt
Specific assets aren't debts, so it isn't debt for debt
explanation: Per the Basis for 5/2, specific assets and their usufructs do not represent debt, so the sale is not one of debt against debt.

title: Options to Revoke Contracts Due to Incomplete Performance
q: A car sold as "automatic" turns out to be manual, and it cannot now be returned. What is the buyer entitled to?
options: A replacement automatic car at no cost
A full refund while keeping the car
A refund of the price difference between the two types
Nothing, since the car cannot be returned and the option to revoke has therefore lapsed
explanation: Per 4/3/2, if return is impossible, the buyer gets a partial refund equal to the price difference between an item fulfilling the description and one that does not.

title: Documentary Credit
q: Bank A wishes to amend a documentary credit it issued without consulting the seller (beneficiary). For which type of credit is this possible?
options: An irrevocable credit
A revocable credit
A confirmed credit
A standby credit
explanation: Per 2/3/1, a revocable credit can be amended or cancelled without consulting the beneficiary; an irrevocable credit needs the parties' consent.

title: Agency and the Act of an Uncommissioned Agent (Fodooli)
q: A debtor appoints his mortgagee as agent to sell the mortgaged asset on maturity. Later, the debtor tries to revoke this agency. What is the ruling?
options: He can, provided he notifies the mortgagee in writing and pays him damages
He cannot, but only if the agency is a paid one
He can, since agency is basically a non-binding contract for the principal
He cannot: the agency is binding as it involves others' rights
explanation: Per 4/3/1, agency becomes binding when it involves rights of others, as when the mortgagor appoints the mortgagee as agent to sell on maturity.

title: Hiring of Persons
q: Bank A hires a contractor for a project and wants a clause making the contractor pay a set amount for delay in finishing the work. Is such a clause permissible?
options: No; penalties of this kind are Riba in all contracts
Yes, but only if the amount is paid to charity
Yes, if set with regard to normal practice and justice
No; only the employer can be penalized for delay
explanation: Per 7/1/3, in hiring of persons a penalty code may require the employee to pay a specific amount for delay, determined by normal practice and justice.

title: Investment Sukuk
q: An investor argues that his Investment Sukuk are simply a debt claim on the issuer, like a bond. Per the standard, what do the Sukuk actually represent?
options: A common share in ownership of the assets made available for investment
A loan from the holder repayable with an agreed return
A right to a fixed periodic coupon independent of the assets' performance
A debt owed by the issuer for the nominal value of the Sukuk
explanation: Per 4/2, Investment Sukuk represent a common share in ownership of the investment assets; they do not represent a debt.

title: Concession Contracts
q: A licensee hires land from the State to build a power plant and hands it back to the State at the end on the basis of Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek. May it sublease the land to a builder?
options: No, as the land is owned by the State
No, the licensee must build the power plant itself without sub-contracting
Yes, through an operating or diminishing Ijarah sub-contract
Yes, but only through a Salam contract
explanation: Per 8/1, the licensee may hire the land and present the project back under Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek, using an operating or diminishing Ijarah sub-contract.

title: Sale of Debt
q: Bank A enters into a new Murabaha with a delinquent customer. What limit applies to the profit rate in the new Murabaha?
options: It may include compensation for the delinquency
It must equal the first debt's profit rate
It may be raised to reflect his higher risk
Not above his rate if he were not delinquent
explanation: Per 4/1/3/4(d), the Institution may not compensate itself for the delinquency, and the rate may not exceed that for a non-delinquent customer.

title: Financial Rights and How They Are Exercised and Transferred
q: Bank A sells a car on instalments and stipulates that it retains ownership until the last instalment. Per the basis, what is the correct position?
options: Valid, as the seller may protect its deferred price
Invalid; it may instead retain possession as security
Valid only if the buyer agrees in writing
Invalid, and no security of any kind may be taken
explanation: Per the basis and IIFA 51 (6/2), transfer of ownership is a legal effect of sale; the seller may not retain ownership but may retain possession as security.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: The partners of a Sharikah decide not to distribute this year's profit and to set aside a share of it as an investment risk reserve. Is this allowed?
options: Yes, both non-distribution and such reserves are permissible
No, all realised profit must be distributed to partners at the end of each year
Only a profit equalisation reserve is permitted
Only by a court order on the request of a partner
explanation: Per 3/1/5/13, it is permissible not to distribute profits and to set aside a ratio of profit as a solvency, investment risk or profit equalisation reserve.

title: Ju’alah
q: After a worker has started on a Ju'alah task, the offeror prevents him from continuing. What must the offeror pay?
options: Only the worker's out-of-pocket costs
The full agreed compensation
Reasonable wages
Nothing, since the result was not achieved
explanation: Per 6/2, if the offeror prevents the worker from working after the work has commenced, the offeror is bound to pay reasonable wages.

title: Rules for Calculating Profit in Financial Transactions
q: What evidence does the Shari'ah basis cite for not stipulating a maximum profit limit?
options: "No harm and no reciprocal harm"
"Muslims are bound by their conditions"
"Allah has permitted sale and prohibited Riba" alone
"...except it be a trade amongst you, by mutual consent"
explanation: Per the basis, the absence of a profit cap rests on the Verse "...except it be a trade amongst you, by mutual consent", confirmed by an Islamic Fiqh Academy resolution.

title: Protection of Capital and Investments
q: Bank B, unrelated to the fund manager, undertakes free of charge to indemnify investors for losses caused by the manager's negligence, with recourse to the manager. Is this allowed?
options: Yes; recourse is allowed for losses from misconduct or negligence
Yes, but only if Bank B waives every right of recourse to him
No; any recourse by a guarantor to the manager is prohibited
Yes, but only if Bank B charges a fee for providing the guarantee
explanation: Per 4/2/5, a third party may, without consideration, indemnify against loss from the manager's misconduct or negligence and has a right of recourse to the manager.

title: Waqf
q: A leased Waqf asset needs renovation, and the Waqf lacks funds. The tenant offers to carry out the renovation. What may the superintendent grant?
options: Ownership of a share of the Waqf asset in return for the cost
Priority to remain tenant until his cost is fully repaid
Nothing; tenants may never renovate Waqf assets
A rent-free lease for as long as he lives
explanation: Per 8/1/3, the superintendent may allow the tenant to renovate, against priority to continue as tenant until he gets full repayment of his debt.

title: Settlement of Debt by Set-Off
q: Bank A and Bank B exchange promises that future debts between them, one in USD and one in EUR, will be settled by set-off. Which rate must the promise use?
options: A fixed rate agreed in the promise itself
The average rate over the life of the debts
The current exchange rate at the time of actual set-off
The rate prevailing on the date the promises are exchanged
explanation: Per 3, for future debts in different currencies, the promise must be based on the current rate at the time of actual set-off, to prevent roundabout Riba.

title: Loan (Qard)
q: During the loan period, a borrower sends his lender an expensive gift because of the loan. They had never exchanged gifts before. What is the ruling?
options: Not permissible, as it is given for the sake of the Qard
Permissible if its value is below 1% of the loan
Permissible, as it was not stipulated in the contract
Permissible if the lender reports it to the borrower's bank
explanation: Per 5/1, the borrower may not give property or a benefit to the lender during the Qard for its sake, unless it was a practice between them before the Qard.

title: Online Financial Dealings
q: A monopoly supplier of an indispensable service offers uniform online terms the public cannot change; price and terms are fair. What is the status?
options: It is voidable at the option of the adhering party
It is permissible and binding on its two parties
It is void because the adhering party cannot negotiate
It is binding only on the supplier, not on the adhering party
explanation: Per 8/3/3, if the price in an online adhesion contract is fair and the terms entail no injustice to the adhering party, it is permissible and binding.

title: Options to Revoke Contracts Due to Incomplete Performance
q: A man bought a servant, used him for work, found a defect and returned him. Which statement of the Prophet does the Shari'ah basis cite from this case?
options: "Overcharging a trusting buyer is forbidden"
"Muslims are bound by their conditions"
"No harm and no reciprocal harm"
"No yield without risk taking"
explanation: Per the basis, the Hadith of 'A'ishah on a returned defective serf, where the Prophet said "No yield without risk taking", supports the option to revoke due to defect.

title: Distribution of Profit in Mudarabah-Based Investment Accounts
q: Holders deposit and withdraw at different times during the period in Bank A's general investment pool. Which method can be used to distribute profit among them?
options: Equal shares for every account regardless of the amount deposited
Shares based only on the year-end balance
The scoring method: amount multiplied by period of stay
Shares based only on the opening balance
explanation: Per 5/1, the scoring method (currency unit x time unit) can be used; holders implicitly exchange Mubara'ah for aspects that cannot practically be catered for.

title: Gold and Its Trading Parameters in Shari’ah
q: An item containing 40% gold mixed with other metals (not silver) is sold for currency. Which treatment applies?
options: The currency must be worth more than the gold it contains, to avoid riba
No spot exchange, since it is not deemed gold
The sale is not permissible at all, since gold is mixed with other metals
Spot exchange is required as it is sold for currency
explanation: Per 3/3/1/1 (second type), at 50% gold or less it is not deemed a sale of gold, unless sold for gold, silver or currencies, when spot exchange is required.

title: Irrigation Partnership (Musaqat)
q: The crop did not materialize within the Musaqat term. In all, the worker worked 6 months, then stopped with a valid excuse; the crop took 12 months to materialize. What does he get?
options: A market wage for the six months worked
Half of his share, in proportion to time worked
His full share, as he stopped with a valid excuse before the contract ended
Nothing, since he stopped before the crop
explanation: Per 10/2, a worker who stops with a valid excuse gets the portion of his share corresponding to time worked relative to the total time the crop took to materialize.

title: Combination of Contracts
q: In a combined set, the object of a subsidiary contract is not precisely known. Does this Jahalah invalidate it?
options: No, it may be ignored in a subsidiary contract
No, but only if the Jahalah is very minor
Yes, unless the main contract is a sale
Yes, Jahalah always invalidates a contract
explanation: Per 5/2/2, Jahalah, which affects financial contracts, may be ignored with regard to the object of a subsidiary contract.

title: Unilateral and Bilateral Promise
q: Ahmad buys a car from Bank A on credit for 120,000 and, after the sale, promises to sell it back to Bank A on spot for 100,000. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible, since the promise followed the sale and was not part of the contract
Prohibited as 'Inah, though the promise came after the sale
Permissible, since a promise is not a contract
Permissible if a third party acts as intermediary
explanation: Per 3/3, a promise resulting in a repurchase ('Inah) is prohibited whether part of the sale or given before or after it; using a colluding intermediary is also prohibited.

title: Agency and the Act of an Uncommissioned Agent (Fodooli)
q: A broker known to provide agency services only against payment acts for Ahmad. Their contract is silent on any fee. Is the broker entitled to remuneration?
options: No, since no fee was stipulated, the agency is unpaid despite the custom
Yes, but only half of the usual market rate for such services
Yes, remuneration ascertained by customary practice is valid
No, unless Ahmad later agrees to pay him voluntarily after the work
explanation: Per 4/2/1, paid agency is permissible whether the fee is stipulated or ascertained by custom, as when the agent provides such service only for a fee.

title: Buyback
q: Bank A buys listed shares from Company X, which keeps the legal registration of the shares in its own name. What does the standard require?
options: Nothing, since registration decides ownership
Transfer of the registration into Bank A's name before any buyback
A guarantee by Company X of the shares' value at the buyback date
A document, e.g. counter deed, confirming Bank A's ownership
explanation: Per 4/2, if the seller retains legal registration, a document such as a counter deed must confirm the buyer's ownership; seller holds as trust.

title: Documentary Credit
q: A trader who is the beneficiary of a credit asks the executing bank to make part of the credit available to his own supplier. Which type of credit permits this?
options: A transferable documentary credit
A red clause credit
A standby credit
A revolving or renewable credit
explanation: Per 2/3/3, a transferable credit entitles the beneficiary to request the executing bank to make it available, partially or totally, to other beneficiaries.

title: Controls on Gharar in Financial Transactions
q: A sale contract gives the buyer an option to rescind with no time limit. What is the effect on the contract?
options: The option is void but the sale remains valid
The contract is void, due to Gharar in its form
The contract is valid but the price becomes deferred
The contract is valid; the option lasts three days
explanation: Per item 7, a contract becomes null and void if it contains a condition causing Gharar in its form, such as an option without time limit.

title: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek
q: A customer promises to lease an asset that Bank A will acquire. The Bank requires a sum of money to confirm his seriousness. What may the Bank deduct from it?
options: Only the actual damage it suffers from his breach
The whole sum, as the customer broke his promise
The rentals it expected to earn over the whole lease term
A fixed penalty amount agreed in the promise document
explanation: Per 2/3, nothing may be deducted from the sum except in proportion to the actual damage suffered by the Institution if the customer does not fulfil his promise.

title: Zakah
q: Ahmad holds Ijarah Sukuk. On what basis does he pay Zakah?
options: Always on the Sukuk's face value
On the market value regardless of assets
Only on the periodic distributions received
On the basis of the Sukuk's underlying assets
explanation: Per 5/1/4/2, owners of investment Sukuk pay Zakah on the basis of the underlying assets of these Sukuk, as indicated in the standard.

title: Procrastinating Debtor
q: Bakr, a solvent guarantor, delays paying a guaranteed debt after Bank A's demand. Which rulings apply to him?
options: None, since he is only a guarantor and not the original debtor
Only the rulings on penalty clauses agreed in the contract
The same rulings as apply to a defaulting debtor
Only the black list ruling, not the recovery of expenses
explanation: Per 2/2(b), all rulings applicable to debtors in default are equally applicable to guarantors in default.

title: Trading in Currencies
q: In a spot currency exchange, Company X asks to include a three-day conditional option allowing it to cancel the deal. What is the ruling?
options: Allowed if the option is granted to both parties
Allowed if the option period is three days or less
Allowed if the countervalues are delivered at once
Not allowed: no conditional option may be included
explanation: Per 2/1/3, a currency exchange contract shall not contain any conditional option or deferment clause regarding delivery of one or both countervalues.

title: Commercial Papers
q: Bank A, which holds a balance at one of its own branches, draws a cheque on that branch to pay a supplier. Is the use of this cheque permitted?
options: No, a bank may not draw a cheque on itself, as it would be both drawer and drawee
Yes, but only if the supplier holds an account there
Yes, a bank may draw a cheque on its own branch
No, only clients may draw cheques on banks where they hold balances
explanation: Per 3/3(a), a cheque with a balance may be drawn by the client against the bank, or by the bank against another bank, itself or one of its branches.

title: Options to Reconsider (Cooling-Off Options, Either-Or Options, and Options to Revoke Due to Non-Payment)
q: Under an either-or option, the period expires without the buyer choosing which item he will take. The seller has not revoked. What is the position?
options: The buyer is legally obliged to make his choice
The buyer must take all the items
The contract lapses automatically and the price is returned to the buyer
The seller picks the item for him, whichever he prefers
explanation: Per 4/2/3, if the period expires without the buyer choosing, he is legally obligated to do so unless the seller chooses to revoke the contract.

title: Islamic Insurance
q: The insurance assets managed by Islamic Insurance Company T fall in value due to market factors, with no fault of the company. Must the company make up the loss?
options: Yes, as it is the manager of the assets
No, only for misconduct, negligence or breach
Yes, if the loss exceeds a set percentage
Yes, up to the amount of its agency fee
explanation: Per 10/2, the company should not guarantee the insurance assets except in case of misconduct, negligence or breach of contractual obligations.

title: Waqf
q: On what basis does the standard hold that a change in purchasing power does not affect the value of a cash Waqf?
options: Analogy with cash loans
Analogy with Murabahah deferred prices
Custom in currency markets
The Waqif's presumed intention
explanation: Basis 2/4/13/4: by analogy upon such assets not being affected in cash loans.

title: Salam and Parallel Salam
q: Bank A's Parallel Salam has the same commodity description as its first Salam. Why is this not 'two sales in one', per the Shari'ah basis?
options: Because the second is a promise only
Because only one price is paid
Because the parties are the same
They are two separable Salam deals
explanation: The basis: Parallel Salam is two Salam deals separable from each other despite similar descriptions, so it does not lead to two sales in one.

title: Stipulations and Ethics of Fatwa in the Institutional Framework
q: A Fatwa offers Bank A a choice between two permissible actions. One realizes a lawful interest; the other leaves the door open for blight. What should the board do?
options: Always choose the option that is more profitable to the Bank
Avoid the option that leaves the door open for blight
Prohibit both options to be safe
Leave the choice entirely to management
explanation: Per 8/3, preference goes to the easier option, but if one choice leaves the door open for blight, it should be avoided.

title: Financial Paper (Shares and Bonds)
q: A manufacturing company with permissible activity has interest-based loans equal to 35% of its market capitalization. May Bank A invest in its shares?
options: Yes, if Bank A eliminates the interest portion
Yes, as the limit for borrowing is 50%
No; interest-based borrowing exceeds the 30% limit
Yes, as its primary activity is permissible
explanation: Per 3/4/2, the total amount of interest-based loans must not exceed 30% of the corporation's market capitalization.

title: Murabahah
q: Customer C suggested Supplier S to Bank A, and the Bank asks C to guarantee S's good performance. In what capacity does C give this guarantee?
options: In his capacity as co-buyer with the Bank
In his personal capacity
In his capacity as purchase orderer
In his capacity as the Bank's agent
explanation: Per 2/5/1, the customer guarantees the supplier's performance in his personal capacity, not as purchase orderer or as the Institution's agent.

title: Impact of Contingent Incidents on Commitments
q: After signing an Ijarah contract, the lessee claims his consent was defective from the very time of signing, though its effect appeared later. How does the standard on contingent incidents treat this?
options: It is a contingent incident that necessitates amending the rent
It is an external reason that terminates the contract automatically
It is a contingent incident because its impact appeared after signing
A defect of will, outside the standard, not a contingent incident
explanation: Per 1 and 2, defects of will exist from the time of signing even if their impact occurs later; they differ from contingent incidents and are excluded from the standard.

title: Options to Reconsider (Cooling-Off Options, Either-Or Options, and Options to Revoke Due to Non-Payment)
q: In a sale with a cooling-off option, the buyer voluntarily pays the price, but the seller holds back delivery of the item. What may the buyer do?
options: Claim compensation for the delay
Force the seller to deliver immediately
Demand return of the price he paid
Nothing; payment has confirmed the contract
explanation: Per 2/4/3, payment and delivery are not required; if one party pays or delivers and the other holds back, the first may demand return of what it paid or delivered.

title: Hawalah
q: After a Hawalah is validly concluded, Ahmad, the transferor, wants to cancel it on his own. Can he?
options: No, Hawalah is a binding contract
Yes, while the debt is not yet due
Yes, by giving notice to the payer
Yes, until the payer makes payment
explanation: Per 4/2, Hawalah is a binding contract and therefore is not subject to unilateral termination.

title: Impact of Contingent Incidents on Commitments
q: Bank A agreed to lease imported equipment to a client in an Ijarah, but the State then bans import of such equipment. How does the standard classify this incident?
options: A matter outside the standard because it was caused by the State
A defect of will existing at signing, which renders the whole lease void
A contingency requiring amendment, not termination, of the contract
A Jawa'ih incident requiring a discount of the full rent amount
explanation: Per 4/3, prevention of importation of goods for a Murabahah or Ijarah is an amendment-type contingency; actual harm is removed by reconciliation, arbitration or law.

title: Sharikah (Musharakah) and Modern Corporations
q: Partners in a joint-liability company agreed on a ten-year duration. In year four, one partner notifies the others he is withdrawing. What is the ruling?
options: He may not withdraw, as the agreed duration must be observed
He may withdraw if he brings in a substitute partner approved by the court
He may withdraw without notice at any time
He may withdraw since the contract is not binding on any of the partners
explanation: Per 4/2/2/2, withdrawal is allowed if no duration was set; if partners agreed on a duration it must be observed. Notice and no damage are also required.

title: Insolvency
q: After Ahmad's assets have been distributed, creditor E proves a debt that existed before the insolvency. How does E obtain his share?
options: From Ahmad's tools of trade and his home, which were left to him after sequestration
From each existing creditor, by mutual consent or litigation
From the fees paid to the administrators
He cannot, since the distribution is final
explanation: Per 8/3/6, if a debt is discovered after distribution, the new creditor obtains his share from each existing creditor by mutual consent or through litigation.

title: Controls on Gharar in Financial Transactions
q: Which reported prohibition does the Shari'ah basis cite to support nullity of a contract whose duration is unknown?
options: Bay' al-Thunya, sale with an exception that is not specified
Bay' al-Munabadhah, throwing the sold goods
Bay' al-Hasah, sale concluded by the throw of a stone
Habal al-Habalah, price deferred to an unborn camel's birth
explanation: The basis cites the prohibition of Bay' Habal al-Habalah, where the price is postponed until a camel's fetus is born and gives birth, and the verse on fixed-term debts.

title: Istisna’a and Parallel Istisna’a
q: Bank A takes over a project abandoned by a customer's previous contractor. Must the Bank use that previous contractor to finish the work?
options: No, it may finish the work by any means it sees fit
Yes, the previous contractor must finish his own work
No, but the customer must choose the builder
Yes, unless the customer agrees to another contractor
explanation: Per 4/2/2, the Institution is not bound to deal with the previous contractor and may stipulate that the work be completed by any means it deems fit.

title: Waqf
q: Ahmad wants to make a Waqf whose income goes to a specific group of wealthy relatives, not to any charity. The purpose involves no sin. What is the ruling?
options: Impermissible; every Waqf must be charitable from the start
Impermissible; Waqf for the rich is barred
Permissible only if the relatives are poor
Permissible; a Waqf need not be charitable at inception
explanation: Per 3/3/1 and 3/3/2, Waqf must not be for an impermissible purpose but need not be charitable from inception; Waqf for the rich is permissible.

title: Concession Contracts
q: Which of the following is outside the scope of the standard on Concession Contracts?
options: Concessions for management of public utilities
Concessions for construction of projects
Franchises
Concessions for the utilization of minerals
explanation: Per Scope (1), the standard does not cover franchises, which should be dealt with by a separate standard, nor legal or consensual subsidiary concession rights.

title: Mortgage and its Contemporary Applications
q: A client offers Bank A, as mortgage, usufruct-based Sukuk representing common shares in the usufructs of specific assets. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible only if converted into tangible assets
Permissible to mortgage them
Impermissible unless the lessee agrees
Impermissible, as usufructs cannot be sold
explanation: Per 4/2, it is permissible to mortgage usufruct-based Sukuk representing common shares in the usufructs of specific assets.

title: Financial Rights and How They Are Exercised and Transferred
q: Company X bought a co-owned plot on deferred payment over two years. The co-owner Ahmad exercises Shuf'ah. On what terms does he acquire it?
options: At the market value on the date of exercise
On deferred terms, but the conveyancing costs fall on Company X as buyer
Only for immediate cash payment of the price
On the buyer's terms, including deferral, with the usual costs
explanation: Per 7/2/1, the preemptor takes the buyer's place and buys on the same terms (e.g. deferred payment), also assuming the buyer's liabilities such as usual conveyancing costs.

title: Agency and the Act of an Uncommissioned Agent (Fodooli)
q: Karim sold Ahmad's car on Ahmad's behalf. Only afterwards did Karim learn that Ahmad had appointed him as agent before the sale. How is the sale treated?
options: It falls under agency from the moment Karim learns of it
It falls under agency, as the appointment came first
The prior sale does not fall under the agency contract
It binds Ahmad because an agent is a trustee
